2025-in-review-sexual-violence-cases-rul.en:
The year 2025 began with a sentence in the RG Kar case and ended with the Supreme Court stepping into the Unnao case. In between, India watched a former MP convicted of rape, two campuses become crime scenes, a student die after her complaint went nowhere, and its highest court argue with itself and with the government about teenagers and consent. This timeline puts the year's cases and rulings in order. No survivor is named, and accused people are named only if convicted. Each event has its own case file on this site.

## January to March: verdicts, a bus depot and a rebuke

**20 January.** A Sealdah court sentenced the man convicted of the August 2024 rape and murder of a trainee doctor at RG Kar Medical College to life imprisonment for the rest of his natural life, refusing the death penalty because the crime was not "rarest of the rare" [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. On 7 February the Calcutta High Court dismissed the state's appeal for death, leaving the CBI's appeal to proceed [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]].

**25 February.** A woman was allegedly raped inside a parked state transport bus at Swargate bus station in Pune [[theprint-msrtc-audit-2025]]. Within two days Maharashtra ordered a security audit of every state bus depot; in March four officials were suspended for negligence [[fpj-msrtc-suspensions-2025]], and in mid-April police filed an 893-page chargesheet [[tribune-pune-chargesheet-2025]].

**17 and 26 March.** An Allahabad High Court judge held that acts alleged against two men in a case involving an 11-year-old girl were "preparation", not attempt to rape. Nine days later the Supreme Court stayed his observations, saying they were unknown to the "canons of law" and showed an "inhuman approach" [[livelaw-allahabad-stay-2025]] [[pti-allahabad-stay-2025]]. In April the same bench criticised another Allahabad bail order that said a complainant had "invited trouble" [[scroll-invited-trouble-2025]].

## May to July: teenagers, campuses and a committee that failed

**23 May.** In In Re: Right to Privacy of Adolescents, the Supreme Court used Article 142 to spare a man convicted under POCSO from his 20-year sentence, because the girl, now his wife, had been harmed more by the system than by the act [[sc-adolescents-privacy-2025]]. "The society judged her, the legal system failed her, and her own family abandoned her," it wrote [[scobserver-adolescents-2025]]. It asked the Women and Child Development Ministry to set up an expert committee on suggestions including comprehensive sex education.

**25 June.** A law student was allegedly gang-raped inside her college in south Kolkata; a chargesheet followed in 58 days [[ians-kasba-chargesheet-2025]]. On 3 July the Calcutta High Court shut every student union room in West Bengal until student elections are held [[livelaw-calcutta-hc-union-rooms-2025]].

**1 to 15 July.** A 20-year-old student in Balasore, Odisha, complained in writing to her college's Internal Complaints Committee that the head of her department was sexually harassing her. Within two weeks she had died [[pti-balasore-complaint-2025]]. On 15 July the UGC set up a fact-finding committee on the college's compliance with its harassment regulations [[odishabytes-ugc-panel-2025]].

**Late July.** In the long-pending Nipun Saxena case, the court's amicus asked it to stop criminalising consensual sex between 16- and 18-year-olds [[barandbench-age-of-consent-2025]]. The Centre replied that 18 must stay, and that leeway in hard cases must remain with judges [[tribune-age-of-consent-centre-2025]].

## August to December: a life sentence, a remark and a nine-year wait

**1 and 2 August.** A Bengaluru special court convicted former MP Prajwal Revanna of raping a domestic worker employed by his family, under the provision for rape by a man in a position of control or dominance, and sentenced him to life [[theprint-revanna-sentence-2025]]. On 5 August the Supreme Court gave the national task force on doctors' safety, set up after RG Kar, eight more weeks to reply to the states' reports [[theprint-ntf-reply-2025]].

**10 October.** A medical student was allegedly gang-raped near her college in Durgapur; police filed a chargesheet in 20 days [[ians-durgapur-chargesheet-2025]]. West Bengal's Chief Minister said "The girls should not be allowed to go outside (college) at night", later saying her words had been twisted [[tribune-durgapur-remark-2025]].

**December.** On 3 December the Karnataka High Court refused to suspend Revanna's sentence pending appeal [[livelaw-revanna-hc-suspension-2025]]. On 8 and 12 December an Ernakulam court convicted six men in the 2017 Kerala actor assault case, sentencing each to 20 years, and acquitted four [[thefederal-kerala-actor-verdict-2025]]. On 29 December the Supreme Court stayed the Delhi High Court's suspension of the Unnao convict's life sentence [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]].

## The pattern underneath

Three threads run through the year.

**Speed at the start, delay at the end.** Police filed chargesheets in 20 days in Durgapur, 58 in Kolkata and under two months in Pune. But fast-track courts disposed of 66,500 rape and POCSO cases in 2025, down from 85,595 in 2024 [[pib-fast-track-courts-impact-2026]], and 2,45,579 such cases were pending before them at the end of 2025 [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. None of the three campus and transport trials had produced a verdict we could find by November 2026.

**Words as harm.** A judge's description of a child's case, a bail order that said a woman "invited trouble", a Chief Minister's advice to keep girls in at night. In February 2026 the Supreme Court finally set the Allahabad order aside and asked for formal guidelines on judicial sensitivity [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]] [[hansindia-sc-sets-aside-allahabad-2026]]; in July 2026 it sent those guidelines to every court in the country [[theprint-sc-sensitivity-guidelines-2026]].

**Power inside institutions.** An MP and the woman who worked in his family's home. A former student who ran a union room. A head of department and a complaints committee. In 2025 the danger was rarely a stranger. It was someone with access and authority, inside a place that was supposed to be safe.

The age-of-consent hearing was listed from 12 November 2025 [[dtnext-age-of-consent-hearing-2025]]; we found no ruling as of 23 November 2026. Several 2025 cases are now in appeal. The year's real verdict is still pending. If any of this is weighing on you, Tele-MANAS is on 14416, free and round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].
2025-in-review-sexual-violence-cases-rul.hg:
2025 ki shuruaat RG Kar case mein saza se hui aur ant Unnao case mein Supreme Court ke dakhal se. Beech mein India ne dekha ki ek former MP rape ka doshi paaya gaya, do campus crime ki jagah bane, ek student ki maut hui jab uski complaint kahin nahi pahunchi, aur desh ki sabse oonchi court teenagers aur consent par khud se aur sarkar se behas karti rahi. Yeh timeline saal ke cases aur faislon ko kram se rakhti hai. Kisi survivor ka naam nahi hai, aur accused ka naam sirf tab hai jab conviction hua ho. Har ghatna ki is site par apni case file hai.

## January se March: verdicts, ek bus depot aur ek fatkaar

**20 January.** Sealdah court ne August 2024 mein RG Kar Medical College mein ek trainee doctor ke rape aur murder ke convict ko baaki poori natural life ki umrqaid di, aur death penalty se mana kiya kyunki crime "rarest of the rare" nahi tha [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. 7 February ko Calcutta High Court ne death ke liye state ki appeal khaarij ki, aur CBI ki appeal aage badhne di [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]].

**25 February.** Pune ke Swargate bus station par khadi ek state transport bus mein ek aurat ka kathit rape hua [[theprint-msrtc-audit-2025]]. Do din mein Maharashtra ne har state bus depot ka security audit order kiya; March mein chaar officials laparwahi ke liye suspend hue [[fpj-msrtc-suspensions-2025]], aur April ke beech police ne 893 pages ki chargesheet file ki [[tribune-pune-chargesheet-2025]].

**17 aur 26 March.** Allahabad High Court ke ek judge ne kaha ki 11 saal ki bachchi ke case mein do aadmiyon par lage aarop "preparation" the, attempt to rape nahi. Nau din baad Supreme Court ne unke observations par rok lagayi, kehte hue ki yeh "canons of law", yaani law ke usoolon ke liye anjaan hain aur ek "inhuman approach", yaani amaanviya soch, dikhate hain [[livelaw-allahabad-stay-2025]] [[pti-allahabad-stay-2025]]. April mein usi bench ne Allahabad ke ek aur bail order ki aalochna ki jisme kaha gaya tha ki complainant ne "invited trouble" [[scroll-invited-trouble-2025]].

## May se July: teenagers, campus aur ek fail committee

**23 May.** In Re: Right to Privacy of Adolescents mein Supreme Court ne Article 142 se POCSO ke ek convict ko 20 saal ki saza se bacha liya, kyunki ladki, jo ab uski patni thi, ko act se zyada system ne nuksaan pahunchaya tha [[sc-adolescents-privacy-2025]]. Court ne likha: "The society judged her, the legal system failed her, and her own family abandoned her" [[scobserver-adolescents-2025]]. Usne Women and Child Development Ministry se comprehensive sex education samet suggestions par expert committee banane ko kaha.

**25 June.** South Kolkata mein ek law student ka uske college mein kathit gang rape hua; 58 din mein chargesheet aayi [[ians-kasba-chargesheet-2025]]. 3 July ko Calcutta High Court ne West Bengal ke har student union room ko student elections hone tak band kar diya [[livelaw-calcutta-hc-union-rooms-2025]].

**1 se 15 July.** Odisha ke Balasore mein ek 20 saal ki student ne apne college ki Internal Complaints Committee ko likh kar complaint ki ki uske department ka head use sexually harass kar raha hai. Do hafton ke andar uski maut ho gayi [[pti-balasore-complaint-2025]]. 15 July ko UGC ne college ke harassment regulations ke paalan par fact-finding committee banayi [[odishabytes-ugc-panel-2025]].

**July ka aakhir.** Barson se pending Nipun Saxena case mein court ki amicus ne kaha ki 16 se 18 saal ke teenagers ke beech consensual sex ko crime maanna band ho [[barandbench-age-of-consent-2025]]. Centre ne jawab diya ki 18 hi rahe, aur mushkil cases mein chhoot judges ke haath mein rahe [[tribune-age-of-consent-centre-2025]].

## August se December: umrqaid, ek remark aur nau saal ka intezaar

**1 aur 2 August.** Bengaluru ki special court ne former MP Prajwal Revanna ko unke parivaar ke ghar kaam karne wali domestic worker ke rape ka doshi paaya, us provision ke under jo control ya dabdabe ki position wale aadmi ke rape ke liye hai, aur umrqaid di [[theprint-revanna-sentence-2025]]. 5 August ko Supreme Court ne RG Kar ke baad bani doctors ki safety wali national task force ko states ki reports par jawab ke liye aath hafte aur diye [[theprint-ntf-reply-2025]].

**10 October.** Durgapur mein ek medical student ka uske college ke paas kathit gang rape hua; police ne 20 din mein chargesheet file ki [[ians-durgapur-chargesheet-2025]]. West Bengal ki Chief Minister ne kaha "The girls should not be allowed to go outside (college) at night", aur baad mein kaha ki unke shabdon ko tod-marod diya gaya [[tribune-durgapur-remark-2025]].

**December.** 3 December ko Karnataka High Court ne appeal ke dauraan Revanna ki saza suspend karne se mana kiya [[livelaw-revanna-hc-suspension-2025]]. 8 aur 12 December ko Ernakulam ki court ne 2017 ke Kerala actor assault case mein chhe aadmiyon ko doshi paaya, har ek ko 20 saal ki saza di, aur chaar ko bari kiya [[thefederal-kerala-actor-verdict-2025]]. 29 December ko Supreme Court ne Unnao convict ki umrqaid suspend karne wale Delhi High Court ke order par rok lagayi [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]].

## Neeche chhupa pattern

Saal mein teen dhaage saaf dikhte hain.

**Shuru mein tezi, ant mein deri.** Police ne Durgapur mein 20 din, Kolkata mein 58 din aur Pune mein do mahine se kam mein chargesheets file ki. Lekin fast-track courts ne 2025 mein 66,500 rape aur POCSO cases nipataye, jo 2024 ke 85,595 se kam hain [[pib-fast-track-courts-impact-2026]], aur 2025 ke end mein unke saamne aise 2,45,579 cases pending the [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. November 2026 tak teeno campus aur transport trials mein humein koi verdict nahi mila.

**Shabd bhi nuksaan hain.** Ek bachchi ke case ka judge ka description, ek bail order jo kehta hai ki aurat ne "invited trouble", ek Chief Minister ki salaah ki ladkiyon ko raat mein andar rakho. February 2026 mein Supreme Court ne aakhirkaar Allahabad order ko radd kiya aur judicial sensitivity par formal guidelines maangi [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]] [[hansindia-sc-sets-aside-allahabad-2026]]; July 2026 mein usne yeh guidelines desh ki har court tak bhejne ka order diya [[theprint-sc-sensitivity-guidelines-2026]].

**Institutions ke andar power.** Ek MP aur unke parivaar ke ghar kaam karne wali aurat. Ek former student jo union room chalata tha. Ek head of department aur ek complaints committee. 2025 mein khatra kam hi kisi ajnabi se tha. Woh kisi aise insaan se tha jiske paas pahunch aur authority thi, ek aisi jagah ke andar jo safe honi chahiye thi.

Age of consent ki sunwai 12 November 2025 se list thi [[dtnext-age-of-consent-hearing-2025]]; 23 November 2026 tak humein koi faisla nahi mila. 2025 ke kai cases ab appeal mein hain. Saal ka asli verdict abhi baaki hai. Agar yeh sab aap par bhaari pad raha hai, toh Tele-MANAS 14416 par hai, free aur 24 ghante [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

aparajita-bill-death-penalty-bengal-conv.en:
On 3 September 2024, less than four weeks after a trainee doctor was raped and murdered at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]], the West Bengal Assembly unanimously passed the Aparajita Bill [[barandbench-aparajita-bill-2024]]. Its promise was simple: death for rapists. In the same year, West Bengal's courts convicted the accused in 203 crimes-against-women cases and acquitted them in 12,301 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. This investigation puts those two facts side by side, because a punishment that almost never arrives cannot protect anyone, however harsh it looks on paper.

## What the Aparajita Bill says

The Aparajita Woman and Child (West Bengal Criminal Laws Amendment) Bill, 2024 rewrites parts of India's criminal law for one state. Where a rape victim dies or is left in a vegetative state, it makes the death penalty mandatory [[barandbench-aparajita-bill-2024]]. For every rape under Section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), it makes life imprisonment the minimum and death the maximum. It also cuts the deadline for rape investigations from two months to 21 days, extendable by 15 [[livelaw-aparajita-explainer-2024]].

Compare that with the law as it stands. Under the BNS, rape carries at least 10 years and up to life. A rape that kills a woman or leaves her in a vegetative state already carries at least 20 years, imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. For a rape that kills, the harshest punishment already exists; what the Bill adds there is compulsion.

A state cannot change central criminal law on its own; it needs the President's assent. On 6 September 2024 the Governor reserved the Bill for the President [[livelaw-aparajita-explainer-2024]]. This story could not confirm that it has since become law.

## Mandatory death: what the Bill takes away

Today a judge must weigh each case. When the Supreme Court confirmed the death sentences in the 2012 Delhi gang rape case, it did so because it found that the aggravating circumstances outweighed the mitigating ones [[sc-mukesh-nct-delhi-2017]]. In January 2025 a Sealdah judge did the same weighing in the RG Kar case, found it was not "rarest of the rare", and chose imprisonment for the rest of natural life [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]].

Under Aparajita's version of the law, that judge would have had no choice. A mandatory sentence removes the one step where a court weighs the circumstances of the crime and the person in the dock before deciding whether he should die. Courts have warned against punishment by public mood: in 2021 the Bombay High Court held that a constitutional court cannot award punishment based on public opinion [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]]. A mandatory sentence passed weeks after RG Kar risks writing that mood into the statute. Our RG Kar case file explains that sentence.

## 1.6% and 3,84,388: the numbers behind the promise

National Crime Records Bureau data for 2024 show where West Bengal's system was actually failing. The state had the lowest conviction rate for crimes against women of any state, 1.6%. It also had the largest trial backlog in India: 3,84,388 cases pending at the end of the year, 96.6% of all such cases before its courts [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Set that against the country. Nationally, courts convicted in 25.7% of crimes-against-women trials completed in 2024, and 24,32,527 cases were pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. West Bengal alone held nearly one in six of them. Among large states, Karnataka managed 4.8% and Uttar Pradesh 76.6% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. State rates are not perfectly comparable, since they depend on which trials finish and how cases are classified. But no reading of the data turns 1.6% into a working system.

These figures cover every crime against women, including rape, child sexual abuse and kidnapping. That is why they matter: a death sentence can only come at the end of a completed trial that ends in conviction. In West Bengal in 2024, a completed trial was rare and a conviction rarer still.

The 21-day deadline does not touch this. Indian law already says police must finish a rape investigation within two months, and that a rape trial must end within two months of the chargesheet, but it sets no consequence when either deadline is missed [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A shorter deadline for the police means little while trials pile up by the lakh.

## Severity or certainty: what the Verma Committee warned

The argument is not new. After the 2012 Delhi gang rape, the Justice J.S. Verma Committee advised against the death penalty for rape, noting that it "may not have a deterrent effect" [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament did not follow that advice, and in 2018 it made raping a girl under 12 punishable by death [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. A separate case file looks at what Parliament ignored in the Verma report.

A law can promise two different things. Severity is how harsh the punishment is on paper. Certainty is how likely it is that an offender is caught, tried and convicted. Aparajita's headline changes are about severity. Certainty is where West Bengal was failing: 203 convictions against 12,301 acquittals in 2024.

Harsher laws also raise a question their supporters rarely ask. In West Bengal, 84.9% of rape cases registered in 2024 involved an offender known to the victim [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. When the accused is a neighbour, a relative or a partner, ask what a compulsory death sentence means for a survivor and her family deciding whether to report, or whether to keep going in court.

## How to read the next 'death for rapists' promise

Laws like Aparajita are quick to pass and easy to cheer. The next time a leader promises death for rapists, ask four questions. What is the state's conviction rate in crimes against women? How many cases are waiting for trial? What will this law do about either number? Does it leave judges free to weigh each case?

If a promise cannot answer those questions, it is a headline, not a reform. The test of a tough law is not how loudly it threatens but how often it delivers a verdict. This is general information, not legal advice.
aparajita-bill-death-penalty-bengal-conv.hg:
Kolkata ke RG Kar Medical College and Hospital mein ek trainee doctor ka rape aur murder hua [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. Chaar hafte bhi nahi beete the ki 3 September 2024 ko West Bengal Assembly ne ek raay se, bina kisi virodh ke, Aparajita Bill pass kar diya [[barandbench-aparajita-bill-2024]]. Bill ka vaada simple tha: rapists ko death. Usi saal West Bengal ki courts ne crimes against women ke sirf 203 cases mein accused ko convict kiya, aur 12,301 cases mein bari kar diya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh investigation in dono facts ko saath rakh kar dekhti hai, kyunki jo saza lagbhag kabhi milti hi nahi, woh kisi ko protect nahi kar sakti, chahe kaagaz par kitni bhi kadi ho.

## Aparajita Bill mein kya likha hai

Aparajita Woman and Child (West Bengal Criminal Laws Amendment) Bill, 2024 ek state ke liye India ke criminal law ke kuch hisse badalta hai. Agar rape ke baad victim ki maut ho jaye ya woh vegetative state mein chali jaye, toh Bill mein death penalty mandatory hai [[barandbench-aparajita-bill-2024]]. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 64 ke under har rape ke liye Bill kehta hai: kam se kam umrqaid, zyada se zyada death. Bill rape investigation ki deadline bhi do mahine se ghata kar 21 din karta hai, jo 15 din aur badh sakti hai [[livelaw-aparajita-explainer-2024]].

Ab ise aaj ke law se compare kijiye. BNS mein rape ki saza kam se kam 10 saal hai, jo umrqaid tak ja sakti hai. Jis rape mein aurat ki maut ho jaye ya woh vegetative state mein chali jaye, usme aaj bhi saza hai: kam se kam 20 saal, baaki poori natural life ki qaid, ya death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yaani jis rape mein maut ho jaye, uske liye sabse kadi saza pehle se law mein hai; wahan Bill naya sirf itna jodta hai ki judge ke paas koi aur option na bache.

Koi state central criminal law ko akele nahi badal sakta; uske liye President ki manzoori chahiye. 6 September 2024 ko Governor ne Bill President ke paas bhej diya [[livelaw-aparajita-explainer-2024]]. Yeh Bill ab tak law bana ya nahi, hum confirm nahi kar paaye.

## Mandatory death: Bill judges se kya chheen leta hai

Aaj judge ko har case tolna padta hai. 2012 ke Delhi gang rape case mein Supreme Court ne death sentences isliye confirm kiye kyunki use aggravating circumstances, mitigating circumstances se bhaari lage [[sc-mukesh-nct-delhi-2017]]. January 2025 mein Sealdah ke judge ne RG Kar case mein wahi tol kiya, paaya ki case "rarest of the rare" nahi hai, aur baaki poori natural life ki qaid chuni [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]].

Aparajita wale law ke hisaab se us judge ke paas koi option hi nahi hota. Mandatory saza court ka woh step hi mita deti hai jisme judge crime ke haalaat aur katghare mein khade insaan ko tol kar decide karta hai ki use maut mile ya nahi. Courts public mood se saza dene ke khilaaf warn kar chuki hain: 2021 mein Bombay High Court ne kaha tha ki constitutional court public opinion ke basis par saza nahi de sakti [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]]. RG Kar ke kuch hafton baad pass hui mandatory saza, usi mood ko law mein likh dene ka risk hai. Hamari RG Kar case file us saza ki poori kahani batati hai.

## 1.6% aur 3,84,388: vaade ke peeche ke numbers

National Crime Records Bureau ka 2024 data dikhata hai ki West Bengal ka system asal mein kahan fail ho raha tha. Crimes against women mein state ka conviction rate kisi bhi state se kam tha: sirf 1.6%. Trial ka backlog bhi India mein sabse bada yahin tha: saal ke end mein 3,84,388 cases pending, yaani courts ke saamne aise jitne cases the, unme se 96.6% atke pade the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ab poore desh se compare kijiye. 2024 mein India bhar mein crimes-against-women ke jitne trials poore hue, unme se 25.7% mein conviction hua, aur 24,32,527 cases pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inme se lagbhag har chhata case akele West Bengal ka tha. Bade states mein Karnataka ka rate 4.8% tha aur Uttar Pradesh ka 76.6% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. States ke rates ki seedhi comparison poori tarah sahi nahi hoti, kyunki yeh is par depend karta hai ki kaun se trials poore hue aur cases kaise classify hue. Lekin data ko kisi bhi tarah padhiye, 1.6% ko chalta hua system nahi kaha ja sakta.

Yeh figures crimes against women ki har category ke hain, jisme rape, child sexual abuse aur kidnapping bhi shaamil hain. Isiliye yeh important hain: death sentence sirf tab aa sakti hai jab trial poora ho aur conviction mein khatam ho. 2024 mein West Bengal mein trial poora hona hi rare tha, aur conviction usse bhi rare.

21 din ki deadline is problem ko chhooti tak nahi. Law mein pehle se likha hai ki police rape investigation do mahine mein poori kare, aur chargesheet ke baad do mahine mein trial khatam ho, lekin deadline miss hone par koi consequence tay nahi hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jab trials laakhon mein atke hon, toh police ke liye chhoti deadline ka zyada matlab nahi.

## Severity ya certainty: Verma Committee ne kya warning di thi

Yeh behas nayi nahi hai. 2012 ke Delhi gang rape ke baad Justice J.S. Verma Committee ne rape ke liye death penalty ke khilaaf salaah di thi, aur kaha tha ki yeh "may not have a deterrent effect", yaani iska crime rokne wala asar shayad na ho [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament ne yeh salaah nahi maani, aur 2018 mein 12 saal se kam umar ki bachchi ke rape ke liye death penalty jod di [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. Verma report ki kin baaton ko Parliament ne ignore kiya, us par hamari ek alag case file hai.

Koi bhi law do alag cheezon ka vaada kar sakta hai. Severity yaani kaagaz par saza kitni kadi hai. Certainty yaani offender ke pakde jaane, trial hone aur convict hone ki kitni ummeed hai. Aparajita ke headline badlaav severity ke baare mein hain. West Bengal ki kamzori certainty thi: 2024 mein 203 convictions, aur 12,301 acquittals.

Kade laws ek sawaal bhi khada karte hain jo unke supporters kam hi poochte hain. 2024 mein West Bengal mein rape ke 84.9% cases mein offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jab accused padosi, rishtedaar ya partner ho, toh poochiye: compulsory death sentence us survivor aur uski family ke liye kya matlab rakhti hai jo tay kar rahe hain ki complaint karein ya nahi, ya court mein case aage ladein ya nahi.

## Agli baar 'rapists ko death' ka vaada suniye, toh kaise parkhein

Aparajita jaise laws jaldi pass hote hain aur taaliyan bhi khoob batorte hain. Agli baar koi neta rapists ko death ka vaada kare, toh chaar sawaal poochiye. State mein crimes against women ka conviction rate kya hai? Kitne cases trial ke intezaar mein hain? Naya law in dono numbers ke liye kya karega? Kya judges ke paas har case tolne ki azaadi bachi rahegi?

Agar kisi vaade ke paas in sawaalon ka jawab nahi hai, toh woh sirf headline hai, reform nahi. Kade law ki asli parakh yeh nahi ki woh kitni zor se darata hai, balki yeh ki woh kitni baar sach mein verdict tak pahunchta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

aparna-bhat-2021-rakhi-bail-conditions.en:
A man accused of sexual assault in Madhya Pradesh asked a High Court for bail. He got it, on condition that he "visits the house of the complainant and requests her to tie the Rakhi band to him" [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. The court did not just let him go home. It sent him to her door, to ask her to make him her brother. On 18 March 2021, in Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh, the Supreme Court struck the condition down and set rules for every court in India [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Five years later, the Supreme Court says efforts to sensitise judges have not delivered what it expected.

## The rakhi condition: a bail order that made the accused a 'brother'

Bail is not a verdict. It lets an accused person stay out of jail during the trial, on conditions meant to protect the case: report to the police, don't leave the city, don't go near the witnesses. The rakhi condition turned that logic upside down. It required contact, at the complainant's home, through a ritual in which a sister ties a thread and a brother promises to protect her.

Think about what that told the complainant. The man she accused would now arrive, on a court's instructions, as a relative she owed a ceremony to. It told her family that the matter could be smoothed over like a household quarrel. None of this needed a single threat. The pressure was written into the order.

## 18 March 2021: the rules the Supreme Court laid down

A bench of Justices A.M. Khanwilkar and S. Ravindra Bhat set the condition aside and laid down rules for all courts [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]:

- Bail conditions "should not mandate, require or permit contact between the accused and the victim."
- Courts must not "suggest or entertain any notions" of compromise between the accused and the survivor, including marriage.
- Judges must keep "stereotypical or patriarchal notions about women" out of their orders and remarks.
- Every judge must be trained in gender sensitisation as part of their foundational training.

Two years later, the Supreme Court's Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes put the principle in one line: "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape." Rape, it adds, does not taint the honour of the survivor or her family [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## No contact, no compromise, no marriage offers

Pressure to settle rarely arrives as a court order. It comes as the accused's relatives at the door, a call from a community elder, an offer of money, a marriage proposal. Aparna Bhat means a judge may not add the court's weight to any of it.

The pull towards settlement shows in the data, even outside sexual offences. In 2024, 16,396 cruelty-by-husband cases in Indian courts ended in compromise or compounding, more than the 10,689 that ended in conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Cruelty is a different crime, and the data do not say how many of those compromises were freely chosen. But they show how often violence against women inside a family ends in a settlement rather than a conviction.

Time works for the pressure. At the end of 2024, 24,32,527 crime-against-women cases were waiting for trial, 92.1% of all such cases before the courts [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. For a survivor, that can mean years of living near an accused who is out on bail, and years in which the offers can keep coming.

## 2026: the Supreme Court admits sensitisation has fallen short

The rules did not end stereotyping in bail orders. In 2022, a sessions court in Kerala, deciding a bail plea, wrote that photographs showed the complainant "exposing to dresses which are having some sexual provocative one". The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook quotes that order while rejecting the stereotype that a woman's clothing invites sexual contact [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

On 10 February 2026, ruling on a High Court order that had reduced the charges in a child sexual assault case, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and N.V. Anjaria said efforts to sensitise judges "have not borne the fruit that was expected". It asked a National Judicial Academy expert committee, headed by former judge Aniruddha Bose, to draft guidelines on sensitivity in sexual-offence cases [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

Gender-sensitisation training was one of the 2021 rules; five years on, the court's own verdict is that such efforts have fallen short. Whether the rules reach a particular courtroom can depend on the judge, and on whether the survivor's lawyer cites them.

## Your rights when the accused asks for bail

This is general information, not legal advice. Consider this situation: a 22-year-old in Kanpur reports a colleague for sexual assault. He gets bail. A week later his mother turns up with sweets and an offer: withdraw the complaint and the families will "sort it out". Here is what the law gives her.

- **No contact.** No bail condition may require or permit the accused to contact her [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Report any visit, call or message from him or his side, with dates and screenshots, to the investigating officer and the public prosecutor.
- **Information.** Police must update her on the investigation within 90 days. If she has a lawyer, she is entitled to free copies of the police report, the FIR and the statements within 14 days of the accused's first appearance in court. And no court may allow the prosecution to be withdrawn without first hearing her [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Protection from inducement.** If she is a Dalit or Adivasi woman and the case falls under the SC/ST Atrocities Act, that Act makes it the state's duty to protect her, her dependants and witnesses from intimidation, coercion, inducement or violence, and gives her the right to timely notice of court proceedings, including bail hearings [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].
- **A lawyer of her own.** Legal services authorities provide free legal aid [[nalsa]]. She does not have to face a bail hearing alone.

These are victims' rights, so they belong to boys, men and transgender survivors too. A rakhi asks a brother for protection. Since 2021, no court may send the man a survivor has accused to ask her for one.
aparna-bhat-2021-rakhi-bail-conditions.hg:
Madhya Pradesh mein sexual assault ke ek accused ne High Court se bail maangi. Bail mili, is shart par ki woh "visits the house of the complainant and requests her to tie the Rakhi band to him", yaani complainant ke ghar jaaye aur usse rakhi bandhwaane ki request kare [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Court ne use sirf ghar jaane nahi diya. Use seedha uske darwaaze par bhej diya, taaki woh use apna bhai bana le. 18 March 2021 ko, Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh case mein, Supreme Court ne ye shart radd kar di aur India ke har court ke liye rules tay kiye [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Paanch saal baad, Supreme Court khud keh raha hai ki judges ko sensitise karne ki koshishon se jo ummeed thi, woh poori nahi hui.

## Rakhi wali shart: ek bail order jisne accused ko 'bhai' bana diya

Bail koi faisla nahi hai. Isse accused trial ke dauraan jail se bahar reh sakta hai, un sharton par jo case ko bachaane ke liye hoti hain: police ke paas haaziri lagao, shehar mat chhodo, gawahon ke paas mat jao. Rakhi wali shart ne is logic ko ulta kar diya. Isne complainant ke ghar par, ek aisi rasm ke zariye contact zaroori bana diya jisme behen dhaaga baandhti hai aur bhai uski hifaazat ka vaada karta hai.

Sochiye ki isse complainant ko kya sandesh mila. Jis aadmi par usne aarop lagaaya, woh ab court ke kehne par ek rishtedaar ban kar aayega, jiske liye use ek rasm nibhaani hai. Uske parivaar ko sandesh mila ki maamla ghar ke kisi jhagde ki tarah suljhaaya ja sakta hai. Iske liye ek bhi dhamki ki zaroorat nahi padi. Dabaav order mein hi likha tha.

## 18 March 2021: Supreme Court ke banaaye rules

Justices A.M. Khanwilkar aur S. Ravindra Bhat ki bench ne shart radd ki aur sabhi courts ke liye rules tay kiye [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]:

- Bail conditions "should not mandate, require or permit contact between the accused and the victim", yaani bail ki shartein accused aur victim ke beech contact ki na maang karein, na use zaroori banaayein, na uski ijaazat dein.
- Courts accused aur survivor ke beech compromise ka, shaadi samet, "suggest or entertain any notions" na karein, yaani na sujhaav dein, na aise kisi khayal ko jagah dein.
- Judges apne orders aur baaton mein "stereotypical or patriarchal notions about women" se door rahein, yaani auraton ke baare mein stereotype aur patriarchal soch se.
- Har judge ki foundational training mein gender sensitisation ki training ho.

Do saal baad, Supreme Court ki Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes ne is baat ko ek line mein kaha: "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape", yaani shaadi rape ki hinsa ka ilaaj nahi hai. Handbook ye bhi kehti hai ki rape se survivor ya uske parivaar ki izzat par koi daag nahi lagta [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## Na contact, na compromise, na shaadi ka offer

Settle karne ka dabaav kam hi court order ki shakal mein aata hai. Woh aata hai darwaaze par khade accused ke rishtedaaron ke roop mein, samaaj ke kisi bade ke phone call ke roop mein, paison ke offer ya shaadi ke rishte ke roop mein. Aparna Bhat ka matlab hai ki koi judge in mein se kisi bhi dabaav ke saath court ka vazan nahi jod sakta.

Settlement ki taraf ye kheench data mein bhi dikhti hai, sexual offences ke bahar bhi. 2024 mein Indian courts mein cruelty-by-husband ke 16,396 cases compromise ya compounding par khatam hue, jo conviction wale 10,689 cases se zyada hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Cruelty ek alag crime hai, aur data ye nahi bataata ki inme se kitne compromise apni marzi se hue. Lekin ye dikhata hai ki parivaar ke andar auraton ke khilaaf hinsa kitni baar conviction ki jagah settlement par khatam hoti hai.

Waqt dabaav ke haq mein kaam karta hai. 2024 ke end mein crime-against-women ke 24,32,527 cases trial ka intezaar kar rahe the, yaani courts ke saamne aise sabhi cases ka 92.1% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek survivor ke liye iska matlab ho sakta hai bail par bahar accused ke aas-paas saalon tak rehna, aur saalon tak offers aate rehna.

## 2026: Supreme Court ne maana ki sensitisation kam pada

Rules ke baad bhi bail orders mein stereotype khatam nahi hue. 2022 mein Kerala ke ek sessions court ne bail ki ek arzi par faisla dete hue likha ki photos mein complainant "exposing to dresses which are having some sexual provocative one", yaani court ke hisaab se aise kapdon mein dikh rahi thi jo sexually provocative the. Supreme Court ki 2023 ki handbook is order ko quote karti hai, aur saath hi is stereotype ko khaarij karti hai ki aurat ke kapde sexual contact ko nyota dete hain [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

10 February 2026 ko, ek High Court ke us order par faisla dete hue jisne ek child sexual assault case mein charges ghata diye the, Chief Justice Surya Kant aur Justices Joymalya Bagchi aur N.V. Anjaria ki bench ne kaha ki judges ko sensitise karne ki koshishein "have not borne the fruit that was expected", yaani ummeed ke mutaabik nateeje nahi laayin. Bench ne National Judicial Academy ki ek expert committee se, jiske head former judge Aniruddha Bose hain, sexual-offence cases mein sensitivity par guidelines ka draft banane ko kaha [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

Gender-sensitisation training 2021 ke rules mein se ek thi; paanch saal baad court ka apna aakalan hai ki aisi koshishein kam padi hain. Rules kisi khaas courtroom tak pahunchte hain ya nahi, ye judge par bhi nirbhar ho sakta hai, aur is par bhi ki survivor ka lawyer unka hawala deta hai ya nahi.

## Jab accused bail maange: survivor ke haq

Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi. Is situation ke baare mein sochiye: Kanpur ki ek 22 saal ki ladki apne colleague ke khilaaf sexual assault ki complaint karti hai. Use bail mil jaati hai. Ek hafte baad uski maa mithai aur ek offer lekar aati hai: complaint wapas le lo, dono parivaar "aapas mein suljha lenge". Law us ladki ko ye haq deta hai:

- **Koi contact nahi.** Bail ki koi bhi shart accused ko usse contact karne ki maang ya ijaazat nahi de sakti [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Accused ya uski taraf se aaye har visit, call ya message ki report, dates aur screenshots ke saath, investigating officer aur public prosecutor ko kariye.
- **Jaankari.** Police ko 90 din ke andar use investigation ki progress batani hogi. Agar uska lawyer hai, toh accused ki court mein pehli peshi ke 14 din ke andar use police report, FIR aur statements ki free copies milne ka haq hai. Aur koi bhi court use sune bina prosecution wapas lene ki ijaazat nahi de sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Laalach aur dabaav se suraksha.** Agar woh Dalit ya Adivasi hai aur case SC/ST Atrocities Act ke under aata hai, toh ye Act state ki zimmedaari banata hai ki woh use, uske dependants aur gawahon ko dhamki, zabardasti, laalach ya hinsa se bachaaye, aur use bail hearing samet court ki har kaarvaai ki samay par jaankari paane ka haq deta hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].
- **Apna lawyer.** Legal services authorities free legal aid deti hain [[nalsa]]. Use bail hearing mein akele khade hone ki zaroorat nahi.

Ye victims ke haq hain, isliye ladkon, aadmiyon aur transgender survivors par bhi laagu hote hain. Rakhi bhai se hifaazat maangti hai. 2021 ke baad koi court us aadmi ko, jis par survivor ne aarop lagaaya hai, usse rakhi bandhwaane nahi bhej sakta.

citizens-who-forced-landmark-rulings.en:
Many of India's biggest changes on sexual violence did not begin in Parliament. They began with people who read a judgment closely, filed a petition, looked inside an institution or demanded a report the government was sitting on. The tools they used are open to any student, teacher or employee.

## 1979: four teachers and a letter

On 15 September 1978 the Supreme Court acquitted two policemen accused of raping a minor girl inside a police station in Maharashtra in 1972 [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. It noted that no marks of injury were found on the girl and described the alleged intercourse as "a peaceful affair" [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].

In September 1979 four law teachers, Upendra Baxi, Raghunath Kelkar, Lotika Sarkar and Vasudha Dhagamwar, wrote an open letter to the Chief Justice of India protesting the judgment's view of consent [[wikipedia-mathura-rape-case]]. The letter is widely credited with starting India's anti-rape law reform movement. Protests followed, and Parliament passed the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983, which made custodial rape a separate aggravated offence, required rape trials to be held in camera and made it a crime to disclose a victim's identity [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

The four had no client and no case of their own. They read the judgment and argued with it in public.

## Petitions that changed the law: Vishaka, Independent Thought, Just Rights for Children

In 1992 a social worker was gang-raped in a Rajasthan village; in November 1995 a Jaipur court acquitted all five accused of rape [[bbc-bhanwari-2017]]. A petition prompted by that case took the wider problem to the Supreme Court. On 13 August 1997, in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan, a bench headed by Chief Justice J.S. Verma laid down binding guidelines against sexual harassment at work, to be treated as law until Parliament legislated [[sc-vishaka-rajasthan-1997]]. Parliament took nearly 16 years: the POSH Act was gazetted on 23 April 2013 [[pib-law-posh-act-gazette-2013]].

In 2013 Parliament raised the age of consent to 18 but kept the marital exception for wives aged 15 and above, so a husband's sex with a 15-to-17-year-old wife was not legally rape [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. An organisation called Independent Thought challenged that gap in the Supreme Court. On 11 October 2017 the Supreme Court read the exception down: sex with a wife under 18 is rape [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

In January 2024 the Madras High Court quashed a criminal case over stored child sexual abuse material. Just Rights for Children Alliance appealed. On 23 September 2024 the Supreme Court called that ruling an "egregious error" and held that storing or possessing such material can itself be an offence under Section 15 of POCSO, even if it is never shared, when the circumstances show the intent the law specifies [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. It also told courts to say "Child Sexual Exploitation and Abuse Material" instead of "child pornography" [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]].

In the Independent Thought and Just Rights for Children cases, the organisations that went to court were not the ones harmed. A public-interest petition lets a group raise a wrong that victims, often children, poor or afraid, cannot raise themselves.

## The audit police did not do: Muzaffarpur

In April 2018 the Tata Institute of Social Sciences submitted a social audit of Bihar's children's homes, done for the state government. It flagged sexual abuse at several institutions, including a state-funded girls' shelter home in Muzaffarpur [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]], where 34 minor girls had been sexually abused [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. In January 2020 a Delhi POCSO court convicted 19 of the 20 accused [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

It was not a police investigation that exposed the home, but an outside team that went in and wrote down what it found. That is all a social audit is: organised, documented looking.

## RTI and a report kept back for nearly five years: the Hema Committee

Kerala set up the Justice K. Hema Committee in 2017, after the abduction and sexual assault of an actor that February and a petition by the Women in Cinema Collective, to study sexual harassment and gender inequality in Malayalam cinema [[hindu-hema-coverage-2024]]. It submitted its report in December 2019. The report was made public only on 19 August 2024, after the State Information Commission ordered its release and the Kerala High Court rejected a challenge [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]]. It came out under the Right to Information Act, with 63 pages removed from the 295-page draft to protect the identities of witnesses and the accused [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

Three weeks later the Kerala High Court asked why the government had been "inactive or silent" since 31 December 2019, although the police chief had a copy from February 2021, and ordered the unredacted report handed to a Special Investigation Team [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-sit-2024]].

What finally opened the report was not a minister's decision but a legal right to ask.

## Your toolkit: write, petition, audit, ask

- **Write.** A reasoned letter to someone with power to act, such as a Chief Justice, a vice-chancellor or a State Commission for Women, puts a problem on record. Quote the rule you rely on, as the four teachers did.
- **Petition.** Bring documents, not just anger: every petition here rested on a judgment, an incident or a report.
- **Audit.** Check whether your workplace has an Internal Complaints Committee. The POSH Act requires employers to set one up (workplaces with fewer than 10 workers are covered by the district's Local Committee), and an employer who fails can be fined up to Rs 50,000, doubled on a repeat [[indiacode-posh-2013]].
- **Ask.** If a body is run by the government, you can request its records under the RTI Act and appeal if you are refused. The Hema report came out after the State Information Commission ordered its release.
- **Protect.** Never identify a survivor while campaigning. Publishing her name or anything that could identify her is a crime under Section 72 of the BNS unless she authorises it in writing [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

This is general information, not legal advice.

Imagine students in Bhopal who suspect their college's internal committee exists only on a notice board. They can ask in writing who sits on it and how many complaints it heard last year, use RTI if it is a government college, and take the answer to the university or the State Commission for Women.

None of these people waited for permission. They read, documented, wrote and asked, and kept going until an institution had to answer.
citizens-who-forced-landmark-rulings.hg:
India mein sexual violence par kai sabse bade badlaav Parliament se shuru nahi hue. Woh un logon se shuru hue jinhone kisi judgment ko dhyaan se padha, petition file ki, kisi institution ke andar jhaanka, ya woh report maangi jis par sarkar baithi hui thi. Unke tools aaj bhi har student, teacher aur employee ke liye khule hain.

## 1979: chaar teachers aur ek letter

15 September 1978 ko Supreme Court ne do policewalon ko bari kar diya, jin par 1972 mein Maharashtra ke ek police station ke andar ek naabaalig ladki ke rape ka aarop tha [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. Judgment mein likha gaya ki ladki ke shareer par chot ke koi nishaan nahi mile, aur kathit intercourse ko "a peaceful affair" kaha gaya [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].

September 1979 mein chaar law teachers, Upendra Baxi, Raghunath Kelkar, Lotika Sarkar aur Vasudha Dhagamwar, ne Chief Justice of India ko ek open letter likha aur judgment ki consent wali soch ka virodh kiya [[wikipedia-mathura-rape-case]]. Is letter ko India mein rape law reform movement ki shuruaat maana jaata hai. Phir protests hue, aur Parliament ne Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983 paas kiya: custodial rape ek alag aur zyada gambhir (aggravated) offence bana, rape trials ka in camera hona zaroori hua, aur victim ki identity kholna crime ban gaya [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

In chaaron ka na koi client tha, na apna koi case. Unhone bas judgment padha aur sabke saamne usse behes ki.

## Petitions jinhone law badla: Vishaka, Independent Thought, Just Rights for Children

1992 mein Rajasthan ke ek gaon mein ek social worker ka gang rape hua; November 1995 mein Jaipur ki ek court ne paanchon accused ko rape ke aarop se bari kar diya [[bbc-bhanwari-2017]]. Us case ke baad ek petition is badi samasya ko Supreme Court tak le gayi. 13 August 1997 ko Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan mein Chief Justice J.S. Verma ki aguwai wali bench ne kaam ki jagah par sexual harassment ke khilaaf binding guidelines di, jinhe tab tak law maana jaana tha jab tak Parliament kanoon na banaye [[sc-vishaka-rajasthan-1997]]. Parliament ko lagbhag 16 saal lage: POSH Act 23 April 2013 ko gazette mein aaya [[pib-law-posh-act-gazette-2013]].

2013 mein Parliament ne age of consent badhakar 18 kar di, lekin marital exception 15 aur usse zyada umr ki patniyon ke liye rehne diya, yaani 15 se 17 saal ki patni ke saath pati ka sex legally rape nahi tha [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. Independent Thought naam ki ek organisation ne Supreme Court mein is gap ko challenge kiya. 11 October 2017 ko Supreme Court ne exception ko read down kiya: 18 se kam umr ki patni ke saath sex rape hai [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

January 2024 mein Madras High Court ne store kiye gaye child sexual abuse material ke ek criminal case ko quash kar diya. Just Rights for Children Alliance ne appeal ki. 23 September 2024 ko Supreme Court ne High Court ke us faisle ko "egregious error" kaha, aur kaha ki aisa material store karna ya apne paas rakhna, share na kiya ho tab bhi, POCSO ki Section 15 ke under khud ek offence ho sakta hai, jab haalaat se woh irada dikhe jo law batata hai [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Court ne yeh bhi kaha ki "child pornography" ki jagah "Child Sexual Exploitation and Abuse Material" kaha jaye [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]].

Independent Thought aur Just Rights for Children ke cases mein court jaane wali organisations woh nahi thi jinhe nuksaan hua tha. Public-interest petition kisi group ko woh galat baat uthane deti hai jo victims, aksar bachche, gareeb ya dare hue log, khud nahi utha paate.

## Woh audit jo police ne nahi kiya: Muzaffarpur

April 2018 mein Tata Institute of Social Sciences ne Bihar ke children's homes ka ek social audit jama kiya, jo state sarkar ke liye kiya gaya tha. Usne kai institutions mein sexual abuse ki taraf ishaara kiya, jinme Muzaffarpur ka ek sarkari paise se chalne wala girls' shelter home bhi tha [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]], jahan 34 naabaalig ladkiyon ka sexual abuse hua tha [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. January 2020 mein Delhi ki ek POCSO court ne 20 mein se 19 accused ko convict kiya [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

Is home ka sach kisi police investigation ne nahi, balki bahar ki ek team ne khola, jo andar gayi aur jo dekha use likh diya. Social audit bas yahi hai: organised tareeke se dekhna, aur jo dikhe use document karna.

## RTI aur lagbhag paanch saal dabi rahi report: Hema Committee

February 2017 mein ek actor ke abduction aur sexual assault, aur Women in Cinema Collective ki petition ke baad, Kerala ne 2017 mein Justice K. Hema Committee banayi, taaki Malayalam cinema mein sexual harassment aur gender inequality ki jaanch ho [[hindu-hema-coverage-2024]]. Committee ne December 2019 mein apni report de di. Lekin report 19 August 2024 ko jaakar public hui, jab State Information Commission ne use release karne ka order diya aur Kerala High Court ne uske khilaaf challenge khaarij kar diya [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]]. Report Right to Information Act ke under bahar aayi, aur 295 pages ke draft se 63 pages hata diye gaye taaki witnesses aur accused logon ki pehchaan chhupi rahe [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

Teen hafte baad Kerala High Court ne poocha ki sarkar 31 December 2019 se "inactive or silent" kyun thi, jabki police chief ke paas February 2021 se report ki copy thi, aur poori, bina kaat-chhaant wali report ek Special Investigation Team ko dene ka order diya [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-sit-2024]].

Report ko aakhirkaar kisi minister ke faisle ne nahi, balki sawaal poochne ke ek legal haq ne bahar nikala.

## Aapka toolkit: likhiye, petition kijiye, audit kijiye, poochiye

- **Likhiye.** Jiske paas action lene ki power hai, jaise Chief Justice, vice-chancellor ya State Commission for Women, use soch-samajh kar likha gaya ek letter problem ko record par le aata hai. Jis rule par aap tike hain, use quote kijiye, jaise un chaar teachers ne kiya.
- **Petition.** Sirf gussa nahi, documents laiye: yahan har petition kisi judgment, ghatna ya report par tiki thi.
- **Audit.** Check kijiye ki aapke office mein Internal Complaints Committee hai ya nahi. POSH Act employers ko yeh committee banane ko kehta hai (10 se kam workers wali jagahon ke liye district ki Local Committee hoti hai), aur jo employer aisa nahi karta us par Rs 50,000 tak ka fine lag sakta hai, dobara galti par double [[indiacode-posh-2013]].
- **Poochiye.** Agar koi body sarkar chalati hai, toh aap RTI Act ke under uske records maang sakte hain, aur mana ho toh appeal kar sakte hain. Hema report State Information Commission ke order ke baad hi bahar aayi.
- **Bachaiye.** Campaign karte waqt kabhi kisi survivor ki pehchaan mat kholiye. Uska naam ya koi bhi aisi detail chhaapna jisse woh pehchaani jaye, BNS ki Section 72 ke under crime hai, jab tak woh khud likh kar ijaazat na de [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Maan lijiye Bhopal ke kuch students ko shak hai ki unke college ki internal committee sirf notice board par hai. Woh likh kar pooch sakte hain ki usme kaun hai aur pichhle saal usne kitni complaints suni, college sarkari hai toh RTI laga sakte hain, aur jo jawab mile use university ya State Commission for Women tak le ja sakte hain.

In mein se kisi ne ijaazat ka intezaar nahi kiya. Unhone padha, document kiya, likha aur poocha, aur tab tak lage rahe jab tak kisi institution ko jawab dena hi pada.

custodial-rape-acquittal-1978-peaceful-a.en:
On 15 September 1978, three judges of the Supreme Court of India acquitted two policemen accused of raping a minor girl inside a police station in Maharashtra in 1972 [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. The judges noted that no injuries were found on her. They described the alleged intercourse as "a peaceful affair" [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. Several protections survivors rely on today trace back to the anger over that judgment.

## The case the Supreme Court decided in 1978

Three courts heard the case, and they did not agree. The sessions court acquitted both policemen. The Bombay High Court convicted them: five years for one man for rape (Section 376 IPC), one year for the other for outraging her modesty (Section 354 IPC). The Supreme Court then reversed the High Court and set both men free [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].

The case is popularly known by the girl's first name, and its formal title carries the name of one of the acquitted policemen. We use neither. We cite the judgment by its law-report number, AIR 1979 SC 185, and add nothing about her.

## 'A peaceful affair': reading consent from the absence of injuries

The court's reasoning leaned on what it did not find. "No marks of injury were found on the person of the girl after the incident," it noted, and it concluded that the sexual intercourse was "not proved to amount to rape" [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].

Read that logic slowly. It treats a struggle as the only proof of a no, and the absence of a struggle as a yes. It expects a girl in police custody, facing two policemen, to fight hard enough to leave marks. It puts the whole burden on the person with the least power in the room.

In 2026, the Supreme Court's own publication "Judgments and Gender" described the case as the "rape of a minor girl in police custody" and listed it as an acquittal "due to restrictive reasoning on consent" [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]]. That is the court, decades later, naming the mistake.

## Four law teachers write to the Chief Justice

In September 1979, four law teachers, Upendra Baxi, Raghunath Kelkar, Lotika Sarkar and Vasudha Dhagamwar, wrote an open letter to the Chief Justice of India protesting the judgment's view of consent. The letter is widely credited with starting India's movement to reform its rape law [[wikipedia-mathura-rape-case]].

They read a judgment closely, said in public what was wrong with it, and refused to treat the Supreme Court's word as the last word. Protests followed.

## 1983 and 2013: from a presumption in custody to "not resisting is not consent"

The protests led Parliament to pass the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983 (Act No. 43 of 1983), in force from 25 December 1983 [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. It changed four things:

- Custodial rape became a separate, aggravated offence.
- In a custodial rape trial, if the woman says she did not consent, the court presumes she did not (Section 114A of the Evidence Act) [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].
- Rape trials had to be held in camera, away from the public.
- Disclosing a rape victim's identity became a crime under Section 228A of the IPC [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

In custody, the court now had to start from her word, not his. But no statute yet said that a woman who did not resist had not, for that reason, consented. That came only with the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, which rewrote Section 375 of the IPC. It defined consent as "an unequivocal voluntary agreement" and said that a woman who does not physically resist "shall not by the reason only of that fact, be regarded as consenting" [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. The logic of the 1978 judgment was finally reversed in the text of the law itself.

## Resistance, injuries and consent: what the law says now

Since 1 July 2024, rape is defined in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which replaced the IPC [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]]. Section 63 keeps the 2013 words: consent must be unequivocal and voluntary, and not physically resisting is not, by itself, consent [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. For a girl under 18, consent is not even the question: Section 63 treats sex with her as rape whatever she says [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and the POCSO Act protects every child under 18, boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Our myth-check on dating and consent shows how the resistance rule works between people who know each other. Here is how the law works where the 1978 case began: in custody.

- Rape by a police officer in a police station or of a woman in custody, or by a public servant, jail or hospital staff member of a woman in their custody or care, is aggravated rape under Section 64: at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment, up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- A person in authority who abuses his position to get a woman in his custody or care to have sex with him, even when it falls short of rape, faces 5 to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment under Section 68 [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- Rape trials must still be held in camera, as far as practicable before a woman judge [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], and naming a survivor is a crime under Section 72 [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

If not resisting cannot be read as consent, then the absence of the marks a struggle leaves cannot be read as consent either. A person may freeze. She may go along because refusing feels more dangerous.

The danger the 1978 judgment ignored has not gone away. In 2024, police registered 27 cases under the category of rape by police personnel and 3 against staff of jails, remand homes or other places of custody [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These count only cases where police filed an FIR under those clauses, so they show the floor, not the full picture.

Nor have the attitudes gone. In February 2026, the Supreme Court said efforts to sensitise judges in sexual-offence cases "have not borne the fruit that was expected" and asked an expert committee to draft guidelines [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

This is general information, not legal advice. If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, the law no longer treats not fighting back as consent. You can report it at any police station, wherever it happened [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], and an officer who refuses to record an FIR for rape commits a crime [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
custodial-rape-acquittal-1978-peaceful-a.hg:
15 September 1978 ko Supreme Court ke teen judges ne do policewalon ko bari kar diya. Un par 1972 mein Maharashtra ke ek police station ke andar ek minor ladki ke rape ka aarop tha [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. Judges ne note kiya ki ladki ke body par chot ka koi nishaan nahi mila. Unhone us kathit intercourse ko "a peaceful affair" kaha, yaani shaanti se hua maamla [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. Aaj survivors ko jo kai legal protections milti hain, unki jadd isi faisle par phoote gusse mein hai.

## 1978 mein Supreme Court ne kya faisla diya

Teen courts ne ye case suna, aur teeno ek raay par nahi the. Sessions court ne dono policewalon ko bari kar diya. Phir Bombay High Court ne dono ko convict kiya: ek ko rape (IPC Section 376) ke liye paanch saal ki saza, doosre ko ladki ki modesty outrage karne (IPC Section 354) ke liye ek saal ki. Aakhir mein Supreme Court ne High Court ka faisla palat diya aur dono ko chhod diya [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].

Ye case aam taur par ladki ke pehle naam se jaana jaata hai, aur case ke formal title mein bari hue ek policewale ka naam hai. Hum inme se koi bhi naam use nahi karte. Hum judgment ko uske law-report number, AIR 1979 SC 185, se cite karte hain, aur ladki ke baare mein kuch nahi jodte.

## 'A peaceful affair': chot nahi, toh consent?

Court ka argument us cheez par tika tha jo use nahi mili. Faisle mein likha gaya: "No marks of injury were found on the person of the girl after the incident", yaani incident ke baad ladki ke body par chot ka koi nishaan nahi mila. Phir court ne kaha ki ye sexual intercourse "not proved to amount to rape" hai, yaani rape saabit nahi hota [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].

Is logic ko dhyaan se samjhiye. Iske hisaab se 'na' ka ek hi saboot hai, aur woh hai struggle. Struggle nahi hua, toh maan lo 'haan' thi. Ye logic police custody mein do policewalon ke saamne khadi ek ladki se umeed karta hai ki woh itna lade ki body par nishaan pad jaayein. Yaani saara bojh us par daal diya gaya, jiske paas wahan sabse kam taqat thi.

2026 mein Supreme Court ki apni publication "Judgments and Gender" ne is case ko "rape of a minor girl in police custody", yaani police custody mein ek minor ladki ka rape, bataya. Usne ise un faislon mein gina jinme accused "due to restrictive reasoning on consent", yaani consent ko bahut seemit nazar se dekhne ki wajah se, bari hue [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]]. Yaani dashkon baad court khud us galti ka naam le raha hai.

## Chaar law teachers ne Chief Justice ko letter likha

September 1979 mein law padhane wale chaar teachers, Upendra Baxi, Raghunath Kelkar, Lotika Sarkar aur Vasudha Dhagamwar, ne Chief Justice of India ke naam ek open letter likha. Unhone faisle mein consent ki samajh par sawaal uthaya. Aam taur par maana jaata hai ki isi letter se India mein rape law reform ka movement shuru hua [[wikipedia-mathura-rape-case]].

Unhone judgment ko dhyaan se padha, jo galat tha use sabke saamne khulkar kaha, aur Supreme Court ki baat ko aakhri baat maanne se inkaar kar diya. Iske baad desh mein protests hue.

## 1983 aur 2013: custody mein 'consent nahi thi' maanne se 'resist na karna consent nahi' tak

In protests ke baad Parliament ne Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983 (Act No. 43 of 1983) paas kiya, jo 25 December 1983 se laagu hua [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Isne chaar badi cheezein badlin:

- Custodial rape ko alag aur zyada serious, yaani aggravated, offence banaya gaya.
- Custodial rape ke case mein agar aurat kahe ki uski consent nahi thi, toh court yahi maan kar chalega ki consent nahi thi. Ye Evidence Act ka Section 114A hai [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].
- Rape cases ki sunwai band kamre mein (in camera) hone lagi, public se door.
- Rape victim ki pehchaan reveal karna IPC Section 228A ke under crime ban gaya [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

Ab custody wale case mein court ko ladki ki baat se shuru karna tha, policewale ki baat se nahi. Lekin kisi law mein ab tak ye nahi likha tha ki resist na karne bhar se aurat ki consent nahi maani ja sakti. Ye badlaav Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 se aaya, jisne IPC ka Section 375 dobara likha. Isme consent ka matlab likha gaya: "an unequivocal voluntary agreement", yaani saaf aur apni marzi se di gayi razaamandi. Ye bhi likha gaya ki jo aurat physically resist nahi karti, use "shall not by the reason only of that fact, be regarded as consenting", yaani sirf is wajah se consenting nahi maana jaayega [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Yaani 1978 ke judgment ka logic aakhirkaar law ki kitaab mein hi palat diya gaya.

## Resist, chot aur consent: aaj law kya kehta hai

1 July 2024 se rape ki definition Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) mein hai, jisne IPC ki jagah li [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]]. BNS ke Section 63 mein 2013 wale shabd bane hue hain: consent saaf aur apni marzi se honi chahiye, aur physically resist na karna apne aap mein consent nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 18 saal se kam umar ki ladki ke maamle mein toh consent ka sawaal hi nahi uthta: Section 63 ke hisaab se uske saath sex rape hai, chahe woh kuch bhi kahe [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Aur POCSO Act 18 se kam umar ke har bachche ko protect karta hai, ladka ho ya ladki [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Dating aur consent par hamara myth-check batata hai ki resist wala rule jaan-pehchaan walon ke beech kaise kaam karta hai. Yahan dekhiye ki law wahan kaise kaam karta hai jahan se 1978 wala case shuru hua tha: custody mein.

- Agar koi policewala police station mein ya apni custody mein rakhi aurat ka rape kare, ya koi sarkari karmachari, jail ya hospital staff apni custody ya dekhrekh mein rah rahi aurat ka rape kare, toh ye Section 64 ke under aggravated rape hai. Iski saza kam se kam 10 saal ki kadi qaid hai, jo baaki poori zindagi ki jail tak ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- Agar koi authority wala apne pad ka galat istemaal karke apni custody ya dekhrekh mein rah rahi aurat ko apne saath sex ke liye taiyaar karta hai, aur maamla rape tak nahi bhi pahunchta, tab bhi Section 68 ke under use 5 se 10 saal ki kadi qaid ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- Rape cases ki sunwai aaj bhi band kamre mein honi chahiye, aur jahan tak ho sake kisi woman judge ke saamne [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Survivor ka naam chhaapna Section 72 ke under crime hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Agar resist na karne ko consent nahi maana ja sakta, toh chot ke nishaan na hone ko bhi consent nahi maana ja sakta. Nishaan toh struggle se padte hain. Darr ke maare insaan freeze ho sakta hai. Woh isliye bhi chup reh sakti hai kyunki mana karna aur zyada khatarnaak lagta hai.

1978 ke judgment ne jis khatre ko ignore kiya, woh aaj bhi hai. 2024 mein police ne 'rape by police personnel' category mein 27 cases darj kiye, aur jail, remand home ya custody ki doosri jagahon ke staff ke khilaaf 3 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inme sirf wahi cases gine gaye hain jinme police ne inhi clauses mein FIR likhi. Isliye ye number kam se kam ki ginti hai, poori tasveer nahi.

Soch bhi poori tarah nahi badli hai. February 2026 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki sexual offence cases mein judges ko sensitise karne ki koshishein "have not borne the fruit that was expected", yaani unka utna phal nahi mila jitni umeed thi. Court ne ek expert committee se iske liye guidelines banane ko kaha [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi. Agar aapke ya aapke kisi jaanne wale ke saath sexual assault hua hai, toh law ab fight back na karne ko consent nahi maanta. Aap kisi bhi police station mein complaint kar sakte hain, chahe ghatna kahin bhi hui ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], aur rape ki FIR likhne se mana karne wala police officer khud crime karta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

delhi-gang-rape-2012-case-file.en:
On 16 December 2012, a young woman was gang-raped in Delhi. She did not survive, and the courts tried the case as gang rape and murder [[sc-mukesh-nct-delhi-2017]]. In court, it ended with four men hanged together at Tihar Jail on 20 March 2020 [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]]. In between came a new rape law, a new juvenile law and a women's safety fund carrying the name the media gave her. This file follows the case through the courts, then asks what it changed and what it left untouched.

## December 2012: what followed the crime

We will not describe the attack; the legal words, gang rape and murder, are enough. What matters is what followed.

That December, the government set up a three-member committee under Justice J.S. Verma to propose changes to the rape law. It reported on 23 January 2013 [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. In the Budget speech for 2013-14, the Finance Minister said "recent incidents have cast a long, dark shadow on our liberal and progressive credentials", and proposed a Nirbhaya Fund with Rs 1,000 crore from the government [[indiabudget-speech-2013-14]].

## From the trial court to the Supreme Court's 2017 judgment

Six people were accused. One adult was found dead in jail in March 2013. One was a juvenile, whose case went to the juvenile justice system [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]]. The four remaining adults were convicted and sentenced to death, and the Delhi High Court confirmed the sentences [[sc-mukesh-nct-delhi-2017]].

On 5 May 2017, a Supreme Court bench of Justices Dipak Misra, R. Banumathi and Ashok Bhushan dismissed the appeals of all four men and confirmed the death sentences, holding that "the aggravating circumstances outweigh the mitigating circumstances" [[sc-mukesh-nct-delhi-2017]]. In sentencing, aggravating circumstances make a crime worse; mitigating ones argue for a lighter sentence, such as an offender's youth or chance of reform.

## 20 March 2020: four hangings, and a juvenile already free

The four men were hanged together at Tihar at 5:30 am on 20 March 2020. By then the juvenile accused had been free for years: he was released in 2015 after three years in a correctional home [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]]. We do not name him or the men who were hanged; this file is about a system.

After his release, Parliament rewrote juvenile law. Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, assented to on 31 December 2015, a Juvenile Justice Board makes a "preliminary assessment" of any child aged 16 or above accused of a heinous offence (one with a minimum punishment of seven years or more), and can send the case to a Children's Court for trial as an adult [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]. Even then, the law bars a death sentence, or life in prison without the possibility of release, for such a child [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]].

## What the case changed, and what it could not

The rape law changed first. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, deemed in force from 3 February 2013, widened the legal definition of rape, fixed the age of consent at 18, set a 20-year minimum for gang rape, and created the offences of stalking, voyeurism, sexual harassment and acid attack [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. Our case file on the Verma Committee covers what Parliament ignored, including the committee's advice against the death penalty for rape, which it said "may not have a deterrent effect" [[thehindu-verma-2013]].

The money came next. According to a written Rajya Sabha reply reported by ThePrint in July 2026, allocations to the Nirbhaya Fund since 2013-14 had reached Rs 7,990.85 crore, of which Rs 6,703.02 crore (83.9%) had been released and used, leaving Rs 1,287.83 crore unspent [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. "Released and used" is one combined figure, so it does not show what was spent on the ground. Three schemes, Safe City projects, One Stop Centres and fast-track courts, took 63% of the money released. Some projects listed as ongoing had spent nothing at all, including a Panchayati Raj programme to sensitise men [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

One thing the case could not fix was how it was counted. Because NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence, the 2012 Delhi case was recorded as murder, not rape, according to a 2022 study in BMC Public Health [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]]. A case like it today falls under a separate head, murder with rape or gang rape, which recorded 266 cases in 2024, and still stays out of the rape total [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Our story on the principal offence rule explains what else that rule hides.

Nor did one verdict clear the queue behind it. At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial, and courts convicted in 24.4% of the rape trials they completed that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Why her name is never used, and what to call the case instead

The country never needed her name to understand what happened. In 2018 the Supreme Court observed that "without disclosing her true identity 'Nirbhaya' became the most effective symbol of protest the country has ever known". It ruled that a rape victim's identity must not be disclosed even after her death and even with her family's consent, unless a Sessions Judge decides it is justified, and that the bar covers print, electronic and social media alike [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Publishing a survivor's name or any identifying detail is a crime under Section 72 of the BNS, punishable with up to 2 years in prison and a fine [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

"Nirbhaya", meaning fearless, is a name the media gave her. Call the case "the 2012 Delhi gang rape case". If a post carries her real name or photo, do not forward it, even as a tribute.

This is general information, not legal advice. If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call 112. Every hospital, public or private, must give a rape survivor immediate free treatment [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
delhi-gang-rape-2012-case-file.hg:
16 December 2012 ko Delhi mein ek young woman ka gang rape hua. Woh bach nahi paayi, aur courts ne is case ko gang rape aur murder ke taur par chalaya [[sc-mukesh-nct-delhi-2017]]. Court mein iska ant 20 March 2020 ko hua, jab Tihar Jail mein chaar aadmiyon ko ek saath phaansi di gayi [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]]. In saalon ke beech ek naya rape law aaya, ek naya juvenile law aaya, aur women's safety ke liye ek fund bana jiska naam wahi hai jo media ne use diya tha. Ye file courts mein case ka safar dikhati hai, aur phir poochti hai ki isse kya badla aur kya jaisa tha waisa hi reh gaya.

## December 2012: crime ke baad kya hua

Hum hamle ki details nahi denge; legal shabd kaafi hain: gang rape aur murder. Zaroori ye hai ki uske baad kya hua.

Usi December mein sarkar ne Justice J.S. Verma ki leadership mein teen logon ki ek committee banayi, taaki rape law mein badlaav suggest kiye ja sakein. Committee ne 23 January 2013 ko apni report di [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. 2013-14 ke Budget speech mein Finance Minister ne kaha ki "recent incidents have cast a long, dark shadow on our liberal and progressive credentials", yaani haal ki ghatnaon ne desh ki liberal aur progressive image par ek lambi, kaali chhaaya daal di hai. Unhone Nirbhaya Fund ka proposal rakha, jisme sarkar Rs 1,000 crore degi [[indiabudget-speech-2013-14]].

## Trial court se Supreme Court ke 2017 ke faisle tak

Is case mein chhe log accused the. Ek adult accused March 2013 mein jail mein mrit paaya gaya. Ek juvenile tha, jiska case juvenile justice system mein gaya [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]]. Baaki chaar adults ko convict karke death sentence di gayi, aur Delhi High Court ne ise confirm kiya [[sc-mukesh-nct-delhi-2017]].

5 May 2017 ko Supreme Court mein Justices Dipak Misra, R. Banumathi aur Ashok Bhushan ki bench ne chaaron aadmiyon ki appeals dismiss kar di aur death sentences confirm ki, ye kehte hue ki "the aggravating circumstances outweigh the mitigating circumstances", yaani saza badhane wali baatein saza kam karne wali baaton par bhaari hain [[sc-mukesh-nct-delhi-2017]]. Saza tay karte waqt aggravating circumstances woh hain jo crime ko aur bura banati hain; mitigating woh jo kam saza ki taraf le jaati hain, jaise convict ki kam umar ya uske sudharne ki umeed.

## 20 March 2020: chaar phaansiyan, aur juvenile pehle hi azaad

Chaaron ko 20 March 2020 ko subah 5:30 baje Tihar mein ek saath phaansi di gayi. Tab tak juvenile accused ko chhute hue kai saal ho chuke the: woh correctional home mein teen saal rehne ke baad 2015 mein release ho gaya tha [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]]. Hum na uska naam likhte hain, na phaansi paane walon ka; ye file ek system ke baare mein hai.

Uski release ke baad Parliament ne juvenile law badla. Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 ko 31 December 2015 ko President ki manzoori mili. Iske under agar 16 saal ya usse bade kisi bachche par heinous offence ka aarop ho, yaani aisa crime jisme kam se kam saat saal ki saza hai, toh Juvenile Justice Board pehle uska "preliminary assessment" karta hai, aur case Children's Court bhej sakta hai jahan uska trial adult ki tarah ho sakta hai [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]. Tab bhi law aise bachche ko phaansi ya bina release ki umeed wali umrqaid dene se rokta hai [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]].

## Is case se kya badla, aur kya nahi badal saka

Sabse pehle rape law badla. Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ko 3 February 2013 se laagu maana gaya. Isne rape ki legal definition ko bada kiya, age of consent 18 saal tay ki, gang rape ke liye kam se kam 20 saal ki saza rakhi, aur stalking, voyeurism, sexual harassment aur acid attack ko alag offences banaya [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. Verma Committee par hamari case file batati hai ki Parliament ne committee ki kaunsi baatein nahi maani, jinme rape ke liye death penalty ke khilaaf uski salaah bhi thi; committee ne kaha tha ki iska "may not have a deterrent effect", yaani darr paida karne wala asar shayad na ho [[thehindu-verma-2013]].

Phir paisa aaya. July 2026 mein ThePrint ne Rajya Sabha ke ek likhit jawab ke hawaale se bataya ki 2013-14 se ab tak Nirbhaya Fund ke liye kul Rs 7,990.85 crore rakhe ja chuke the. Inme se Rs 6,703.02 crore (83.9%) release hokar use hue, aur Rs 1,287.83 crore kharch nahi hue [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. "Release aur use" ek hi milaa-jula figure hai, isliye isse ye pata nahi chalta ki zameen par asal mein kitna kharch hua. Teen schemes, yaani Safe City projects, One Stop Centres aur fast-track courts, ko release hue paise ka 63% mila. Kuch projects jinhe "ongoing" bataya gaya, un par ek rupaya bhi kharch nahi hua, jaise panchayaton ke zariye mardon ko sensitise karne ka ek programme [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

Ek cheez ye case nahi badal saka: iski ginti. NCRB har FIR ko sirf ek baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke naam par. 2022 ki ek BMC Public Health study ke mutaabik isi wajah se 2012 ka Delhi case rape nahi, murder ke taur par record hua [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]]. Aaj aisa case ek alag category mein jaata hai, murder with rape ya gang rape, jisme 2024 mein 266 cases darj hue, aur ye bhi rape ke total se bahar rehte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Principal offence rule par hamari story batati hai ki ye rule aur kya-kya chhupa deta hai.
