Ek case ke faisle se uske peeche lagi lambi line khatam nahi hui. 2024 ke end mein rape ke 1,85,785 cases trial ke intezaar mein the, aur us saal jin rape trials ka faisla aaya unme se 24.4% mein hi conviction hua [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Uska naam kabhi kyun nahi liya jaata, aur case ko kya kahein

Kya hua tha, ye samajhne ke liye desh ko kabhi uske naam ki zaroorat nahi padi. 2018 mein Supreme Court ne kaha: "without disclosing her true identity 'Nirbhaya' became the most effective symbol of protest the country has ever known", yaani asli pehchaan saamne aaye bina hi "Nirbhaya" desh mein protest ka sabse effective symbol ban gayi. Court ne faisla diya ki rape victim ki pehchaan uski maut ke baad bhi, aur family ki marzi ho tab bhi, reveal nahi ki ja sakti, jab tak Sessions Judge ye tay na kare ki aisa karna sahi hai. Ye rok print, electronic aur social media, sab par laagu hai [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Kisi survivor ka naam ya pehchaan batane wali koi bhi detail publish karna BNS Section 72 ke under crime hai, jisme 2 saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

"Nirbhaya" ka matlab hai fearless, jo dare nahi. Ye naam use media ne diya tha. Case ko "2012 Delhi gang rape case" kahiye. Agar kisi post mein uska asli naam ya photo hai, toh use aage mat bhejiye, tribute ke taur par bhi nahi.

Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi. Agar aapke ya aapke kisi jaanne wale ke saath sexual assault hua hai, toh 112 par call kariye. Har hospital ko, sarkari ho ya private, rape survivor ka turant free ilaaj karna hi hoga [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

durgapur-medical-student-case-2025.en:
On the night of 10 October 2025 a second-year MBBS student at a private medical college in Durgapur, West Bengal, was allegedly gang-raped near her campus. Police arrested six men [[ians-durgapur-chargesheet-2025]]. None had been convicted as of November 2026, so none is named here; neither is the student, her college or her home state.

It was the second time in just over a year that a young woman training to be a doctor in West Bengal became a national headline. That is why this case file reads it alongside RG Kar.

## The police moved fast

On 30 October 2025, 20 days after the crime, police filed a chargesheet in the Durgapur sub-divisional court naming six accused: one charged with rape, three with gang rape and two with extortion. The survivor had identified the accused in a test identification parade, and the court directed a speedy trial [[ians-durgapur-chargesheet-2025]] [[newsarena-durgapur-chargesheet-2025]].

Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, every member of a group that rapes a woman faces at least 20 years' rigorous imprisonment [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Under the companion procedure code, the trial should end within two months of the chargesheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. We found no verdict as of 23 November 2026.

## The remark that moved the blame

Two days after the crime, Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee said: "The girls should not be allowed to go outside (college) at night" [[tribune-durgapur-remark-2025]]. Her critics called it victim-blaming; she said her words had been "twisted and taken out of context" [[theweek-durgapur-remark-2025]].

Set aside the politics and look at the idea, because it is common far beyond one politician. "Don't let girls out at night" sounds like protection. In practice it does three things. It makes the survivor's movements the issue, not the attacker's choice. It makes women's education and work conditional on curfews, which hits medical students hardest, since hospitals run at night. And it lets the state off the hook for what it does control: lighting, patrols, transport and policing.

> A curfew for women is a confession that the state cannot keep a street safe. The fix is the street, not the women.

## A year after RG Kar: what the task force was still waiting for

On 9 August 2024 a trainee doctor was raped and murdered inside RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata. On 20 August 2024 the Supreme Court set up a National Task Force on the safety of medical professionals. The Chief Justice said: "If women cannot go to a place of work and feel safe, we are denying them equal opportunity" [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]].

In 2025 the criminal case moved; the safety work moved slowly. On 20 January 2025 a Sealdah court sentenced the convicted man to life imprisonment for the rest of his natural life [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. On 7 February 2025 the Calcutta High Court dismissed the state government's appeal for the death penalty, leaving the CBI's appeal to proceed [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]].

But on 5 August 2025, almost a year after creating the task force, the Supreme Court was still giving it eight more weeks to respond to the reports states and others had filed on preventing gender-based violence and on hospital safety protocols [[theprint-ntf-reply-2025]] [[medicaldialogues-ntf-2025]]. Two months later came Durgapur. We could not find what the task force's work produced after that hearing.

## The state's record

West Bengal is where both cases unfolded, and its numbers are the backdrop. In 2024 the state had the lowest conviction rate for crimes against women in India, 1.6%, and the largest pending caseload, 3,84,388 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Fast chargesheets in famous cases sit on top of that backlog. For most women in the state, the case does not end in a verdict at all.

## What safety should look like for a student

Consider a third-year medical student in Bankura whose ward posting ends at 9 p.m. and whose hostel is a kilometre away. A safe system would give her a college vehicle or an escorted route, lit paths, a guard at the gate who logs who enters, and a helpline that answers. Telling her to stay in would end her training. Building those things would end the excuse.

If an assault happens anywhere, she can report it at any police station, which must register it even if the crime happened in another area [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Her identity is protected by law, and publishing it is a crime [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.
durgapur-medical-student-case-2025.hg:
10 October 2025 ki raat West Bengal ke Durgapur mein ek private medical college ki second-year MBBS student ka uske campus ke paas kathit gang rape hua. Police ne chhe aadmiyon ko arrest kiya [[ians-durgapur-chargesheet-2025]]. November 2026 tak kisi ka conviction nahi hua tha, isliye yahan kisi ka naam nahi hai; na student ka, na uske college ka, na uske home state ka.

Ek saal se thode hi zyada samay mein yeh doosri baar tha jab West Bengal mein doctor banne ki training le rahi ek young aurat national headline bani. Isiliye yeh case file ise RG Kar ke saath padhti hai.

## Police ne tezi dikhayi

30 October 2025 ko, crime ke 20 din baad, police ne Durgapur sub-divisional court mein chargesheet file ki jisme chhe accused the: ek par rape, teen par gang rape aur do par extortion (vasooli) ka charge. Survivor ne test identification parade mein accused ko pehchaana tha, aur court ne tez trial ka order diya [[ians-durgapur-chargesheet-2025]] [[newsarena-durgapur-chargesheet-2025]].

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita mein kisi aurat ka rape karne wale group ke har member ko kam se kam 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Saath wale procedure code ke hisaab se trial chargesheet ke do mahine ke andar khatam hona chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. 23 November 2026 tak humein koi verdict nahi mila.

## Woh remark jisne blame ki disha badli

Crime ke do din baad Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee ne kaha: "The girls should not be allowed to go outside (college) at night", yaani ladkiyon ko raat mein college se bahar nahi jaane dena chahiye [[tribune-durgapur-remark-2025]]. Critics ne ise victim-blaming kaha; unhone kaha ki unke shabdon ko "twisted and taken out of context", yaani tod-marod kar aur context se bahar pesh kiya gaya [[theweek-durgapur-remark-2025]].

Politics ko ek taraf rakhiye aur idea ko dekhiye, kyunki yeh soch ek neta se kahin aage tak phaili hai. "Ladkiyon ko raat mein bahar mat jaane do" suraksha jaisa lagta hai. Asal mein yeh teen kaam karta hai. Yeh survivor ke aane-jaane ko mudda bana deta hai, hamlavar ki choice ko nahi. Yeh aurton ki padhai aur kaam ko curfew par tika deta hai, jo medical students par sabse zyada bhaari padta hai, kyunki hospital raat mein bhi chalte hain. Aur yeh state ko un cheezon ki zimmedari se chhutkara deta hai jo uske haath mein hain: roshni, patrolling, transport aur policing.

> Aurton ke liye curfew yeh kabool karna hai ki state ek sadak safe nahi rakh sakta. Sudhaar sadak ka hona chahiye, aurton ka nahi.

## RG Kar ke ek saal baad: task force kis cheez ka intezaar kar rahi thi

9 August 2024 ko Kolkata ke RG Kar Medical College and Hospital mein ek trainee doctor ka rape aur murder hua. 20 August 2024 ko Supreme Court ne medical professionals ki safety par National Task Force banayi. Chief Justice ne kaha: "If women cannot go to a place of work and feel safe, we are denying them equal opportunity", yaani agar aurtein kaam ki jagah safe mehsoos nahi kar sakti, toh hum unhe barabar ka mauka nahi de rahe [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]].

2025 mein criminal case aage badha; safety ka kaam dheere chala. 20 January 2025 ko Sealdah court ne convict ko baaki poori natural life ki umrqaid di [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. 7 February 2025 ko Calcutta High Court ne death penalty ke liye state sarkar ki appeal khaarij kar di, aur CBI ki apni appeal aage badhne di [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]].

Lekin 5 August 2025 ko, task force banne ke lagbhag ek saal baad, Supreme Court use states aur doosron ki gender-based violence rokne aur hospital safety protocols wali reports par jawab dene ke liye aath hafte aur de raha tha [[theprint-ntf-reply-2025]] [[medicaldialogues-ntf-2025]]. Do mahine baad Durgapur hua. Us hearing ke baad task force ke kaam ka kya nateeja nikla, yeh hum nahi dhoondh paaye.

## State ka record

Dono case West Bengal mein hue, aur uske numbers hi background hain. 2024 mein state mein aurton ke khilaaf crimes ka conviction rate India mein sabse kam, 1.6%, tha, aur pending cases sabse zyada, 3,84,388 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Mashhoor cases mein tez chargesheets isi backlog ke upar baithi hain. State ki zyadatar aurton ke liye case verdict tak pahunchta hi nahi.

## Ek student ke liye safety kaisi dikhni chahiye

Sochiye, Bankura mein ek third-year medical student ki ward posting raat 9 baje khatam hoti hai aur uska hostel ek kilometre door hai. Ek safe system use college ki gaadi ya escort wala raasta dega, roshni wale raaste, gate par ek guard jo aane-jaane walon ko darj kare, aur ek helpline jo phone uthaye. Use ghar mein rehne ko kehna uski training khatam kar dega. Yeh cheezein banana bahaanon ko khatam karega.

Agar kahin bhi assault ho, toh woh kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakti hai, jise use register karna hoga chahe crime kisi aur ilaake mein hua ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Uski identity law se protected hai, aur use publish karna crime hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

gujarat-2002-gang-rape-remission-quashed.en:
In 2002, during the riots in Gujarat, a pregnant woman was gang-raped and 14 of her relatives were murdered [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. She chose to fight in public, and the case is widely known by her name. Indian law makes it a crime to reveal a rape survivor's identity, with narrow exceptions such as her written authorisation [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and this magazine never prints survivors' names. So this file calls it what it is: the 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case. It is the story of a verdict that had to be won again and again for 22 years.

## 2002: a gang rape and 14 murders during the Gujarat riots

Under today's law, two facts about this crime mark it out for heavier punishment. Rape during communal violence and rape of a pregnant woman are both among the 13 aggravated forms of rape under Section 64(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), punishable with 10 years up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life. Gang rape, under Section 70, carries at least 20 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Why single out communal violence? Our reading: in a riot a woman can be targeted for the community she belongs to, not only as an individual, and at a time when the usual protections (neighbours, police, hospitals) are at their weakest.

## A trial moved to Mumbai, and convictions upheld in 2017

The case was not tried in Gujarat. On 21 January 2008 a special court in Mumbai sentenced 11 men to life imprisonment for the gang rape and the 14 murders [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. The same court convicted a police officer of deliberately recording the FIR incorrectly. It acquitted five police personnel and two doctors.

On 4 May 2017 the Bombay High Court upheld all 11 convictions and convicted the seven who had been acquitted [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. In one case, courts found fault not only with the attackers but with police personnel and doctors, the people whose job was to record the crime and examine its evidence.

Today, a public servant who fails to record an FIR for rape commits a crime punishable with six months to two years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The trial's move to Mumbai would matter again years later. A separate story looks at why several of India's biggest rape trials had to leave the states where the crimes happened.

## 2019: Rs 50 lakh, a job and a home

On 23 April 2019 the Supreme Court ordered the Gujarat government to pay the survivor Rs 50 lakh in compensation and to give her a government job and housing [[livelaw-bilkis-compensation-2019]]. It was an order against the state itself, seventeen years after the crime.

Most survivors never reach the Supreme Court. But the law lets any survivor apply to the State or District Legal Services Authority for compensation, even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Another story compares what courts have ordered in India's landmark cases with what any survivor can claim.

Three years after the 2019 order, the same state government issued the orders that let the 11 men go.

## 15 August 2022: 11 life convicts walk out

On 15 August 2022, Independence Day, all 11 men walked out of Godhra jail. The Gujarat government had granted them remission under its 1992 remission policy, by orders dated 10 August 2022 [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]].

Remission is the government's power to cut short a sentence a court has passed. A life sentence does not automatically mean a convict will die in prison: a government can order early release, and courts can check whether it had the power to do so. The law gives that power to the "appropriate government". In this case, those two words decided everything. This is general information, not legal advice.

Consider what an early release means from the other side. Imagine a woman in a small town who testified for years, then learns from a WhatsApp forward that the men she testified against are free and back on her street. For a government, remission is a file. For a survivor, it can mean fear at her own front door.

## January 2024: 'obtained by fraud', and the return to jail

On 8 January 2024 a Supreme Court bench of Justices B.V. Nagarathna and Ujjal Bhuyan quashed the remission [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. Gujarat, it held, had no power to grant it. Maharashtra, where the trial was held, was the appropriate government. The court went further: its own order of May 2022, which had directed Gujarat to decide the remission, had been obtained by suppressing facts and by fraud.

> The Supreme Court ruled that its own May 2022 order was "obtained by fraud" and therefore "a nullity". (8 January 2024)

The ruling came on petitions that included one filed by the survivor herself. The 11 men were told to report to jail within two weeks. Their pleas for more time cited the ill-health of ageing parents, a family wedding and the crop harvest. On 19 January the court refused. All 11 surrendered at Godhra sub-jail in Panchmahal district late on the night of 21 January 2024, the deadline [[scroll-bilkis-surrender-2024]].

Count the stages: a trial, an appeal, a compensation order, a remission, a second fight in the Supreme Court, a surrender. Each time the verdict had to be defended again, and the survivor had to keep going back. Under the 2024 ruling, any future plea for early release has to be decided by Maharashtra, not Gujarat.

The lesson for every reader is plain. A conviction is not the end of a case. Who holds the power to release a convict matters as much as the sentence, and those decisions can be challenged in court.
gujarat-2002-gang-rape-remission-quashed.hg:
2002 mein Gujarat ke riots ke dauraan ek pregnant aurat ka gang rape hua aur uske 14 rishtedaaron ka murder kar diya gaya [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. Usne yeh ladaai khul kar, sabke saamne ladi, aur yeh case uske naam se jaana jaata hai. Lekin law kehta hai ki rape survivor ki identity kholna crime hai, kuch gini-chuni exceptions ke saath, jaise uski written permission [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur hamari magazine kisi survivor ka naam kabhi nahi chhaapti. Isliye hum ise wahi kahenge jo yeh hai: 2002 ke Gujarat riots ka gang rape case. Yeh ek aise verdict ki kahani hai jise 22 saal tak baar-baar jeetna pada.

## 2002: Gujarat riots mein ek gang rape aur 14 murders

Aaj ke law mein is crime ki do baatein ise aur kadi saza ke laayak banati hain. Communal violence ke dauraan rape, aur pregnant aurat ka rape, dono Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 64(2) mein gine gaye rape ke 13 aggravated forms mein shaamil hain, jinki saza 10 saal se lekar baaki poori natural life ki qaid tak hai. Gang rape ke liye Section 70 mein kam se kam 20 saal ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Communal violence ko alag se kyun gina gaya? Hamari samajh yeh hai: riot mein aurat ko sirf ek insaan ki tarah nahi, balki uski community ki wajah se target kiya ja sakta hai, aur woh bhi aise waqt jab normal protections (padosi, police, hospitals) sabse kamzor hote hain.

## Mumbai mein chala trial, aur 2017 mein convictions par muhar

Yeh case Gujarat mein nahi chala. 21 January 2008 ko Mumbai ki ek special court ne gang rape aur 14 murders ke liye 11 logon ko umrqaid di [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. Usi court ne ek police officer ko bhi convict kiya, jisne jaan-boojh kar FIR galat record ki thi. Court ne paanch police personnel aur do doctors ko bari kar diya.

4 May 2017 ko Bombay High Court ne saare 11 convictions uphold kiye, aur jo saat log bari hue the, unhe bhi convict kar diya [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. Ek hi case mein courts ne sirf hamlawaron mein nahi, police personnel aur doctors mein bhi dosh paaya, yaani un logon mein jinka kaam crime record karna aur uske evidence ki jaanch karna tha.

Aaj agar koi public servant rape ki FIR record nahi karta, toh yeh crime hai, jiski saza chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Trial ka Mumbai jaana kai saal baad phir bahut matter karne wala tha. India ke kai bade rape trials ko un states se bahar kyun le jaana pada jahan crime hua tha, is par hamari ek alag story hai.

## 2019: Rs 50 lakh, naukri aur ghar

23 April 2019 ko Supreme Court ne Gujarat sarkar ko order diya ki survivor ko Rs 50 lakh compensation, ek sarkari naukri aur rehne ke liye ghar diya jaye [[livelaw-bilkis-compensation-2019]]. Yeh order seedha state ke khilaaf tha, aur crime ke satrah saal baad aaya.

Zyadatar survivors kabhi Supreme Court tak nahi pahunchtin. Lekin law har survivor ko State ya District Legal Services Authority mein compensation ke liye apply karne deta hai, chahe offender kabhi pakda hi na jaye aur koi trial na ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Landmark cases mein courts ne kitna compensation diya aur aam survivor kya claim kar sakti hai, is par hamari ek aur story hai.

2019 ke us order ke teen saal baad, usi state sarkar ne woh orders jaari kiye jinse yeh 11 log reha ho gaye.

## 15 August 2022: umrqaid wale 11 convicts bahar aaye

15 August 2022, yaani Independence Day ko, saare 11 log Godhra jail se bahar aa gaye. Gujarat sarkar ne unhe apni 1992 ki remission policy ke under remission di thi, jiske orders 10 August 2022 ko jaari hue the [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]].

Remission ka matlab hai ki sarkar court ki di hui saza ko beech mein hi kam kar de. Umrqaid ka matlab hamesha yeh nahi hota ki convict jail mein hi marega: sarkar use pehle chhod sakti hai, aur court check kar sakti hai ki sarkar ke paas aisa karne ki power thi ya nahi. Law yeh power "appropriate government" ko deta hai. Is case mein inhi do shabdon ne sab kuch tay kiya. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Ab zara doosri taraf se sochiye. Maan lijiye kisi chhote shehar ki ek aurat ne saalon tak court mein gawahi di. Phir ek din WhatsApp forward se pata chalta hai ki jinke khilaaf usne gawahi di thi, woh chhoot gaye hain aur uski gali mein laut aaye hain. Sarkar ke liye remission bas ek file hai. Survivor ke liye iska matlab apne hi darwaaze par darr ho sakta hai.

## January 2024: 'fraud se liya gaya order', aur jail waapsi

8 January 2024 ko Justices B.V. Nagarathna aur Ujjal Bhuyan ki Supreme Court bench ne remission radd kar di [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. Court ne kaha ki Gujarat ke paas yeh remission dene ki power hi nahi thi; trial Maharashtra mein chala tha, isliye appropriate government Maharashtra thi. Court ne ek aur badi baat kahi: May 2022 mein Supreme Court ne hi Gujarat ko remission par faisla karne ko kaha tha, aur woh order facts chhupa kar aur fraud se liya gaya tha.

> Supreme Court ne kaha ki uska apna May 2022 ka order "obtained by fraud" tha, aur isliye "a nullity", yaani uski koi legal value nahi. (8 January 2024)

Yeh faisla kai petitions par aaya, jinme ek petition khud survivor ne file ki thi. 11 logon ko do hafte ke andar jail authorities ke saamne report karne ko kaha gaya. Unhone aur time maanga, aur wajah batayi: boodhe maa-baap ki bimaari, family mein shaadi aur fasal ki katai. 19 January ko court ne mana kar diya. Deadline 21 January 2024 thi, aur usi raat der se saare 11 ne Panchmahal district ki Godhra sub-jail mein surrender kiya [[scroll-bilkis-surrender-2024]].

Ab saare padaav giniye: ek trial, ek appeal, compensation ka ek order, remission, Supreme Court mein doosri ladaai, aur phir surrender. Har baar us verdict ko phir se bachana pada, aur survivor ko baar-baar court lautna pada. 2024 ke faisle ke baad, early release ki koi bhi nayi application par faisla Maharashtra karega, Gujarat nahi.

Har reader ke liye sabak saaf hai. Conviction case ka end nahi hai. Convict ko chhodne ki power kiske paas hai, yeh bhi utna hi matter karta hai jitni saza, aur aise faislon ko court mein challenge kiya ja sakta hai.

hathras-2020-night-cremation-verdict.en:
On 14 September 2020, a 19-year-old Dalit woman in Hathras, Uttar Pradesh, was assaulted. She died 15 days later, on 29 September. Police then cremated her in the middle of the night, without her family's consent [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]]. The CBI later charged four men with rape, gang rape and murder; in 2023 a court convicted none of them of rape. This case file is about the hours in which a case like this is won or lost.

## 14 to 29 September 2020: a death, and a cremation at night

She lived for 15 more days. Her account came in stages: the court would later say that the other three accused were named eight days later [[theprint-hathras-verdict-2023]]. Hold on to that detail.

The cremation took two things at once: her family's right to say goodbye, and any chance of a second, independent examination of her body. The state, not her family, made that decision.

## The CBI's case: rape, gang rape and murder

In December 2020 the CBI charged four men with rape, gang rape and murder under the IPC, and with offences under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]]. But no investigation can collect evidence that is already gone. No one can know whether earlier evidence, or a second examination, would have changed the outcome. That uncertainty is itself a harm.

## March 2023: what the special court found, and what it did not

On 2 March 2023, the special SC/ST court in Hathras acquitted three of the four accused. It convicted the main accused of culpable homicide not amounting to murder (Section 304 of the IPC) and of SC/ST Act offences. None of the four was found guilty of gang rape or murder [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]]. The convicted man was sentenced to life imprisonment and a fine of Rs 50,000, Rs 40,000 of it for her mother [[theprint-hathras-verdict-2023]].

The court held that the prosecution had failed to prove rape. It said, in ThePrint's translation of the Hindi order, that the other three accused were named later "after being coached by her relatives" [[theprint-hathras-verdict-2023]]. That reasoning is open to appeal; the family said it would appeal [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]], and we could not confirm where that stands.

"Not proved" is a finding about evidence, not proof that a woman lied, as our piece on the "false case" myth explains. In August 2023, five months after this verdict, the Supreme Court's handbook for judges rejected the stereotype that a woman who delays reporting rape is lying, noting that "lack of familial support or fear of repercussions" can cause delay [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. That guidance came later and does not decide this case, but it shows the top court rejects the idea that a late account must be false.

## Evidence that cannot be recovered: why the first 24 hours matter

Rape cases often turn on evidence that fades: what a medical examination can find, the clothes, the survivor's first full statement. That is why the law sets clocks. Under Section 184 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which replaced the CrPC in July 2024 [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]], police must send a rape survivor for a medical examination, with her consent, within 24 hours of receiving information; the doctor's report must reach the investigating officer within 7 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Under Section 183, a magistrate, as far as practicable a woman, must record her statement as soon as police learn of the offence. Under Section 173, any police station must register the FIR wherever the crime happened, and she gets a free copy [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Read them as a chain. A statement recorded early by a magistrate leaves less room for later claims of coaching. An examination within a day captures what delay erases. A body that is cremated can never be examined again. Our 72-hour guide explains what to do in those first days.

## The rights a Dalit survivor and her family have

Caste was never a side issue here. The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook calls it a stereotype that dominant-caste men do not want sexual relations with women from oppressed castes, so any rape complaint by such a woman against such a man must be false. It says instead that "Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. In 2024, police registered 4,262 rape cases of Scheduled Caste women and girls, about 12 a day [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Even that is a floor: NCRB counts a crime against a Scheduled Caste person only when the SC/ST Act is applied [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

The 2015 amendment to the SC/ST Act gives families tools few know about:

- A non-SC/ST public servant who wilfully neglects duties under the Act, including registering the FIR under the correct sections and filing a charge sheet within 60 days, faces six months to one year in prison [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].
- Under Section 15A, the state must protect victims, their dependants and witnesses from intimidation, and victims have the right to timely notice of every court hearing, including bail [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].
- Exclusive Special Courts must hear atrocity trials day to day and, as far as possible, finish them within two months of the charge sheet [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

This is general information, not legal advice. Hathras was tried by a special court, and the verdict still came more than two years after the charge sheet. Even so, each of these rights is a question a family can ask from the first hour: has the SC/ST Act been added, when will she be examined, who will tell us about the bail hearing? In Hathras, her family did not get to decide even her last rites.
hathras-2020-night-cremation-verdict.hg:
14 September 2020 ko Uttar Pradesh ke Hathras mein ek 19 saal ki Dalit ladki par hamla hua. 15 din baad, 29 September ko uski maut ho gayi. Uske baad police ne aadhi raat ko uska antim sanskar kar diya, uski family ki marzi ke bina [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]]. Baad mein CBI ne chaar aadmiyon par rape, gang rape aur murder ka charge lagaya, lekin 2023 mein court ne inmein se kisi ko rape ki sazaa nahi di. Yeh case file un ghanton ke baare mein hai jinmein aisa koi case banta ya bigadta hai.

## 14 se 29 September 2020: ek maut, aur aadhi raat ka antim sanskar

Hamle ke baad woh 15 din zinda rahi. Uski baat tukdon mein saamne aayi: court ne baad mein kaha ki baaki teen accused ke naam aath din baad liye gaye [[theprint-hathras-verdict-2023]]. Yeh baat yaad rakhiye.

Us raat ke antim sanskar ne ek saath do cheezein chheen leen. Pehli, family ka apne tareeke se beti ko aakhri vidaai dene ka haq. Doosri, uske shareer ki dobara aur alag se jaanch ka har mauka. Uske shareer ka kya hoga, yeh uski family ne nahi, state ne tay kiya.

## CBI ka case: rape, gang rape aur murder

December 2020 mein Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) ne chaar aadmiyon par IPC ke tahat rape, gang rape aur murder ka charge lagaya, saath mein SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act ke tahat bhi [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]]. Lekin koi bhi investigation, chahe kitni bhi badi agency kare, woh saboot nahi juta sakti jo pehle hi mit chuka ho. Ab koi nahi jaan sakta ki pehle jutaye gaye saboot, ya dobara hui jaanch, faisla badal deti ya nahi. Yeh anishchitta apne aap mein ek nuksaan hai.

## March 2023: special court ne kya paaya, aur kya nahi

2 March 2023 ko Hathras ki special SC/ST court ne chaar mein se teen accused ko bari kar diya. Main accused ko culpable homicide not amounting to murder, yaani gair-iraadatan hatya (IPC ki Section 304), aur SC/ST Act ke offences ka doshi maana gaya. Chaaron mein se kisi ko gang rape ya murder ka doshi nahi paaya gaya [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]]. Convict ko umrqaid hui aur Rs 50,000 ka jurmana laga, jismein se Rs 40,000 ladki ki maa ko milne the [[theprint-hathras-verdict-2023]].

Court ne kaha ki prosecution rape saabit nahi kar paaya. Hindi mein likhe order ke ThePrint ke translation ke mutaabik, court ne kaha ki baaki teen accused ke naam baad mein "after being coached by her relatives", yaani rishtedaaron ke sikhaane par, liye gaye [[theprint-hathras-verdict-2023]]. Is reasoning ko appeal mein challenge kiya ja sakta hai. Family ne kaha tha ki woh appeal karegi [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]]; woh appeal abhi kis haal mein hai, yeh hum confirm nahi kar paaye.

"Saabit nahi hua" saboot ke baare mein faisla hai, yeh saboot nahi ki aurat ne jhooth bola. "False case" wali galatfehmi par hamara article yahi samjhata hai. Is faisle ke paanch mahine baad, August 2023 mein, Supreme Court ne judges ke liye ek handbook nikaali. Usmein is soch ko galat bataya gaya ki rape ki complaint der se karne wali aurat jhooth bol rahi hai. Handbook kehti hai ki "lack of familial support or fear of repercussions", yaani family ka saath na milna ya anjaam ka darr, bhi der ki wajah ho sakta hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Yeh guidance baad mein aayi aur is case ka faisla nahi karti. Par isse saaf hai ki desh ki sabse badi court yeh nahi maanti ki der se aayi baat jhoothi hi hogi.

## Jo saboot laut kar nahi aate: pehle 24 ghante kyun zaroori hain

Rape ke case aksar aise saboot par tike hote hain jo waqt ke saath mit jaate hain: medical exam mein kya milta hai, kapde, aur survivor ka pehla poora statement. Isiliye law ne ghadi tay ki hai. July 2024 se CrPC ki jagah Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) laagu hai [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]]. Iski Section 184 kehti hai ki police ko jaankari milne ke 24 ghante ke andar survivor ko, uski marzi se, medical exam ke liye bhejna hoga. Doctor ki report 7 din mein investigating officer tak pahunchni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Section 183 ke mutaabik police ko crime ka pata chalte hi magistrate ko uska statement record karna hoga, jahan tak ho sake ek woman magistrate. Section 173 ke tahat koi bhi police station FIR darj karega, crime chahe kahin bhi hua ho, aur survivor ko uski copy free milegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Inhe ek chain ki tarah dekhiye. Magistrate ke saamne jaldi record hua statement baad mein "coaching" jaise daavon ki gunjaaish kam kar deta hai. Ek din ke andar hua medical exam woh pakad leta hai jo deri mita deti hai. Aur jis shareer ka antim sanskar ho gaya, uski jaanch phir kabhi nahi ho sakti. Shuru ke dinon mein kya karna hai, yeh hamari 72-hour guide batati hai.

## Dalit survivor aur uski family ke haq

Is case mein caste kabhi side ki baat nahi thi. Supreme Court ki 2023 ki handbook is soch ko stereotype batati hai ki dominant caste ke aadmi oppressed castes ki auraton se sexual rishta nahi chahte, isliye aisi aurat ki aise aadmi ke khilaaf rape complaint jhoothi hi hogi. Handbook iske ulat kehti hai: "Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies", yaani dabang caste ke aadmiyon ne caste ki oonch-neech banaye rakhne ke liye lambe samay se sexual violence ko hathiyaar banaya hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. 2024 mein police ne Scheduled Caste auraton aur ladkiyon se rape ke 4,262 case darj kiye, yaani roz kareeb 12 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Asli sankhya isse kam nahi, zyada hi hogi, kyunki NCRB kisi crime ko Scheduled Caste ke khilaaf crime tabhi ginta hai jab usmein SC/ST Act lagaya gaya ho [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

2015 mein SC/ST Act mein jo badlaav hue, woh families ko kuch aise hathiyaar dete hain jinke baare mein kam log jaante hain:

- Agar koi non-SC/ST public servant is Act ke tahat apni duty mein jaanbujhkar laaparwahi kare, jaise sahi sections mein FIR darj na karna ya 60 din mein chargesheet file na karna, toh use chhe mahine se ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].
- Section 15A ke tahat state ki zimmedaari hai ki victims, un par nirbhar logon aur witnesses ko daraane-dhamkaane se bachaye. Victims ko bail samet har court hearing ki jaankari time par paane ka haq hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].
- Exclusive Special Courts ko aise trials roz-roz sunne honge, aur jahan tak ho sake chargesheet ke do mahine ke andar khatam karne honge [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Hathras ka trial special court mein hi chala, phir bhi faisla chargesheet ke do saal se zyada baad aaya. Iske bawajood, inmein se har haq ek sawaal hai jo family pehle ghante se pooch sakti hai: kya FIR mein SC/ST Act joda gaya, medical exam kab hoga, bail ki hearing ke baare mein humein kaun batayega? Hathras mein toh family ko apni beti ka antim sanskar tak tay karne nahi diya gaya.

hema-committee-report-malayalam-cinema.en:
In February 2017 an actor was abducted and sexually assaulted in Kerala. We do not name her. That year the state set up a committee to study what women face in Malayalam cinema [[hindu-hema-coverage-2024]]. Its central finding, that sexual harassment in the industry "remains shockingly rampant" [[bbc-hema-report-2024]], then sat with the government for nearly five years. Here is what it found, how the report stayed buried, and what the law already required of every film set.

## 2017: an assault and a committee

The Kerala government formed the committee in 2017, after a petition from the Women in Cinema Collective (WCC), a group of women working in Malayalam films. It had three members: a retired High Court judge, Justice K. Hema; the former actor Sharada; and the retired IAS officer K.B. Valsala Kumari. Its brief was sexual harassment and gender inequality in the industry [[hindu-hema-coverage-2024]].

The collective did not wait for it. In 2018 the WCC went to the Kerala High Court, arguing that the actors' association, AMMA, was bound by the Vishaka guidelines and the POSH Act to have an Internal Complaints Committee or grievance cell, and had none. By 2022 the collective said AMMA still had none [[livelaw-kwc-wcc-pil-2022]].

## Five years unpublished: December 2019 to August 2024

The committee submitted its report in December 2019. It was released on 19 August 2024, after the State Information Commission ordered it made public and the Kerala High Court dismissed a challenge to that order [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]]. It came out under the Right to Information Act with 63 of its 295 pages removed, to protect the identities of witnesses and of those accused [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

The government had the report all along. On 10 September 2024 the Kerala High Court asked why the state had been "inactive or silent" since 31 December 2019, when the state police chief had held a copy since February 2021. It ordered the full, unredacted report handed to a Special Investigation Team [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-sit-2024]].

That is how an inquiry gets buried: no ban, no denial, just years of nothing. It took an information commission's order and a failed legal challenge in the High Court before a government's own report reached the women it was written about.

## What the report found: harassment, a casting couch and a 'power group'

The committee called sexual harassment the "worst evil" women in the industry face, and said it "goes on unchecked and uncontrolled". Men in the industry, it wrote, "make open demands for sex without any qualms as if it's their birthright" [[bbc-hema-report-2024]].

It confirmed a casting couch. Junior artists were told they would get a chance in films if they complied with demands for sex, and women who agreed were referred to by a code name: "cooperating artists" [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

Above this sat a "power group": 10 to 15 men, all directors, producers and actors, who decide who stays in the industry and can ban even prominent figures. Anyone who offends them, the report says, "will be wiped off the industry". The committee was told that a prominent actor had called this lobby a "mafia" [[tnm-hema-mafia-bans-2024]]. The findings rest on testimony, the names in the report are redacted, and we name no one.

The point is structural. When a small group can end a career, a casting couch does not need force. Saying no costs the next job.

## No toilets, no changing rooms, and fear of speaking

Some findings concern the most basic dignity at work. Junior women artists on Malayalam film sets had no toilets or changing rooms. "There are no toilets, so women have to go in the bushes or behind thick trees," the report records. Holding urine for long hours, and being unable to change sanitary napkins during periods, made women sick, in some cases needing hospitalisation [[bbc-hema-report-2024]].

Many women were afraid to testify at all, because "they were afraid they would lose their jobs". The committee first found that fear strange, then concluded it was "well-founded", and said it was concerned for the safety of witnesses and their close relatives [[bbc-hema-report-2024]].

Consider a hypothetical case: a junior artist from a small town on an outdoor shoot. There is nowhere private to change, and nobody on set has told her who to complain to. If a senior crew member harasses her, the person she would report him to may be his friend, and her next booking depends on both of them. Her silence is not agreement. It is the price of the next job.

## Film sets are workplaces: what the POSH Act requires

This is general information, not legal advice. The POSH Act's definition of "workplace" expressly covers private organisations carrying on "entertainmental" activities [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. On 17 March 2022, deciding the WCC's petitions, the Kerala High Court held that each film's production unit is a workplace and must have an Internal Complaints Committee if it engages more than 10 workers. It did not accept the collective's case in full: film associations such as AMMA, it held, are not the actors' employers and need a committee only for their own office staff. AMMA volunteered to set one up [[kerala-hc-wcc-judgment-2022]].

The Act protects any woman "of any age whether employed or not" who is harassed at a workplace [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Even so, the Kerala High Court has remarked orally that the Act does not reach women who are only seeking work, which is the stage at which a casting couch operates; whether job-seekers are covered is contested. On 8 October 2025 the state told the court that a draft law for the entertainment industry would go to the cabinet in November, and that the SIT investigation was over [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-draft-law-2025]]. We could not confirm whether that law has since been passed.

A complaint must be made in writing within three months of the incident, extendable by three more, and the inquiry must finish within 90 days [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. A complaint against the employer, or from a workplace with fewer than ten workers, goes to the district's Local Committee [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. A woman can also complain on the government's SHe-Box portal [[shebox]].

The report took nearly five years to reach the public. The law that should protect the next junior artist already exists. The test is whether production units obey it before another committee has to be set up.
hema-committee-report-malayalam-cinema.hg:
February 2017 mein Kerala mein ek actor ko agwa karke uske saath sexual assault kiya gaya. Hum unka naam nahi likhte. Usi saal state ne ek committee banayi, ye samajhne ke liye ki Malayalam cinema mein aurton ko kya jhelna padta hai [[hindu-hema-coverage-2024]]. Committee ka sabse bada nateeja tha ki industry mein sexual harassment "remains shockingly rampant", yaani hairaan kar dene ki had tak phaila hua hai [[bbc-hema-report-2024]]. Phir ye report lagbhag paanch saal tak sarkar ke paas padi rahi. Jaaniye committee ko kya mila, report kaise dabi rahi, aur law har film set se pehle se kya maangta tha.

## 2017: ek assault aur ek committee

Kerala sarkar ne 2017 mein ye committee banayi, Women in Cinema Collective (WCC) ki petition ke baad. WCC Malayalam films mein kaam karne wali aurton ka group hai. Committee mein teen members the: High Court ki retired judge Justice K. Hema, former actor Sharada, aur retired IAS officer K.B. Valsala Kumari. Iska kaam tha industry mein sexual harassment aur gender inequality ki jaanch karna [[hindu-hema-coverage-2024]].

Collective ne committee ke bharose intezaar nahi kiya. 2018 mein WCC Kerala High Court gaya. Uski daleel thi ki Vishaka guidelines aur POSH Act ke hisaab se actors ki association AMMA mein Internal Complaints Committee ya grievance cell hona zaroori hai, aur wahan aisa kuch nahi tha. 2022 tak bhi collective ka kehna tha ki AMMA mein aisi koi committee nahi bani [[livelaw-kwc-wcc-pil-2022]].

## Paanch saal tak chhupi: December 2019 se August 2024

Committee ne apni report December 2019 mein saunp di. Ye 19 August 2024 ko jaari hui, jab State Information Commission ne ise public karne ka order diya aur Kerala High Court ne us order ke khilaaf challenge khaarij kar diya [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]]. Report Right to Information Act ke under aayi, aur uske 295 pages mein se 63 hata diye gaye the, taaki witnesses aur accused logon ki pehchaan chhupi rahe [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

Report sarkar ke paas shuru se thi. 10 September 2024 ko Kerala High Court ne poocha ki 31 December 2019 se state "inactive or silent", yaani chup aur bekaar kyun baitha raha, jabki state ke police chief ke paas February 2021 se iski copy thi. Court ne order diya ki poori, bina kaat-chhaant wali report ek Special Investigation Team ko di jaaye [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-sit-2024]].

Kisi inquiry ko aise hi dabaya jaata hai: na ban lagta hai, na inkaar hota hai, bas saalon tak kuch nahi hota. Information commission ka order aaya aur High Court mein ek legal challenge naakaam hua, tab jaakar sarkar ki apni report un aurton tak pahunchi jinke baare mein woh likhi gayi thi.

## Report mein kya mila: harassment, casting couch aur 'power group'

Committee ne sexual harassment ko industry mein aurton ke saamne "worst evil", yaani sabse badi buraai kaha, aur likha ki ye "goes on unchecked and uncontrolled", yaani bina kisi rok-tok ke chal raha hai. Report ke mutabik industry ke aadmi "make open demands for sex without any qualms as if it's their birthright", yaani bina jhijhak khule-aam sex ki demand karte hain, jaise ye unka janamsiddh haq ho [[bbc-hema-report-2024]].

Committee ne casting couch ki baat confirm ki. Junior artists se kaha jaata tha ki agar woh sex ki demands maanengi toh films mein mauka milega, aur jo aurtein maan jaati thin unhe ek code name se bulaya jaata tha: "cooperating artists" [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

Iske upar baitha tha ek "power group": 10 se 15 aadmi, sab directors, producers aur actors, jo tay karte hain ki industry mein kaun rahega aur jo bade-bade naamon par bhi ban laga sakte hain. Report kehti hai ki jo inhe naraaz kare, woh "will be wiped off the industry", yaani industry se mita diya jaayega. Committee ko bataya gaya ki ek mashhoor actor ne is lobby ko "mafia" kaha tha [[tnm-hema-mafia-bans-2024]]. Ye nateeje gawahiyon par tike hain, report mein naam chhupaye gaye hain, aur hum kisi ka naam nahi lete.

Asli baat system ki hai. Jab kuch log kisi ka career khatam kar sakte hon, toh casting couch ko zabardasti ki zaroorat nahi padti. Na kehne ki keemat agla kaam hota hai.

## Na toilet, na changing room, aur bolne ka darr

Kuch nateeje kaam ki jagah par sabse buniyaadi izzat ke baare mein hain. Malayalam film sets par junior women artists ke liye na toilets the, na changing rooms. Report mein darj hai: "There are no toilets, so women have to go in the bushes or behind thick trees", yaani toilet nahi hain, isliye aurton ko jhaadiyon ya mote pedon ke peeche jaana padta hai. Ghanton tak peshab rokne aur periods mein sanitary napkins na badal paane se aurtein beemar padti thin, kuch ko hospital tak jaana pada [[bbc-hema-report-2024]].

Kai aurtein gawahi dene se hi darti thin, kyunki "they were afraid they would lose their jobs", yaani unhe naukri chhin jaane ka darr tha. Committee ko pehle ye darr ajeeb laga, phir usne maana ki ye darr "well-founded", yaani bilkul jaayaz hai, aur kaha ki use witnesses aur unke kareebi rishtedaaron ki suraksha ki chinta hai [[bbc-hema-report-2024]].

Ek hypothetical case sochiye: ek chhote shehar se aayi junior artist, jo kisi outdoor shoot par hai. Kapde badalne ki koi private jagah nahi hai, aur set par kisi ne use nahi bataya ki complaint kisse kare. Agar koi senior crew member use harass kare, toh jisse woh complaint karegi woh shayad usi ka dost ho, aur uski agli booking dono par tiki ho. Uski chuppi uski haan nahi hai. Woh agle kaam ki keemat hai.

## Film sets bhi workplace hain: POSH Act kya maangta hai

Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi. POSH Act ki "workplace" wali definition mein woh private organisations saaf taur par shaamil hain jo "entertainmental", yaani entertainment ka kaam karti hain [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. 17 March 2022 ko WCC ki petitions par faisla dete hue Kerala High Court ne kaha ki har film ki production unit ek workplace hai, aur agar woh 10 se zyada workers rakhti hai toh usme Internal Complaints Committee honi chahiye. Court ne collective ki poori baat nahi maani: usne kaha ki AMMA jaisi film associations actors ki employer nahi hain, aur unhe committee sirf apne office staff ke liye chahiye. AMMA ne khud ek committee banane ki peshkash ki [[kerala-hc-wcc-judgment-2022]].

Act har us aurat ko protect karta hai jo "of any age whether employed or not", yaani kisi bhi umar ki ho, naukri mein ho ya na ho, aur workplace par harass hui ho [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Phir bhi Kerala High Court ne zubaani taur par kaha hai ki ye Act un aurton tak nahi pahunchta jo abhi sirf kaam dhoondh rahi hain, aur casting couch theek isi stage par chalta hai; job dhoondhne wali aurtein cover hoti hain ya nahi, is par behas hai. 8 October 2025 ko state ne court ko bataya ki entertainment industry ke liye ek draft law November mein cabinet ke saamne jaayega, aur SIT ki jaanch poori ho chuki hai [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-draft-law-2025]]. Woh law ab tak paas hua ya nahi, ye hum confirm nahi kar paaye.

Complaint incident ke teen mahine ke andar likh kar deni hoti hai, jise teen mahine aur badhaya ja sakta hai, aur inquiry 90 din mein poori honi chahiye [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Agar complaint employer ke khilaaf hai, ya workplace mein das se kam workers hain, toh complaint district ki Local Committee mein jaati hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Aurtein sarkar ke SHe-Box portal par bhi complaint kar sakti hain [[shebox]].

Report ko public tak pahunchne mein lagbhag paanch saal lage. Jo law agli junior artist ko bachana chahiye, woh pehle se maujood hai. Asli imtihaan ye hai ki production units us law ko maanti hain ya nahi, isse pehle ki ek aur committee banani pade.

hyderabad-encounter-2019-sirpurkar-commi.en:
In 2019, a young woman was raped and murdered near Hyderabad. Soon after, Telangana police shot dead the four men accused of the crime. No court had heard a single witness. To many people it felt like justice. A commission appointed by the Supreme Court later called it something else: the four, it found, were "deliberately fired upon by the police with an intent to cause their death", and three of them were minors [[livelaw-hyderabad-encounter-commission-2022]]. We do not name the woman who was killed, the four men or the officers involved.

## 2019: four accused, shot dead before any trial

"Encounter" is police language. It suggests a sudden exchange of fire in which officers had no choice. When the shooting is staged, the law has a plainer word for it: murder.

The four men were accused, which means the police suspected them. No court had found them guilty of anything. Before any trial could begin, all four were dead.

On 12 December 2019, the Supreme Court set up a commission to find out what had happened, led by former Supreme Court judge V.S. Sirpurkar, with former Bombay High Court judge Rekha Baldota and former CBI Director D.R. Karthikeyan [[leaflet-hyderabad-encounter-sc-2022]].

## What the Sirpurkar Commission found

The commission found that the police had fired on the four deliberately, intending to kill them, and that the police version of events was concocted. Three of the four dead were minors. It recommended that all ten officers involved be tried for murder [[livelaw-hyderabad-encounter-commission-2022]].

Telangana then asked the Supreme Court to keep the report sealed. On 20 May 2022, a bench of Chief Justice N.V. Ramana and Justice Hima Kohli refused, ordered the report shared with the parties and sent the matter to the Telangana High Court [[leaflet-hyderabad-encounter-sc-2022]]. The state whose police did the shooting had wanted the findings kept from the public.

## Three minors: what the Juvenile Justice Act required

Three of the dead were children in law. India has a separate system for children accused of crimes, and it has no place for a police bullet.

Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, a Juvenile Justice Board must make a "preliminary assessment" of any child aged 16 or above who is accused of a heinous offence, one with a minimum punishment of seven years or more. Only after that can the case go to a Children's Court for trial as an adult [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]. A board, an assessment, a court: even the harshest route the law allows for a child runs through three checks. The police skipped all of them, and the trial too. Our explainer on the ages at which Indian law stops treating you as a child sets out the rest.

Saying this defends no one accused of rape and murder. It is the reason procedures exist: to find out who did what, and to punish within limits a court can check. This is general information, not legal advice.

## No trial, no verdict: what "instant justice" takes from her family

A trial is where evidence is tested, witnesses are questioned and a court says, in public and on the record, who did it. With the four accused dead, no court will ever say who raped and killed her. If they were guilty, they escaped a verdict. If any of them was not, the police killed an innocent person, possibly a child. Either way, the truth was buried with them.

Trials can deliver, even against the police. In the Kathua case, a Pathankot court convicted six of the seven accused it tried in June 2019, including three policemen who had destroyed evidence [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. The RG Kar rape and murder happened on 9 August 2024 [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]; on 20 January 2025 a Sealdah court sentenced the convict and warned that courts must resist "the temptation to bow to public pressure or emotional appeals" [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. NCRB data show that when rape-murder trials do reach a verdict, most end in conviction; the bigger problem is how many are still waiting [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

In 2024 alone, NCRB recorded 266 cases of murder with rape or gang rape [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Every one of those families is owed what this family was denied: a verdict.

## Where the case stands, and how to answer the next call for an encounter

We could not confirm whether any officer has been prosecuted, or what the Telangana High Court has done since 2022. More than four years after the report was made public, its central recommendation, a murder trial for ten officers, has no confirmed outcome.

The next time someone cheers an encounter, three answers help.

First, ask for speed, not shortcuts. The law already sets deadlines: police must finish a rape investigation within two months (Section 193 of the BNSS), the trial should end within two months of the charge sheet (Section 346), and appeals should be decided within six months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Missing these deadlines carries no penalty. Demand the judges, prosecutors and forensic labs that would make them real.

Second, ask what punishment can do. The Verma Committee, set up after the 2012 Delhi gang rape, advised against the death penalty for rape, noting that it "may not have a deterrent effect" [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. A staged encounter is a death sentence carried out with no judge at all. And it did not end rape in Telangana: police there registered 1,148 rape cases in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Third, ask who is next. If police can kill accused people on their own word, they can kill anyone, including the wrong person, and including a child.

Justice for the woman killed near Hyderabad needed a courtroom. Her family never got one.
hyderabad-encounter-2019-sirpurkar-commi.hg:
2019 mein Hyderabad ke paas ek young aurat ka rape hua aur uska murder kar diya gaya. Kuch hi samay baad Telangana police ne is crime ke chaaron accused ko goli maar di. Tab tak kisi court ne ek bhi witness ki baat nahi suni thi. Bahut logon ko laga ki yahi insaaf hai. Lekin Supreme Court ke banaye ek commission ne baad mein ise kuch aur kaha. Commission ne paaya ki chaaron par "deliberately fired upon by the police with an intent to cause their death", yaani police ne unki jaan lene ke iraade se jaanbujhkar goli chalayi, aur inmein se teen minor the [[livelaw-hyderabad-encounter-commission-2022]]. Hum na us aurat ka naam lenge, na un chaar aadmiyon ka, na ismein shaamil officers ka.

## 2019: chaar accused, trial se pehle hi maare gaye

"Encounter" police ki bhasha hai. Isse lagta hai ki achanak firing hui aur officers ke paas koi chaara nahi tha. Agar firing banaawati ho, toh law mein iska seedha naam hai: murder.

Yeh chaaron aadmi accused the, yaani police ko un par shak tha. Kisi court ne unhe kisi baat ka doshi nahi thehraya tha. Trial shuru hone se pehle hi chaaron maare ja chuke the.

12 December 2019 ko Supreme Court ne yeh pata lagane ke liye ek commission banaya ki aakhir hua kya tha. Iski aguwai Supreme Court ke former judge V.S. Sirpurkar ne ki, saath mein Bombay High Court ki former judge Rekha Baldota aur CBI ke former Director D.R. Karthikeyan the [[leaflet-hyderabad-encounter-sc-2022]].

## Sirpurkar Commission ne kya paaya

Commission ne paaya ki police ne chaaron par jaanbujhkar, jaan lene ke iraade se goli chalayi thi, aur police ki batayi kahani gadhi hui thi. Marne wale chaar mein se teen minor the. Commission ne sifaarish ki ki ismein shaamil sabhi das officers par murder ka trial chalaya jaaye [[livelaw-hyderabad-encounter-commission-2022]].

Iske baad Telangana sarkar ne Supreme Court se kaha ki report sealed hi rehne di jaaye. 20 May 2022 ko Chief Justice N.V. Ramana aur Justice Hima Kohli ki bench ne yeh maang thukra di, report sabhi parties ko dene ka order diya, aur maamla Telangana High Court bhej diya [[leaflet-hyderabad-encounter-sc-2022]]. Jis state ki police ne goli chalayi thi, wahi state chahta tha ki findings public tak na pahunchein.

## Teen minors: Juvenile Justice Act kya kehta hai

Marne walon mein se teen law ki nazar mein bachche the. Crime ke accused bachchon ke liye India mein alag system hai, aur usmein police ki goli ki koi jagah nahi hai.

Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 kehta hai ki agar 16 saal ya usse bade kisi bachche par heinous, yaani bahut serious, offence ka aarop ho, toh Juvenile Justice Board ko pehle uska "preliminary assessment" karna hoga. Heinous offence woh hai jiski kam se kam sazaa saat saal ya usse zyada ho. Iske baad hi case Children's Court mein bheja ja sakta hai, jahan us par adult ki tarah trial chal sakta hai [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]. Board, assessment, court: kisi bachche ke liye law ka sabse sakht raasta bhi in teen padaavon se hokar jaata hai. Police ne yeh teeno chhod diye, aur trial bhi. Kis umar mein law aapko bachcha maanna band karta hai, is par hamara explainer baaki baatein samjhata hai.

Yeh kehna rape aur murder ke kisi accused ka bachaav nahi hai. Process isiliye hota hai: taaki pata chale ki kisne kya kiya, aur sazaa un hadon mein di jaaye jinhe court parakh sake. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Na trial, na faisla: "instant justice" uski family se kya chheen leta hai

Trial woh jagah hai jahan saboot parkhe jaate hain, witnesses se sawaal hote hain, aur court sabke saamne, record par batati hai ki crime kisne kiya. Chaaron accused ki maut ke baad koi court kabhi nahi batayegi ki us aurat ka rape aur murder kisne kiya. Agar woh doshi the, toh faisle se bach nikle. Agar unmein se koi begunaah tha, toh police ne ek begunaah ko maar diya, shayad ek bachche ko. Dono hi soorat mein sach unke saath dafan ho gaya.

Trials nateeja de sakte hain, police ke khilaaf bhi. Kathua case mein June 2019 mein Pathankot ki court ne jin saat accused par trial chalaya, unmein se chhe ko doshi thehraya, jinmein teen policewale the jinhone saboot mitaaye the [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. RG Kar rape aur murder 9 August 2024 ko hua [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]; 20 January 2025 ko Sealdah ki court ne convict ko sazaa sunayi aur warning di ki courts ko "the temptation to bow to public pressure or emotional appeals", yaani public pressure ya emotional appeals ke aage jhukne ke laalach, se bachna chahiye [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. NCRB data batata hai ki rape ke saath murder ke jin trials ka faisla aata hai, unmein se zyadatar mein conviction hota hai; badi dikkat yeh hai ki kitne case abhi bhi intezaar mein hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Akele 2024 mein NCRB ne rape ya gang rape ke saath murder ke 266 case darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inmein se har family ko woh milna chahiye jo is family ko nahi mila: ek faisla.

## Case abhi kahan hai, aur agli baar encounter ki maang ka jawaab kaise dein

Hum confirm nahi kar paaye ki kisi officer par trial chala ya nahi, ya 2022 ke baad Telangana High Court ne kya kiya. Report saamne aaye chaar saal se zyada ho gaye, aur uski sabse badi sifaarish, yaani das officers par murder ka trial, ka koi pakka nateeja ab tak saamne nahi hai.

Agli baar koi encounter par taali bajaye, toh yeh teen jawaab kaam aayenge.

Pehla, jaldi insaaf maangiye, shortcut nahi. Law mein deadlines pehle se tay hain: police ko rape ki investigation do mahine mein poori karni hai (BNSS ki Section 193), trial chargesheet ke do mahine mein khatam hona chahiye (Section 346), aur appeal ka faisla chhe mahine mein hona chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh deadlines toot jaayein toh koi penalty nahi hai. Isliye woh judges, public prosecutors aur forensic labs maangiye jinse yeh deadlines sach mein poori ho sakein.

Doosra, poochiye ki sazaa se asal mein kya hota hai. 2012 ke Delhi gang rape ke baad bani Verma Committee ne rape ke liye death penalty ke khilaaf salaah di thi, yeh maante hue ki uska "may not have a deterrent effect", yaani crime rokne wala asar shayad na ho [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Banaawati encounter toh bina kisi judge ke di gayi death penalty hai. Aur isse Telangana mein rape khatam nahi hue: 2024 mein wahan police ne rape ke 1,148 case darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Teesra, poochiye ki agla kaun hoga. Agar police sirf apne kehne par accused ko maar sakti hai, toh woh kisi ko bhi maar sakti hai, galat aadmi ko bhi, aur kisi bachche ko bhi.

Hyderabad ke paas maari gayi aurat ke liye insaaf ka raasta court se hokar jaata tha. Uski family ko woh raasta kabhi nahi mila.

independent-thought-2017-child-brides-ma.en:
Picture two 16-year-old girls in the same district in 2015. If an adult man had sex with the first, unmarried girl, the law called it rape, whatever she said. If the second girl had been married to him, the Indian Penal Code said it was not rape. From 2013 until 2017, India's rape law protected a girl from every man except the one she had been married to. This file follows how that gap opened, and how the Supreme Court closed it in Independent Thought v. Union of India.

## 2013: a new age of consent, with an exception for husbands

After the 2012 Delhi gang rape, Parliament rewrote the rape law. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, which received assent on 2 April 2013, made sexual intercourse with a girl under 18 rape whether or not she consented [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Until then the line had been 16 [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]].

The same Act kept Exception 2 to Section 375: "Sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under fifteen years of age, is not rape" [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. So from 2013 until 2017, a husband's sex with his 15-to-17-year-old wife was not legally rape [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

Parliament had been advised to do the opposite. In January 2013 the Justice Verma Committee recommended deleting the marital rape exception altogether [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament kept it, along with the lower age written into it.

## Two ages of consent in one section

The result was a contradiction inside one section of the law. Section 375 said a girl under 18 could not consent to sex. Its own exception said that once a girl of 15 was married, her refusal did not count.

Child marriage itself was already illegal. Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, a girl under 18 is a child, and an adult man who marries her commits an offence [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Yet the rape law shielded him inside that illegal marriage.

The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, in force since 14 November 2012, pointed the other way. It defines a child as anyone under 18 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], and that definition says nothing about marriage. Two laws gave opposite answers about the same girl. The organisation Independent Thought asked the Supreme Court to resolve the conflict [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

## 11 October 2017: the exception read down to 18

On 11 October 2017, Justices Madan B. Lokur and Deepak Gupta read down the exception so that sexual intercourse by a man with his wife aged between 15 and 18 is rape. The court noted that Parliament had raised the age of consent to 18 in 2013 but left the exception at 15 [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

The judgment applies prospectively, from the date it was delivered. It did not end the marital exception either: it expressly left the question of adult wives undecided [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. When the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the IPC, it wrote the court's line into the text: Exception 2 to Section 63 now covers only a wife "not being under eighteen years of age" [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. For wives of 18 and above, the exception stands. As of 19 November 2026 the Supreme Court had still not ruled on the challenge to it, and a bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant said it would fix the final hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026 [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

For a married girl, the change is concrete. Her husband can be prosecuted for rape, and for sexual offences against a child under POCSO. Marriage no longer erases her age.

## Child marriage in 2026: the numbers and the missing FIRs

The ruling covers a very large group of girls. In provisional NFHS-6 data for 2023-24, 20.1% of women aged 20-24 had been married before 18: 23.3% in rural areas and 11.4% in urban areas [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Few of these marriages ever reach a police file. State figures cited by the Supreme Court in October 2024 show that over three years Telangana reported 4,440 child marriage cases but filed only 149 FIRs, and Andhra Pradesh about 3,400 cases, most of them marriages that were stopped, but 10 FIRs. Tamil Nadu filed 2,392 FIRs on 8,966 cases [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. A marriage stopped in time may not need an FIR. But across India, police registered only 1,499 cases under the child marriage law in 2024, and courts convicted in 209 such cases against 625 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

A household survey and a police register measure different things, so these numbers are not one series. Read together, they show the distance between the 2017 ruling and a girl's life. If her marriage never reaches an official, neither does what happens to her inside it.

## Stopping or ending a child marriage

**Before the wedding.** Call 1098, the Child Helpline [[wcd-childline]], which is linked to the 112 emergency system [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]], or tell the police. The Supreme Court's October 2024 guidelines direct states to appoint district Child Marriage Prohibition Officers with no other duties, and ask magistrates to issue injunctions on their own, especially around "auspicious days" for mass weddings [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. An adult groom, anyone who performs the marriage and anyone who promotes or permits it faces up to two years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

**After the wedding.** A child marriage is not automatically void. It is voidable at the option of the person who was a child, who can petition a district court to annul it until two years after reaching adulthood [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. For a girl, that means before she turns 20. Consider a girl married at 16 who is 19 now and wants out: she still has time, and a lawyer or the District Legal Services Authority can help her file.

Independent Thought closed one gap: no wedding can make sex with a girl under 18 legal. The harder part is making sure she knows it, and that someone answers when she calls.

This is general information, not legal advice.
independent-thought-2017-child-brides-ma.hg:
Imagine kijiye, 2015 mein ek hi district ki do 16 saal ki ladkiyan. Agar kisi adult aadmi ne pehli ladki ke saath, jo unmarried thi, sex kiya, to law ise rape kehta tha, chahe ladki ne kuch bhi kaha ho. Agar doosri ladki ki shaadi usi aadmi se ho chuki thi, to Indian Penal Code kehta tha ki yeh rape nahin hai. 2013 se 2017 tak India ka rape law ladki ko har aadmi se bachata tha, sivaay us aadmi ke jisse uski shaadi kar di gayi thi. Yeh file batati hai ki yeh gap kaise bana, aur Supreme Court ne Independent Thought v. Union of India case mein ise kaise band kiya.

## 2013: consent ki nayi umar, lekin pati ke liye exception

2012 ke Delhi gang rape ke baad Parliament ne rape law dobara likha. Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, jise 2 April 2013 ko manzoori mili, ne 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke saath sexual intercourse ko rape bana diya, chahe usne consent diya ho ya nahin [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Tab tak yeh line 16 saal par thi [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]].

Lekin isi Act ne Section 375 ka Exception 2 bana rehne diya: "Sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under fifteen years of age, is not rape", yaani agar patni 15 saal ya usse badi hai, to pati ka uske saath sex rape nahin hai [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Isliye 2013 se 2017 tak pati ka apni 15 se 17 saal ki patni ke saath sex law ki nazar mein rape nahin tha [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

Parliament ko iska ulta karne ki salah mili thi. January 2013 mein Justice Verma Committee ne marital rape exception ko poori tarah hata dene ki sifaarish ki thi [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament ne exception rakha, aur usmein likhi kam umar bhi.

## Ek hi section mein consent ki do umrein

Nateeja yeh hua ki law ke ek hi section ke andar contradiction tha. Section 375 kehta tha ki 18 se kam umar ki ladki sex ke liye consent nahin de sakti. Uska apna exception kehta tha ki 15 saal ki ladki ki shaadi ho gayi, to uske mana karne ka koi matlab nahin.

Child marriage khud pehle se gair-kaanooni thi. Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 ke hisaab se 18 se kam umar ki ladki child hai, aur jo adult aadmi usse shaadi karta hai, woh offence karta hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Phir bhi rape law us gair-kaanooni shaadi ke andar use bachata tha.

Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, jo 14 November 2012 se laagu hai, ulti disha mein khada tha. Woh 18 se kam umar ke har insaan ko child maanta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], aur yeh definition shaadi ke baare mein kuch nahin kehti. Ek hi ladki ke baare mein do laws ulte jawab dete the. Independent Thought naam ke organisation ne Supreme Court se yeh takraav suljhaane ko kaha [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

## 11 October 2017: exception 18 tak padha gaya

11 October 2017 ko Justices Madan B. Lokur aur Deepak Gupta ne exception ko "read down" kiya, yaani uska matlab chhota kar diya, taaki 15 se 18 saal ki patni ke saath pati ka sexual intercourse rape maana jaye. Court ne note kiya ki Parliament ne 2013 mein consent ki umar 18 kar di thi, lekin exception 15 par hi chhod diya tha [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

Yeh faisla prospective hai, yaani faisle ki tareekh se aage laagu hota hai. Isne marital exception bhi khatam nahin kiya: isne adult patniyon ka sawaal saaf taur par khula chhod diya [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. Jab Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ne IPC ki jagah li, to usne court ki line text mein likh di: Section 63 ka Exception 2 ab sirf us patni par laagu hota hai jo "not being under eighteen years of age", yaani 18 se kam umar ki nahin hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 18 aur usse badi umar ki patniyon ke liye exception ab bhi bana hua hai. 19 November 2026 tak Supreme Court ne iske khilaaf challenge par faisla nahin diya tha, aur Chief Justice Surya Kant ki aguwai wali bench ne kaha ki woh final hearing 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko rakhegi [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

Ek shaadishuda ladki ke liye iska matlab saaf hai. Uske pati par rape ka case chal sakta hai, aur POCSO ke tahat child ke khilaaf sexual offences ka bhi. Shaadi ab uski umar nahin mitaati.

## 2026 mein child marriage: numbers aur gayab FIRs

Yeh faisla ladkiyon ke ek bahut bade group par laagu hota hai. 2023-24 ke provisional NFHS-6 data mein 20-24 saal ki 20.1% aurton ki shaadi 18 se pehle ho chuki thi: gaon mein 23.3% aur shehron mein 11.4% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Inmein se kam hi shaadiyan kabhi police file tak pahunchti hain. Supreme Court ne October 2024 mein jo state figures bataye, unke hisaab se teen saal mein Telangana ne 4,440 child marriage cases report kiye lekin sirf 149 FIRs darj hui. Andhra Pradesh mein lagbhag 3,400 cases the, jinmein zyada tar shaadiyan rok di gayi thi, lekin FIRs sirf 10 hui. Tamil Nadu ne 8,966 cases par 2,392 FIRs darj ki [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Waqt par roki gayi shaadi mein shayad FIR ki zaroorat na pade. Lekin poore India mein 2024 mein police ne child marriage law ke tahat sirf 1,499 cases darj kiye, aur courts ne aise 209 cases mein conviction diya, jabki 625 mein acquittal hua [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Household survey aur police register alag-alag cheezein naapte hain, isliye yeh numbers ek series nahin hain. Lekin saath padhne par yeh 2017 ke faisle aur ek ladki ki asli zindagi ke beech ki doori dikhate hain. Agar uski shaadi kabhi kisi official tak nahin pahunchti, to us shaadi ke andar uske saath jo hota hai, woh bhi nahin pahunchta.

## Child marriage rokna ya khatam karna

**Shaadi se pehle.** 1098 par call kijiye, jo Child Helpline hai [[wcd-childline]] aur 112 emergency system se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]], ya police ko bataiye. Supreme Court ki October 2024 ki guidelines states se kehti hain ki har district mein aise Child Marriage Prohibition Officers appoint karein jinke paas koi aur kaam na ho, aur magistrates se kehti hain ki woh khud aage badhkar injunctions jaari karein, khaas kar mass weddings wale "auspicious days", yaani shubh dinon ke aas-paas [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Adult dulhe, shaadi karwane wale aur use badhawa dene ya ijaazat dene wale, sabko do saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment aur 1 lakh rupaye tak ka fine ho sakta hai [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

**Shaadi ke baad.** Child marriage apne aap void, yaani shuru se hi radd, nahin hoti. Woh voidable hai: jo shaadi ke waqt child tha, woh chahe to use radd karwa sakta hai, aur iske liye adult hone ke do saal ke andar district court mein petition daal sakta hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Ladki ke liye iska matlab hai 20 saal ki hone se pehle. Sochiye, 16 saal mein byaahi gayi ek ladki ab 19 ki hai aur is shaadi se bahar nikalna chahti hai: uske paas abhi samay hai, aur koi lawyer ya District Legal Services Authority petition daalne mein uski madad kar sakte hain.

Independent Thought ne ek gap band kiya: koi bhi shaadi 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke saath sex ko legal nahin bana sakti. Mushkil kaam yeh pakka karna hai ki ladki yeh jaane, aur jab woh call kare, to koi jawab de.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahin.

india-2026-cases-rulings-campaigns-timel.en:
India's year on sexual violence and sexual health did not turn on one law. It turned on dozens of smaller moves: a notice to a platform, a rule with a two-hour clock, Supreme Court orders on toilets and on late abortions, and a fast trial in one child's case. Most of the change came from courts and ministries, not Parliament, and much of it is still waiting for governments to act. Here is 2026, month by month. Survivors are not named; accused people are named only where a court has convicted them.

## January

- **2 January:** The IT ministry gave X 72 hours to report what it had done about its Grok AI tool producing sexualised images of women and children [[businesstoday-meity-grok-notice-2026]].
- **9 January:** Two Supreme Court judges asked the Centre to consider a "Romeo-Juliet clause" shielding genuine adolescent relationships from POCSO. It was a suggestion, not a ruling [[scroll-romeo-juliet-sc-2026]].
- **30 January:** In *Dr Jaya Thakur v. Government of India*, the Supreme Court held menstrual health part of the right to life and ordered every school to provide working girls' toilets with water, free sanitary napkins and safe disposal [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]].

## February

- **5 February:** The UN CEDAW Committee asked India what it had done to criminalise marital rape under the BNS [[cedaw-india-loipr-2026]].
- **6 February:** The Supreme Court allowed a young woman who had conceived as a minor to end a 30-week pregnancy, overruling a High Court that had pointed to adoption [[livelaw-sc-mother-of-x-2026]].
- **10 February:** The IT Amendment Rules, 2026 were notified. From 20 February, platforms must remove nude or morphed images within two hours of a complaint [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. The same day the Supreme Court asked a judicial academy committee to draft guidelines on sensitivity in sexual-offence cases, saying past efforts "have not borne the fruit that was expected" [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].
- **28 February:** A free national HPV vaccination campaign began at Ajmer, offering one dose to girls aged 14 [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]].

## March

- **6 March:** Karnataka announced a social media ban for children under 16 in its budget. No law followed [[techcrunch-karnataka-social-media-ban-2026]].
- **13 March:** The Supreme Court declined to order nationwide menstrual leave, warning a mandate could make employers reluctant to hire women [[businesstoday-sc-menstrual-leave-2026]].
- **13-30 March:** Parliament passed the Transgender Persons Amendment Bill within 12 days of its introduction, and it received assent on 30 March [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]] [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

## April

- **7 April:** A nine-judge bench began hearing the Sabarimala reference, which will shape the case against female genital cutting in the Dawoodi Bohra community [[scobserver-sabarimala-reference-2026]]. Judgment was reserved on 14 May [[scobserver-sabarimala-day16-2026]].
- **24-30 April:** The Supreme Court let a 15-year-old rape survivor end a pregnancy of about 30 weeks [[tribune-sc-aiims-curative-2026]], refused AIIMS's challenge, and the Chief Justice orally asked the government to remove the time limit for minor rape survivors [[thewire-sc-amend-mtp-minors-2026]].

## May

- **4 May:** The Chief Justice said the 2013 acid-attack provisions had had "no deterrent effect" [[livelaw-acid-harsher-punishment-2026]].
- **6 May:** NCRB released *Crime in India 2024*, still the latest edition [[theprint-ncrb-cii-2024-release-2026]].
- **15 May:** The Supreme Court set aside the Delhi High Court order suspending the life sentence of former MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar, and sent the matter back [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]]. A Delhi trial court convicted and sentenced him in December 2019 for the 2017 Unnao rape [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]; his appeal against the conviction is pending in the Delhi High Court.
- **23 May:** Police arrested two men in the 2026 Sulur case near Coimbatore, involving the sexual assault and killing of a 10-year-old [[ians-sulur-chargesheet-2026]].

## June

- **NFHS-6:** The new survey put spousal violence at 22.3% of ever-married women, down from 29.2% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Experts quoted in June doubted the fall, saying women may not disclose abuse with family members present [[deccanherald-nfhs6-gbv-2026]].
- **Madras High Court:** It observed that Tamil Nadu had seen 59 honour killings in ten years [[livelaw-madras-hc-honour-killings-2026]].
