- **10 June:** An 819-page chargesheet was filed in the Sulur case, less than three weeks after the arrests [[ians-sulur-chargesheet-2026]].

## July

- **Sex education:** The Centre told the Supreme Court it had accepted a 26-member committee's plan for comprehensive sex education in schools, pending the court's approval [[fpj-sex-education-centre-sc-2026]].
- **Money:** Rs 1,287.83 crore of the Nirbhaya Fund remained unused, and the 2025-26 allocation was the lowest ever [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. 985 One Stop Centres were working [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

## August

- **11 August:** A CDSCO expert panel backed generic lenacapavir, a twice-yearly HIV prevention injection, without new local trials [[theprint-lenacapavir-cdsco-2026]].
- **17 August:** Hearing challenges to the transgender amendment, the Supreme Court was told existing identity cards remain valid [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

## September

- **1 September:** The Supreme Court said it was discontented with states' compliance on school menstrual hygiene [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]].
- **9 September:** A three-judge bench posted the marital rape cases for final hearing [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].
- **11 September:** More than 80 lakh HPV doses had been given [[pib-hpv-80-lakh-doses-2026]].
- **28 September:** The Centre told the Chief Justice's bench it would bar under-18s from opening social media accounts [[medianama-sc-social-media-minors-2026]].

## October

- **15 October:** A Supreme Court bench held internet access a fundamental right of children too, rejected blanket bans and ordered a national database to remove child sexual abuse material [[barandbench-sc-internet-right-children-2026]]. In an order reported the same day, the court gave states "one last opportunity" on menstrual hygiene in schools [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-contempt-oct-2026]].
- **24 October:** The Delhi High Court let a 17-year-old rape survivor end a pregnancy of over 29 weeks, saying the 24-week limit alone could not decide the question [[tribune-delhi-hc-29-weeks-2026]].
- **27 October:** The Supreme Court said the Centre's acid-sale rules had "miserably failed" [[livelaw-acid-policy-failure-2026]].

## November

- **4 November:** The Cabinet extended the fast-track court scheme to March 2031, with up to 850 courts. 779 were functioning, 399 of them only for POCSO [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]].
- **Coming up:** the Sulur verdict on 27 November [[thenewsmill-sulur-verdict-deferred-2026]], and the marital rape final hearing on 9 or 10 December [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

> The pattern of 2026: courts said what dignity requires, and then waited for governments to deliver it.

## What 2026 leaves unfinished

The marital rape exception still stands. The MTP Act still stops at 24 weeks for survivors. The Romeo-Juliet clause, the sex-education plan and the under-18 account bar exist only as suggestions and promises. The year's clearest gains are the ones a reader can use today: a two-hour takedown rule, a free HPV vaccine, and court orders that give schools no excuse.
india-2026-cases-rulings-campaigns-timel.hg:
Sexual violence aur sexual health par India ka yeh saal kisi ek law par nahi ghooma. Yeh darjanon chhote kadmon par ghooma: ek platform ko notice, do ghante ki ghadi wala ek rule, toilets aur late abortions par Supreme Court ke orders, aur ek bachchi ke case mein tez trial. Zyadatar badlaav Parliament se nahi, courts aur ministries se aaya, aur uska bada hissa ab bhi sarkaron ke kadam ka intezaar kar raha hai. Yeh raha 2026, mahine-dar-mahine. Survivors ke naam nahi diye gaye; accused ka naam sirf wahin hai jahan court ne doshi thehraaya.

## January

- **2 January:** IT ministry ne X ko 72 ghante diye yeh batane ke liye ki uske Grok AI tool se aurton aur bachchon ki sexualised images banne par usne kya kiya [[businesstoday-meity-grok-notice-2026]].
- **9 January:** Supreme Court ke do judges ne Centre se POCSO mein "Romeo-Juliet clause" par sochne ko kaha, jo teenagers ke sachche rishton ko bachaye. Yeh sujhaav tha, faisla nahi [[scroll-romeo-juliet-sc-2026]].
- **30 January:** *Dr Jaya Thakur v. Government of India* mein Supreme Court ne menstrual health ko right to life ka hissa maana aur har school ko paani wale chalte hue girls' toilets, free sanitary napkins aur safe disposal dene ka order diya [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]].

## February

- **5 February:** UN CEDAW Committee ne India se poocha ki BNS ke tahat marital rape ko crime banane ke liye usne kya kiya [[cedaw-india-loipr-2026]].
- **6 February:** Supreme Court ne ek young woman ko, jo minor rehte pregnant hui thi, 30 hafte ki pregnancy khatam karne di, aur High Court ka adoption wala raasta palat diya [[livelaw-sc-mother-of-x-2026]].
- **10 February:** IT Amendment Rules, 2026 notify hue. 20 February se platforms ko complaint ke do ghante mein nude ya morphed images hataani hoti hain [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Usi din Supreme Court ne ek judicial academy committee se sexual-offence cases mein sanvedansheelta par guidelines banwaane ko kaha, yeh kehte hue ki pichhli koshishon ka "woh phal nahi mila jiski ummeed thi" [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].
- **28 February:** Ajmer se free national HPV vaccination campaign shuru hua, 14 saal ki ladkiyon ke liye ek dose [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]].

## March

- **6 March:** Karnataka ne budget mein 16 se kam umr ke bachchon ke liye social media ban ka elaan kiya. Koi law nahi aaya [[techcrunch-karnataka-social-media-ban-2026]].
- **13 March:** Supreme Court ne desh bhar mein menstrual leave ka order dene se mana kiya, yeh chetaavni dete hue ki mandate se employers aurton ko naukri dene se katra sakte hain [[businesstoday-sc-menstrual-leave-2026]].
- **13-30 March:** Parliament ne Transgender Persons Amendment Bill pesh hone ke 12 din ke andar pass kar diya, aur 30 March ko ise assent mila [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]] [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

## April

- **7 April:** Nau judges ki bench ne Sabarimala reference ki sunwaai shuru ki, jo Dawoodi Bohra community mein female genital cutting ke khilaaf case ko shape karega [[scobserver-sabarimala-reference-2026]]. 14 May ko faisla surakshit rakha gaya [[scobserver-sabarimala-day16-2026]].
- **24-30 April:** Supreme Court ne ek 15 saal ki rape survivor ko lagbhag 30 hafte ki pregnancy khatam karne di [[tribune-sc-aiims-curative-2026]], AIIMS ki chunauti thukraayi, aur Chief Justice ne zubaani taur par sarkar se minor rape survivors ke liye time limit hataane ko kaha [[thewire-sc-amend-mtp-minors-2026]].

## May

- **4 May:** Chief Justice ne kaha ki 2013 ke acid-attack provisions ka "koi deterrent asar nahi" hua [[livelaw-acid-harsher-punishment-2026]].
- **6 May:** NCRB ne *Crime in India 2024* jaari kiya, jo ab bhi latest edition hai [[theprint-ncrb-cii-2024-release-2026]].
- **15 May:** Supreme Court ne former MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar ki umrqaid rokne wala Delhi High Court ka order radd kiya aur maamla waapas bheja [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]]. Delhi ki ek trial court ne December 2019 mein use 2017 ke Unnao rape ke liye convict karke saza di thi [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]; conviction ke khilaaf uski appeal Delhi High Court mein pending hai.
- **23 May:** Coimbatore ke paas 2026 ke Sulur case mein, jismein ek 10 saal ki bachchi ka sexual assault aur hatya hui, police ne do aadmiyon ko giraftaar kiya [[ians-sulur-chargesheet-2026]].

## June

- **NFHS-6:** Naye survey ne spousal violence ko 22.3% ever-married women par bataya, jo pehle 29.2% tha [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. June mein quote kiye gaye experts ne is giraawat par shak jataaya, kehte hue ki family ke saamne aurtein abuse nahi bataatin [[deccanherald-nfhs6-gbv-2026]].
- **Madras High Court:** Court ne kaha ki Tamil Nadu mein das saal mein 59 honour killings hui [[livelaw-madras-hc-honour-killings-2026]].
- **10 June:** Sulur case mein arrests ke teen hafte se kam mein 819 pages ki chargesheet file hui [[ians-sulur-chargesheet-2026]].

## July

- **Sex education:** Centre ne Supreme Court ko bataya ki usne schools mein comprehensive sex education ke liye 26 members ki committee ka plan maan liya hai, court ki approval ke baad laagu hoga [[fpj-sex-education-centre-sc-2026]].
- **Paisa:** Nirbhaya Fund ke Rs 1,287.83 crore ab bhi kharch nahi hue the, aur 2025-26 ka allocation ab tak ka sabse kam tha [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. 985 One Stop Centres chal rahe the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

## August

- **11 August:** CDSCO ke expert panel ne bina naye local trials ke generic lenacapavir, saal mein do baar lagne wale HIV prevention injection, ka samarthan kiya [[theprint-lenacapavir-cdsco-2026]].
- **17 August:** Transgender amendment ke khilaaf challenges ki sunwaai mein Supreme Court ko bataya gaya ki purane identity cards maanya rahenge [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

## September

- **1 September:** Supreme Court ne school menstrual hygiene par states ke paalan se naaraazgi jataayi [[sc-jaya-thakur-order-sept-2026]].
- **9 September:** Teen judges ki bench ne marital rape cases ko final hearing ke liye list kiya [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].
- **11 September:** 80 lakh se zyada HPV doses lag chuki thi [[pib-hpv-80-lakh-doses-2026]].
- **28 September:** Centre ne Chief Justice ki bench ko bataya ki woh 18 se kam umr walon ko social media account kholne se rokega [[medianama-sc-social-media-minors-2026]].

## October

- **15 October:** Supreme Court ki ek bench ne internet access ko bachchon ka bhi fundamental right maana, blanket ban thukraaye, aur child sexual abuse material hataane ke liye national database ka order diya [[barandbench-sc-internet-right-children-2026]]. Usi din report hue ek order mein court ne school menstrual hygiene par states ko "aakhri mauka" diya [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-contempt-oct-2026]].
- **24 October:** Delhi High Court ne ek 17 saal ki rape survivor ko 29 hafte se zyada ki pregnancy khatam karne di, yeh kehte hue ki sirf 24 hafte ki limit se yeh sawaal tay nahi ho sakta [[tribune-delhi-hc-29-weeks-2026]].
- **27 October:** Supreme Court ne kaha ki Centre ke acid-sale rules "buri tarah fail" hue hain [[livelaw-acid-policy-failure-2026]].

## November

- **4 November:** Cabinet ne fast-track court scheme March 2031 tak badha di, 850 courts tak ke provision ke saath. 779 chal rahe the, jinmein 399 sirf POCSO ke liye [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]].
- **Aage:** 27 November ko Sulur verdict [[thenewsmill-sulur-verdict-deferred-2026]], aur 9 ya 10 December ko marital rape ki final hearing [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

> 2026 ka pattern: courts ne bataya ki dignity kya maangti hai, aur phir sarkaron ke use poora karne ka intezaar kiya.

## 2026 kya adhoora chhod raha hai

Marital rape exception ab bhi khada hai. MTP Act survivors ke liye ab bhi 24 hafte par rukta hai. Romeo-Juliet clause, sex-education plan aur under-18 account rok sirf sujhaav aur vaade hain. Saal ki sabse saaf kamaai woh hai jo reader aaj istemaal kar sakta hai: do ghante ka takedown rule, free HPV vaccine, aur court ke orders jo schools ke paas koi bahaana nahi chhodte.

indian-rape-law-timeline-1860-2024.en:
India's rape law has rarely changed because someone read the data. Its two biggest rewrites came after cases the country could not ignore. A 1978 Supreme Court acquittal produced the 1983 amendment. The 2012 Delhi gang rape produced the 2013 rewrite. Then, on 1 July 2024, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced the Indian Penal Code of 1860 [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]]. Here is the timeline: what each change fixed, and what it left open. This is general information, not legal advice.

## 1860 to 1983: the old law and a custodial rape acquittal

The IPC's rape section, Section 375, described a crime committed by a man against a woman, as Section 63 of the BNS still does [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Before 2013 it covered only penile-vaginal intercourse [[prs-cla-bill-2013-as-passed-ls]], set the age of consent at 16 [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]] and exempted husbands [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

On 15 September 1978, three Supreme Court judges acquitted two policemen accused of raping a minor girl inside a police station in Maharashtra. Noting that she had no injuries, they called the intercourse "a peaceful affair" [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].

Protests over the judgment produced the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983, in force from 25 December 1983. It made custodial rape a separate, aggravated offence, told courts in custodial rape trials to presume no consent when the woman said she had not consented, moved rape trials in camera and made it a crime to disclose a survivor's identity [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. What it left open: it did not widen what counted as rape, and it kept the exception for husbands.

## 2013: the Delhi case rewrites the definition

After the 2012 Delhi gang rape, the government set up a committee under Justice J.S. Verma, which reported on 23 January 2013 [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, deemed in force from 3 February 2013, then rewrote Section 375 [[indiacode-cla-2013]]:

- Rape came to cover penetration of the mouth, urethra or anus, and the insertion of objects [[indiacode-cla-2013]].
- The age of consent rose from 16 to 18 [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]].
- Gang rape got a 20-year minimum, and stalking, voyeurism and acid attack became crimes of their own [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

What it left open: the Verma Committee had recommended deleting the marital rape exception [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament kept it, and kept it at 15 even as the age of consent rose to 18. For more than four years, a husband's sex with his 15-to-17-year-old wife was not rape in law, until the Supreme Court read the exception up to 18 on 11 October 2017, in the Independent Thought case [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

## 2018-2019: death for child rape

The next burst came by ordinance on 21 April 2018. Three days earlier, the Delhi High Court had ordered 12 media houses to pay Rs 10 lakh each for identifying the eight-year-old girl raped and murdered in Kathua, 35 years after the 1983 law made that a crime [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]]. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, which replaced the ordinance, raised the minimum sentence for rape from 7 to 10 years, set a 20-year minimum for raping a girl under 16, allowed death for raping a girl under 12 and ordered rape investigations finished within two months [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. In August 2019 POCSO followed: aggravated penetrative sexual assault on a child can now bring death, and the minimum for penetrative sexual assault rose from 7 to 10 years [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

What it left open: the Verma Committee had warned that the death penalty "may not have a deterrent effect" [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Harsher punishments have not made convictions more common: courts convicted in about 24% of the rape trials they completed in 2012 [[ncrb-cii-2012-figures-at-a-glance]], and in 24.4% in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## 1 July 2024: what the BNS moved, and what it kept

Crimes committed before 1 July 2024 are still prosecuted under the IPC, which is why NCRB's 2024 rape count is split: 19,683 cases under the IPC and 9,853 under the BNS [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Most protections won since 1978 survived under new numbers in the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]], the procedure code BNSS [[indiacode-bnss-2023]] and the evidence law BSA [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]:

| Protection | Since | Old section | New section |
|---|---|---|---|
| A survivor's identity may not be published | 1983 | 228A IPC | 72 BNS |
| Rape trials are held in camera | 1983 | 327(2) CrPC | 366 BNSS |
| Court presumes no consent in custodial and other aggravated rape | 1983, rewritten 2013 | 114A Evidence Act | 120 BSA |
| Not resisting is not consent | 2013 | 375 IPC | 63 BNS |
| Sexual history is irrelevant to consent | 2013 | 53A Evidence Act | 48 BSA |

The changes were few. Section 69 created an offence of sex by deceit or a false promise of marriage, and police registered 1,325 cases under it in the last six months of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Section 70 now allows death for the gang rape of any girl under 18, where the 2018 law had allowed it only for girls under 12 [[indiacode-bns-2023]] [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. And Exception 2 to Section 63 stayed: a man's sex with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## The gaps still open: husbands, men and transgender survivors

**Husbands.** The BNS kept the exception in 2023, a decade after the Verma Committee asked for it to go. The challenge is now before the Supreme Court, which said it would fix the final hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026 [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

**Men and transgender people.** The BNS has no counterpart to Section 377, so forced penetrative sex against an adult man or a transgender person is not rape under the new code, and no specific offence replaced it [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In November 2023 Parliament's own Standing Committee warned that dropping Section 377 would leave such offences against men and transgender persons unpunished; the government did not take its advice [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. Even the count vanished: police registered 888 cases under Section 377 in 2023, and in 2024 the category was gone from NCRB's tables [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sexual abuse of a transgender person carries 6 months to 2 years in prison [[indiacode-transgender-persons-2019]]. Below 18, POCSO protects every child of any gender [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]; the gap opens on the 18th birthday.

The biggest changes on this timeline followed cases the country could not ignore. The gaps that remain belong to survivors whose cases rarely make the front page. Their law should not have to wait for one.
indian-rape-law-timeline-1860-2024.hg:
India ka rape law shayad hi kabhi isliye badla ho ki kisi ne data padha. Iske do sabse bade rewrite aise cases ke baad aaye jinhe desh ignore nahi kar saka. 1978 mein Supreme Court ke ek acquittal se 1983 ka amendment aaya. 2012 ke Delhi gang rape se 2013 ka rewrite aaya. Phir 1 July 2024 ko Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne 1860 ke Indian Penal Code ki jagah le li [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]]. Yeh rahi poori timeline: har badlav ne kya theek kiya, aur kya adhoora chhod diya. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 1860 se 1983: purana law aur custody mein rape ka ek acquittal

IPC ka rape section, Section 375, ek aisa crime batata tha jo ek aadmi ek aurat ke khilaaf karta hai, aur BNS ka Section 63 aaj bhi yahi kehta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 2013 se pehle yeh sirf penile-vaginal intercourse ko cover karta tha [[prs-cla-bill-2013-as-passed-ls]], age of consent 16 saal rakhta tha [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]] aur patiyon ko chhoot deta tha [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

15 September 1978 ko Supreme Court ke teen judges ne do policewalon ko bari kar diya. Un par Maharashtra ke ek police station ke andar ek minor ladki ke rape ka aarop tha. Judges ne note kiya ki ladki ko koi chot nahi thi, aur us intercourse ko "a peaceful affair", yaani shaanti se hua maamla, kaha [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].

Is faisle ke khilaaf protests se Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983 aaya, jo 25 December 1983 se laagu hua. Isne custody mein rape ko ek alag, aggravated offence banaya. Custody wale rape trials mein courts se kaha ki agar aurat kahe ki usne consent nahi diya, toh maana jaaye ki consent nahi tha. Rape trials band kamre mein, yaani in camera, hone lage, aur survivor ki pehchaan bataana crime ban gaya [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Kya adhoora raha: isne rape ki definition ko chauda nahi kiya, aur patiyon wali chhoot bani rahi.

## 2013: Delhi case ne definition dobara likhi

2012 ke Delhi gang rape ke baad sarkar ne Justice J.S. Verma ki ek committee banayi, jisne 23 January 2013 ko apni report di [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Phir Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ne, jo 3 February 2013 se laagu maana gaya, Section 375 ko dobara likha [[indiacode-cla-2013]]:

- Rape mein ab mouth, urethra ya anus mein penetration, aur kisi object ko andar daalna bhi shaamil hua [[indiacode-cla-2013]].
- Age of consent 16 se badhkar 18 saal ho gayi [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]].
- Gang rape ke liye kam se kam 20 saal ki saza tay hui, aur stalking, voyeurism aur acid attack apne aap mein alag crimes bane [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

Kya adhoora raha: Verma Committee ne marital rape exception hataane ki sifarish ki thi [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament ne use rakha, aur age of consent 18 karte hue bhi exception ko 15 saal par hi chhod diya. Chaar saal se zyada tak, 15 se 17 saal ki patni ke saath pati ka sex law mein rape nahi tha. Phir 11 October 2017 ko Independent Thought case mein Supreme Court ne exception ko read down karke 18 saal kar diya [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

## 2018-2019: bachchon ke rape par maut ki saza

Agla jhatka 21 April 2018 ko ek ordinance ke zariye aaya. Usse teen din pehle Delhi High Court ne un 12 media houses ko Rs 10 lakh har ek dene ka hukm diya tha jinhone Kathua mein rape aur murder ki shikaar aath saal ki bachchi ki pehchaan zaahir kar di thi, jabki 1983 ke law ne 35 saal pehle hi ise crime bana diya tha [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]]. Ordinance ki jagah aaye Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 ne rape ki minimum saza 7 se badhakar 10 saal kar di, 16 se kam umar ki ladki ke rape par minimum 20 saal tay kiye, 12 se kam umar ki ladki ke rape par maut ki saza ka raasta khola, aur rape ki investigation do mahine mein poori karne ka hukm diya [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. August 2019 mein POCSO bhi badla: bachche par aggravated penetrative sexual assault ke liye ab maut ki saza ho sakti hai, aur penetrative sexual assault ki minimum saza 7 se 10 saal ho gayi [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Kya adhoora raha: Verma Committee ne chetaya tha ki maut ki saza "may not have a deterrent effect", yaani shayad isse logon mein darr paida na ho [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Kadi saza se conviction zyada nahi hue: 2012 mein courts ne jitne rape trials poore kiye, unme se lagbhag 24% mein conviction hua [[ncrb-cii-2012-figures-at-a-glance]], aur 2024 mein 24.4% mein [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## 1 July 2024: BNS ne kya shift kiya, aur kya rakha

1 July 2024 se pehle hue crimes ka case abhi bhi IPC ke under chalta hai, isiliye NCRB ka 2024 ka rape count do hisson mein bata hai: 19,683 cases IPC ke under aur 9,853 BNS ke under [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 1978 ke baad jeeti gayi zyada tar protections naye numbers ke saath bachi rahin: BNS mein [[indiacode-bns-2023]], procedure code BNSS mein [[indiacode-bnss-2023]] aur evidence law BSA mein [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]:

| Protection | Kab se | Purana section | Naya section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Survivor ki pehchaan chhaapi nahi ja sakti | 1983 | 228A IPC | 72 BNS |
| Rape trials band kamre mein hote hain | 1983 | 327(2) CrPC | 366 BNSS |
| Custody aur doosre aggravated rape mein court maanta hai ki consent nahi tha | 1983, 2013 mein dobara likha gaya | 114A Evidence Act | 120 BSA |
| Resist na karna consent nahi hai | 2013 | 375 IPC | 63 BNS |
| Sexual history ka consent se koi lena-dena nahi | 2013 | 53A Evidence Act | 48 BSA |

Badlav kam the. Section 69 ne dhokhe se, ya shaadi ke jhoothe vaade se, sex ka ek naya offence banaya, aur 2024 ke aakhri chhah mahino mein police ne iske under 1,325 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Section 70 ab 18 se kam umar ki kisi bhi ladki ke gang rape par maut ki saza ki ijaazat deta hai, jabki 2018 ka law yeh sirf 12 se kam umar ki ladkiyon ke liye deta tha [[indiacode-bns-2023]] [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. Aur Section 63 ka Exception 2 bana raha: apni patni ke saath pati ka sex, agar patni 18 ya usse zyada umar ki hai, rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Jo gaps abhi bhi khule hain: pati, aadmi aur transgender survivors

**Pati.** BNS ne 2023 mein bhi yeh exception rakha, Verma Committee ke ise hataane ko kehne ke ek dashak baad. Challenge ab Supreme Court mein hai, jisne kaha hai ki woh final hearing 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko rakhega [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

**Aadmi aur transgender log.** BNS mein Section 377 jaisa koi section nahi hai, isliye kisi adult aadmi ya transgender insaan ke saath zabardasti penetrative sex naye code mein rape nahi hai, aur uski jagah koi khaas offence nahi laaya gaya [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. November 2023 mein Parliament ki apni Standing Committee ne chetaya tha ki Section 377 hataane se aadmiyon aur transgender logon ke khilaaf aise offences bina saza ke reh jaayenge, lekin sarkar ne uski salah nahi maani [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. Ginti bhi gayab ho gayi: 2023 mein police ne Section 377 ke under 888 cases darj kiye the, aur 2024 mein NCRB ki tables se yeh category hi hat gayi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Transgender insaan ke sexual abuse ki saza 6 mahine se 2 saal ki jail hai [[indiacode-transgender-persons-2019]]. 18 saal se kam umar tak POCSO har bachche ko protect karta hai, chahe uska gender kuch bhi ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]; gap 18th birthday par khulta hai.

Is timeline ke sabse bade badlav aise cases ke baad aaye jinhe desh ignore nahi kar saka. Jo gaps bache hain, woh un survivors ke hain jinke cases shayad hi kabhi front page tak pahunchte hain. Unke law ko kisi aise case ka intezaar nahi karna chahiye.

just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024-c.en:
The case began as one tip among millions. A report to the US-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) was routed through India's National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) to police in Tamil Nadu [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]]. On 23 September 2024 it produced a Supreme Court judgment, Just Rights for Children Alliance (2024 INSC 716), that changed what Indian law treats as possession of child sexual abuse material, and what courts may call it [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. The ruling revived a prosecution; it convicted no one, so we do not name the accused. This is general information, not legal advice.

## January 2024: the Madras High Court ruling

On 11 January 2024 the Madras High Court quashed the criminal proceedings [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. It treated privately viewing or storing such material, without sharing it, as no crime [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]].

The logic sounds tidy: if nobody else saw it, nobody was harmed. It fails at the first step. A child was abused to make the material, and every copy, view and forward keeps that abuse in circulation. Just Rights for Children Alliance appealed.

## September 2024: possession, viewing and 'constructive possession'

The Supreme Court set the High Court's judgment aside as an "egregious error" and restored the case [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Three holdings matter most.

**Storing is enough.** Storing or possessing such material is itself an offence under Section 15 of the POCSO Act when the circumstances show the intent the law specifies, even if it is never shared [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. The section covers three intents: keeping it, without deleting, destroying or reporting it, in order to share it; keeping it to transmit, display or distribute; and keeping it for commercial purposes. Having the material and not deleting or reporting it can be enough to show that intent [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]].

**Watching can be possession.** Viewing such material online without downloading it can amount to possession, through the doctrine of "constructive possession", if the viewer exercised control over it [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. A stream is not a loophole.

**The IT Act covers consumption.** Section 67B punishes the creation, possession, propagation and consumption of such material [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Its text names creating, collecting, browsing, downloading and exchanging it, with up to five years in prison and a fine of up to Rs 10 lakh on a first conviction, and up to seven years on a repeat [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

## Why 'child pornography' is the wrong word

The court also retired a phrase. It told every court in India to stop using "child pornography" in orders and judgments and to say "child sexual exploitation and abuse material" (CSEAM) instead, and it urged Parliament to amend POCSO to make the same change [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Such images, it said, "are not merely pornographic but are records of incidents" of abuse [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

The word matters. "Pornography" suggests performers, consent and an adult audience. None of that exists here: there is a child, an abuser and a camera. Calling the result "porn" turns a crime scene into content, and the person watching it into a customer instead of a part of the harm.

## Platforms, NCMEC and Indian police: who must report

The tip that started this case followed a well-worn route. Under an agreement between NCRB and NCMEC, platforms report suspected material to NCMEC, which passes the reports to NCRB, which forwards them to the states through the national cybercrime portal [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. In 2024 NCMEC attributed 2,252,528 reports to India, the most of any country, though report counts are not a measure of how much abuse takes place [[ncmec-cybertipline-by-country-2024]].

The court held that this route alone is not enough. A platform that reports to NCMEC must also report to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or the local police, as Section 19 of POCSO requires, and complying with the IT Act's safe-harbour conditions does not absolve it [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

The far end of the pipeline is thin. In 2024 police registered 1,099 cases under Section 67B for publishing or transmitting material depicting children in sexually explicit acts, with 1,123 child victims [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In NCRB's tables on crimes against children, courts convicted in 65 such cases that year, a conviction rate of 39.4%, while 2,765 were pending trial at year's end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A tip is not a case, and a case is not a conviction. But at every step, the numbers shrink.

## If it reaches your phone: do not forward, report

Imagine a 19-year-old in Patna whose college WhatsApp group suddenly carries a video of a child being sexually abused. Someone types "disgusting, share so everyone knows". Sharing it is not activism. Exchanging such material is an offence under Section 67B [[indiacode-it-act-2000]], and keeping it without deleting or reporting it can show an intention to share [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. What to do instead:

- Do not download, save, screenshot or forward it, not even as "proof".
- Note where it came from: the group, the username or number that sent it, the link. Leave the chat undeleted so it can be traced.
- Report it on the platform, and at cybercrime.gov.in, or by calling 1930 [[cybercrime-portal]].
- If you know of a child in danger, call 1098 or 112.
- If an image of you taken before you turned 18 is circulating, NCMEC's free Take It Down service can help remove it from participating platforms without you sending the image to anyone [[ncmec-take-it-down]].

Seeing such material can be deeply distressing. Tele-MANAS, on 14416, is a free mental-health helpline, open round the clock.
just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024-c.hg:
Ye case laakhon tips mein se ek tip se shuru hua. US ke National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) ko mili ek report India ke National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ke raaste Tamil Nadu police tak pahunchi [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]]. 23 September 2024 ko isi case se Supreme Court ka judgment aaya, Just Rights for Children Alliance (2024 INSC 716), jisne badal diya ki Indian law child sexual abuse material ke 'possession' ko kaise dekhta hai, aur courts use kis naam se bula sakte hain [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Is faisle ne case ko dobara zinda kiya; kisi ko convict nahi kiya, isliye hum accused ka naam nahi le rahe. Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## January 2024: Madras High Court ka faisla

11 January 2024 ko Madras High Court ne criminal proceedings quash kar di, yaani case khatam kar diya [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Court ne maana ki aisa material akele mein dekhna ya store karna, bina share kiye, crime nahi hai [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]].

Ye logic suljha hua lagta hai: kisi aur ne nahi dekha, toh kisi ka nuksaan nahi hua. Lekin ye pehle hi kadam par gir jaata hai. Ye material banane ke liye ek bachche ka abuse hua, aur har copy, har view aur har forward us abuse ko ghumaata rehta hai. Just Rights for Children Alliance ne appeal ki.

## September 2024: possession, dekhna aur 'constructive possession'

Supreme Court ne High Court ke judgment ko "egregious error", yaani gambhir galti, bata kar radd kiya aur case bahaal kar diya [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Teen baatein sabse zaroori hain.

**Store karna hi kaafi hai.** Aisa material store karna ya apne paas rakhna POCSO Act ke Section 15 ke under khud mein offence hai, agar halaat se woh iraada dikhe jo law batata hai, chahe use kabhi share na kiya gaya ho [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Ye section teen tarah ke iraade cover karta hai: share karne ke maqsad se use bina delete, destroy ya report kiye rakhna; use transmit, display ya distribute karne ke liye rakhna; aur commercial maqsad se rakhna. Material paas hona aur use delete ya report na karna, us iraade ko dikhane ke liye kaafi ho sakta hai [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]].

**Dekhna bhi possession ho sakta hai.** Aisa material bina download kiye online dekhna bhi "constructive possession" ke siddhaant ke zariye possession maana ja sakta hai, agar dekhne wale ka us par control tha [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Stream karna koi loophole nahi hai.

**IT Act consumption ko bhi cover karta hai.** Section 67B aise material ko banane, rakhne, phailane aur consume karne, sabko punish karta hai [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Iske text mein banana, collect karna, browse karna, download karna aur exchange karna likha hai; pehli conviction par paanch saal tak ki jail aur Rs 10 lakh tak ka fine, aur dobara conviction par saat saal tak ki jail [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

## 'Child pornography' shabd galat kyun hai

Court ne ek phrase ko bhi retire kiya. Usne India ki har court ko kaha ki orders aur judgments mein "child pornography" likhna band karein aur uski jagah "child sexual exploitation and abuse material" (CSEAM) kahein, aur Parliament se POCSO mein bhi yahi badlaav karne ki guzaarish ki [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Court ke mutabik aisi images "are not merely pornographic but are records of incidents", yaani ye sirf pornographic nahi, balki abuse ki ghatnaon ka record hain [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

Shabd maayne rakhta hai. "Pornography" sunkar performers, consent aur adult audience ka khayal aata hai. Yahan inme se kuch nahi hai: yahan ek bachcha hai, ek abuser hai aur ek camera hai. Ise "porn" kehna ek crime scene ko content bana deta hai, aur dekhne wale ko us nuksaan ka hissa nahi, balki ek customer bana deta hai.

## Platforms, NCMEC aur Indian police: report kise karna hai

Is case ki shuruaat wali tip ek jaane-pehchaane raaste se aayi thi. NCRB aur NCMEC ke beech ek agreement ke under platforms shaq wala material NCMEC ko report karte hain, NCMEC woh reports NCRB ko bhejta hai, aur NCRB unhe national cybercrime portal ke zariye states tak pahunchata hai [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. 2024 mein NCMEC ne 2,252,528 reports India se jodi, kisi bhi desh se zyada, haalaanki reports ki ginti se ye nahi naapa ja sakta ki kitna abuse hota hai [[ncmec-cybertipline-by-country-2024]].

Court ne kaha ki sirf ye raasta kaafi nahi. Jo platform NCMEC ko report karta hai, use POCSO ke Section 19 ke mutabik Special Juvenile Police Unit ya local police ko bhi report karna hoga, aur IT Act ki safe-harbour conditions poori kar lene se woh is zimmedaari se bach nahi sakta [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

Pipeline ka doosra sira bahut patla hai. 2024 mein police ne Section 67B ke under bachchon ko sexually explicit acts mein dikhane wala material publish ya transmit karne ke 1,099 cases darj kiye, jinme 1,123 bachche victim the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Crimes against children wali NCRB tables ke mutabik us saal courts ne aise 65 cases mein conviction diya, yaani 39.4% conviction rate, jabki saal ke aakhir tak 2,765 cases trial ke intezaar mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Tip case nahi hai, aur case conviction nahi hai. Lekin har kadam par numbers sikudte jaate hain.

## Agar ye aapke phone par aaye: forward nahi, report kariye

Sochiye, Patna mein kisi 19 saal ke student ke college WhatsApp group mein achanak ek video aata hai jisme ek bachche ka sexual abuse ho raha hai. Koi likhta hai "disgusting, sab tak pahunchao". Ise share karna activism nahi hai. Aisa material exchange karna Section 67B ke under offence hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]], aur use delete ya report kiye bina rakhna share karne ka iraada dikha sakta hai [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Iski jagah ye kariye:

- Use download, save, screenshot ya forward mat kariye, "saboot" ke liye bhi nahi.
- Note kariye ki ye kahan se aaya: group, bhejne wale ka username ya number, link. Chat delete mat kariye, taaki use trace kiya ja sake.
- Platform par report kariye, aur cybercrime.gov.in par, ya 1930 par call karke [[cybercrime-portal]].
- Agar aap jaante hain ki koi bachcha khatre mein hai, toh 1098 ya 112 par call kariye.
- Agar aapki koi image, jo 18 saal se pehle li gayi thi, circulate ho rahi hai, toh NCMEC ki free Take It Down service use participating platforms se hatane mein madad kar sakti hai, aur iske liye aapko image kisi ko bhejni nahi padti [[ncmec-take-it-down]].

Aisa material dekhna gehra sadma de sakta hai. Tele-MANAS, 14416, ek free mental health helpline hai jo din-raat khuli rehti hai.

juvenile-accused-tried-as-adults-jj-act.en:
Six people were accused in the 2012 Delhi gang rape and murder. Four adults were hanged at Tihar Jail on 20 March 2020. One was found dead in jail in March 2013. The sixth was a juvenile, released in 2015 after three years in a correctional home [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]]. To many people, those two endings to one crime looked like a loophole. Before that year was out, Parliament had passed a law that can send a 16-year-old to an adult trial. We name no accused person here, child or adult. This is general information, not legal advice.

## 2015: a release, then a new law

Before 2015 was over, on 31 December, the President gave assent to a new Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]].

The Act did not turn 16-year-olds into adults. It still calls them children. What it added is one narrow door, for a child aged 16 or above accused of what the Act calls a "heinous" offence: one with a minimum punishment of seven years or more [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]].

Sexual offences fall well inside it. Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, rape carries at least 10 years and gang rape at least 20 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Under POCSO, penetrative sexual assault on a child carries at least 10 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## How the 'preliminary assessment' works for 16- and 17-year-olds

Imagine a 17-year-old in Kanpur arrested for gang rape. On television that night, the debate is about hanging him. The Juvenile Justice Board has to ask different questions, in a fixed order [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]:

| Question | What the 2015 Act says |
|---|---|
| Is the offence "heinous"? | Yes, if its minimum punishment is seven years or more |
| Is the child 16 or older? | Then the Board must make a preliminary assessment (Section 15) |
| What can the Board decide? | To send the case to a Children's Court, which can try the child as an adult (Sections 18 and 19) |
| What is the ceiling? | No death sentence, and no life imprisonment without the possibility of release (Section 21) |

The charge alone does not move a teenager to an adult trial. A Board decides, one child at a time, and a child under 16 cannot be sent at all.

Had this law existed in 2012, the juvenile in the Delhi case might have faced an adult trial. He could not have been hanged with the four adults.

## Kathua 2022: when age itself is disputed

Every row of that table rests on a date of birth, so age is the first thing fought over.

In the 2018 Kathua case, the rape and murder of an eight-year-old girl, a Pathankot court convicted six of the seven accused it tried on 10 June 2019 [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. One more accused was dealt with separately. A Kathua court had declared him a juvenile, and the Jammu and Kashmir High Court had agreed.

On 16 November 2022, the Supreme Court (Justices Ajay Rastogi and J.B. Pardiwala) set both orders aside and ruled that he must be tried as an adult. A medical estimate of age, the bench said, is "only an opinion, and not a statutory substitute for proof" [[scroll-kathua-juvenile-2022]]. We could not verify how his trial ended.

A real child wrongly treated as an adult loses every protection in the table. An adult wrongly treated as a child escapes an adult trial. Courts have to decide age on evidence, which is why a birth certificate or school record can end up mattering. That holds for survivors too: POCSO protects anyone under 18, boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Hyderabad 2019: three minors, no trial

An adult trial is the harshest route Indian law allows for a child. In 2019, police near Hyderabad took a route that is in no law at all. Four people accused of a rape and murder were shot dead before any court heard the case.

The Supreme Court set up an inquiry commission on 12 December 2019, led by former Supreme Court judge V.S. Sirpurkar [[leaflet-hyderabad-encounter-sc-2022]]. It found that the police had fired on the four deliberately, "with an intent to cause their death", that three of the four were minors, and that all ten officers involved should be tried for murder [[livelaw-hyderabad-encounter-commission-2022]]. We could not confirm whether any officer has been prosecuted.

For those three, no Board asked for proof of age or made any assessment, and no court tested the evidence. Many people called it justice. The murdered woman's family got no trial and no verdict, and can never have one.

## Teenage accused, child survivors: what justice requires

Three cases, three endings: release after three years, an adult trial ordered after a fight over age, death without any trial. None of them settles what a survivor needs.

**Punishment is not where most cases fail.** Courts convicted the accused in only 32.3% of POCSO cases whose trials ended in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Moving a teenager to an adult court does not make a weak investigation stronger.

**The law reaches far beyond one gang rape.** In 2024, 23,497 of the 44,567 child victims of penetrative sexual assault recorded under POCSO, 52.7%, were aged 16 to 18. In 22,308 of the 44,126 cases, 50.6%, the person accused was a friend, online friend or live-in partner "on pretext of marriage" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That category mixes grooming with relationships between adolescents. Sex with anyone under 18 is an offence under POCSO whatever the "consent", so a 17-year-old boyfriend can face a charge with a 10-year minimum, and the same preliminary assessment as the teenager in Kanpur.

**A survivor's rights do not depend on the accused's age.** Police must record a complaint at any station, wherever the offence took place. Compensation can be claimed from the State or District Legal Services Authority even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

India can hold a 17-year-old to account for rape and still refuse to hang a child. The 2015 Act tries to do both. What decides most cases happens much earlier: whether the complaint was recorded, whether the evidence was kept, and whether a court got to rule at all.
juvenile-accused-tried-as-adults-jj-act.hg:
2012 ke Delhi gang rape aur murder mein chhe log accused the. Chaar adults ko 20 March 2020 ko Tihar Jail mein phaansi hui. Ek March 2013 mein jail mein mara hua mila. Chhatha ek juvenile tha, jo correctional home mein teen saal bitane ke baad 2015 mein rihaa ho gaya [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]]. Bahut logon ko ek hi crime ke yeh do anjaam law ka loophole lage. Wahi saal khatam hone se pehle Parliament ne ek aisa law paas kar diya tha jo 16 saal ke bachche ko adult trial tak bhej sakta hai. Hum yahan kisi accused ka naam nahin le rahe, chahe woh bachcha ho ya adult. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahin.

## 2015: ek rihaai, phir ek naya law

2015 khatam hone se pehle, 31 December ko, President ne naye Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act ko assent de diya [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]].

Is Act ne 16 saal ke bachchon ko adult nahin bana diya. Act unhe ab bhi "child" hi kehta hai. Usne bas ek tang darwaza khola, us bachche ke liye jo 16 saal ya usse bada ho aur jis par aise offence ka aarop ho jise Act "heinous" kehta hai: yaani jiski minimum saza saat saal ya usse zyada ho [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]].

Sexual offences is definition ke kaafi andar aate hain. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita mein rape ki saza kam se kam 10 saal hai aur gang rape ki kam se kam 20 saal [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. POCSO mein bachche par penetrative sexual assault ki saza kam se kam 10 saal hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## 16 aur 17 saal ke accused ke liye 'preliminary assessment' kaise kaam karta hai

Sochiye ki Kanpur mein ek 17 saal ka ladka gang rape ke aarop mein arrest hota hai. Us raat TV par debate chal rahi hai ki use phaansi honi chahiye ya nahin. Juvenile Justice Board ko alag sawaal poochhne hote hain, ek tay order mein [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]:

| Sawaal | 2015 ka Act kya kehta hai |
|---|---|
| Kya offence "heinous" hai? | Haan, agar uski minimum saza saat saal ya usse zyada hai |
| Kya bachcha 16 ya usse bada hai? | To Board ko preliminary assessment karna hi hoga (Section 15) |
| Board kya tay kar sakta hai? | Case ko Children's Court bhejna, jo bachche par adult ki tarah trial chala sakti hai (Sections 18 aur 19) |
| Saza ki upari hadd kya hai? | Death sentence nahin, aur aisi life imprisonment bhi nahin jisme release ki possibility na ho (Section 21) |

Sirf aarop lag jaane se koi teenager adult trial mein nahin pahunch jaata. Board har bachche ke liye alag se tay karta hai, aur 16 se kam umar ke bachche ko bheja hi nahin ja sakta.

Agar yeh law 2012 mein hota, to Delhi case ke juvenile par shayad adult ki tarah trial chalta. Lekin use un chaar adults ke saath phaansi nahin di ja sakti thi.

## Kathua 2022: jab age par hi jhagda ho

Us table ki har line ek date of birth par tiki hai, isliye sabse pehli ladai age par hi hoti hai.

2018 ke Kathua case mein, yaani aath saal ki ek bachchi ke rape aur murder mein, Pathankot court ne 10 June 2019 ko jin saat accused par trial chala unmein se chhe ko convict kiya [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. Ek aur accused ka case alag chala. Kathua ki ek court ne use juvenile maana tha, aur Jammu and Kashmir High Court ne bhi yahi maana.

16 November 2022 ko Supreme Court (Justices Ajay Rastogi aur J.B. Pardiwala) ne dono orders radd kar diye aur kaha ki us par adult ki tarah trial chalega. Bench ne kaha ki age ka medical andaaza "only an opinion, and not a statutory substitute for proof" hai, yaani sirf ek raay, law ke hisaab se saboot ki jagah nahin [[scroll-kathua-juvenile-2022]]. Uske trial ka nateeja hum verify nahin kar paaye.

Agar ek asli bachche ko galti se adult maan liya jaaye, to table ki har suraksha uske haath se nikal jaati hai. Agar ek adult ko galti se bachcha maan liya jaaye, to woh adult trial se bach jaata hai. Courts ko age evidence par tay karni hoti hai, isliye birth certificate ya school record kisi din bahut kaam aa sakta hai. Yeh baat survivors par bhi laagu hoti hai: POCSO 18 se kam umar ke har bachche ko protect karta hai, ladka ho ya ladki [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Hyderabad 2019: teen minor, koi trial nahin

Adult trial woh sabse sakht raasta hai jo Indian law ek bachche ke liye deta hai. 2019 mein Hyderabad ke paas police ne woh raasta liya jo kisi law mein hai hi nahin. Ek rape aur murder ke chaar accused ko kisi bhi court mein sunwai se pehle goli maar di gayi.

Supreme Court ne 12 December 2019 ko ek inquiry commission banaya, jiske head former Supreme Court judge V.S. Sirpurkar the [[leaflet-hyderabad-encounter-sc-2022]]. Commission ne paaya ki police ne chaaron par jaan-boojhkar goli chalayi, "with an intent to cause their death", yaani unhe maarne ke iraade se, ki chaar mein se teen minor the, aur ki isme shaamil sabhi das officers par murder ka trial chalna chahiye [[livelaw-hyderabad-encounter-commission-2022]]. Kisi officer par prosecution hua ya nahin, yeh hum confirm nahin kar paaye.

Un teenon ke liye kisi Board ne age ka saboot nahin maanga, koi assessment nahin hua, aur kisi court ne evidence nahin parkha. Bahut logon ne ise justice kaha. Jis aurat ka murder hua, uski family ko na trial mila na faisla, aur ab kabhi mil bhi nahin sakta.

## Teenage accused, child survivors: justice ke liye kya chahiye

Teen cases, teen anjaam: teen saal baad rihaai, age ki ladai ke baad adult trial ka order, aur bina kisi trial ke maut. Inmein se koi bhi yeh tay nahin karta ki survivor ko kya chahiye.

**Zyada tar cases saza par nahin haarte.** 2024 mein jin POCSO cases ke trial khatam hue, unmein se sirf 32.3% mein courts ne accused ko convict kiya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Teenager ko adult court bhej dene se kamzor investigation mazboot nahin ho jaati.

**Yeh law ek gang rape se bahut aage tak pahunchta hai.** 2024 mein POCSO ke tahat darj penetrative sexual assault ke 44,567 child victims mein se 23,497, yaani 52.7%, 16 se 18 saal ke the. 44,126 cases mein se 22,308 mein, yaani 50.6% mein, accused ek friend, online friend ya "on pretext of marriage" wala live-in partner tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is category mein grooming aur teenagers ke aapsi relationships dono mile hue hain. POCSO mein 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi insaan ke saath sex crime hai, "consent" ho ya na ho. Isliye ek 17 saal ke boyfriend par bhi 10 saal ki minimum saza wala charge lag sakta hai, aur uska bhi wahi preliminary assessment ho sakta hai jo Kanpur wale teenager ka hua.

**Survivor ke rights accused ki age par depend nahin karte.** Crime kahin bhi hua ho, police ko kisi bhi station mein complaint darj karni hogi. State ya District Legal Services Authority se compensation maanga ja sakta hai, chahe offender kabhi pakda na jaaye aur koi trial na ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

India ek 17 saal ke accused ko rape ke liye jawaabdeh thehra sakta hai aur phir bhi ek bachche ko phaansi dene se mana kar sakta hai. 2015 ka Act dono karne ki koshish karta hai. Zyada tar cases ka faisla usse bahut pehle ho jaata hai: complaint darj hui ya nahin, evidence bacha ya nahin, aur court ko faisla sunane ka mauka mila ya nahin.

kathua-2018-trial-moved-policemen-convic.en:
In January 2018, an eight-year-old girl was raped and murdered in Kathua, in Jammu and Kashmir [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. She is not named here, and under Indian law she must never be. This file follows something else: what happened to the truth about her death. Policemen were convicted of destroying it. A court across the state border protected it.

## January 2018: an eight-year-old and the investigation

Some of the accused were policemen. Three of them, a special police officer, a sub-inspector and a head constable, were later convicted of destroying evidence [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]: people whose job is to protect it.

Even her identity was not safe. On 18 April 2018 the Delhi High Court directed 12 media houses that had revealed it to pay Rs 10 lakh each to Jammu and Kashmir's victim compensation fund; their lawyers said they had wrongly believed a dead victim could be named [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]]. That December the Supreme Court made it explicit: a rape victim's identity must not be disclosed even after her death, even with her family's consent, unless a sessions judge decides it is justified [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Our report on those media houses shows how it still happens.

## May 2018: the Supreme Court moves the trial to Pathankot

On 7 May 2018, a Supreme Court bench of Chief Justice Dipak Misra and Justices D.Y. Chandrachud and Indu Malhotra moved the trial out of Jammu and Kashmir to Pathankot in Punjab. It ordered the trial held in camera, and on a day-to-day basis "to avoid any delay" [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]].

Each order protects something. A trial in another state is further from local pressure. A closed courtroom keeps out the public and cameras, shielding the child's identity and the witnesses. Day-to-day hearings leave fewer gaps in which witnesses can be pressured or worn down.

Kathua was not the only such case. The Supreme Court moved all the Unnao trials from Lucknow to Delhi [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]], and on 7 February 2019 it sent the Muzaffarpur shelter home trial to a court in Delhi's Saket [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]]. Our Unnao case file tells that story.

A closed courtroom is not special treatment. Rape trials have had to be held in camera since 1983 [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Today Section 366 of the BNSS requires it for rape and POCSO trials, as far as practicable before a woman judge, and bars publishing anything about the proceedings without the court's permission [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## June 2019: six convictions, including three policemen

On 10 June 2019, the Pathankot court gave its verdict [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]:

| Accused | Verdict |
|---|---|
| 3 men | Life imprisonment for murder, and 25 years for gang rape |
| 3 policemen | 5 years each for destroying evidence |
| 1 man | Acquitted |

In all, 6 of 7 accused were convicted. Appeals were expected in the Punjab and Haryana High Court; we could not verify their outcome. We name none of the men, and the one acquitted must never be named.

The lesson for every police station: destroying evidence is a crime in itself. The three policemen were punished not for carelessness but for making the truth harder to find.

Evidence decides cases. In 2024, police across India closed 1,044 rape cases that they themselves recorded as true, because the evidence was insufficient or the accused could not be traced [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## The accused who claimed to be a child: the 2022 age ruling

One more accused was dealt with separately. A Kathua court had declared him a juvenile, and the Jammu and Kashmir High Court had agreed. On 16 November 2022 the Supreme Court (Justices Ajay Rastogi and J.B. Pardiwala) set both orders aside and ruled that he must be tried as an adult. The bench said a medical expert's estimate of age is "only an opinion, and not a statutory substitute for proof" [[scroll-kathua-juvenile-2022]].

Why does age matter so much? It decides which system hears the case. Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, when a child aged 16 or above is accused of a heinous offence, one with a minimum punishment of seven years or more, a Juvenile Justice Board must make a "preliminary assessment" and can send the case to a Children's Court for trial as an adult. Even then, the Act bars a death sentence or life imprisonment without release for such a child [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]. A claim to be under 18 can change the court, the procedure and the possible punishment, so it has to be tested on evidence.

He is not named: we found no verdict convicting him.

## Protecting evidence and demanding a fair trial

Most families will never see the Supreme Court move their case. What any family can do is make evidence harder to lose.

- **Report at any police station.** Under Section 173 of the BNSS, police must register a complaint wherever the crime happened (a Zero FIR), a woman's complaint of a sexual offence must be recorded by a woman officer, and you must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Name the crime if police refuse.** Refusing to record a rape FIR is punishable with six months to two years in prison under Section 199 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Our guide to a refused FIR sets out the next steps.
- **Ask for the medical examination early.** A rape survivor must be sent for one within 24 hours of police receiving the information, only with consent, and the doctor must send the report to the investigating officer within 7 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Our 72-hour guide covers the medical steps in order.
- **Keep your own record:** copies of the FIR and medical papers, the dates, and the names of the officers you met.

Outrage does not guarantee a conviction. In 2024, courts convicted in only 32.3% of POCSO cases whose trials ended [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Acquittals have many causes, from victims or families turning hostile to age disputes; lost evidence is one a family can help prevent. Kathua shows what is still possible when evidence survives, even after the people meant to guard it tried to destroy it.

This is general information, not legal advice.
kathua-2018-trial-moved-policemen-convic.hg:
January 2018 mein Jammu and Kashmir ke Kathua mein ek aath saal ki bachchi ka rape aur murder hua [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. Hum uska naam nahin likhenge, aur Indian law kehta hai ki uska naam kabhi saamne nahin aana chahiye. Yeh file kuch aur follow karti hai: uski maut ke sach ke saath kya hua. Kuch policemen us sach ko mitaane ke doshi paaye gaye. Aur state border ke paar ek court ne us sach ko bachaya.

## January 2018: aath saal ki bachchi, aur investigation

Accused mein kuch policemen bhi the. Inmein se teen, ek special police officer, ek sub-inspector aur ek head constable, baad mein evidence mitaane ke liye convict hue [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]: yaani woh log jinka kaam hi evidence bachana hai.

Bachchi ki pehchaan bhi safe nahin rahi. 12 media houses ne uski pehchaan saamne la di thi. 18 April 2018 ko Delhi High Court ne in sabko 10-10 lakh rupaye Jammu and Kashmir ke victim compensation fund mein dene ko kaha. Unke lawyers ne kaha ki unhe galatfehmi thi ki ek mari hui victim ka naam chhapa ja sakta hai [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]]. Usi saal December mein Supreme Court ne saaf kar diya: rape victim ki pehchaan uski maut ke baad bhi nahin batayi ja sakti, family ki marzi ho tab bhi nahin, jab tak koi sessions judge ise sahi na thehraye [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Un media houses par hamari report batati hai ki yeh aaj bhi kaise hota hai.

## May 2018: Supreme Court ne trial Pathankot bheja

7 May 2018 ko Chief Justice Dipak Misra aur Justices D.Y. Chandrachud aur Indu Malhotra ki Supreme Court bench ne trial Jammu and Kashmir se bahar, Punjab ke Pathankot bhej diya. Court ne kaha ki trial in camera, yaani band courtroom mein, aur day-to-day hoga, "to avoid any delay", yaani koi deri na ho [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]].

Har order kisi cheez ko bachata hai. Dusre state mein chal raha trial wahan ke local pressure se zyada door rehta hai. Band courtroom mein public aur cameras bahar rehte hain, jisse bachchi ki pehchaan aur gawah dono bachte hain. Roz ki hearing se beech ke lambe gaps kam hote hain, jinmein gawahon par pressure daala ja sakta hai ya unhe thaka kar toda ja sakta hai.

Kathua akela case nahin tha. Supreme Court ne Unnao ke saare trials Lucknow se Delhi bheje [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]], aur 7 February 2019 ko Muzaffarpur shelter home case Delhi ke Saket ki ek court mein bheja [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]]. Unnao par hamari case file woh kahani batati hai.

Band courtroom koi special treatment nahin hai. 1983 se rape trials ka in camera hona zaroori hai [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Aaj BNSS ka Section 366 rape aur POCSO trials ke liye yahi zaroori banata hai, jahan tak ho sake ek woman judge ke saamne, aur court ki permission ke bina proceedings ke baare mein kuch bhi chhapna mana hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## June 2019: chhe convictions, jinmein teen policemen bhi

10 June 2019 ko Pathankot court ne faisla sunaya [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]:

| Accused | Faisla |
|---|---|
| 3 aadmi | Murder ke liye life imprisonment, aur gang rape ke liye 25 saal |
| 3 policemen | Evidence mitaane ke liye 5-5 saal |
| 1 aadmi | Bari |

Kul milakar 7 mein se 6 accused convict hue. Punjab and Haryana High Court mein appeals hone ki ummeed thi; unka nateeja hum verify nahin kar paaye. Hum kisi bhi aadmi ka naam nahin le rahe, aur jo bari hua uska naam kabhi nahin liya jaana chahiye.

Har police station ke liye sabak: evidence mitana khud mein ek crime hai. Teeno policemen ko laaparwahi ki saza nahin mili. Unhe sach tak pahunchna mushkil banane ki saza mili.

Evidence hi case ka faisla karta hai. 2024 mein poore India mein police ne 1,044 aise rape cases band kar diye jinhe usne khud sach maana tha, kyunki evidence kaafi nahin tha ya accused ka pata nahin chala [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Jis accused ne khud ko bachcha bataya: 2022 ka age ruling

Ek aur accused ka case alag chala. Kathua ki ek court ne use juvenile maana tha, aur Jammu and Kashmir High Court ne bhi yahi maana. 16 November 2022 ko Supreme Court (Justices Ajay Rastogi aur J.B. Pardiwala) ne dono orders radd kar diye aur kaha ki us par adult ki tarah trial chalega. Bench ne kaha ki age ke baare mein medical expert ka andaaza "only an opinion, and not a statutory substitute for proof" hai, yaani sirf ek raay, law ke hisaab se saboot ki jagah nahin [[scroll-kathua-juvenile-2022]].

Age itni important kyun hai? Kyunki age se tay hota hai ki case kaun sunega. Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 ke hisaab se, agar 16 saal ya usse bade kisi bachche par heinous offence ka aarop hai, yaani aisa crime jiski minimum saza saat saal ya usse zyada ho, to Juvenile Justice Board ek "preliminary assessment" karega aur case ko Children's Court bhej sakta hai, jahan us par adult ki tarah trial chale. Tab bhi Act aise bachche ko death sentence ya bina release wali life imprisonment dene se rokta hai [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]. 18 se kam umar ka daava court, procedure aur possible saza, sab badal sakta hai, isliye use evidence par parakhna zaroori hai.

Hum uska naam nahin le rahe, kyunki humein use convict karne wala koi faisla nahin mila.

## Evidence bachaiye, fair trial maangiye

Zyada tar families ka case Supreme Court kabhi dusre state nahin bhejega. Lekin har family itna kar sakti hai ki evidence aasani se na khoye.

- **Kisi bhi police station mein report kijiye.** BNSS Section 173 ke hisaab se crime kahin bhi hua ho, police ko complaint darj karni hogi (Zero FIR), kisi aurat ki sexual offence complaint woman officer likhegi, aur aapko FIR ki free copy milegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Police mana kare to crime ka naam boliye.** Rape FIR darj na karne par BNS Section 199 mein chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Refused FIR par hamari guide aage ke steps batati hai.
- **Medical examination jaldi karwane ko kahiye.** Police ko jaankari milne ke 24 ghante ke andar rape survivor ko medical examination ke liye bhejna hoga, sirf consent ke saath, aur doctor ko 7 din ke andar report investigating officer ko bhejni hogi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Hamari 72-hour guide medical steps order mein batati hai.
- **Apna record khud rakhiye:** FIR aur medical papers ki copies, dates, aur jin officers se mile unke naam.

Sirf gussa conviction ki guarantee nahin hai. 2024 mein POCSO ke jin cases ka trial poora hua, unmein se sirf 32.3% mein conviction hua [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Bari hone ki kai wajahein hoti hain, jaise victim ya family ka hostile ho jaana ya umar par vivaad; evidence ka kho jaana ek aisi wajah hai jise rokne mein family khud madad kar sakti hai. Kathua dikhata hai ki evidence bach jaye to kya mumkin hai, bhale hi use bachane ki zimmedari walon ne hi use mitaane ki koshish ki ho.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahin.

kerala-actor-assault-verdict-2025.en:
On 17 February 2017 an actor in Kerala was abducted and sexually assaulted. On 8 December 2025, almost nine years later, the Principal Sessions Court in Ernakulam convicted six men and acquitted four. On 12 December 2025 Judge Honey M. Varghese sentenced each of the six to 20 years' rigorous imprisonment [[thefederal-kerala-actor-verdict-2025]] [[southfirst-kerala-actor-sentence-2025]].

The case is widely known, and so is the survivor. This magazine still does not name her, and does not name anyone who was acquitted. The law protects her identity whatever others have published, and an acquitted person is, in law, not guilty.

## What the court decided

The six convicted men were found guilty of the assault and related offences, including gang rape and kidnapping; one was also convicted under the IT Act for recording the assault [[onmanorama-kerala-actor-appeal-2026]]. Because the crime was in 2017, the old Indian Penal Code applied. Since 2013 it had set a minimum of 20 years for gang rape [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. So the court gave each man the lowest sentence the law allowed.

The four acquittals were about a different question: whether the assault was planned by someone else. The prosecution had alleged a conspiracy with a mastermind. The court found that this wider conspiracy was not proved [[onmanorama-kerala-actor-appeal-2026]].

That distinction matters. The court did not doubt that the assault happened or who carried it out. It found the evidence not strong enough to convict those accused of being behind it.

## The appeal

Kerala's government appealed to the High Court in February 2026. It asked the court to overturn the four acquittals, arguing the conspiracy had been wrongly held unproven, and to give the six convicted men harsher sentences. The High Court admitted the appeal on 22 June 2026 [[onmanorama-kerala-actor-appeal-2026]]. We found no ruling as of 23 November 2026. The case is not over.

## What the case changed before it ended

The case did not wait for its verdict to have consequences. After the assault, the Women in Cinema Collective petitioned the state, and in 2017 the Kerala government set up the three-member Justice K. Hema Committee to study sexual harassment and gender inequality in the Malayalam film industry [[hindu-hema-coverage-2024]]. Its report was submitted in December 2019 but made public only on 19 August 2024, nearly five years later [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]]. In 2022 the Kerala High Court held that every film production unit with more than 10 workers must have an Internal Complaints Committee under the POSH Act [[kerala-hc-wcc-judgment-2022]].

So one survivor's decision to report, in 2017, set off a chain: a collective, a committee, a court ruling on film sets, and, eventually, a report that described an industry. The criminal trial was the slowest link in that chain.

## Nine years is a sentence too

The trial's length is its own finding. A survivor who reports in her twenties or thirties can spend most of a decade as a witness, cross-examined, followed by headlines, waiting. Across India, 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial at the end of 2024, and courts convicted in 24.4% of the rape trials they completed that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A famous case with a determined survivor and constant media attention still took almost nine years to reach a first verdict.

> The survivor in this case did what the system asks of every survivor: report, testify, wait. The system's answer took almost nine years and is still under appeal.

## If you work in a film unit, a studio or any set

Imagine a 23-year-old assistant director on a web series in Kochi whom a senior crew member keeps cornering after pack-up. She can go to the police for any sexual offence. She can also complain to the production's Internal Complaints Committee, which the law requires on any unit of that size [[kerala-hc-wcc-judgment-2022]]. And whoever she tells, her identity is protected: publishing anything that could identify a survivor of rape is a crime under Section 72 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The 2025 verdict proved the assault. The appeal will decide the rest. This is general information, not legal advice.
kerala-actor-assault-verdict-2025.hg:
17 February 2017 ko Kerala mein ek actor ka abduction aur sexual assault hua. 8 December 2025 ko, lagbhag nau saal baad, Ernakulam ki Principal Sessions Court ne chhe aadmiyon ko doshi paaya aur chaar ko bari kiya. 12 December 2025 ko Judge Honey M. Varghese ne chhe mein se har ek ko 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment di [[thefederal-kerala-actor-verdict-2025]] [[southfirst-kerala-actor-sentence-2025]].

Yeh case mashhoor hai, aur survivor bhi. Phir bhi yeh magazine uska naam nahi leti, aur bari hue kisi insaan ka naam bhi nahi leti. Law uski identity ko protect karta hai, doosron ne chahe kuch bhi chhapa ho, aur bari hua insaan law ki nazar mein doshi nahi hai.

## Court ne kya tay kiya

Chhe convicts ko assault aur usse jude offences ka doshi paaya gaya, jinme gang rape aur kidnapping shaamil hain; ek ko IT Act ke under assault record karne ka bhi doshi paaya gaya [[onmanorama-kerala-actor-appeal-2026]]. Crime 2017 ka tha, isliye purana Indian Penal Code laagu hua. 2013 se usme gang rape ki minimum saza 20 saal thi [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Yaani court ne har aadmi ko law ki sabse kam ijaazat wali saza di.

Chaar acquittals ek alag sawaal par the: kya yeh assault kisi aur ne plan kiya tha. Prosecution ne ek mastermind wali conspiracy ka aarop lagaya tha. Court ne paaya ki yeh badi conspiracy saabit nahi hui [[onmanorama-kerala-actor-appeal-2026]].

Yeh farq maayne rakhta hai. Court ko is par shak nahi tha ki assault hua aur kisne kiya. Usne paaya ki jin par iske peeche hone ka aarop tha, unhe doshi tehraane ke liye saboot kaafi mazboot nahi the.

## Appeal

Kerala sarkar ne February 2026 mein High Court mein appeal ki. Usne chaar acquittals palatne ki maang ki, yeh kehte hue ki conspiracy ko galat tareeke se unproven maana gaya, aur chhe convicts ke liye kadi saza maangi. High Court ne 22 June 2026 ko appeal admit ki [[onmanorama-kerala-actor-appeal-2026]]. 23 November 2026 tak humein koi faisla nahi mila. Case khatam nahi hua hai.

## Case ne khatam hone se pehle kya badla

Is case ke nateeje verdict ka intezaar nahi kar rahe the. Assault ke baad Women in Cinema Collective ne state se maang ki, aur 2017 mein Kerala sarkar ne Malayalam film industry mein sexual harassment aur gender inequality ki jaanch ke liye teen member wali Justice K. Hema Committee banayi [[hindu-hema-coverage-2024]]. Uski report December 2019 mein jama hui, lekin public sirf 19 August 2024 ko hui, lagbhag paanch saal baad [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]]. 2022 mein Kerala High Court ne kaha ki 10 se zyada workers wale har film production unit mein POSH Act ke under Internal Complaints Committee honi chahiye [[kerala-hc-wcc-judgment-2022]].

Yaani 2017 mein ek survivor ke report karne ke faisle se ek chain shuru hui: ek collective, ek committee, film sets par court ka ruling, aur aakhir mein ek report jisne poori industry ki tasveer dikhayi. Criminal trial us chain ki sabse dheemi kadi thi.

## Nau saal bhi ek saza hai

Trial ki lambaai khud ek finding hai. Jo survivor apne bees ya tees ki umar mein report karti hai, woh lagbhag ek dashak gawah ban kar bita sakti hai: cross-examination, headlines ka peecha, intezaar. 2024 ke end mein poore India mein 1,85,785 rape cases trial mein pending the, aur us saal jo rape trials poore hue unme courts ne 24.4% mein conviction diya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek mashhoor case, jisme survivor date rahi aur media ki lagataar nazar thi, use bhi pehle verdict tak lagbhag nau saal lage.

> Is case ki survivor ne wahi kiya jo system har survivor se maangta hai: report, gawahi, intezaar. System ka jawab lagbhag nau saal mein aaya aur abhi bhi appeal mein hai.

## Agar aap film unit, studio ya kisi set par kaam karti hain

Sochiye, Kochi mein ek web series ki 23 saal ki assistant director ko pack-up ke baad ek senior crew member baar-baar akele mein gherta hai. Woh kisi bhi sexual offence ke liye police ke paas ja sakti hai. Woh production ki Internal Complaints Committee mein bhi complaint kar sakti hai, jo law ke hisaab se itne bade har unit mein honi chahiye [[kerala-hc-wcc-judgment-2022]]. Aur woh jise bhi bataye, uski identity protected hai: rape survivor ki pehchaan bata sakne wali koi bhi cheez publish karna BNS ki Section 72 ke under crime hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

2025 ke verdict ne assault saabit kiya. Baaki appeal tay karegi. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

kolkata-law-college-case-2025.en:
On 25 June 2025 a woman law student was allegedly gang-raped on the premises of her own college in south Kolkata. Police arrested four men: a former student who was working at the college on contract, two current students and a security guard [[ians-kasba-chargesheet-2025]] [[ians-kasba-charges-framed-2026]].

None of them has been convicted, so none is named here. Nor is the college: naming a small institution and a student's course could point to her. This file is about what the case revealed and how the system responded.

## Who had power on that campus

The details that emerged in court were not about the crime but about the place. A petition to the Calcutta High Court said the assault took place partly in a room belonging to the college's student union, and that the main accused ran activities in the union's name. It pointed out that West Bengal had held no student union elections since 2017, yet union offices kept operating, often run by former students and people no one had elected [[barandbench-calcutta-hc-union-rooms-2025]].

The High Court asked the state the obvious question: how was a former student allowed inside the campus after official hours [[barandbench-law-college-identity-2025]]?

That is the core of this case. Sexual violence on campuses is rarely about strangers breaking in. It is about people with informal power, a senior who controls a room, a staff member who holds keys, a group nobody supervises, using spaces after the teachers have gone home.

## The court's answer: lock the rooms

On 3 July 2025 a bench of Justices Soumen Sen and Smita Das De ordered every student union room in West Bengal's colleges and universities shut until student elections are held [[livelaw-calcutta-hc-union-rooms-2025]] [[barandbench-calcutta-hc-union-rooms-2025]]. The court also asked the media not to reveal the survivor's identity [[barandbench-law-college-identity-2025]].

Closing rooms is a blunt tool. It removes one space where power gathered unchecked, but it does not create what was missing: elected student bodies that are accountable, clear rules on who can be on campus at night, guards who answer to the institution and not to a faction, and an Internal Complaints Committee that students trust. Writing those rules down costs little. Enforcing them is the real reform.

## The investigation and the trial

Police filed a chargesheet of about 650 pages in August 2025, 58 days after the crime, against all four accused. It included a DNA report that matched the main accused and statements from about 80 people; the charges include gang rape, wrongful confinement and kidnapping [[ians-kasba-chargesheet-2025]]. That was within the two months the law allows for a rape investigation [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

On 14 January 2026 an Alipore court framed charges against all four and fixed 27 January 2026 for the trial to begin, with 83 witnesses listed [[ians-kasba-charges-framed-2026]]. We found no verdict as of 23 November 2026. Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, gang rape carries at least 20 years' rigorous imprisonment, up to the rest of natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The state's record is the reason to watch this trial closely. In 2024 West Bengal had the lowest conviction rate for crimes against women of any state, 1.6%, and the largest backlog of such cases in India, 3,84,388 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Across India, 1,537 gang rape cases were recorded that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A fast chargesheet in a famous case does not change the odds for the rest.

## A year after RG Kar

The case came less than a year after the rape and murder of a trainee doctor at RG Kar Medical College in the same city, which had already pushed the Supreme Court to set up a National Task Force on the safety of medical professionals [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. Within months, Kolkata had two institutions of learning, a hospital and a law college, where women were attacked inside the buildings meant to train them. The lesson was the same both times: the danger was inside, among people with access and authority.

## What a student can do

Imagine a first-year student at a college in Howrah who notices that a group of seniors and ex-students use an unmarked room late in the evening and pressure juniors to come. She does not need proof of a crime to act. She can raise it in writing with the principal, ask who controls the room's keys, and take it to the college's Internal Complaints Committee if anyone is harassed.

If an assault happens, the survivor's identity is protected by law: printing or publishing anything that could reveal it is a crime under Section 72 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.
kolkata-law-college-case-2025.hg:
25 June 2025 ko south Kolkata mein ek law student ka uske apne college ke parisar mein kathit gang rape hua. Police ne chaar aadmiyon ko arrest kiya: ek former student jo college mein contract par kaam kar raha tha, do maujooda students aur ek security guard [[ians-kasba-chargesheet-2025]] [[ians-kasba-charges-framed-2026]].

Inme se kisi ka conviction nahi hua hai, isliye yahan kisi ka naam nahi hai. College ka naam bhi nahi: ek chhote institution aur student ke course ka naam usse uski pehchaan tak le ja sakta hai. Yeh file is baare mein hai ki case ne kya dikhaya aur system ne kya jawab diya.

## Us campus par power kiske paas thi

Court mein jo details saamne aayi, woh crime se zyada jagah ke baare mein thi. Calcutta High Court mein ek petition ne kaha ki assault ka kuch hissa college ke student union ke kamre mein hua, aur main accused union ke naam par activities chalata tha. Petition ne bataya ki West Bengal mein 2017 se student union elections nahi hue, phir bhi union offices chalte rahe, aksar former students aur aise logon ke haathon jinhe kisi ne chuna nahi tha [[barandbench-calcutta-hc-union-rooms-2025]].

High Court ne state se seedha sawaal poocha: ek former student ko official ghanton ke baad campus mein aane kaise diya gaya [[barandbench-law-college-identity-2025]]?

Yahi is case ka core hai. Campus par sexual violence aam taur par ajnabiyon ke ghus aane ki baat nahi hoti. Yeh informal power wale logon ki baat hoti hai: ek senior jo kisi kamre ko control karta hai, ek staff jiske paas chaabiyan hain, ek group jispar koi nazar nahi rakhta, aur jo teachers ke ghar jaane ke baad jagahon ko use karte hain.

## Court ka jawab: kamron par taala

3 July 2025 ko Justices Soumen Sen aur Smita Das De ki bench ne order diya ki West Bengal ke sabhi colleges aur universities ke student union rooms tab tak band rahenge jab tak student elections nahi hote [[livelaw-calcutta-hc-union-rooms-2025]] [[barandbench-calcutta-hc-union-rooms-2025]].
