Court ne media se survivor ki identity reveal na karne ko bhi kaha [[barandbench-law-college-identity-2025]].

Kamre band karna ek mota auzaar hai. Isse woh ek jagah hat jaati hai jahan bina rok-tok power jamaa thi, lekin jo gayab tha woh nahi banta: jawabdeh, chuni hui student bodies, raat mein campus par kaun reh sakta hai iske saaf rules, aise guards jo institution ko jawab dein na ki kisi gut ko, aur ek Internal Complaints Committee jispar students bharosa karein. In rules ko likhna aasaan hai. Inhe laagu karna asli reform hai.

## Investigation aur trial

Police ne August 2025 mein, crime ke 58 din baad, chaaron accused ke khilaaf lagbhag 650 pages ki chargesheet file ki. Isme ek DNA report thi jo main accused se match hui, aur lagbhag 80 logon ke bayaan the; charges mein gang rape, galat tareeke se band rakhna aur kidnapping shaamil hain [[ians-kasba-chargesheet-2025]]. Yeh rape investigation ke liye law ke diye do mahine ke andar tha [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

14 January 2026 ko Alipore ki ek court ne chaaron par charges frame kiye aur trial shuru karne ke liye 27 January 2026 tay ki, 83 gawahon ki list ke saath [[ians-kasba-charges-framed-2026]]. 23 November 2026 tak humein koi verdict nahi mila. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita mein gang rape par kam se kam 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, baaki natural life tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

State ka record hi is trial ko dhyaan se dekhne ki wajah hai. 2024 mein West Bengal mein aurton ke khilaaf crimes ka conviction rate kisi bhi state mein sabse kam, 1.6%, tha, aur aise cases ka backlog India mein sabse bada, 3,84,388 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Us saal poore India mein gang rape ke 1,537 cases darj hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek mashhoor case mein tez chargesheet baaki cases ki tasveer nahi badalti.

## RG Kar ke ek saal baad

Yeh case usi shehar ke RG Kar Medical College mein ek trainee doctor ke rape aur murder ke ek saal se bhi kam samay baad aaya. Us case ne pehle hi Supreme Court ko medical professionals ki safety par National Task Force banane par majboor kiya tha [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. Kuch hi mahinon mein Kolkata ki do padhai ki jagahon, ek hospital aur ek law college, mein aurton par unhi imaaraton ke andar hamla hua jo unhe train karne ke liye bani thi. Dono baar sabak ek hi tha: khatra andar tha, un logon ke beech jinke paas pahunch aur authority thi.

## Ek student kya kar sakti hai

Sochiye, Howrah ke ek college ki first-year student dekhti hai ki kuch seniors aur ex-students shaam ko der tak ek bina naam ke kamre ko use karte hain aur juniors ko wahan aane ke liye dabaav dete hain. Kadam uthane ke liye use crime ka saboot nahi chahiye. Woh principal ko likh kar bata sakti hai, pooch sakti hai ki kamre ki chaabi kiske paas hai, aur agar kisi ko harass kiya jaaye toh college ki Internal Complaints Committee tak le ja sakti hai.

Agar assault hota hai, toh survivor ki identity law se protected hai: aisi koi bhi cheez print ya publish karna jisse woh pehchaani jaaye, BNS ki Section 72 ke under crime hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

landmark-rape-cases-compensation-compare.en:
In India, the money a court orders for a survivor of sexual violence or her family varies enormously from one case to the next. In 2019 the Supreme Court ordered the Gujarat government to pay the survivor of the 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case Rs 50 lakh, and to give her a government job and housing [[livelaw-bilkis-compensation-2019]]. In 2023 the Hathras trial court directed Rs 40,000 to the victim's mother, out of a convict's Rs 50,000 fine [[theprint-hathras-verdict-2023]]. Most survivors will never stand in either courtroom. Here is what the landmark cases produced, and what the law promises everyone else.

## The landmark awards, side by side

| Case | Court and year | What was ordered | Who pays |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case | Supreme Court, 2019 | Rs 50 lakh, a government job and housing [[livelaw-bilkis-compensation-2019]] | Gujarat government |
| Unnao, 2017 | Delhi trial court, 2019 | A Rs 25 lakh fine, Rs 10 lakh of it for the survivor [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]] | The convict |
| RG Kar, Kolkata, 2024 | Sealdah court, 2025 | Rs 17 lakh to the family [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]] | West Bengal government |
| Hathras, 2020 | Special SC/ST court, 2023 | A Rs 50,000 fine, Rs 40,000 of it for the victim's mother [[theprint-hathras-verdict-2023]] | The convict |

Read the last column first: two of these sums are owed by a government, two by a convicted man. The Gujarat order came 17 years after the crime. The Unnao convict, a former MLA, has appealed. In May 2026 the Supreme Court set aside the Delhi High Court's suspension of his sentence and asked that court either to decide his appeal quickly or to pass a fresh order [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]].

Hathras ended without a rape conviction. The special court acquitted three of the four accused and convicted one of culpable homicide not amounting to murder and of offences under the SC/ST Act [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]]. It held that rape had not been proved, a finding that remains open to appeal [[theprint-hathras-verdict-2023]]. An order is not proof of payment: the table shows only what courts ordered.

## Fines, compensation and court orders: three different things

A **fine** is part of the punishment. The convict pays it, and it reaches the survivor only if the judge directs part of it to her, as the Hathras court did, or if the law requires it. Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, any fine for raping a girl under 16 must be paid to the victim [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A fine is only as good as the convict's means.

**Compensation** is paid by the state through the legal services authorities, and it does not wait for a conviction [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

A **court-ordered award**, like the Supreme Court's in 2019, is a third route: a court directing a government to pay beyond any standard scale.

Set these sums against the national scheme below. Rs 50 lakh is five times the top of its range for gang rape. The RG Kar figure of Rs 17 lakh equals the scheme's highest amount for rape, Rs 7 lakh, plus its highest amount for the loss of a life, Rs 10 lakh [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. In other words, the RG Kar award did not go beyond the ceiling of a scheme that any woman survivor can claim under.

## What NALSA's 2018 scheme sets out for women survivors

The national model is the National Legal Services Authority's 2018 compensation scheme for women survivors of sexual assault and other crimes, framed on the Supreme Court's directions in the Nipun Saxena case. States pay through their own legal services authorities, so actual payouts vary [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

| Harm | Compensation under the scheme |
|---|---|
| Rape | Rs 4 lakh to Rs 7 lakh |
| Gang rape | Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh |
| Death of the woman (paid to her family) | Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh |
| Pregnancy resulting from rape | Rs 3 lakh to Rs 4 lakh |
| Loss of a foetus or of fertility | Rs 2 lakh to Rs 3 lakh |

These limits are 50% higher when the survivor is a minor, and the authority must finish its inquiry within 60 days of receiving the claim [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. For acid attacks, the Supreme Court set a floor in 2013: at least Rs 3 lakh for every victim, Rs 1 lakh of it within 15 days of the attack [[sc-laxmi-2013]]. The Centre has also released Rs 200 crore from the Nirbhaya Fund as a one-time grant to states under the Central Victim Compensation Fund [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. The money has been set aside. A survivor still has to claim it.

## No trial, no arrest, still eligible: Section 396 BNSS

Section 396 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, which replaced Section 357A of the old CrPC, requires every state to run a victim compensation scheme. If the offender is never traced or identified and no trial takes place, the survivor or her dependants can apply directly to the State or District Legal Services Authority, which must complete its inquiry within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Compensation is also available when a trial ends in acquittal, and whatever the state pays comes on top of any fine paid to the survivor. The section speaks of "the victim" without limiting it to women; the NALSA scale above is written for women survivors.

Consider a 22-year-old in Indore raped by a man she met on a dating app. He used a false name, the police cannot trace him, and there may never be a trial. She can still apply, and the authority must finish its inquiry within two months. This is general information, not legal advice; your District Legal Services Authority can explain your state's scheme.

## How to apply through your District Legal Services Authority

1. **Collect the papers:** the FIR (police must give the victim a free copy) [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], the medical report and treatment bills.
2. **Apply to the District Legal Services Authority** for your district.
3. **Ask whether interim relief is available** if money is needed now, for treatment or safety.
4. **Ask for a free lawyer** [[nalsa]], who can also help you follow the criminal case.
5. **Follow up in writing.** If two months pass without a decision, write again citing Section 396, and keep dated copies.

A few cases reached courts that ordered far more than the standard scale, and one of those orders came 17 years after the crime. A survivor's claim should not depend on whether the country knows her case. The scheme exists so that it does not.
landmark-rape-cases-compensation-compare.hg:
India mein court sexual violence ki survivor ya uski family ke liye kitne paison ka order karti hai, yeh ek case se doosre case mein bahut zyada badal jaata hai. 2019 mein Supreme Court ne Gujarat sarkar ko order diya ki 2002 ke Gujarat riots gang rape case ki survivor ko Rs 50 lakh diye jayein, saath mein sarkari naukri aur ghar bhi [[livelaw-bilkis-compensation-2019]]. 2023 mein Hathras ki trial court ne ek convict ke Rs 50,000 ke fine mein se Rs 40,000 victim ki maa ko dene ko kaha [[theprint-hathras-verdict-2023]]. Zyadatar survivors in dono mein se kisi courtroom tak kabhi nahi pahunchengi. Toh dekhte hain ki landmark cases mein kya order hua, aur law baaki sabse kya waada karta hai.

## Landmark awards, aamne-saamne

| Case | Court aur saal | Kya order hua | Kaun dega |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case | Supreme Court, 2019 | Rs 50 lakh, sarkari naukri aur ghar [[livelaw-bilkis-compensation-2019]] | Gujarat sarkar |
| Unnao, 2017 | Delhi trial court, 2019 | Rs 25 lakh ka fine, jisme se Rs 10 lakh survivor ke liye [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]] | Convict |
| RG Kar, Kolkata, 2024 | Sealdah court, 2025 | Family ko Rs 17 lakh [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]] | West Bengal sarkar |
| Hathras, 2020 | Special SC/ST court, 2023 | Rs 50,000 ka fine, jisme se Rs 40,000 victim ki maa ke liye [[theprint-hathras-verdict-2023]] | Convict |

Pehle aakhri column padhiye: do rakamein sarkar ko deni hain, do ek convict ko. Gujarat wala order crime ke 17 saal baad aaya. Unnao ke convict ne, jo pehle MLA tha, appeal ki hai. May 2026 mein Supreme Court ne Delhi High Court ka uski saza suspend karne wala order radd kar diya aur High Court se kaha ki ya toh woh uski appeal par jaldi faisla kare ya naya order paas kare [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]].

Hathras case rape conviction ke bina khatam hua. Special court ne chaar mein se teen accused ko bari kar diya, aur ek ko culpable homicide not amounting to murder aur SC/ST Act ke offences mein convict kiya [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]]. Court ne kaha ki rape prove nahi hua; is finding ko abhi bhi appeal mein challenge kiya ja sakta hai [[theprint-hathras-verdict-2023]]. Order hone ka matlab yeh nahi ki payment ho gaya: table mein sirf woh hai jo courts ne order kiya.

## Fine, compensation aur court ka order: teen alag cheezein

**Fine** saza ka hissa hai. Convict use bharta hai, aur woh survivor tak tabhi pahunchta hai jab judge uska kuch hissa use dene ko kahe, jaise Hathras court ne kiya, ya jab law khud aisa kehta ho. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke under, 16 saal se kam umr ki ladki ke rape mein jo bhi fine lagega, woh victim ko hi diya jayega [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Fine utna hi kaam ka hai jitni convict ki haisiyat.

**Compensation** state deti hai, legal services authorities ke through, aur iske liye conviction ka intezaar nahi karna padta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

**Court ka order kiya hua award**, jaise 2019 mein Supreme Court ka, teesra raasta hai: court kisi sarkar ko kisi bhi standard scale se aage jaakar paise dene ka order deti hai.

Ab in rakamon ko neeche di gayi national scheme ke saamne rakhiye. Rs 50 lakh scheme mein gang rape ki sabse oonchi rakam ka paanch guna hai. RG Kar ka Rs 17 lakh theek utna hai jitna scheme mein rape ki sabse oonchi rakam, Rs 7 lakh, aur jaan jaane ki sabse oonchi rakam, Rs 10 lakh, ko jodne par banta hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Yaani RG Kar ka award us scheme ki upper limit se aage nahi gaya, jiske under koi bhi mahila survivor claim kar sakti hai.

## NALSA ki 2018 scheme mahila survivors ke liye kya tay karti hai

National model hai National Legal Services Authority ki 2018 ki compensation scheme, jo sexual assault aur doosre crimes ki shikaar auraton ke liye hai. Yeh Supreme Court ke Nipun Saxena case ke directions par bani thi. States apni legal services authorities ke through paise deti hain, isliye asal payment state ke hisaab se badalta hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

| Nuksaan | Scheme ke under compensation |
|---|---|
| Rape | Rs 4 lakh se Rs 7 lakh |
| Gang rape | Rs 5 lakh se Rs 10 lakh |
| Aurat ki maut (family ko) | Rs 5 lakh se Rs 10 lakh |
| Rape se hui pregnancy | Rs 3 lakh se Rs 4 lakh |
| Foetus ya fertility ka nuksaan | Rs 2 lakh se Rs 3 lakh |

Survivor minor ho toh yeh limits 50% zyada hoti hain, aur authority ko claim milne ke 60 din ke andar apni inquiry poori karni hoti hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Acid attack ke liye Supreme Court ne 2013 mein ek minimum tay kiya: har victim ko kam se kam Rs 3 lakh, jisme se Rs 1 lakh attack ke 15 din ke andar [[sc-laxmi-2013]]. Centre ne Nirbhaya Fund se Central Victim Compensation Fund ke under states ko Rs 200 crore ki one-time grant bhi di hai [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. Paisa rakha hua hai. Lekin claim toh survivor ko hi karna padega.

## Na trial, na arrest, phir bhi haq: Section 396 BNSS

Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita ki Section 396, jo purane CrPC ki Section 357A ki jagah aayi hai, har state ko victim compensation scheme chalane ko kehti hai. Agar offender kabhi trace ya identify hi na ho aur koi trial na ho, tab bhi survivor ya uske dependants seedhe State ya District Legal Services Authority mein apply kar sakte hain, aur authority ko do mahine mein inquiry poori karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Trial acquittal par khatam ho, tab bhi compensation mil sakta hai, aur state jo bhi deti hai, woh survivor ko mile kisi bhi fine ke upar hota hai. Section mein "the victim" likha hai, sirf auraton ki baat nahi; upar di gayi NALSA ki scale mahila survivors ke liye likhi gayi hai.

Maan lijiye Indore ki ek 22 saal ki ladki ka rape ek aise aadmi ne kiya jisse woh dating app par mili thi. Usne naqli naam bataya tha, police use trace nahi kar paa rahi, aur ho sakta hai kabhi trial hi na ho. Woh phir bhi apply kar sakti hai, aur authority ko do mahine mein apni inquiry poori karni hoti hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi; aapki District Legal Services Authority aapke state ki scheme samjha sakti hai.

## District Legal Services Authority mein apply kaise karein

1. **Papers jama kijiye:** FIR (police ko victim ko iski free copy deni hoti hai) [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], medical report aur treatment ke bills.
2. **Apne district ki District Legal Services Authority mein apply kijiye.**
3. **Poochiye ki interim relief mil sakti hai ya nahi**, agar treatment ya safety ke liye abhi paison ki zaroorat hai.
4. **Free lawyer maangiye** [[nalsa]], jo criminal case par nazar rakhne mein bhi madad kar sake.
5. **Likh kar follow up kijiye.** Do mahine mein faisla na aaye toh Section 396 ka hawala dekar dobara likhiye, aur har letter ki date wali copy rakhiye.

Kuch cases aisi courts tak pahunche jinhone standard scale se kahin zyada ka order diya, aur unme se ek order crime ke 17 saal baad aaya. Survivor ka claim is baat par depend nahi karna chahiye ki desh uska case jaanta hai ya nahi. Scheme isiliye bani hai ki aisa na ho.

marital-rape-case-delhi-split-verdict-to.en:
One line of Indian law still says that sex forced on a wife by her husband is not rape, if she is 18 or older. It is Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. For married women, husbands are not an edge case: in NFHS-5, 82% of ever-married women who had faced sexual violence named their current husband as the perpetrator [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Since 2017, Indian courts have argued over that one line. This is the courtroom history, step by step, up to the hearing the Supreme Court has promised for December 2026.

## 2017: under-18 wives protected, adult wives left out

The argument began with the youngest wives. In January 2013 the Justice J.S. Verma Committee recommended deleting the exception altogether [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament did not. When the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 raised the age of consent to 18, it kept the exception for wives aged 15 and above [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. A 16-year-old could not legally consent to sex, yet if she was married, the law did not call forced sex by her husband rape.

On 11 October 2017, in Independent Thought v. Union of India, the Supreme Court read down the exception in Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code: sex with a wife under 18 is rape [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. Justices Madan B. Lokur and Deepak Gupta marked the limit themselves: "we have not at all dealt with the larger issue of marital rape of adult women" [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. The protection was tied to her age, not her consent. It ends on her 18th birthday.

## March 2022: Karnataka's "not absolute" ruling

The first opening for adult wives came from Karnataka. In March 2022 its High Court held that the exception is not absolute, and that a husband who forces non-consensual sex on his wife can be prosecuted under the rape provision, then Section 376 IPC [[indianexpress-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. It did not strike the exception down. It refused to let it shield this husband from a rape charge.

The Supreme Court stayed that judgment in July 2022, and the husband's appeal is now the lead case before it [[indianexpress-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. We do not name him: he has not been convicted.

## 11 May 2022: one bench, two answers in Delhi

Weeks later, in RIT Foundation v. Union of India, two Delhi High Court judges ruled on whether the exception is constitutional, and gave opposite answers: a 1-1 split. Justice Rajiv Shakdher held the exception "violative of Articles 14, 15, 19(1)(a) and 21 of the Constitution" and struck it down. Justice C. Hari Shankar held that the challenges "have to fail" [[scconline-rit-foundation-split-verdict-2022]].

Their reasons are the two sides of the whole debate. For Justice Shakdher, the exception discriminates against married women and violates their bodily autonomy. For Justice Hari Shankar, sexual relations are a legitimate expectation within marriage, so the exception stands [[scobserver-marital-rape-exception-2025]]. Both judges certified the case for appeal to the Supreme Court [[scconline-rit-foundation-split-verdict-2022]]. A split changes nothing, so the law stayed as it was.

That September, in an abortion case, the Supreme Court held that "rape" in the MTP Act includes marital rape, so a wife made pregnant by forced sex can seek an abortion up to 24 weeks without filing an FIR [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Yet when the new penal code came into force on 1 July 2024 [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]], it carried the exception over into Section 63 [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## 2024-2025: the Centre's affidavit and an adjourned hearing

In an affidavit verified on 3 October 2024, the Union government told the Supreme Court that marital rape is "more of a social issue rather than a legal issue". It accepted that "a husband certainly does not have any fundamental right to violate the consent of the wife", but argued that calling it rape "can be arguably considered to be excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]]. Married women, it said, already have remedies under other laws, including the domestic violence law [[scobserver-marital-rape-exception-2025]].

A bench led by Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud began hearing the case on 17 October 2024 and adjourned it on 23 October, because the hearing could not finish before his retirement [[indianexpress-marital-rape-deferred-2024]]. In December 2024 the government told the Rajya Sabha it had no proposal to criminalise marital rape [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]]. A fresh petition then challenged the exception in its new home, Section 63 BNS; the Supreme Court issued notice on 23 May 2025 and tagged it with the pending cases [[clpr-aweksha-v-union-2025]].

## December 2026: what the Supreme Court must decide

On 9 September 2026 a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana posted the cases for final hearing. It will decide two things: whether the exception is valid, and whether a husband can be prosecuted for rape while it stands [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. In November the bench said it would fix the hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026 and try to hear it before the winter break [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. As of 20 November 2026 it had not ruled [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].

Consider a hypothetical case to see what is at stake: a 24-year-old in Indore, married for two years, whose husband forces sex on her. Under Exception 2, it is not rape. If she moves back to her parents' home and he forces sex on her there, Section 67 BNS applies: two to seven years in prison, far below the ten-year minimum for raping any other woman [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. If she becomes pregnant, the abortion law treats her as a rape survivor. One act, three legal answers, depending on where she lives and what she needs.

If the exception is struck down, the rape law would no longer carve out husbands of adult wives. If it survives, the second question decides whether a rape charge like the one in Karnataka can still go ahead. In NFHS-5, 4.6% of ever-married women aged 18 to 49 said their husband had physically forced them to have intercourse when they did not want to [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. For every one of them who was 18 or older at the time, the law as it stands on 20 November 2026 does not call it rape.

This article is general information about the law, not legal advice.
marital-rape-case-delhi-split-verdict-to.hg:
Indian law ki ek line aaj bhi kehti hai ki agar patni 18 saal ya usse badi hai, toh pati ka uske saath zabardasti sex karna rape nahi hai. Ye line hai Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 63 ka Exception 2 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Shaadi-shuda aurton ke liye pati koi rare case nahi hain: NFHS-5 mein jin ever-married aurton ne sexual violence jhela tha, unmein se 82% ne apne current pati ko iska zimmedaar bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. 2017 se Indian courts isi ek line par behas kar rahe hain. Ye us behas ki courtroom history hai, step by step, December 2026 ki us hearing tak jiska vaada Supreme Court ne kiya hai.

## 2017: 18 se kam umar ki patniyan protected, adult patniyan chhoot gayin

Behas sabse kam umar ki patniyon se shuru hui. January 2013 mein Justice J.S. Verma Committee ne sifarish ki ki ye exception poori tarah hata diya jaaye [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament ne aisa nahi kiya. Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ne age of consent 18 kar di, lekin 15 saal aur usse badi patniyon ke liye exception bana rehne diya [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. Yaani 16 saal ki ladki law ki nazar mein sex ke liye consent nahi de sakti thi, lekin agar uski shaadi ho chuki thi, toh pati ki zabardasti ko law rape nahi kehta tha.

11 October 2017 ko Independent Thought v. Union of India case mein Supreme Court ne Indian Penal Code ke Section 375 wale exception ko "read down" kiya: 18 se kam umar ki patni ke saath sex rape hai [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. Justices Madan B. Lokur aur Deepak Gupta ne apni seema khud likh di: "we have not at all dealt with the larger issue of marital rape of adult women", yaani adult patniyon ke marital rape ke bade sawaal ko unhone chhua tak nahi [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. Ye suraksha uski umar se judi thi, uske consent se nahi. Uske 18th birthday par ye khatam ho jaati hai.

## March 2022: Karnataka ka "not absolute" faisla

Adult patniyon ke liye pehla raasta Karnataka se khula. March 2022 mein wahan ke High Court ne kaha ki ye exception "absolute" nahi hai, aur jo pati apni patni par bina consent ke sex thopta hai, us par rape wale provision, us waqt Section 376 IPC, ke under case chal sakta hai [[indianexpress-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. Court ne exception ko khatam nahi kiya. Bas use is pati ke liye rape charge se bachne ki dhaal nahi banne diya.

Supreme Court ne July 2022 mein is faisle par rok laga di, aur ab wahan isi pati ki appeal lead case hai [[indianexpress-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. Hum uska naam nahi likhte, kyunki use convict nahi kiya gaya hai.

## 11 May 2022: Delhi mein ek bench, do jawab

Kuch hafton baad RIT Foundation v. Union of India case mein Delhi High Court ke do judges ne faisla diya ki exception constitutional hai ya nahi, aur dono ke jawab ulte nikle: faisla 1-1 se bat gaya. Justice Rajiv Shakdher ne exception ko "violative of Articles 14, 15, 19(1)(a) and 21 of the Constitution" maana, yaani Constitution ke in Articles ke khilaaf, aur use strike down kar diya. Justice C. Hari Shankar ne kaha ki ye challenges "have to fail", yaani tik nahi sakte [[scconline-rit-foundation-split-verdict-2022]].

Inke tark hi is poori behas ke do pehlu hain. Justice Shakdher ke hisaab se exception shaadi-shuda aurton ke saath bhedbhaav karta hai aur unki bodily autonomy, yaani apne shareer par unke haq, ko todta hai. Justice Hari Shankar ke hisaab se shaadi mein sexual relations ek "legitimate expectation", yaani jaayaz ummeed, hain, isliye exception bana rahega [[scobserver-marital-rape-exception-2025]]. Dono judges ne Supreme Court mein appeal ke liye certificate diya [[scconline-rit-foundation-split-verdict-2022]]. Bata hua faisla kuch nahi badalta, isliye law jaisa tha waisa hi raha.

Usi September ek abortion case mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki MTP Act mein "rape" ke andar marital rape bhi aata hai. Yaani pati ki zabardasti se pregnant hui patni bina FIR ke 24 hafte tak abortion le sakti hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Phir bhi 1 July 2024 ko jab naya penal code laagu hua [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]], toh usne ye exception Section 63 mein jaise ka taisa utaar liya [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## 2024-2025: Centre ka affidavit aur taali gayi hearing

3 October 2024 ko verify hue ek affidavit mein Union government ne Supreme Court se kaha ki marital rape "more of a social issue rather than a legal issue" hai, yaani kanooni se zyada samaajik masla. Sarkar ne maana ki "a husband certainly does not have any fundamental right to violate the consent of the wife", yaani pati ko patni ka consent todne ka koi fundamental right nahi hai. Lekin uski daleel thi ki ise rape kehna "can be arguably considered to be excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate", yaani bahut zyada sakht aur zaroorat se zyada saza hogi [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]]. Sarkar ke mutabik shaadi-shuda aurton ke paas doosre laws mein, jaise domestic violence law mein, pehle se raaste hain [[scobserver-marital-rape-exception-2025]].

Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ki bench ne 17 October 2024 ko case sunna shuru kiya aur 23 October ko ise taal diya, kyunki unke retirement se pehle hearing poori nahi ho sakti thi [[indianexpress-marital-rape-deferred-2024]]. December 2024 mein sarkar ne Rajya Sabha mein kaha ki marital rape ko crime banane ka uske paas koi proposal nahi hai [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]]. Phir ek nayi petition ne exception ko uske naye ghar, Section 63 BNS, mein challenge kiya; Supreme Court ne 23 May 2025 ko notice jaari kiya aur ise pending cases ke saath jod diya [[clpr-aweksha-v-union-2025]].

## December 2026: Supreme Court ko kya tay karna hai

9 September 2026 ko Chief Justice Surya Kant aur Justices Joymalya Bagchi aur V. Mohana ki bench ne cases ko final hearing ke liye list kiya. Bench do baatein tay karegi: kya exception valid hai, aur jab tak ye law mein hai, kya tab tak kisi pati par rape ka case chal sakta hai [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. November mein bench ne kaha ki woh hearing 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko tay karegi aur winter break se pehle sunne ki koshish karegi [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. 20 November 2026 tak koi faisla nahi aaya tha [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].

Ek hypothetical case sochiye, taaki samajh aaye ki kya daav par hai: Indore ki 24 saal ki ek ladki, shaadi ko do saal hue hain, aur pati uske saath zabardasti sex karta hai. Exception 2 ke hisaab se ye rape nahi hai. Agar woh maayke laut jaaye aur pati wahan uske saath zabardasti kare, toh Section 67 BNS laagu hota hai: do se saat saal ki jail, jo kisi bhi doosri aurat ke rape ki das saal ki minimum saza se kaafi kam hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Agar woh pregnant ho jaaye, toh abortion law use rape survivor maanta hai. Ek hi ghatna, teen alag kanooni jawab, sirf is par depend karta hai ki woh kahan rehti hai aur use kis cheez ki zaroorat hai.

Agar exception strike down hota hai, toh rape law mein adult patniyon ke patiyon ke liye bani ye chhoot nahi rahegi. Agar exception bach jaata hai, toh doosra sawaal tay karega ki Karnataka jaisa rape charge aage chal sakta hai ya nahi. NFHS-5 mein 18 se 49 saal ki 4.6% ever-married aurton ne bataya ki unke pati ne unki marzi ke khilaaf physically force karke unke saath intercourse kiya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Inmein se jo bhi us waqt 18 ya usse zyada umar ki thi, uske saath jo hua use 20 November 2026 ka law rape nahi kehta.

Ye article law ke baare mein general information hai, legal advice nahi.

metoo-defamation-acquittal-2021.en:
In October 2018, at the height of India's #MeToo movement, a Union minister of state filed a criminal defamation case in a Delhi court against a woman journalist who had accused him of sexual harassment. Several other women also accused him. He denied the allegations, and resigned from the government days later [[livelaw-ramani-acquittal-2021]]. On 17 February 2021 the court acquitted her [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]]. We name neither: no court has found him guilty of any offence, and she is a woman who reported sexual harassment. What matters for every other woman is what the judge wrote.

## October 2018: #MeToo, an allegation and a defamation case

India's #MeToo movement gathered pace in the Hindi film industry in late 2018 and spread within weeks, as women in the news media, films and government spoke publicly about sexual harassment [[bbc-hema-report-2024]]. The journalist's account was one of them.

The minister's answer was a criminal case. In criminal defamation, the person who spoke becomes the accused. She, not he, had to stand trial and defend her words in court for more than two years. That is how defamation law can be turned against people who speak up: even when they win, the process itself is a punishment, and everyone watching learns what speaking can cost.

## 17 February 2021: what the Delhi court held

Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Ravindra Kumar Pandey acquitted her. His central sentence reads: "The woman cannot be punished for raising voice against the sex-abuse on the pretext of criminal complaint of defamation as the right of reputation cannot be protected at the cost of the right of life and dignity of woman as guaranteed in Indian Constitution under article 21" [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]].

The judgment also describes how harassment works. Most of the time, it said, sexual harassment is committed "in the close doors or privately", and most women who suffer abuse "do not speak up about it or against it for simple reason 'The Shame' or the social stigma". Abuse "takes away her dignity and her self confidence" [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]].

Then came the line the case is remembered for: "The woman has a right to put her grievance at any platform of her choice and even after decades" [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]].

## 'Even after decades': why delay is not doubt

The court also asked what a woman could have done at the time. It took into consideration "the systematic abuse at the workplace due to lack of the mechanism to redress the grievance of sexual-harassment" before the 1997 Vishaka guidelines and the 2013 POSH Act [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]]. Before Vishaka, there was no complaints committee to go to.

The Supreme Court says the same about rape. Its 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes rejects the belief that a woman who delays reporting is lying, noting that "lack of familial support or fear of repercussions" can cause a survivor to delay [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. The same year it observed that women harassed at work are often reluctant to report, and "many of them even drop out from their job" [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]].

Now set that against the deadline the law gives. The POSH Act requires a written complaint within three months of the incident, extendable by three more [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Consider a hypothetical case: a nurse in Lucknow who was harassed by a senior doctor when she was 24, and who finds the words for it at 37. The POSH route is long closed to her. Speaking publicly is one of the few routes left, and a public account can bring a defamation case. The 2021 verdict backs that choice, but it is a magistrate's ruling, not a High Court or Supreme Court judgment, so other courts are not bound by it.

## The appeal, five years on

The former minister appealed. The Delhi High Court admitted the appeal in January 2022 and listed it for final hearing on 24 September 2026, more than five years after the trial verdict [[livelaw-akbar-appeal-2026]]. We could not confirm what happened at that listing. Until the High Court rules otherwise, the acquittal stands.

This is the part of the case that warns everyone else. A woman who has already won in court still cannot put the case behind her.

## Speaking up safely: POSH complaints, SHe-Box and legal help

This is general information, not legal advice.

- If it is happening now, complain in writing to your Internal Committee. The inquiry must be completed within 90 days [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- Being unable to prove a complaint is not, by itself, a ground for action against you; malicious intent has to be established through an inquiry first [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- If your workplace has fewer than ten workers, or the complaint is against the employer, go to the district's Local Committee [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- You can also complain online on SHe-Box, the government's portal [[shebox]].
- Before you name someone publicly, talk to a lawyer. Free legal aid is available through legal services authorities, including the National Legal Services Authority [[nalsa]].

The court's sentence belongs to everyone who has stayed quiet for years: a woman may speak "even after decades". The law still has to make sure that speaking does not cost her another five years in court.
metoo-defamation-acquittal-2021.hg:
October 2018 mein, jab India mein #MeToo movement apne peak par tha, ek Union minister of state ne Delhi ki ek court mein ek woman journalist ke khilaaf criminal defamation ka case kiya. Journalist ne un par sexual harassment ka ilzaam lagaya tha. Kai aur aurton ne bhi un par ilzaam lagaye. Unhone ilzaamon se inkaar kiya, aur kuch dinon baad sarkar se istifa de diya [[livelaw-ramani-acquittal-2021]]. 17 February 2021 ko court ne journalist ko bari kar diya [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]]. Hum dono mein se kisi ka naam nahi lete: kisi court ne unhe kisi offence ka doshi nahi paaya hai, aur woh ek aurat hain jinhone sexual harassment report kiya. Baaki har aurat ke liye jo maayne rakhta hai, woh hai judge ka likha hua faisla.

## October 2018: #MeToo, ek ilzaam aur defamation ka case

India mein #MeToo movement ne 2018 ke aakhir mein Hindi film industry mein zor pakda aur kuch hi hafton mein phail gaya, jab news media, films aur sarkar mein kaam karne wali aurton ne sexual harassment ke baare mein khul kar bolna shuru kiya [[bbc-hema-report-2024]]. Is journalist ki baat bhi unhi mein se ek thi.

Minister ka jawab ek criminal case tha. Criminal defamation mein bolne wala hi accused ban jaata hai. Trial unhe nahi, journalist ko jhelna pada, aur do saal se zyada tak court mein apne shabdon ka bachaav karna pada. Defamation law ko awaaz uthane walon ke khilaaf aise hi istemaal kiya ja sakta hai: jeet jaane par bhi poora process apne aap mein ek saza hai, aur dekhne wale sab seekh lete hain ki bolne ki keemat kya ho sakti hai.

## 17 February 2021: Delhi ki court ne kya kaha

Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Ravindra Kumar Pandey ne unhe bari kiya. Faisle ki sabse ahem line ye hai: "The woman cannot be punished for raising voice against the sex-abuse on the pretext of criminal complaint of defamation as the right of reputation cannot be protected at the cost of the right of life and dignity of woman as guaranteed in Indian Constitution under article 21". Yaani sex-abuse ke khilaaf awaaz uthane wali aurat ko defamation ke bahane saza nahi di ja sakti, kyunki kisi ki reputation ko aurat ke Article 21 wale jeevan aur dignity ke haq ki keemat par nahi bachaya ja sakta [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]].

Faisla ye bhi samjhata hai ki harassment hota kaise hai. Court ke mutabik zyadatar waqt sexual harassment "in the close doors or privately", yaani band darwazon ke peeche ya akele mein hota hai, aur abuse jhelne wali zyadatar aurtein "do not speak up about it or against it for simple reason 'The Shame' or the social stigma", yaani sharm aur samaaj ke kalank ki wajah se is baare mein nahi bolti. Abuse "takes away her dignity and her self confidence", yaani aurat se uski dignity aur uska aatmavishwas chheen leta hai [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]].

Phir aayi woh line jiske liye ye case yaad kiya jaata hai: "The woman has a right to put her grievance at any platform of her choice and even after decades", yaani aurat ko haq hai ki woh apni shikaayat apni marzi ke kisi bhi platform par, dashkon baad bhi, rakhe [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]].

## 'Even after decades': der se bolna shak ki wajah nahi

Court ne ye bhi poocha ki us waqt ek aurat kar kya sakti thi. Usne 1997 ki Vishaka guidelines aur 2013 ke POSH Act se pehle ke "the systematic abuse at the workplace due to lack of the mechanism to redress the grievance of sexual-harassment" ko dhyaan mein rakha, yaani shikaayat sunne ka koi system na hone ki wajah se workplace par hone wala lagataar abuse [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]]. Vishaka se pehle jaane ke liye koi complaints committee thi hi nahi.

Supreme Court rape ke baare mein yahi kehta hai. Uski 2023 ki gender stereotypes wali handbook is soch ko galat maanti hai ki der se report karne wali aurat jhooth bol rahi hai, aur kehti hai ki "lack of familial support or fear of repercussions", yaani parivaar ka saath na milna ya nateejon ka darr, survivor ko der karwa sakta hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Usi saal court ne kaha ki kaam ki jagah par harass hone wali aurtein aksar report karne se jhijhakti hain, aur "many of them even drop out from their job", yaani kai toh naukri hi chhod deti hain [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]].

Ab ise law ki deadline ke saamne rakhiye. POSH Act ke under incident ke teen mahine ke andar written complaint deni hoti hai, jo teen mahine aur badh sakti hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Ek hypothetical case sochiye: Lucknow ki ek nurse, jise 24 saal ki umar mein ek senior doctor ne harass kiya, aur jo 37 ki umar mein jaakar us baare mein bolne ke shabd dhoondh paati hai. POSH ka raasta uske liye kab ka band ho chuka hai. Public mein apni baat kehna un gine-chune raaston mein se ek hai jo bache hain, aur public mein kahi baat par defamation ka case ho sakta hai. 2021 ka faisla is choice ke saath khada hai, lekin ye ek magistrate ka faisla hai, High Court ya Supreme Court ka nahi, isliye doosri courts is par chalne ke liye bandhi nahi hain.

## Appeal, paanch saal baad

Former minister ne appeal ki. Delhi High Court ne January 2022 mein appeal admit ki aur use 24 September 2026 ko final hearing ke liye list kiya, trial ke faisle ke paanch saal se bhi zyada baad [[livelaw-akbar-appeal-2026]]. Us din kya hua, ye hum confirm nahi kar paaye. Jab tak High Court kuch aur nahi kehta, tab tak journalist ka bari hona bana rehta hai.

Case ka yahi hissa baaki sabko chetavni deta hai. Jo aurat court mein jeet chuki hai, woh bhi ab tak is case ko peeche nahi chhod paayi.

## Safely awaaz uthana: POSH complaint, SHe-Box aur legal madad

Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

- Agar harassment abhi ho raha hai, toh apni Internal Committee ko likh kar complaint dijiye. Inquiry 90 din ke andar poori honi chahiye [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- Complaint saabit na kar paana apne aap mein aapke khilaaf action ki wajah nahi hai; pehle inquiry mein ye saabit karna padta hai ki complaint jaan-boojh kar buri neeyat se ki gayi thi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- Agar aapki workplace mein das se kam workers hain, ya complaint employer ke khilaaf hai, toh district ki Local Committee mein jaaiye [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- Aap sarkar ke online portal SHe-Box par bhi complaint kar sakti hain [[shebox]].
- Kisi ka naam public mein lene se pehle lawyer se baat kariye. National Legal Services Authority samet legal services authorities ke through free legal aid milti hai [[nalsa]].

Court ki ye line har us insaan ki hai jo saalon se chup raha hai: aurat "even after decades", yaani dashkon baad bhi bol sakti hai. Law ko ab bhi ye pakka karna hai ki bolne ki keemat court mein paanch saal aur na ho.

muzaffarpur-shelter-home-2018-tiss-audit.en:
The sexual abuse of girls in a shelter home in Muzaffarpur, Bihar, was not exposed by a police raid, a court or a complaint from inside the building. It came to light because the state government had asked a university to audit its children's homes, and the auditors put what they found in writing [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. This file follows that audit, the Delhi trial that ended in 19 convictions, and the law that already required anyone who knew to speak. No child is identified here, and none ever should be.

## 2018: what a university audit found

The Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) carried out a social audit of Bihar's children's homes for the state government and submitted its report in April 2018. It flagged sexual abuse at several institutions, including a state-funded girls' shelter home in Muzaffarpur [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) later took over the criminal case [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

Notice what broke the silence: not a routine inspection or a complaint, but outsiders sent in by the state to look. That matters because a child in residential care depends on the adults who run the home for food, shelter and almost every contact with the outside world. If those adults are the abusers, or protect them, a complaint has nowhere to go.

## 34 girls in the state's own care

The Supreme Court's 2025 Handbook on Child Rights and the Law records that the TISS report revealed the sexual abuse of 34 minor girls at the state-run shelter home in Muzaffarpur [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. These were children in the state's own care, in a building paid for with public money.

The case also shows how such abuse gets counted. Crime data records what reaches the police. Abuse inside a closed institution reaches the police only when someone breaks the silence, and here it took an audit to do it.

The girls' identities are protected by law. Section 23 of the POCSO Act bars any media report from revealing a child victim's name, address, photograph, family details, school or neighbourhood unless the Special Court permits it in the child's interest; breaking that rule can mean up to a year in prison [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## The Delhi trial: 19 of 20 convicted

On 7 February 2019 the Supreme Court transferred the trial out of Bihar to a POCSO court at Saket in Delhi. On 20 January 2020 that court convicted 19 of the 20 accused, and 11 were later sentenced to life imprisonment [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]]. On 11 February 2020 the same court sentenced the home's operator, Brajesh Thakur, to life imprisonment for the remainder of his life and fined him about Rs 32 lakh [[livelaw-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

These are trial-court verdicts. Appeals go to the Delhi High Court, and we could not verify where they stand. We name no one else, and the person who was acquitted must not be named.

The verdict is unusual. In 2024, courts convicted the accused in only 32.3% of POCSO cases whose trials ended, and 2,86,903 POCSO cases were still pending trial at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. POCSO asks Special Courts to finish a trial, as far as possible, within a year of taking cognizance [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The Muzaffarpur verdict came less than a year after the transfer.

Most survivors get none of what this case had: a national investigating agency, a trial moved beyond local influence, and the Supreme Court's attention. The national figures show what ordinary cases face instead: long waits, and acquittal more often than conviction.

## Mandatory reporting: who had to speak

Abuse on this scale inside one building raises a hard question: who else knew? The law is clear about what they owed the children. Under Section 19 of POCSO, anyone who knows or suspects that a child sexual offence has been committed, or is likely to be, must report it to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or the local police [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Under Section 21, failing to report is punishable with up to six months in prison, a fine or both, and the head of a company or institution who fails to report an offence by a subordinate faces up to one year and a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

In a shelter home, that duty covers everyone: the superintendent, the cook, the guard, the visiting doctor, the counsellor and any official who inspects it. The heavier penalty for the person in charge makes sense: the head of an institution is best placed to see abuse by staff, and is the person whose silence protects it longest.

## How to raise the alarm about a hostel, shelter or school

Imagine you teach a weekend class at a girls' hostel in your town. A 13-year-old tells you that a staff member calls girls to his room at night, and that telling the warden changed nothing. What should you do?

- **Listen, then write it down.** Do not question her in detail or confront the staff member. Tell her she was right to tell you, and note her words and the date.
- **Report it the same day.** Go to the police, or call 1098, the Child Helpline [[wcd-childline]], which runs 24x7 and is linked to the 112 emergency system [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. You do not need proof; the duty is to report what you know or suspect.
- **Report the institution too.** Say that the warden was told. A head who fails to report a subordinate's offence is committing an offence as well.
- **Keep her out of the story.** Do not post about it with names, photos or the hostel's name, which could identify her.

The same steps apply in a boys' hostel or home: POCSO protects boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Muzaffarpur was exposed because someone from outside was sent in to look. Every hostel, shelter and school depends on the same thing: adults who notice, and who report.

This is general information, not legal advice.
muzaffarpur-shelter-home-2018-tiss-audit.hg:
Muzaffarpur, Bihar ke ek shelter home mein ladkiyon ka sexual abuse kisi police raid, court ya building ke andar se aayi complaint se expose nahin hua. Yeh tab saamne aaya jab state government ne ek university se apne children's homes ka audit karwaya, aur auditors ne jo dekha woh likh kar de diya [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. Yeh file us audit ko follow karti hai, Delhi ke us trial ko jo 19 convictions par khatam hua, aur us law ko jo pehle se kehta tha ki jise bhi pata ho, woh bole. Yahan kisi bachchi ki pehchaan nahin batayi gayi hai, aur kabhi batayi bhi nahin jaani chahiye.

## 2018: ek university audit ne kya paaya

Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) ne state government ke liye Bihar ke children's homes ka social audit kiya aur April 2018 mein apni report di. Report ne kai institutions mein sexual abuse ki taraf ishaara kiya, jinmein Muzaffarpur ka ek state-funded girls' shelter home bhi tha [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. Baad mein criminal case Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) ne apne haath mein le liya [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

Dhyaan dijiye ki chuppi kisne todi: koi routine inspection ya complaint nahin, balki bahar ke log, jinhe state ne andar dekhne ke liye bheja tha. Yeh isliye maayne rakhta hai kyunki residential care mein rehne wala bachcha khane, chhat aur bahar ki duniya se lagbhag har contact ke liye home chalane walon par hi depend karta hai. Agar wahi log abuser hon, ya abusers ko bachayein, to complaint ke paas jaane ki koi jagah nahin bachti.

## State ki apni dekhrekh mein 34 ladkiyan

Supreme Court ki 2025 ki Handbook on Child Rights and the Law record karti hai ki TISS report ne Muzaffarpur ke state-run shelter home mein 34 naabaalig ladkiyon ke sexual abuse ka khulasa kiya [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. Yeh bachchiyan state ki apni dekhrekh mein thi, ek aisi building mein jiska kharcha public ke paise se chalta tha.

Yeh case yeh bhi dikhata hai ki aisa abuse ginti mein kaise aata hai. Crime data mein wahi darj hota hai jo police tak pahunchta hai. Band institution ke andar ka abuse police tak tabhi pahunchta hai jab koi chuppi tode, aur yahan yeh kaam ek audit ne kiya.

Ladkiyon ki pehchaan law se protected hai. POCSO Act ka Section 23 kisi bhi media report ko child victim ka naam, pata, photo, family details, school ya mohalla batane se rokta hai, jab tak Special Court bachche ke hit mein iski permission na de; yeh rule todne par ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Delhi ka trial: 20 mein se 19 convict

7 February 2019 ko Supreme Court ne trial Bihar se bahar, Delhi ke Saket ki ek POCSO court mein transfer kar diya. 20 January 2020 ko us court ne 20 mein se 19 accused ko convict kiya, aur baad mein 11 ko life imprisonment ki saza mili [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]]. 11 February 2020 ko usi court ne home chalane wale Brajesh Thakur ko baaki poori zindagi ke liye life imprisonment ki saza di aur us par lagbhag 32 lakh rupaye ka fine lagaya [[livelaw-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

Yeh trial court ke faisle hain. Appeals Delhi High Court mein jaati hain, aur unki abhi ki sthiti hum verify nahin kar paaye. Hum kisi aur ka naam nahin le rahe, aur jo bari hua uska naam nahin liya jaana chahiye.

Yeh faisla aam nahin hai. 2024 mein POCSO ke jin cases ka trial khatam hua, unmein se sirf 32.3% mein courts ne accused ko convict kiya, aur saal ke ant mein 2,86,903 POCSO cases ka trial pending tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. POCSO kehta hai ki Special Court, jahan tak ho sake, cognizance lene ke ek saal ke andar trial poora kare [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Muzaffarpur ka faisla transfer ke ek saal se bhi kam samay mein aa gaya.

Zyada tar survivors ko woh kuch nahin milta jo is case ko mila: ek national investigating agency, local asar se door chala trial, aur Supreme Court ka dhyaan. National figures batate hain ki aam cases ke hisse mein iske badle kya aata hai: lamba intezaar, aur conviction se zyada acquittal.

## Mandatory reporting: kise bolna tha

Ek hi building mein itne bade paimane par abuse ek mushkil sawaal khada karta hai: aur kaun jaanta tha? Law saaf hai ki un logon par bachchon ki kya zimmedari thi. POCSO ke Section 19 ke hisaab se, jise bhi pata ho ya shak ho ki kisi bachche ke saath sexual offence hua hai, ya hone wala hai, use Special Juvenile Police Unit ya local police ko report karna hoga [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Section 21 ke hisaab se, report na karne par chhe mahine tak ki jail, fine ya dono ho sakte hain, aur kisi company ya institution ka head agar apne neeche kaam karne wale ke offence ki report nahin karta, to use ek saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Shelter home mein yeh duty sab par lagti hai: superintendent, cook, guard, visit karne wale doctor, counsellor, aur har us official par jo inspection karta hai. Incharge ke liye bhaari saza samajh mein aati hai: institution ka head staff ka abuse dekhne ki sabse achhi jagah par hota hai, aur usi ki chuppi abuse ko sabse lambe samay tak bachaati hai.

## Hostel, shelter ya school ke baare mein alarm kaise uthayein

Imagine kijiye, aap apne shehar ke ek girls' hostel mein weekend class lete hain. Ek 13 saal ki ladki aapko batati hai ki ek staff member raat ko ladkiyon ko apne kamre mein bulata hai, aur warden ko batane se kuch nahin badla. Aap kya karenge?

- **Suniye, phir likh lijiye.** Usse detail mein sawaal mat kijiye, aur staff member ko confront mat kijiye. Use bataiye ki usne aapko batakar sahi kiya, aur uske shabd aur tareekh note kar lijiye.
- **Usi din report kijiye.** Police ke paas jaiye, ya 1098 par call kijiye, jo Child Helpline hai [[wcd-childline]], 24x7 chalti hai aur 112 emergency system se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Aapko kuch saabit nahin karna hai; duty sirf itni hai ki jo aap jaante hain ya jis par shak hai, woh report karein.
- **Institution ki bhi report kijiye.** Bataiye ki warden ko bataya gaya tha. Jo head apne neeche kaam karne wale ke offence ki report nahin karta, woh khud bhi offence kar raha hai.
- **Use kahani se bahar rakhiye.** Iske baare mein naam, photo ya hostel ke naam ke saath post mat kijiye, isse uski pehchaan khul sakti hai.

Yahi steps boys' hostel ya home par bhi laagu hote hain: POCSO ladkon aur ladkiyon ko barabar protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Muzaffarpur isliye expose hua kyunki bahar se kisi ko andar dekhne bheja gaya. Har hostel, shelter aur school isi cheez par tika hai: aise adults jo dhyaan dein, aur report karein.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahin.

nipun-saxena-2018-survivor-identity-ban.en:
Disclosing a rape survivor's identity has been a crime in India since 25 December 1983 [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Nearly 35 years later, on 11 December 2018, Supreme Court judges Madan B. Lokur and Deepak Gupta had to say it again, more precisely than the law ever had: no person may print or publish her name "or even in a remote manner disclose any facts which can lead to the victim being identified" [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. The rule now sits in Section 72 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). In its first six months, July to December 2024, police across India registered 11 cases under it [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Anyone with a phone is a publisher now.

## Why the Supreme Court had to say it again in 2018

The 1983 amendment created Section 228A of the IPC for exactly this, and moved rape trials behind closed doors [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. The law was old. The leaks kept coming.

The judgment recorded how reports got around the rule without printing a name. One said the victim had topped her state board exam and named the state; it "would not require rocket science" to find her, the judges wrote. Another blurred her face on TV but showed her relatives, her neighbours and the name of her village [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

The lesson is that identification does not happen on the page. It happens in the head of a reader who knows her. A detail that means nothing to a stranger, a school, a street, a father's shop, can mean everything to a neighbour.

## 'Even in a remote manner': the directions

The first direction, in full: "No person can print or publish in print, electronic, social media, etc. the name of the victim or even in a remote manner disclose any facts which can lead to the victim being identified and which should make her identity known to the public at large" [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

Three phrases do the work. "No person" means the rule is not only for journalists. "Social media" means a post, a story or a forward can count. "Even in a remote manner" means a hint is enough.

The statute says the same. Under Section 72 of the BNS, publishing a survivor's name or anything that may make her identity known can bring up to two years in prison and a fine, unless she authorises it in writing [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. That clause matters: an adult survivor may choose to speak. The law takes the choice away from everyone else, not from her.

## Dead victims, FIRs and One Stop Centres

The judgment went further than the old law in three ways.

**Death does not end the protection.** If the victim is dead or of unsound mind, her identity must not be disclosed even with her family's authorisation, unless a Sessions Judge finds that disclosure is justified. The court noted that the victim of the 2012 Delhi gang rape, called "Nirbhaya", became "the most effective symbol of protest the country has ever known" without her true identity being disclosed [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

**FIRs stay out of public view.** FIRs in rape and POCSO cases must not be put in the public domain [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. An FIR can carry the complainant's name and address. A screenshot of one, forwarded with the word "justice", identifies her more completely than any news report could.

**Support, not just silence.** The court asked every state and union territory to set up at least one One Stop Centre in every district within a year, that is, by December 2019 [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. These centres are meant to bring support for women facing violence under one roof. By July 2026, 985 of the 1,033 approved centres were running, and they had assisted over 15.20 lakh women since April 2015 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. More than six years after the deadline, some approved centres had still not opened.

## 11 cases: how rarely the law is enforced

Police registered 11 cases under Section 72 between July and December 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That is fewer than two a month, in a country where WhatsApp groups, local news pages and comment sections pore over every high-profile case.

Read the number for what it is. It counts FIRs, not posts, and it starts in July 2024, with no earlier series to compare. NCRB also counts only the most serious offence in each FIR, so a disclosure charged alongside a graver crime may not show up at all [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Think about who would file such a complaint. A survivor whose identity has leaked must go back to a police station, and risk more attention, to start a second case. Everyone else can simply scroll past. A law that is almost never tested teaches the people who break it that nothing happens.

## Before you post or forward: a checklist

The rule works, if at all, before someone presses send. Ask:

- **Could someone who knows her recognise her?** Her name, initials, nickname or photo; her school, college, workplace or village; her father's job; the accused's name if he is her relative or neighbour. If any of these is there, don't share it.
- **Is it a document?** An FIR, medical report or court paper from a rape or POCSO case is not meant to be public. Don't forward it, even cropped.
- **Is it a guessing game?** Comments like "isn't this the girl from…?" narrow the circle until she is found. Don't start one; don't join one.
- **Has she died?** The same rule applies, and her family cannot waive it; only a Sessions Judge can allow disclosure [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].
- **Has she chosen to speak?** If an adult survivor has gone public, follow her lead: share her own words, not details she has not chosen to give.
- **Did someone else break the rule?** Report the post to the platform, and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

This is general information, not legal advice. A case can trend without her face and make demands without her name. The 2018 judgment asks one thing of every reader: let the crime be public, and let her remain a private person.
nipun-saxena-2018-survivor-identity-ban.hg:
India mein rape survivor ki pehchaan kholna 25 December 1983 se crime hai [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Lagbhag 35 saal baad, 11 December 2018 ko, Supreme Court ke judges Madan B. Lokur aur Deepak Gupta ko ye baat dobara kehni padi, aur is baar law se bhi zyada saaf shabdon mein: koi bhi insaan uska naam print ya publish nahi kar sakta, "or even in a remote manner disclose any facts which can lead to the victim being identified", yaani ishaaron mein bhi aisi koi baat nahi bata sakta jisse victim ki pehchaan ho jaaye [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Aaj ye rule Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 72 mein hai. Iske pehle chhe mahine, July se December 2024, mein poore India mein police ne iske under 11 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aaj jiske haath mein phone hai, woh bhi publisher hai.

## 2018 mein Supreme Court ko ye baat dobara kyun kehni padi

1983 ke amendment ne isi kaam ke liye IPC ka Section 228A banaaya tha, aur rape trials ko band kamre mein kar diya tha [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Law purana tha. Phir bhi pehchaan leak hoti rahi.

Judgment mein darj hai ki reports naam chhaape bina rule ko kaise chakma deti thi. Ek report ne likha ki victim ne state board exam top kiya tha, aur state ka naam bhi de diya; judges ne likha ki use dhoondhne ke liye "would not require rocket science", yaani koi rocket science nahi chahiye. Ek TV report mein uska chehra blur tha, lekin uske rishtedaar, padosi aur gaon ka naam saaf dikh raha tha [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

Sabak ye hai ki pehchaan page par nahi hoti. Woh us reader ke dimaag mein hoti hai jo use jaanta hai. Jo detail kisi ajnabi ke liye kuch nahi, jaise ek school, ek gali, pita ki dukaan, woh kisi padosi ke liye sab kuch bata deti hai.

## 'Even in a remote manner': court ke directions

Pehla direction, poora: "No person can print or publish in print, electronic, social media, etc. the name of the victim or even in a remote manner disclose any facts which can lead to the victim being identified and which should make her identity known to the public at large" [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Yaani koi bhi insaan print, electronic ya social media mein victim ka naam nahi chhaap sakta, na hi door ke ishaaron se aisi koi baat bata sakta hai jisse aam logon ko uski pehchaan pata chal jaaye.

Teen phrases saara kaam karte hain. "No person" ka matlab hai ki ye rule sirf journalists ke liye nahi hai. "Social media" ka matlab hai ki ek post, ek story ya ek forward bhi gina ja sakta hai. "Even in a remote manner" ka matlab hai ki ek ishaara bhi kaafi hai.

Law bhi yahi kehta hai. BNS ke Section 72 ke under, survivor ka naam ya aisi koi bhi cheez publish karna jisse uski pehchaan khul sake, do saal tak ki jail aur fine dila sakta hai, jab tak survivor khud likhit mein ijaazat na de [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Ye clause maayne rakhta hai: ek adult survivor khud bolne ka faisla le sakti hai. Law ye faisla baaki sabse chheenta hai, usse nahi.

## Maut ke baad, FIRs aur One Stop Centres

Judgment purane law se teen tarah aage gaya.

**Maut ke baad bhi suraksha khatam nahi hoti.** Agar victim ki maut ho chuki hai ya woh unsound mind hai, toh uske parivaar ki ijaazat se bhi uski pehchaan nahi kholi ja sakti, jab tak ek Sessions Judge ye na maane ki pehchaan kholna sahi hai. Court ne note kiya ki 2012 ke Delhi gang rape ki victim, jise "Nirbhaya" kaha gaya, apni asli pehchaan khule bina "the most effective symbol of protest the country has ever known", yaani desh ka ab tak ka sabse asardaar protest symbol ban gayi [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

**FIRs public nahi hongi.** Rape aur POCSO cases ki FIRs public domain mein nahi daali ja sakti [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. FIR mein complainant ka naam aur pata ho sakta hai. "Justice" likh kar forward kiya gaya uska ek screenshot kisi bhi news report se zyada poori tarah uski pehchaan khol deta hai.

**Sirf chuppi nahi, madad bhi.** Court ne har state aur union territory se kaha ki ek saal ke andar, yaani December 2019 tak, har district mein kam se kam ek One Stop Centre banaaye [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. In centres ka maqsad hai hinsa jhel rahi auraton ko ek hi chhat ke neeche madad dena. July 2026 tak, 1,033 approved centres mein se 985 chal rahe the, aur April 2015 se ab tak 15.20 lakh se zyada auraton ki madad kar chuke the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Deadline ke chhe saal se zyada baad bhi, kuch approved centres shuru nahi hue the.

## 11 cases: ye law kitna kam laagu hota hai

July se December 2024 ke beech police ne Section 72 ke under 11 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani mahine mein do se bhi kam, us desh mein jahan WhatsApp groups, local news pages aur comment sections har high-profile case ki ek-ek detail khodte hain.

Is number ko sahi nazar se padhiye. Ye FIRs ginta hai, posts nahi, aur ye July 2024 se shuru hota hai, isliye compare karne ke liye koi purana data nahi hai. NCRB har FIR mein sirf sabse gambhir offence ginta hai, isliye mumkin hai ki kisi badi crime ke saath laga disclosure ka charge yahan dikhe hi na [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Sochiye ki aisi complaint karega kaun. Jis survivor ki pehchaan leak ho chuki hai, use doosra case shuru karne ke liye phir police station jaana padega, aur aur zyada logon ki nazar mein aane ka risk lena padega. Baaki sab bas scroll karke aage badh sakte hain. Jo law kabhi test hi nahi hota, woh use todne walon ko yahi sikhaata hai ki kuch nahi hoga.

## Post ya forward karne se pehle: ek checklist

Ye rule agar kaam karta hai, toh send dabaane se pehle. Khud se poochiye:

- **Kya use jaanne wala koi use pehchaan sakta hai?** Uska naam, initials, nickname ya photo; uska school, college, office ya gaon; uske pita ka kaam; accused ka naam agar woh uska rishtedaar ya padosi hai. Inme se kuch bhi ho, toh share mat kariye.
- **Kya ye koi document hai?** Rape ya POCSO case ki FIR, medical report ya court ka kaagaz public karne ke liye nahi hai. Ise forward mat kariye, crop karke bhi nahi.
- **Kya ye andaaze ka khel hai?** "Ye wahi ladki hai na jo…?" jaise comments dayra chhota karte jaate hain, jab tak woh mil na jaaye. Aisa khel shuru mat kariye, usme shaamil bhi mat hoiye.
- **Kya uski maut ho chuki hai?** Rule tab bhi laagu hai, aur uska parivaar ise maaf nahi kar sakta; sirf Sessions Judge pehchaan kholne ki ijaazat de sakta hai [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].
- **Kya usne khud bolne ka faisla kiya hai?** Agar kisi adult survivor ne khud saamne aakar baat ki hai, toh uske peeche chaliye: uske apne shabd share kariye, woh details nahi jo usne khud nahi di.
- **Kya kisi aur ne rule toda?** Platform par post report kariye, aur cybercrime.gov.in par complaint kariye ya 1930 par call kariye [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi. Ek case uske chehre ke bina bhi trend kar sakta hai, aur uske naam ke bina bhi maangein utha sakta hai. 2018 ka judgment har reader se ek hi cheez maangta hai: crime ko public rehne dijiye, aur use ek private insaan rehne dijiye.

nirbhaya-fund-money-trail-2013-2026.en:
When the government reports on the Nirbhaya Fund to Parliament, it gives one figure: money "released and utilised". The phrase sounds like help reaching women. It is an accounting line. By July 2026, Rs 6,703.02 crore of the Rs 7,990.85 crore allocated since 2013-14 had been released and used, and Rs 1,287.83 crore had not [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Here is where the money went, what it bought, and how you can use it.

## February 2013: a fund named after a pseudonym

In his Budget speech of February 2013, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said "recent incidents have cast a long, dark shadow on our liberal and progressive credentials". He proposed a Nirbhaya Fund and said the government would contribute Rs 1,000 crore [[indiabudget-speech-2013-14]].

Nirbhaya, "fearless", was never the name of the woman gang-raped and murdered in Delhi in December 2012. It was the name under which the country protested. The Supreme Court later noted that it became India's most effective symbol of protest without her identity ever being revealed [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. A fund in that name carries a promise: that the next woman would find help faster.

## Rs 7,990.85 crore later: spent, released and unspent

Two official snapshots show the money moving:

| Up to | Allocated | Released and used | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-25 (reported March 2025) | Rs 7,712.85 crore | Rs 5,846.08 crore | about 76% |
| 2025-26 (reported July 2026) | Rs 7,990.85 crore | Rs 6,703.02 crore | 83.9% |

The first row is from a government reply in Parliament [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]], the second from a Rajya Sabha reply reported by ThePrint [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. "Released and used" is a single figure, so it cannot show how much was actually spent on services. The ministry says real use may be higher, as states have not sent in all their utilisation certificates [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]].

Three schemes took 63% of everything released: Safe City projects (Rs 1,686.73 crore), One Stop Centres (Rs 1,299.10 crore) and Fast Track Special Courts for rape and POCSO cases (Rs 1,234.55 crore) [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. The biggest slice, Safe City, covers safer public infrastructure and faster police access in just eight cities: Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Lucknow and Mumbai [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. Everywhere else, a woman is likelier to meet the fund at a police station desk or a One Stop Centre.

## What the money bought: help desks, One Stop Centres, compensation, courts

**Help desks.** In December 2019 the Home Ministry sanctioned Rs 100 crore from the fund for Women Help Desks in police stations, to make stations more approachable for women [[pib-mha-women-help-desks-2019]]. By March 2025 there were 14,658, and 13,743 were headed by women officers [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. NCRB warns that such desks can push registered crime up [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That is the point: a complaint finally written down is not a rise in crime.

**One Stop Centres.** In December 2018 the Supreme Court asked every state and union territory to set up at least one One Stop Centre in every district within a year [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. The idea is in the name: one place to go for help. There were 802 in March 2025 [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]] and 926 in March 2026 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-03]]. By July 2026, 985 of the 1,033 approved centres were running, and they had assisted over 15.20 lakh women since April 2015 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

**Compensation.** The Centre released Rs 200 crore from the fund as a one-time grant to states under the Central Victim Compensation Fund, for survivors of rape, acid attacks, crimes against children and trafficking [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. Under NALSA's 2018 scheme, a rape survivor is entitled to Rs 4 lakh to Rs 7 lakh, and the limits are 50% higher for a minor [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

**Courts.** On 4 November 2026 the Cabinet extended the Fast Track Special Courts scheme to 31 March 2031, with Rs 3,788.04 crore and room for up to 850 courts; the central share, Rs 2,353.15 crore, comes from the Nirbhaya Fund [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Paying for courts is not the same as clearing them: 2,45,579 rape and POCSO cases were pending before these courts at the end of 2025 [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]].

## 2025-26: Rs 278 crore, and projects that spent nothing

For 2025-26 the fund was allocated Rs 278 crore, just over a quarter of the Rs 1,000 crore it began with. The government says the fund is a non-lapsable corpus, so each allocation takes account of unspent money already in it [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

Both can be true. A smaller allocation can be sound bookkeeping, and the bookkeeping can hide money that reaches no one. The same reply listed projects still at zero: a Railways pilot of AI-based facial recognition at seven stations and a Panchayati Raj programme to sensitise men were "ongoing" with no spending, while a proposal for CCTV cameras at village panchayats was still awaiting financial approval [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

## How to use what the fund built

Consider a 20-year-old in Lucknow who has been sexually assaulted by a man she knows. The fund has already paid for each step open to her. (This is general information, not legal advice.)

- At the police station, she can ask for the Women Help Desk, which is most likely headed by a woman officer.
- She can go to the district's One Stop Centre, the single point of help the Supreme Court wanted in every district.
- She can apply to the District Legal Services Authority for compensation even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place; the authority must decide within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

If the survivor is a girl under 18 made pregnant by rape, a Nirbhaya Fund scheme launched in November 2023 covers shelter, medical and maternity care, legal aid, counselling and support to keep studying [[mwcd-pocso-victim-support-scheme-2023]].

Money spent in a survivor's name is public money. Follow it: ask what your state received, what it used, and whether the help desk, the centre and the court near you actually work.
nirbhaya-fund-money-trail-2013-2026.hg:
Jab sarkar Parliament ko Nirbhaya Fund ka hisaab deti hai, toh ek hi figure batati hai: kitna paisa "released and utilised" hua. Sunne mein lagta hai ki madad aurton tak pahunch gayi. Asal mein yeh accounting ki ek line hai. July 2026 tak, 2013-14 se allocate hue Rs 7,990.85 crore mein se Rs 6,703.02 crore release aur use hue the, aur Rs 1,287.83 crore nahi [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Yeh rahi poori kahani: paisa kahan gaya, usse kya bana, aur aap uska istemaal kaise kar sakte hain.

## February 2013: ek pseudonym ke naam par fund

February 2013 ke Budget speech mein Finance Minister P. Chidambaram ne kaha, "recent incidents have cast a long, dark shadow on our liberal and progressive credentials", yaani haal ki ghatnaon ne desh ki liberal aur progressive chhavi par ek lamba, kaala saaya daal diya hai. Unhone Nirbhaya Fund ka prastaav rakha aur kaha ki sarkar isme Rs 1,000 crore degi [[indiabudget-speech-2013-14]].

Nirbhaya, yaani "jise darr na ho", December 2012 mein Delhi mein gang rape aur murder ki shikaar hui aurat ka naam kabhi tha hi nahi. Yeh woh naam tha jiske saath desh ne protest kiya. Supreme Court ne baad mein kaha ki uski pehchaan zaahir kiye bina hi yeh naam India mein protest ka sabse asardaar symbol ban gaya [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Us naam par bane fund ke saath ek vaada juda hai: ki agli aurat ko madad jaldi milegi.

## Rs 7,990.85 crore baad: kharch, release aur bina kharch ka paisa

Do official snapshots dikhate hain ki paisa kaise aage badha:

| Kab tak | Allocate hua | Release aur use hua | Hissa |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-25 (March 2025 mein bataya gaya) | Rs 7,712.85 crore | Rs 5,846.08 crore | lagbhag 76% |
| 2025-26 (July 2026 mein bataya gaya) | Rs 7,990.85 crore | Rs 6,703.02 crore | 83.9% |

Pehli row Parliament mein sarkar ke ek jawab se hai [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]], aur doosri Rajya Sabha ke ek jawab se, jise ThePrint ne report kiya [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. "Released and used" ek hi figure hai, isliye isse yeh pata nahi chalta ki services par asal mein kitna kharch hua. Ministry ka kehna hai ki asli use isse zyada ho sakta hai, kyunki states ne saare utilisation certificates nahi bheje hain [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]].

Release hue kul paise ka 63% teen schemes mein gaya: Safe City projects (Rs 1,686.73 crore), One Stop Centres (Rs 1,299.10 crore) aur rape aur POCSO cases ke Fast Track Special Courts (Rs 1,234.55 crore) [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Sabse bada hissa, Safe City, public jagahon ko surakshit banane aur police tak tez pahunch ke liye hai, aur woh bhi sirf aath shehron mein: Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Lucknow aur Mumbai [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. Baaki har jagah, kisi aurat ka is fund se saamna zyada sambhav hai police station ke ek desk par ya kisi One Stop Centre mein.

## Paise se kya bana: help desks, One Stop Centres, compensation, courts

**Help desks.** December 2019 mein Home Ministry ne police stations mein Women Help Desks ke liye fund se Rs 100 crore manzoor kiye, taaki aurton ke liye police station jaana aasaan ho [[pib-mha-women-help-desks-2019]]. March 2025 tak aise 14,658 desks the, aur unme se 13,743 ki head women officers thin [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. NCRB chetata hai ki aise desks se darj crime ke numbers badh sakte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yahi toh maqsad hai: jo complaint aakhirkaar likhi gayi, woh crime mein badhottari nahi hai.

**One Stop Centres.** December 2018 mein Supreme Court ne har state aur union territory se kaha ki ek saal ke andar har district mein kam se kam ek One Stop Centre banaye [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Idea naam mein hi hai: madad ke liye ek jagah. March 2025 mein 802 centres the [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]] aur March 2026 mein 926 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-03]]. July 2026 tak 1,033 approved centres mein se 985 chal rahe the, aur April 2015 se ab tak 15.20 lakh se zyada aurton ki madad kar chuke the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

**Compensation.** Centre ne fund se Rs 200 crore ek baar ki grant ke roop mein Central Victim Compensation Fund ke tahat states ko diye, taaki rape, acid attack, bachchon ke khilaaf crime aur trafficking ke survivors ko compensation mil sake [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. NALSA ki 2018 scheme ke tahat rape survivor Rs 4 lakh se Rs 7 lakh tak ki hakdaar hai, aur minor ke liye yeh limits 50% zyada hain [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

**Courts.** 4 November 2026 ko Cabinet ne Fast Track Special Courts scheme ko 31 March 2031 tak badha diya, Rs 3,788.04 crore aur 850 tak courts ki gunjaish ke saath; Centre ka hissa, Rs 2,353.15 crore, Nirbhaya Fund se aata hai [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Courts ka kharcha uthana aur cases nipataana ek baat nahi hai: 2025 ke aakhir mein in courts mein rape aur POCSO ke 2,45,579 cases pending the [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]].

## 2025-26: Rs 278 crore, aur woh projects jinpar kuch kharch nahi hua

2025-26 ke liye fund ko Rs 278 crore mile, yaani shuruaati Rs 1,000 crore ke ek-chauthai se thoda hi zyada. Sarkar ka kehna hai ki fund ek non-lapsable corpus hai, yaani bina kharch hua paisa isi mein pada rehta hai, isliye har allocation us paise ko dhyaan mein rakhkar tay hota hai [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].
