Dono baatein sach ho sakti hain. Chhota allocation achchi bookkeeping ho sakta hai, aur wahi bookkeeping us paise ko chhupa bhi sakti hai jo kisi tak nahi pahunchta. Usi jawab mein aise projects bhi the jinka kharch zero tha: saat stations par AI-based facial recognition ka Railways pilot aur aadmiyon ko sensitise karne ka Panchayati Raj programme "ongoing" bataye gaye, lekin unpar koi kharch nahi hua tha. Village panchayats mein CCTV cameras lagane ka ek prastaav abhi bhi financial approval ka intezaar kar raha tha [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

## Fund se jo bana, uska istemaal kaise karein

Maan lijiye Lucknow ki ek 20 saal ki ladki ka uske jaan-pehchaan wale ek aadmi ne sexual assault kiya hai. Uske saamne jo bhi raasta hai, uska kharcha fund pehle hi utha chuka hai. (Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.)

- Police station mein woh Women Help Desk maang sakti hai, jiski head zyada tar koi woman officer hoti hai.
- Woh district ke One Stop Centre ja sakti hai, madad ki woh ek jagah jo Supreme Court har district mein chahta tha.
- Woh compensation ke liye District Legal Services Authority mein apply kar sakti hai, chahe offender ka kabhi pata na chale aur trial hi na ho; authority ko do mahine mein faisla karna hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Agar survivor 18 se kam umar ki ladki hai jo rape ki wajah se pregnant ho gayi hai, toh November 2023 mein shuru hui Nirbhaya Fund ki ek scheme rehne ki jagah, medical aur maternity care, legal aid, counselling aur padhai jaari rakhne mein madad deti hai [[mwcd-pocso-victim-support-scheme-2023]].

Survivor ke naam par kharch hone wala paisa public ka paisa hai. Uska peechha kariye: poochiye ki aapke state ko kitna mila, kitna use hua, aur kya aapke paas ka help desk, centre aur court sach mein kaam karte hain.

prajwal-revanna-life-sentence-2025.en:
On 1 August 2025 a special court for cases against MPs and MLAs in Bengaluru convicted Prajwal Revanna, until 2024 the Member of Parliament for Hassan in Karnataka, of rape. The next day Judge Santosh Gajanan Bhat sentenced him to life imprisonment, which on one count means the rest of his natural life [[theprint-revanna-sentence-2025]]. It was the first of four sexual-abuse cases registered against him in 2024 [[tnm-revanna-sentence-2025]].

A convicted person may be named; the woman may not, and nothing here describes her beyond what the court's legal finding needs. She was a domestic worker employed by his family. That fact is the heart of the case.

## The section that names power

The court convicted him under two aggravated forms of rape in the old Indian Penal Code, which still applied because the crimes came before the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) took effect on 1 July 2024. Section 376(2)(k) covers rape by a man "in a position of control or dominance over a woman". Section 376(2)(n) covers repeated rape of the same woman. Each carried life imprisonment. He was also convicted of sexual harassment, assault with intent to disrobe, voyeurism and, under the IT Act, of capturing private images without consent [[theprint-revanna-sentence-2025]] [[tnm-revanna-sentence-2025]].

Read that first section again. The law does not treat rape by an employer as an ordinary rape that happens to involve an employer. It treats the power itself as making the crime worse. A woman who depends on a household for her wages and her roof cannot freely refuse, and cannot easily leave or complain. Parliament wrote that into the definition of the aggravated offence.

This is not rare. In 96.8% of the rape cases police registered across India in 2024, the offender was someone the woman knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The stranger in the dark is the exception. The boss, the relative, the landlord and the "family" a worker lives with are the rule.

## How the case came to court

The case did not begin with a complaint that police took seriously on the first day. It began in April 2024, when sexually explicit videos involving the MP circulated in Hassan. The Karnataka government set up a Special Investigation Team on 27 April 2024. He left India for Germany, and was arrested at Bengaluru airport on 31 May 2024 when he returned [[scroll-revanna-sentence-2025]] [[wikipedia-prajwal-revanna]].

So the conviction came about 14 months after his arrest. Compare that with the system most women meet. Courts completed 20,587 rape trials in 2024 and convicted in 24.4% of them; 1,85,785 rape cases were still waiting for trial at the end of that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A dedicated investigation team, a special court for legislators and a national spotlight moved this case faster than most. The verdict shows the law can reach a powerful man. It does not show that it usually does.

## Appeal, and what is still open

He has appealed. On 3 December 2025 the Karnataka High Court refused to suspend his sentence while the appeal is heard, noting the gravity of the offence and that "the witnesses in other cases are likely to be tampered with" if he were released. It listed the appeal for final hearing on 12 January 2026 [[livelaw-revanna-hc-suspension-2025]]. We could not find a final ruling as of 23 November 2026, and the other cases against him were still at trial when the High Court ruled.

The court's words are worth noticing. In the cases of powerful men, the fear of witnesses being pressured is not abstract. That fear is one reason many women who work in homes, farms and offices never complain at all.

## The other victims: the women in the videos

The videos that broke this case open were themselves a form of abuse. Every woman in them was exposed without her consent, and each time a clip was forwarded, the harm was repeated. Under the BNS, voyeurism is punishable with one to three years for a first conviction [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and revealing the identity of a rape victim is a separate crime under Section 72 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Since November 2025, a government procedure requires platforms to remove flagged non-consensual intimate images within 24 hours [[pib-meity-ncii-sop-2025]].

## If you work in someone's home

Consider a 30-year-old woman who cooks and cleans for a wealthy family in Mysuru and lives in their outhouse. The son of the house begins to corner her. She has no HR department. The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act protects any woman employed in a house, including a domestic worker [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Her complaint goes to the district's Local Committee, which must send a prima facie case to the police within seven days [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Rape is a crime she can report directly to the police, at any station.

The Revanna verdict matters because it says, in a court's voice, that the dependence of a worker on an employer makes rape worse, not more forgivable. The test for India is whether the next woman, in a house without cameras or a scandal, is believed as quickly. This is general information, not legal advice. Images shared without consent can be reported at cybercrime.gov.in or on 1930 [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].
prajwal-revanna-life-sentence-2025.hg:
1 August 2025 ko Bengaluru mein MPs aur MLAs ke cases sunne wali special court ne Prajwal Revanna ko rape ka doshi paaya. Woh 2024 tak Karnataka ke Hassan se Member of Parliament the. Agle din Judge Santosh Gajanan Bhat ne unhe umrqaid ki saza di, jo ek count par unki baaki poori natural life tak hai [[theprint-revanna-sentence-2025]]. Yeh 2024 mein unke khilaaf register hue sexual abuse ke chaar cases mein se pehla tha [[tnm-revanna-sentence-2025]].

Convict ka naam liya ja sakta hai; aurat ka nahi. Hum uske baare mein utna hi likhenge jitna court ki legal finding ke liye zaroori hai. Woh unke parivaar ke ghar kaam karne wali domestic worker thi. Yahi baat is case ka dil hai.

## Woh section jo power ka naam leta hai

Court ne unhe purane Indian Penal Code ke do aggravated rape provisions mein doshi paaya. IPC isliye laagu hua kyunki crime Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke 1 July 2024 se laagu hone se pehle ke the. Section 376(2)(k) us aadmi ke rape ke liye hai jo aurat par "position of control or dominance" mein ho, yaani jiska aurat par control ya dabdaba ho. Section 376(2)(n) ek hi aurat ke saath baar-baar rape ke liye hai. Dono mein umrqaid mili. Unhe sexual harassment, kapde utaarne ki niyat se hamla, voyeurism aur IT Act ke under bina consent private images lene ka bhi doshi paaya gaya [[theprint-revanna-sentence-2025]] [[tnm-revanna-sentence-2025]].

Pehla section dobara padhiye. Law employer ke rape ko ek aam rape nahi maanta jisme bas employer shaamil ho. Woh power ko hi crime ko aur bhaari banane wali cheez maanta hai. Jo aurat apni tankhwah aur sar ki chhat ke liye ek ghar par depend karti hai, woh azaadi se mana nahi kar sakti, aur aasaani se chhod ya complaint bhi nahi kar sakti. Parliament ne yahi baat aggravated offence ki definition mein likh di.

Yeh koi rare baat nahi hai. 2024 mein poore India mein police ne jo rape cases register kiye, unme se 96.8% mein offender aurat ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Andhere mein khada ajnabi exception hai. Boss, rishtedaar, makaan-maalik aur woh "parivaar" jiske saath worker rehti hai, yahi rule hai.

## Case court tak kaise pahuncha

Yeh case kisi aisi complaint se shuru nahi hua jise police ne pehle hi din seriously liya ho. Yeh April 2024 mein shuru hua, jab Hassan mein us MP se jude sexually explicit videos circulate hue. Karnataka sarkar ne 27 April 2024 ko Special Investigation Team banayi. Woh India chhod kar Germany chale gaye, aur 31 May 2024 ko lautne par Bengaluru airport par arrest hue [[scroll-revanna-sentence-2025]] [[wikipedia-prajwal-revanna]].

Yaani conviction arrest ke kareeb 14 mahine baad aaya. Ab us system se tulna kijiye jisse zyadatar aurtein guzarti hain. 2024 mein courts ne 20,587 rape trials poore kiye aur unme se 24.4% mein conviction hua; us saal ke end mein 1,85,785 rape cases trial ke intezaar mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek dedicated investigation team, legislators ke liye special court aur poore desh ki nazar ne is case ko zyadatar cases se tez chalaya. Verdict dikhata hai ki law ek taqatwar aadmi tak pahunch sakta hai. Yeh nahi dikhata ki aam taur par pahunchta hai.

## Appeal, aur kya abhi khula hai

Unhone appeal ki hai. 3 December 2025 ko Karnataka High Court ne appeal ki sunwai ke dauraan unki saza suspend karne se mana kar diya. Court ne crime ki gambhirta dekhi aur kaha ki release hone par "the witnesses in other cases are likely to be tampered with", yaani doosre cases ke gawahon par dabaav ka khatra hai. Appeal ki final hearing 12 January 2026 ko list hui [[livelaw-revanna-hc-suspension-2025]]. 23 November 2026 tak humein koi final faisla nahi mila, aur High Court ke order ke waqt unke khilaaf baaki cases trial mein the.

Court ke shabd dhyaan dene layak hain. Taqatwar aadmiyon ke cases mein gawahon par dabaav ka darr koi theory nahi hai. Yahi darr ek wajah hai ki gharon, kheton aur offices mein kaam karne wali bahut si aurtein kabhi complaint hi nahi karti.

## Doosre victims: videos wali aurtein

Jin videos ne yeh case khola, woh khud ek tarah ka abuse the. Unme dikhne wali har aurat bina consent ke expose hui, aur har forward ke saath nuksaan dobara hua. BNS mein voyeurism par pehli baar 1 se 3 saal ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur rape victim ki identity reveal karna Section 72 ke under alag crime hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. November 2025 se ek sarkari procedure ke under platforms ko flag ki gayi non-consensual intimate images 24 ghante mein hatani hoti hain [[pib-meity-ncii-sop-2025]].

## Agar aap kisi ke ghar kaam karti hain

Sochiye, Mysuru mein ek 30 saal ki aurat ek ameer parivaar ke liye khaana banati aur safai karti hai, aur unke outhouse mein rehti hai. Ghar ka beta use akele mein gherne lagta hai. Uske paas koi HR department nahi. Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act ghar mein kaam karne wali har aurat ko protect karta hai, domestic worker ko bhi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Uski complaint district ki Local Committee mein jaati hai, jise prima facie case saat din mein police ko bhejna hota hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Rape ki report woh seedhe kisi bhi police station mein kar sakti hai.

Revanna verdict isliye maayne rakhta hai kyunki yeh court ki awaaz mein kehta hai ki worker ki employer par nirbharta rape ko aur gambhir banati hai, maaf karne layak nahi. India ka asli imtihaan yeh hai ki agli aurat, jiske ghar mein na camera hai na scandal, kya utni hi jaldi believe ki jaayegi. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Bina consent share ki gayi images cybercrime.gov.in par ya 1930 par report ki ja sakti hain [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

pune-bus-depot-rape-case-2025.en:
On 25 February 2025 a woman was allegedly raped inside a parked state transport bus at Swargate, one of Pune's main bus stations, run by the Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) [[theprint-msrtc-audit-2025]].

This file does not describe her or the crime. The accused has not been convicted, so he is not named. What follows is the response: what the police and the state did, how fast, and what is still unfinished.

## A public place that became private

Most rapes in India are committed by someone the woman knows: 96.8% of cases registered in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Cases like Swargate are rarer, and that is exactly why they shake people. They happen in places everyone uses and assumes someone is watching: a bus stand, a station, a parked vehicle.

Pune city registered 244 rape cases in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Very few of them were in a bus depot. But the Swargate case exposed something every city has: buses parked and unlocked for hours, corners with no light, guards stretched thin, and a "public" space that becomes private the moment the crowd leaves.

## Two days to an audit, two weeks to suspensions

The state's first response came fast. Two days after the crime, Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik ordered a security audit of every MSRTC bus station and depot in Maharashtra, replaced the security guards at Swargate, and said buses lying parked in depots would be disposed of [[theprint-msrtc-audit-2025]].

In March 2025 he told the state Assembly that four MSRTC officials, including the senior and junior depot managers, had been suspended for negligence after an inquiry, and that 22 security guards posted at Swargate had been transferred [[fpj-msrtc-suspensions-2025]].

> Suspensions answer the question "who failed here?" An audit answers "where else could this happen?" Only the second protects the next passenger.

Whether the audit's findings were published, and what was fixed depot by depot, is something we could not confirm. That is the question a passenger can ask.

## The investigation: fast by Indian standards

The accused fled and was caught in farm fields near his village after a manhunt that used drones and sniffer dogs [[tribune-pune-chargesheet-2025]]. In mid-April 2025, less than two months after the crime, Pune Police filed an 893-page chargesheet with statements of 82 witnesses and physical, biological, technical and scientific evidence, including CCTV footage [[tribune-pune-chargesheet-2025]].

That met the law's deadline. The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) requires police to complete a rape investigation within two months of recording the information [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## The trial: where speed runs out

The same law says a rape trial should be completed within two months of the chargesheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. By that measure the Swargate trial should have ended in mid-2025. Instead, charges were framed only around June 2026, more than a year after the chargesheet, with the prosecution listing 87 witnesses [[bridgechronicle-swargate-charges-2026]]. In November 2026 the sessions court had only begun recording the woman's own evidence, and there was no verdict as of 23 November 2026 [[puneprimenews-swargate-trial-2026]].

That is not unusual. At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial across India [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Delay has a human cost. Each month the survivor must stay ready to testify, and each adjournment can mean preparing again to relive the worst day of her life in a courtroom, in front of the man accused of it. A fast chargesheet is a police achievement. A fast verdict needs judges, prosecutors, forensic labs and witnesses, all available at once, and the system rarely lines them up.

## What a passenger can expect, and demand

Consider a college student in Nagpur who takes the last bus home twice a week. What should the system owe her? A lit, staffed waiting area. Parked buses locked. Guards who walk the yard, not only the gate. CCTV that is watched, not just recorded. A helpline that answers.

And if the worst happens, the law gives her rights wherever she is. She can report at any police station, which must register a Zero FIR even if the crime happened in another area [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Any hospital, government or private, must give her immediate treatment free of cost [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

The Swargate case showed a state can act within days when a crime becomes national news. The real test is whether the audits and fixes outlast the headlines, and whether the trial ends in time to matter. This is general information, not legal advice.
pune-bus-depot-rape-case-2025.hg:
25 February 2025 ko Pune ke mukhya bus stations mein se ek, Swargate, par khadi ek state transport bus mein ek aurat ka kathit rape hua. Yeh station Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) chalata hai [[theprint-msrtc-audit-2025]].

Yeh file na uske baare mein kuch batati hai, na crime ka description deti hai. Accused ka conviction nahi hua hai, isliye uska naam nahi liya gaya. Aage jo hai woh response hai: police aur state ne kya kiya, kitni jaldi, aur kya abhi adhoora hai.

## Ek public jagah jo private ban gayi

India mein zyadatar rape woh log karte hain jinhe aurat jaanti hai: 2024 mein register hue 96.8% cases mein aisa tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Swargate jaise cases kam hote hain, aur isiliye logon ko hila dete hain. Yeh un jagahon par hote hain jinhe sab use karte hain aur maante hain ki koi na koi dekh raha hai: bus stand, station, khadi gaadi.

2024 mein Pune city mein 244 rape cases register hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Unme se bahut kam kisi bus depot mein the. Lekin Swargate case ne woh cheez saamne rakhi jo har shehar mein hai: ghanton khuli khadi buses, bina roshni ke kone, kam guards, aur ek "public" jagah jo bheed jaate hi private ban jaati hai.

## Audit mein do din, suspension mein do hafte

State ka pehla jawab tez tha. Crime ke do din baad Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik ne Maharashtra ke har MSRTC bus station aur depot ka security audit order kiya, Swargate ke security guards badle, aur kaha ki depots mein khadi buses hata di jaayengi [[theprint-msrtc-audit-2025]].

March 2025 mein unhone state Assembly ko bataya ki inquiry ke baad MSRTC ke chaar officials, senior aur junior depot managers samet, laparwahi ke liye suspend kiye gaye, aur Swargate par tainaat 22 security guards transfer kiye gaye [[fpj-msrtc-suspensions-2025]].

> Suspension is sawaal ka jawab hai ki "yahan kaun fail hua?" Audit is sawaal ka jawab hai ki "aur kahan yeh ho sakta hai?" Agle passenger ko sirf doosra wala bachata hai.

Audit ki findings public hui ya nahi, aur har depot mein kya theek hua, yeh hum confirm nahi kar paaye. Yahi sawaal ek passenger pooch sakta hai.

## Investigation: Indian standard se tez

Accused bhaag gaya tha, aur drones aur sniffer dogs wale search ke baad apne gaon ke paas kheton mein pakda gaya [[tribune-pune-chargesheet-2025]]. April 2025 ke beech mein, crime ke do mahine se kam samay mein, Pune Police ne 893 pages ki chargesheet file ki, jisme 82 gawahon ke bayaan aur physical, biological, technical aur scientific evidence tha, CCTV footage samet [[tribune-pune-chargesheet-2025]].

Yeh law ki deadline ke andar tha. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) kehti hai ki police ko information record karne ke do mahine ke andar rape ki investigation poori karni hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Trial: jahan speed khatam ho jaati hai

Wahi law kehta hai ki rape trial chargesheet ke do mahine ke andar poora hona chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Is hisaab se Swargate trial 2025 ke beech tak khatam ho jaana chahiye tha. Iske bajaay charges lagbhag June 2026 mein jaakar frame hue, chargesheet ke ek saal se bhi zyada baad, aur prosecution ne 87 gawahon ki list di [[bridgechronicle-swargate-charges-2026]]. November 2026 mein sessions court ne aurat ki apni gawahi record karna abhi shuru hi kiya tha, aur 23 November 2026 tak koi verdict nahi aaya tha [[puneprimenews-swargate-trial-2026]].

Yeh anokha nahi hai. 2024 ke end mein poore India mein 1,85,785 rape cases trial mein pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Deri ki ek insaani keemat hoti hai. Har mahine survivor ko gawahi ke liye taiyar rehna padta hai, aur har adjournment ka matlab ho sakta hai ki use apni zindagi ka sabse bura din phir se courtroom mein, us aadmi ke saamne jis par aarop hai, jeene ki taiyari karni pade. Tez chargesheet police ki kaamyaabi hai. Tez verdict ke liye judges, prosecutors, forensic labs aur gawah, sab ek saath chahiye, aur system unhe kam hi ek line mein laata hai.

## Passenger kya ummeed kar sakti hai, aur kya maang sakti hai

Sochiye, Nagpur ki ek college student hafte mein do baar aakhri bus se ghar jaati hai. System uska kya karzdaar hai? Roshni aur staff wala waiting area. Khadi buses par taala. Guards jo sirf gate par nahi, poore yard mein ghoomein. CCTV jise koi dekhe bhi, sirf record na ho. Ek helpline jo phone uthaye.

Aur agar sabse bura ho jaaye, toh law use har jagah adhikaar deta hai. Woh kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakti hai, jise Zero FIR register karni hogi chahe crime kisi aur ilaake mein hua ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Har hospital, sarkari ho ya private, use turant aur free ilaaj dene ke liye bound hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Swargate case ne dikhaya ki jab koi crime national news banta hai toh state kuch dinon mein kadam utha sakta hai. Asli imtihaan yeh hai ki audits aur sudhaar headlines ke baad bhi tikte hain ya nahi, aur trial waqt rehte khatam hota hai ya nahi. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

rajasthan-1992-gang-rape-vishaka-workpla.en:
Every working woman in India can take a complaint of sexual harassment to a committee that must hear her. That right was built on a 1992 gang rape whose five accused were all acquitted of rape. The survivor has campaigned under her own name for three decades, but we do not print survivors' names, so we call her by the job the state gave her: saathin.

## A saathin who tried to stop child marriages

A saathin ("friend") was a village-level worker in the Rajasthan government's Women's Development Programme; her work included campaigning against child marriages. On 22 September 1992 she was gang-raped in her village [[bbc-bhanwari-2017]]. She filed an FIR and testified that dominant-caste men had attacked and raped her in retaliation [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

By her account, she was attacked for doing the work the state had given her, and no workplace system existed to answer that. Looking back at the years before the Vishaka guidelines, a Delhi court noted in 2021 the "systematic abuse at the workplace due to lack of the mechanism to redress the grievance of sexual-harassment" [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]].

## 1995: five acquittals and the reasoning behind them

In November 1995 a district and sessions court in Jaipur acquitted all five accused of rape [[bbc-bhanwari-2017]]. We do not name them.

The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes lists what that trial court observed: that dominant-caste men would not rape an oppressed-caste woman; that men of different castes would not join in a gang rape; that older men could not take part in one; and that it was improbable a woman could be raped in front of her husband [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

None of these is evidence. Each is an assumption about who rapes and how, used to disbelieve a woman. The same handbook now calls the caste belief a stereotype and states: "Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

The state appealed. In 2017 the BBC reported that the Rajasthan High Court had heard the appeal just once in 22 years [[bbc-bhanwari-2017]]. We could not confirm where it stands today.

## Vishaka (1997): the Supreme Court writes the rules Parliament had not

A petition followed, Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan, prompted by what the Supreme Court described as the alleged "brutal gang rape of a social worker in a village of Rajasthan". On 13 August 1997 a bench headed by Chief Justice J.S. Verma laid down binding guidelines against sexual harassment at work, to be treated as law under Article 141 until Parliament passed one [[sc-vishaka-rajasthan-1997]].

The guidelines defined sexual harassment as unwelcome sexually determined behaviour: physical contact and advances, a demand or request for sexual favours, sexually coloured remarks, showing pornography, or any other unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. A criminal court had failed one woman; a petition prompted by her case gave every working woman rules to rely on.

## Nearly 16 years to a law, and a decade of non-compliance

Parliament took nearly 16 years. The POSH Act was published in the Gazette as Act No. 14 of 2013 on 23 April 2013 [[pib-law-posh-act-gazette-2013]] and came into force on 9 December 2013 [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]]. Before the Act and since, the Supreme Court has had to chase enforcement:

- **19 October 2012:** finding that several states had not complied with Vishaka, the Court ordered complaints committees at taluka, district and state level, warning that laws "with sloppy enforcement are not enough" [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]].
- **12 May 2023:** it found "serious lapses in the enforcement" of the Act, and noted that many harassed women "even drop out from their job" [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]].
- **3 December 2024:** it ordered every state to name a District Officer for each district by 31 December 2024 and set up Local Committees by 31 January 2025 [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].
- **By May 2025:** every state had District Officers, but Local Committee compliance was unclear in Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand and Kerala [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].
- **12 August 2025:** told, LiveLaw reported, that only the Andaman and Nicobar Islands had completed the district-wise survey of Internal Committees, the Court gave states and union territories six weeks to finish it [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]].

Look at where the gaps sit. One is the Local Committee, meant for women in small workplaces and domestic work, whose working lives look most like the saathin's. The other is the survey meant to show whether employers have Internal Committees at all. Three decades after her case, the state still cannot say how many workplaces follow the law it produced.

## Your rights at work: Internal Committee, Local Committee and SHe-Box

This is general information, not legal advice.

- Every workplace with 10 or more workers must have an Internal Committee [[indiacode-posh-2013]], headed by a senior woman employee and including an outside member; at least half its members must be women [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- Fewer than 10 workers, a complaint against the employer, or domestic work: go to your district's Local Committee [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- "Workplace" includes places you visit for work, transport your employer provides, and homes where domestic workers are employed [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- Complain in writing within three months of the incident, or of the last one in a series; the committee can allow three more months if circumstances stopped you. The inquiry must finish within 90 days [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. An employer who fails to set up an Internal Committee can be fined up to Rs 50,000, and twice that for a repeat [[indiacode-posh-2013]].
- You can also complain on SHe-Box, the government's online portal [[shebox]].

Consider this situation: a woman cooks in three homes in Pune, and in one an adult son keeps making sexual remarks. She has no HR department. Under the POSH Act that home is her workplace, and her complaint goes to her district's Local Committee, if one exists. If it finds a prima facie case, it must forward her complaint to the police within seven days [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. In a Jagori study of 270 women domestic workers in Delhi-NCR, surveyed in 2024, 24% had faced sexual harassment in the previous two years [[jagori-domestic-workers-report-2025]].

The woman whose case started this law saw all five accused acquitted of rape. The committees exist because of her. Use them.
rajasthan-1992-gang-rape-vishaka-workpla.hg:
India mein har working woman ko ye haq hai ki woh sexual harassment ki complaint ek committee ke paas le jaaye, aur us committee ko uski baat sunni hi padegi. Ye haq 1992 ke ek gang rape ki neenv par khada hai, jiske paanchon accused rape ke charge se bari ho gaye. Survivor teen dashak se apne naam ke saath ye ladaai lad rahi hain, lekin ye magazine kisi survivor ka naam nahi chhaapti. Isliye hum unhe usi kaam ke naam se bulaayenge jo sarkar ne unhe diya tha: saathin.

## Ek saathin jo child marriages rokne nikli thi

Saathin yaani "friend". Ye Rajasthan sarkar ke Women's Development Programme mein village-level worker ka kaam tha, aur unke kaam mein child marriages ke khilaaf campaign chalana bhi shaamil tha. 22 September 1992 ko unke hi gaon mein unke saath gang rape hua [[bbc-bhanwari-2017]]. Unhone FIR darj karayi aur bayaan diya ki dominant caste ke aadmiyon ne badla lene ke liye un par hamla kiya aur rape kiya [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Yaani unke bayaan ke mutaabik, un par hamla usi kaam ki wajah se hua jo sarkar ne unhe diya tha. Aur workplace par aisi baat sunne ka koi system tha hi nahi. Vishaka guidelines se pehle ke daur ko dekhte hue 2021 mein Delhi ki ek court ne "systematic abuse at the workplace due to lack of the mechanism to redress the grievance of sexual-harassment" ki baat ki, yaani complaint sunne ka mechanism na hone ki wajah se workplace par aurton ke saath lagaataar abuse hota raha [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]].

## 1995: paanchon accused bari, aur uske peeche ke tark

November 1995 mein Jaipur ki district and sessions court ne paanchon accused ko rape ke charge se bari kar diya [[bbc-bhanwari-2017]]. Hum unke naam nahi likhte.

Supreme Court ki 2023 ki gender stereotypes wali handbook batati hai ki us trial court ne kya kaha tha: ki dominant caste ke aadmi oppressed caste ki aurat ka rape nahi karenge; ki alag-alag castes ke aadmi milkar gang rape nahi karenge; ki badi umar ke aadmi gang rape mein shaamil nahi ho sakte; aur ki pati ke saamne kisi aurat ka rape hona mumkin nahi lagta [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Inme se ek bhi baat saboot nahi hai. Har baat sirf ek dhaarna hai ki rape kaun karta hai aur kaise, aur isi dhaarna ke sahaare ek aurat ki baat ko jhootha maan liya gaya. Ab wahi handbook caste wali is soch ko stereotype maanti hai aur saaf likhti hai: "Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies", yaani dominant caste ke aadmiyon ne caste ki oonch-neech banaye rakhne ke liye lambe samay se sexual violence ko hathiyaar banaya hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

State ne appeal ki. 2017 mein BBC ne report kiya ki Rajasthan High Court ne 22 saal mein is appeal ki sunwai sirf ek baar ki thi [[bbc-bhanwari-2017]]. Aaj appeal kis haal mein hai, ye hum confirm nahi kar paaye.

## Vishaka (1997): jo rules Parliament ne nahi banaye, Supreme Court ne likh diye

Iske baad ek petition aayi, Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan. Supreme Court ne bataya ki ye petition Rajasthan ke ek gaon mein ek social worker ke kathit gang rape ke baad aayi, jise court ne "brutal gang rape of a social worker in a village of Rajasthan" kaha. 13 August 1997 ko Chief Justice J.S. Verma ki bench ne workplace sexual harassment ke khilaaf binding guidelines banayin, aur kaha ki jab tak Parliament law nahi banati, tab tak Article 141 ke under yahi guidelines law maani jaayengi [[sc-vishaka-rajasthan-1997]].

Guidelines ne sexual harassment ka matlab saaf kiya: koi bhi unwelcome sexual behaviour, jaise bina marzi chhoona ya advances, sexual favours ki demand ya request, sexually coloured remarks, pornography dikhana, ya sexual nature ka koi bhi doosra unwelcome behaviour [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. Ek criminal court ne ek aurat ko insaaf nahi diya; uske case se nikli petition ne har working woman ko rules de diye.

## Law banne mein lagbhag 16 saal, aur phir saalon tak non-compliance

Parliament ko lagbhag 16 saal lage. POSH Act 23 April 2013 ko Gazette mein Act No. 14 of 2013 ke roop mein chhapa [[pib-law-posh-act-gazette-2013]] aur 9 December 2013 se laagu hua [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]]. Act se pehle bhi aur uske baad bhi, Supreme Court ko ise laagu karwane ke liye baar-baar peeche padna pada:

- **19 October 2012:** court ne paaya ki kai states ne Vishaka ka paalan nahi kiya. Usne taluka, district aur state level par complaints committees banane ka order diya, aur warning di ki laws "with sloppy enforcement are not enough", yaani dheele amal wale law kaafi nahi [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]].
- **12 May 2023:** court ne Act ko laagu karne mein "serious lapses in the enforcement" paaye, aur kaha ki harassment jhelne wali kai aurtein "even drop out from their job", yaani naukri tak chhod deti hain [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]].
- **3 December 2024:** court ne har state se kaha ki 31 December 2024 tak har district ke liye District Officer tay karein aur 31 January 2025 tak Local Committees banayein [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].
- **May 2025 tak:** har state ne District Officers tay kar diye the, lekin Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand aur Kerala mein Local Committees ki haalat saaf nahi thi [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].
- **12 August 2025:** LiveLaw ki report ke mutaabik court ko bataya gaya ki Internal Committees ka district-wise survey sirf Andaman and Nicobar Islands ne poora kiya hai. Court ne states aur UTs ko ise poora karne ke liye chhe hafte diye [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]].

Ab dekhiye ki kami kahan hai. Ek kami Local Committee mein hai, jo chhoti workplaces aur gharon mein kaam karne wali aurton ke liye hai, yaani un aurton ke liye jinki working life saathin se sabse zyada milti hai. Doosri kami us survey mein hai jisse pata chalna tha ki employers ne Internal Committee banayi bhi hai ya nahi. Saathin ke case ke teen dashak baad bhi sarkar ye nahi bata sakti ki kitni workplaces us law ko maan rahi hain jo unke case se nikla.

## Workplace par aapke haq: Internal Committee, Local Committee aur SHe-Box

Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

- Jis workplace par 10 ya usse zyada log kaam karte hain, wahan Internal Committee honi chahiye [[indiacode-posh-2013]]. Iski head koi senior woman employee hogi, isme ek bahar ka member bhi hoga, aur kam se kam aadhe members aurtein hongi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- Agar aapki workplace par 10 se kam log kaam karte hain, complaint khud employer ke khilaaf hai, ya aap domestic worker hain, toh apne district ki Local Committee mein jaaiye [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- Law mein "workplace" ka matlab bada hai: kaam ke silsile mein aap jahan jaati hain, employer ki di hui gaadi, aur woh ghar jahan domestic workers kaam karti hain, sab isme aate hain [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- Incident ke teen mahine ke andar written complaint kariye; agar harassment baar-baar hua, toh aakhri incident ke teen mahine ke andar. Agar kisi wajah se aap time par complaint nahi kar paayin, toh committee teen mahine aur de sakti hai. Inquiry 90 din mein poori honi chahiye [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Jo employer Internal Committee nahi banata, us par Rs 50,000 tak ka fine lag sakta hai, aur dobara galti par double [[indiacode-posh-2013]].
- Aap sarkar ke online portal SHe-Box par bhi complaint register kar sakti hain [[shebox]].

Sochiye ye situation: Pune mein ek aurat teen gharon mein khaana banati hai, aur inme se ek ghar mein maalik ka bada beta baar-baar sexual remarks karta hai. Uske paas koi HR department nahi hai. POSH Act ke hisaab se woh ghar uski workplace hai, aur uski complaint uske district ki Local Committee sunegi, agar woh bani hui ho. Agar committee ko pehli nazar mein case banta dikhe, toh use saat din ke andar complaint police ko bhejni hogi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Jagori ki ek study ke liye 2024 mein Delhi-NCR ki 270 domestic worker aurton se baat ki gayi; inme se 24% ne bataya ki pichhle do saal mein unka sexual harassment hua tha [[jagori-domestic-workers-report-2025]].

Jis aurat ke case se ye law shuru hua, unhone paanchon accused ko rape ke charge se bari hote dekha. Ye committees unki wajah se hain. Inka istemaal kariye.

rape-trials-moved-out-of-state.en:
In four of India's most closely followed sexual violence cases, the trial was held outside the state where the crime happened. The Kathua trial went to Punjab. The Unnao cases went from Lucknow to Delhi. The Muzaffarpur shelter home trial went from Bihar to Delhi. The 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case was tried in Mumbai. Every one of those trials ended in convictions. Read together, the verdicts are also a record of what went wrong back home: policemen convicted of destroying evidence, a police officer convicted of recording an FIR incorrectly, a survivor's father dead in custody.

## Four cases, four relocations

On 7 May 2018 a Supreme Court bench headed by Chief Justice Dipak Misra moved the Kathua rape and murder trial out of Jammu and Kashmir to Pathankot, and ordered it held in camera and day to day [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]]. The Supreme Court moved every Unnao case from Lucknow to Delhi [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. On 7 February 2019 it sent the Muzaffarpur shelter home trial to a POCSO court in Saket, Delhi [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]]. The 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case was moved out of Gujarat and tried by a special court in Mumbai [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]].

In the Kathua, Unnao and Muzaffarpur cases the order came from the Supreme Court itself. A transfer does not change the charges or the evidence. It changes the courtroom, and the distance between the witnesses and the people they are testifying against.

## What the transfers produced: the verdicts

| Case | Tried in | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case | Mumbai | 2008: 11 men sentenced to life; a police officer convicted of recording the FIR incorrectly [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]] |
| Kathua, 2018 | Pathankot | 2019: 6 of 7 accused convicted [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]] |
| Unnao, 2017 | Delhi | 2019: a former MLA jailed for the rest of his life, with a Rs 25 lakh fine [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]] |
| Muzaffarpur shelter home, 2018 | Saket, Delhi | 2020: 19 of 20 accused convicted; 11 later got life terms [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]] |

The Muzaffarpur verdict came less than a year after the transfer, and the Kathua verdict just over a year after it. In Kathua, three men got life imprisonment for murder, with 25 years for gang rape, and one accused was acquitted [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. In the Gujarat case, the Bombay High Court in 2017 upheld all 11 convictions and also convicted the five police personnel and two doctors the trial court had acquitted [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. The Unnao convict has appealed; in May 2026 the Supreme Court set aside the Delhi High Court's suspension of his sentence and asked that court either to decide the appeal quickly or to pass a fresh order [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]].

A new address does not create evidence: one accused was acquitted in Kathua and one in Muzaffarpur. What a transfer can do is let the evidence that exists be tested away from the people who might bend it.

## What the verdicts say about local police and power

Look at who else was convicted. In Kathua, three of the six were policemen, sentenced to five years each for destroying evidence [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. In the Gujarat case, a police officer was convicted of deliberately recording the FIR incorrectly [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. In Unnao, the survivor's father was arrested on an illegal-firearms charge after an assault in April 2018 and died in custody; in 2020 a Delhi court sentenced the former MLA and six others to 10 years for culpable homicide over his death [[barandbench-unnao-father-2020]]. In Muzaffarpur, the abuse happened in a state-funded shelter home, and it was a social audit by the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, done for the state government, that flagged it [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]].

That is the uncomfortable pattern in these verdicts: in more than one case, people whose job was to record the crime and protect the evidence were themselves convicted. A transfer protects one trial. It does nothing to change the police station the case came from.

Imagine a family in a district town whose daughter has accused the son of a local strongman. The investigating officer knows the accused's family. Supporters crowd the court corridor on hearing days. Even an honest judge cannot protect a witness who has to take the same bus home. That is the kind of situation in which a family asks for a trial to be moved.

## Remission: why the trial's location mattered again in 2024

On 15 August 2022 the 11 men serving life in the Gujarat case walked out of Godhra jail after the Gujarat government granted them remission [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. On 8 January 2024 the Supreme Court quashed it. Gujarat, it held, had no power to grant remission, because Maharashtra, where the trial was held, was the appropriate government. The court also found that its own May 2022 order directing Gujarat to decide the question had been obtained by suppressing facts and by fraud [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. All 11 surrendered at Godhra sub-jail late on the night of 21 January 2024 [[scroll-bilkis-surrender-2024]].

So a transfer moves more than a courtroom. In this case it decided, years later, which government controls a convict's release.

## Asking for a fair trial: transfer, protection and the state's duties

The Kathua, Unnao and Muzaffarpur orders show that the Supreme Court can move a trial to another state. Whether that is possible in your case is a question for a lawyer. Whatever the route, a record helps: keep a dated note of every threat and a copy of every written complaint you make to the police or the court.

The law also gives protections that need no transfer. Rape and POCSO trials must be held in camera, as far as practicable before a woman judge [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A victim is entitled to an update on the investigation within 90 days and to a hearing before any prosecution is withdrawn [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. For Dalit and Adivasi survivors, Section 15A of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act makes it the state's duty to protect victims, their dependants and witnesses from intimidation, and gives victims the right to timely notice of court hearings, including bail hearings [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

This is general information, not legal advice. A District Legal Services Authority can provide free legal aid for these applications [[nalsa]].

A survivor should not need Pathankot, Delhi or Mumbai to get a fair trial. Until local police everywhere earn that trust, families should know that the Supreme Court has moved trials before, and which protections they can ask for where they are.
rape-trials-moved-out-of-state.hg:
India ke chaar sabse zyada dekhe gaye sexual violence cases mein trial us state ke bahar chala jahan crime hua tha. Kathua ka trial Punjab gaya. Unnao ke cases Lucknow se Delhi gaye. Muzaffarpur shelter home ka trial Bihar se Delhi gaya. 2002 ke Gujarat riots gang rape case ka trial Mumbai mein chala. In sabhi trials ka ant convictions par hua. Saath mein padhein toh yeh verdicts is baat ka record bhi hain ki ghar par kya galat hua: evidence mitane ke doshi policewale, FIR galat record karne ka doshi ek police officer, aur custody mein mara ek survivor ka pita.

## Chaar cases, chaar nayi jagahein

7 May 2018 ko Chief Justice Dipak Misra ki aguwai wali Supreme Court bench ne Kathua rape aur murder trial ko Jammu and Kashmir se bahar Pathankot bhej diya, aur order diya ki trial in camera chale aur rozana sunwai ho [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]]. Supreme Court ne Unnao ke saare cases Lucknow se Delhi shift kiye [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. 7 February 2019 ko usne Muzaffarpur shelter home ka trial Delhi ke Saket ki ek POCSO court mein bheja [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]]. 2002 ke Gujarat riots gang rape case ko Gujarat se bahar le jaaya gaya aur Mumbai ki ek special court mein uska trial chala [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]].

Kathua, Unnao aur Muzaffarpur cases mein yeh order khud Supreme Court ne diya. Transfer se na charges badalte hain, na evidence. Badalta hai courtroom, aur witnesses aur un logon ke beech ki doori jinke khilaaf woh gawahi de rahe hain.

## Transfers ke baad kya hua: verdicts

| Case | Trial kahan chala | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case | Mumbai | 2008: 11 logon ko umrqaid; ek police officer FIR galat record karne ka doshi [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]] |
| Kathua, 2018 | Pathankot | 2019: 7 mein se 6 accused convict [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]] |
| Unnao, 2017 | Delhi | 2019: ek former MLA ko baaki poori zindagi ki jail, saath mein Rs 25 lakh ka fine [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]] |
| Muzaffarpur shelter home, 2018 | Saket, Delhi | 2020: 20 mein se 19 accused convict; baad mein 11 ko umrqaid [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]] |

Muzaffarpur ka verdict transfer ke ek saal se kam mein aaya, aur Kathua ka ek saal se thoda zyada mein. Kathua mein teen logon ko murder ke liye umrqaid mili, saath mein gang rape ke liye 25 saal, aur ek accused bari hua [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. Gujarat case mein Bombay High Court ne 2017 mein saare 11 convictions uphold kiye, aur un paanch police personnel aur do doctors ko bhi convict kiya jinhe trial court ne bari kar diya tha [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. Unnao ke convict ne appeal ki hai; May 2026 mein Supreme Court ne Delhi High Court ka uski saza suspend karne wala order radd kar diya aur High Court se kaha ki ya toh woh appeal par jaldi faisla kare ya naya order paas kare [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]].

Naya pata naya evidence paida nahi karta: Kathua mein ek accused bari hua aur Muzaffarpur mein bhi ek. Transfer bas itna kar sakta hai ki jo evidence maujood hai, use un logon se door parkha jaye jo use tod-marod sakte hain.

## Verdicts local police aur power ke baare mein kya batate hain

Dekhiye aur kaun convict hua. Kathua mein chhe mein se teen policewale the, jinhe evidence mitane ke liye paanch-paanch saal ki saza mili [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. Gujarat case mein ek police officer jaan-boojh kar FIR galat record karne ka doshi paaya gaya [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. Unnao mein survivor ke pita ko April 2018 mein ek hamle ke baad illegal hathiyar ke charge mein arrest kiya gaya, aur custody mein unki maut ho gayi; 2020 mein Delhi ki ek court ne former MLA aur chhe aur logon ko unki maut ke liye culpable homicide mein 10 saal ki saza di [[barandbench-unnao-father-2020]]. Muzaffarpur mein abuse sarkari paise se chalne wale ek shelter home mein hua, aur use saamne laane wala Tata Institute of Social Sciences ka ek social audit tha, jo state sarkar ke liye kiya gaya tha [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]].

In verdicts mein yahi asahaj pattern dikhta hai: ek se zyada case mein woh log khud convict hue jinka kaam crime ko record karna aur evidence ko bachana tha. Transfer ek trial ko bachata hai. Us police station ko nahi badalta jahan se case aaya tha.

Maan lijiye ek district town ki family hai jiski beti ne ek local dabang ke bete par aarop lagaya hai. Investigating officer accused ki family ko jaanta hai. Hearing ke din supporters court ke corridor mein bheed laga dete hain. Ek imaandaar judge bhi us witness ko nahi bacha sakta jise usi bus se ghar lautna hai. Aisi hi haalat mein family trial shift karne ki maang karti hai.

## Remission: 2024 mein trial ki jagah phir kyun matter ki

15 August 2022 ko Gujarat case mein umrqaid kaat rahe 11 log Godhra jail se bahar aa gaye, kyunki Gujarat sarkar ne unhe remission de di thi [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. 8 January 2024 ko Supreme Court ne yeh remission radd kar di. Court ne kaha ki Gujarat ke paas remission dene ki power hi nahi thi, kyunki trial Maharashtra mein chala tha, isliye appropriate government Maharashtra thi. Court ne yeh bhi paaya ki May 2022 ka uska apna order, jisme Gujarat ko is par faisla karne ko kaha gaya tha, facts chhupa kar aur fraud se liya gaya tha [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. Saare 11 ne 21 January 2024 ki der raat Godhra sub-jail mein surrender kiya [[scroll-bilkis-surrender-2024]].

Yaani transfer sirf courtroom nahi badalta. Is case mein usne saalon baad yeh bhi tay kiya ki convict ki reha par power kis sarkar ke paas hai.

## Fair trial kaise maangein: transfer, protection aur state ki zimmedariyan

Kathua, Unnao aur Muzaffarpur ke orders dikhate hain ki Supreme Court trial ko doosre state mein bhej sakti hai. Aapke case mein yeh mumkin hai ya nahi, yeh ek lawyer hi bata sakta hai. Raasta jo bhi ho, record kaam aata hai: har dhamki date ke saath note kijiye, aur police ya court ko di gayi har likhit shikayat ki copy rakhiye.

Law kuch aisi protections bhi deta hai jinke liye transfer ki zaroorat nahi. Rape aur POCSO trials in camera chalne chahiye, jahan tak mumkin ho ek mahila judge ke saamne [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Victim ko 90 din ke andar investigation ka update paane ka, aur prosecution waapas lene se pehle sunwai ka haq hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Dalit aur Adivasi survivors ke liye SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act ki Section 15A victims, unke dependants aur witnesses ko dhamkiyon se bachana state ki zimmedari banati hai, aur victims ko court hearings ki, bail hearings samet, samay par soochna paane ka haq deti hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. District Legal Services Authority in applications ke liye free legal aid de sakti hai [[nalsa]].

Fair trial ke liye kisi survivor ko Pathankot, Delhi ya Mumbai ki zaroorat nahi padni chahiye. Jab tak har jagah ki local police woh bharosa nahi kamaati, families ko pata hona chahiye ki Supreme Court pehle bhi trials shift kar chuki hai, aur woh jahan hain wahan kaun si protections maang sakti hain.

rg-kar-2024-doctor-case-verdict.en:
On 9 August 2024 a trainee doctor was raped and murdered inside RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata, the hospital where she worked [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. The law forbids revealing her identity, so this file uses the name the case is known by: the RG Kar case. She was not on a dark road. She was at her workplace.

The crime was not rare in kind. Police across India registered 266 cases of murder with rape or gang rape in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. What set RG Kar apart was the response it forced from the system, and what that reveals about justice under a national spotlight.

## 9 August 2024: a doctor killed at work

The crime came less than six weeks after the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced the Indian Penal Code on 1 July 2024 [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. So the case was tried under the new code. Its Section 66 covers a rape that causes a woman's death or leaves her in a persistent vegetative state: at least 20 years of rigorous imprisonment, up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

That punishment is not new: it carries over Section 376A of the IPC, added in 2013 [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. The harshest sentence had been law for more than a decade. It had not made a hospital corridor safe.

## The Supreme Court steps in: a national task force

On 20 August 2024 the Supreme Court, which had taken up the case on its own (suo motu), set up a National Task Force on the safety of medical professionals [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. The bench, led by Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud, asked for an interim report in three weeks and a final report in two months.

> "The nation cannot await a rape or murder for real changes on the ground." (Supreme Court, 20 August 2024)

The Chief Justice also said: "If women cannot go to a place of work and feel safe, we are denying them equal opportunity" [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. That is the legal core of this case. Safety at work is a matter of equality, not a favour from management. But a task force can only recommend. Whether its advice changes a ward at 3 a.m. depends on each hospital.

## January 2025: life, not death, and why

On 20 January 2025 a Sealdah court sentenced the convicted man to life imprisonment for the rest of his natural life and a Rs 50,000 fine under BNS Sections 64 (rape), 66 and 103(1) (murder) [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. The CBI had asked for death. The judge refused: "This crime does not fall under the rarest of the rare category." Courts, he said, must resist "the temptation to bow to public pressure or emotional appeals". He also ordered the state to pay the family Rs 17 lakh.

"Rarest of the rare" is the test Indian courts apply before choosing death over life. It does not measure public anger. Judges weigh aggravating circumstances against mitigating ones, as the Supreme Court did when it confirmed death sentences in the 2012 Delhi gang rape case [[sc-mukesh-nct-delhi-2017]]. In 2021 the Bombay High Court, commuting the Shakti Mills death sentences, held that a constitutional court cannot award punishment based on public opinion [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]]. The Sealdah judge applied the same principle and chose the heaviest sentence Section 66 allows short of death.

## Appeals: the state, the CBI and the family

The West Bengal government appealed for death. On 7 February 2025 the Calcutta High Court dismissed that appeal, leaving the CBI, which had investigated and prosecuted the case, to pursue its own [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]]. After the sentence, the family had said it would move a higher court [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. We could not find a ruling on the CBI's appeal as of November 2026.

Notice the pattern. The state government went to court for a death sentence. Within weeks of the crime, the state Assembly had also passed the Aparajita Bill, which makes death mandatory when a rape victim dies or is left in a vegetative state [[barandbench-aparajita-bill-2024]]; a separate investigation tests that Bill against West Bengal's conviction record. Severity in court is the easy part. The RG Kar trial moved from crime to sentence in about five months, while 1,85,785 rape cases across India were still pending trial at the end of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Hospitals are workplaces: what the law requires

Under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 (the POSH Act), "workplace" expressly includes hospitals and nursing homes [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Any hospital with 10 or more workers must set up an Internal Committee headed by a senior woman employee, with at least two staff members and one outside member, and at least half its members must be women [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. A complaint must be made within three months of the incident (the committee can allow three more), the inquiry must finish within 90 days, and an employer who fails to comply can be fined up to Rs 50,000, doubled for a repeat [[indiacode-posh-2013]].

The POSH Act does not punish rape or murder; the BNS does. But it gives every woman working in a hospital, from surgeon to ward cleaner, a committee that must hear her. That matters because most workplace complaints never become police cases: in 2024, police across India registered only 388 cases of sexual harassment at office premises [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In 2023 the Supreme Court found "serious lapses in the enforcement" of the Act a decade on, calling it "a sorry state of affairs" [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]].

Consider a nursing intern in Lucknow whose supervisor keeps messaging her late at night and blocks her way on the ward. She can complain in writing to the Internal Committee. If the hospital never set one up, that failure is itself something the employer can be fined for [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

The Supreme Court said the nation cannot wait for another rape or murder. Inside a hospital, not waiting means a working complaints committee, written complaints about unsafe duty spaces, and colleagues who back each other when someone speaks up. It also means honouring a duty every hospital already has: immediate, free treatment for any rape survivor who comes through its doors [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
rg-kar-2024-doctor-case-verdict.hg:
9 August 2024 ko Kolkata ke RG Kar Medical College and Hospital mein ek trainee doctor ka rape aur murder hua. Yeh wahi hospital tha jahan woh kaam karti thi [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. Law uski identity batane se mana karta hai, isliye hum is case ko usi naam se bulayenge jis naam se yeh jaana jaata hai: RG Kar case. Woh kisi sunsaan sadak par nahi thi. Woh apni workplace par thi.

Yeh crime apni tarah ka akela nahi hai. 2024 mein poore India mein police ne rape ya gang rape ke saath murder ke 266 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. RG Kar alag isliye bana kyunki isne poore system ko jawab dene par majboor kiya. Aur woh jawab dikhata hai ki jab poora desh dekh raha ho, tab justice kaise chalta hai.

## 9 August 2024: kaam ki jagah par ek doctor ka murder

1 July 2024 se Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne purane Indian Penal Code ki jagah le li thi [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. Yeh crime uske chhe hafte se bhi kam samay baad hua, isliye case naye law ke under chala. BNS ki Section 66 us rape ke liye hai jisme aurat ki maut ho jaye ya woh persistent vegetative state, yaani lambe samay tak coma jaisi haalat, mein chali jaye. Saza hai: kam se kam 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment, baaki poori natural life tak ki qaid, ya death [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Yeh saza nayi nahi hai. Yeh IPC ki Section 376A se aayi hai, jo 2013 ke amendment mein judi thi [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Yaani sabse kadi saza das saal se zyada time se law mein thi. Phir bhi woh hospital ka ek corridor safe nahi bana payi.

## Supreme Court aage aaya: ek national task force

Supreme Court ne yeh case khud apni taraf se (suo motu) uthaya tha. 20 August 2024 ko court ne medical professionals ki safety par ek National Task Force banayi [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ki bench ne teen hafte mein interim report aur do mahine mein final report maangi.

> "The nation cannot await a rape or murder for real changes on the ground." Yaani zameen par asli badlaav ke liye desh kisi rape ya murder ka intezaar nahi kar sakta. (Supreme Court, 20 August 2024)

Chief Justice ne yeh bhi kaha: "If women cannot go to a place of work and feel safe, we are denying them equal opportunity" [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. Yahi is case ka legal core hai. Kaam ki jagah par safety barabari ka sawaal hai, management ka koi ehsaan nahi. Lekin task force sirf suggest kar sakti hai. Raat ke 3 baje kisi ward mein kuch badlega ya nahi, yeh har hospital par depend karta hai.

## January 2025: death nahi, umrqaid, aur kyun

20 January 2025 ko Sealdah ki ek court ne convict ko baaki poori natural life ke liye umrqaid aur Rs 50,000 jurmaane ki saza di, BNS ki Sections 64 (rape), 66 aur 103(1) (murder) ke under [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. CBI ne death penalty maangi thi. Judge ne mana kar diya: "This crime does not fall under the rarest of the rare category." Unhone kaha ki courts ko "the temptation to bow to public pressure or emotional appeals" se bachna chahiye. Court ne state ko family ko Rs 17 lakh dene ka order bhi diya.

"Rarest of the rare" woh test hai jisse Indian courts decide karti hain ki umrqaid ki jagah death di jaye ya nahi. Yeh public ka gussa nahi naapta. Judges saza badhane wali baaton (aggravating) ko saza ghatane wali baaton (mitigating) ke saamne tolte hain. 2012 ke Delhi gang rape case mein Supreme Court ne yahi tola tha aur death sentences confirm kiye the [[sc-mukesh-nct-delhi-2017]]. 2021 mein Bombay High Court ne Shakti Mills ki death sentences ko umrqaid mein badalte hue kaha ki constitutional court public opinion ke basis par saza nahi de sakti [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]]. Sealdah ke judge ne bhi yahi principle apnaya aur Section 66 mein death se neeche ki sabse bhaari saza chuni.

## Appeals: state, CBI aur family

West Bengal sarkar ne death ke liye appeal ki. 7 February 2025 ko Calcutta High Court ne woh appeal dismiss kar di [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]]. Investigation aur prosecution CBI ne kiya tha, isliye apni appeal ka raasta CBI ke paas raha. Saza ke baad family ne kaha tha ki woh higher court jayegi [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. November 2026 tak humein CBI ki appeal par koi faisla nahi mila.

Ab is pattern par dhyaan dijiye. State sarkar court mein death sentence maangne gayi. Crime ke kuch hi hafton mein state Assembly ne Aparajita Bill bhi pass kar diya tha, jo rape ke baad victim ki maut ho jaane ya uske vegetative state mein chale jaane par death ko mandatory banata hai [[barandbench-aparajita-bill-2024]]. Hamari ek alag investigation us Bill ko West Bengal ke conviction record se milaa kar dekhti hai. Court mein sakhti dikhana aasaan hissa hai. RG Kar case mein crime se saza tak lagbhag paanch mahine lage, jabki 2024 ke end mein poore India mein rape ke 1,85,785 cases trial mein pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Hospital bhi workplace hai: law kya kehta hai

Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 (POSH Act) mein "workplace" ki definition mein hospitals aur nursing homes saaf likhe hain [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Jis hospital mein 10 ya usse zyada log kaam karte hain, use ek Internal Committee banani hoti hai, jiski head ek senior woman employee ho, kam se kam do staff members aur ek bahar ka member ho, aur kam se kam aadhe members women hon [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Complaint incident ke teen mahine ke andar karni hoti hai (zaroorat ho toh committee teen mahine aur de sakti hai), inquiry 90 din mein poori honi chahiye, aur rules na maanne wale employer par Rs 50,000 tak ka fine lag sakta hai, dobara galti par double [[indiacode-posh-2013]].

POSH Act rape ya murder ki saza nahi deta; woh kaam BNS ka hai. Lekin yeh hospital mein kaam karne wali har aurat ko, surgeon se lekar ward cleaner tak, ek aisi committee deta hai jise uski baat sunni hi padegi. Yeh isliye zaroori hai kyunki kaam ki jagah ki zyadatar complaints kabhi police case nahi banti: 2024 mein poore India mein police ne office premises par sexual harassment ke sirf 388 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2023 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki law bante hue ek decade ho gaya, phir bhi enforcement mein "serious lapses" hain, aur ise "a sorry state of affairs" bataya [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]].

Sochiye, Lucknow mein ek nursing intern hai. Uska supervisor der raat use messages bhejta rehta hai aur ward mein uska raasta rokta hai. Woh Internal Committee ko written complaint de sakti hai. Agar hospital ne committee banayi hi nahi, toh woh khud ek aisi galti hai jiske liye employer par fine lag sakta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Supreme Court ne kaha tha ki desh agle rape ya murder ka intezaar nahi kar sakta. Hospital ke andar intezaar na karne ka matlab hai: ek chalti hui complaints committee, unsafe duty spaces ki written complaints, aur aise colleagues jo bolne wale ke saath khade hon. Aur ek duty jo har hospital par pehle se hai, use nibhana: jo bhi rape survivor hospital ke darwaaze par aaye, use turant aur free ilaaj milna chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

shakti-mills-2013-death-sentences-commut.en:
In 2013, the year Parliament rewrote India's rape law, Mumbai's Shakti Mills gang rape cases set up the first test of one of its harshest new clauses. On 4 April 2014 a Mumbai sessions court sentenced three men to death as repeat offenders under Section 376E, the first time any court had applied it [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]]. On 25 November 2021 the Bombay High Court replaced those death sentences with life imprisonment [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]]. The seven years between the two orders hold most of India's argument about punishment.

## Mumbai, 2013: three repeat offenders

The 2013 amendment, passed after the 2012 Delhi gang rape case, added Section 376E to the IPC. A man "previously convicted" of rape under Section 376, 376A or 376D who is convicted of rape again faces only two possible sentences: prison for the remainder of his natural life, or death [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

In the Shakti Mills cases, the court treated three men as repeat offenders because they had been convicted in more than one of the 2013 gang rape cases [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]]. This file does not describe the survivors or the attacks. The law and the courts are the story.

## April 2014: the first death sentences under Section 376E

The sessions court gave the three men death sentences on 4 April 2014 [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]]. No court had used Section 376E before.

Parliament had been warned. The Justice J.S. Verma Committee, set up after the Delhi case, advised against the death penalty for rape, noting that it "may not have a deterrent effect" [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament added it anyway in 2013: for rape that causes death or leaves a woman in a persistent vegetative state (Section 376A), and for repeat offenders (Section 376E) [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Our case file on the Verma Committee follows that choice.

The death sentences were not the end of the case. They went to the Bombay High Court, and its review took more than seven years.

## November 2021: 'public opinion' cannot decide punishment

On 25 November 2021, a Bombay High Court bench of Justices S.S. Jadhav and P.K. Chavan commuted all 3 death sentences to life imprisonment. The bench held that a constitutional court cannot award punishment based on public opinion [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]].

That sentence is the core of this case. After a crime that shakes a city, the crowd, the TV studio and the politician often ask for the same thing: a hanging. A court's job is different. It must decide on the law and the evidence, case by case, even when the street is louder.

Other courts have drawn the same line. In January 2025 a Sealdah court in Kolkata sentenced the man convicted in the RG Kar Medical College case to life imprisonment for the rest of his natural life. It said the crime was not "rarest of the rare", and that courts must resist "the temptation to bow to public pressure or emotional appeals" [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. Our RG Kar case file tells that story in full.

## Repeat offenders under the BNS today

Since 1 July 2024, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) has replaced the IPC [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]]. The repeat-offender rule survives as Section 71: anyone convicted a second time of rape under Sections 64, 65, 66 or 70 faces imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

What does "life" mean? Many people assume a life sentence means a fixed number of years. For the gravest rape offences, the law spells it out. Gang rape under Section 70 carries at least 20 years, up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life; if the woman is under 18, it is natural life or death. The 13 aggravated forms of rape in Section 64, including rape by police, public servants, relatives, guardians or teachers, carry 10 years up to the rest of natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

| Date | What happened |
|---|---|
| 2013 | Section 376E added: natural life or death for repeat rape offenders |
| 4 April 2014 | Mumbai sessions court gives 3 death sentences, the first under Section 376E |
| 25 November 2021 | Bombay High Court commutes all 3 to life imprisonment |
| 1 July 2024 | BNS replaces the IPC; the rule continues as Section 71 |

## What actually protects the next woman

The repeat-offender rule has a blind spot built in. It works only if the first crime was reported, recorded and proved in court. Consider this: a man attacks a woman, and she never goes to the police, or her case ends in acquittal. If he attacks again, the law sees a first offender. Section 71 cannot reach him.

That is why the numbers that matter most are not about the gallows. In 2024, courts convicted in 24.4% of the rape trials they completed [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In Maharashtra, courts convicted in 8.7% of trials for crimes against women that year, fewer than one in ten [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Mumbai alone registered 411 rape cases in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Every one of them that ends without a conviction leaves the law blind if the same man offends again.

The protections that help the next woman are less dramatic and more useful. Any police station must register a rape complaint wherever the crime happened, as a Zero FIR; a woman's complaint of a sexual offence must be recorded by a woman officer; and she gets a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. An officer who refuses faces six months to two years in prison under Section 199 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Every hospital, public or private, must give a rape survivor immediate free treatment under Section 397 of the BNSS [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

A city that wants fewer repeat attackers needs these to work every time. A death sentence, handed down once in a while, cannot do that job.

This is general information, not legal advice.
shakti-mills-2013-death-sentences-commut.hg:
2013 mein Parliament ne India ka rape law dobara likha. Usi saal hue Mumbai ke Shakti Mills gang rape cases aage chalkar is law ke sabse sakht rules mein se ek ka pehla test bane. 4 April 2014 ko Mumbai ki ek sessions court ne teen aadmiyon ko repeat offenders maankar Section 376E mein phansi sunayi, aur kisi bhi court ne yeh section pehli baar lagaya tha [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]]. 25 November 2021 ko Bombay High Court ne yeh death sentences life imprisonment mein badal di [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]]. In do faislon ke beech ke saat saalon mein saza par India ki lagbhag poori bahas chhupi hai.

## Mumbai, 2013: teen repeat offenders

2012 ke Delhi gang rape case ke baad aaye 2013 ke amendment ne IPC mein Section 376E joda. Iske hisaab se jo aadmi pehle rape (Section 376, 376A ya 376D) mein "previously convicted" ho aur phir se rape ka doshi thehre, uske liye sirf do sazayein hain: bachi hui poori natural life jail, ya phansi [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

Shakti Mills cases mein court ne teen aadmiyon ko repeat offenders maana, kyunki 2013 ke ek se zyada gang rape cases mein unhe convict kiya ja chuka tha [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]]. Is file mein hum survivors ya hamlon ke baare mein kuch nahin batayenge. Kahani law aur courts ki hai.

## April 2014: Section 376E mein pehli death sentences

Sessions court ne 4 April 2014 ko teeno ko phansi ki saza di [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]]. Isse pehle kisi court ne Section 376E use nahin kiya tha.

Parliament ko pehle hi aagaah kiya gaya tha. Delhi case ke baad bani Justice J.S. Verma Committee ne rape ke liye death penalty ke khilaaf salah di thi, yeh note karte hue ki iska "deterrent effect" shayad na ho, yaani zaroori nahin ki phansi ke darr se crime ruke [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Phir bhi Parliament ne 2013 mein death penalty jod di: aise rape ke liye jismein aurat ki maut ho jaye ya woh persistent vegetative state mein chali jaye, yaani body zinda rahe par hosh na laute (Section 376A), aur repeat offenders ke liye (Section 376E) [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Verma Committee par hamari case file isi choice ki kahani batati hai.

Phansi ki in sazaon se case khatam nahin hua. Maamla Bombay High Court gaya, aur wahan review mein saat saal se zyada lag gaye.

## November 2021: 'public opinion' se saza tay nahin ho sakti

25 November 2021 ko Bombay High Court ke Justices S.S. Jadhav aur P.K. Chavan ki bench ne sabhi 3 death sentences ko life imprisonment mein badal diya. Bench ne kaha ki ek constitutional court public opinion ke basis par saza nahin de sakti [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]].

Yahi is case ki asli baat hai. Jab koi crime poore shehar ko hila deta hai, to bheed, TV studio aur neta aksar ek hi cheez maangte hain: phansi. Lekin court ka kaam alag hai. Use har case mein law aur evidence dekhkar faisla karna hota hai, chahe sadak par kitna bhi shor ho.

Dusri courts ne bhi yahi line kheenchi hai. January 2025 mein Kolkata ki Sealdah court ne RG Kar Medical College case ke convict ko life imprisonment di, yaani bachi hui poori natural life jail. Court ne kaha ki yeh crime "rarest of the rare" nahin hai, aur courts ko "the temptation to bow to public pressure or emotional appeals" se bachna chahiye, yaani public pressure ya emotional appeals ke aage jhukne ke laalach se [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. RG Kar par hamari case file poori kahani batati hai.

## Aaj BNS mein repeat offenders ka rule

1 July 2024 se Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne IPC ki jagah le li hai [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]]. Repeat-offender rule ab Section 71 mein hai: jo Sections 64, 65, 66 ya 70 mein doosri baar rape ka convict ho, use bachi hui poori natural life jail ya phansi hogi [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

"Life" ka matlab kya hai? Bahut log maante hain ki life sentence matlab kuch fixed saal. Sabse serious rape cases mein law ise saaf likhta hai. Section 70 mein gang rape ki saza kam se kam 20 saal hai, aur bachi hui poori natural life jail tak ja sakti hai; agar ladki 18 se kam ki hai, to saza natural life jail ya phansi hai. Section 64 mein rape ke 13 aggravated forms hain, jaise police, public servants, rishtedaar, guardian ya teacher dwara rape, jinmein saza 10 saal se lekar bachi hui poori natural life tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

| Date | Kya hua |
|---|---|
| 2013 | Section 376E juda: repeat rape offenders ke liye natural life jail ya phansi |
| 4 April 2014 | Mumbai sessions court ne 3 death sentences di, Section 376E mein pehli baar |
| 25 November 2021 | Bombay High Court ne sabhi 3 ko life imprisonment mein badla |
| 1 July 2024 | BNS ne IPC ki jagah li, rule ab Section 71 mein hai |

## Agli aurat ko asal mein kya bachata hai

Repeat-offender rule mein ek blind spot shuru se hai. Yeh tabhi kaam karta hai jab pehla crime report, record aur court mein prove hua ho. Sochiye: ek aadmi kisi aurat par hamla karta hai, aur woh police ke paas nahin jaati, ya uska case acquittal par khatam ho jata hai. Agar woh aadmi phir hamla kare, to law ki nazar mein woh first-time offender hai. Section 71 us tak pahunch hi nahin paata.

Isliye sabse zaroori numbers phansi ke nahin hain. 2024 mein courts ne jitne rape trials poore kiye, unmein se sirf 24.4% mein conviction hua [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi saal Maharashtra mein crimes against women ke trials mein conviction rate 8.7% tha, yaani das mein se ek se bhi kam [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Akele Mumbai mein 2024 mein 411 rape cases register hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inmein se jo bhi case bina conviction ke khatam hoga, uske baad agar wahi aadmi phir crime kare, to law use repeat offender ki tarah dekh hi nahin payega.

Agli aurat ko jo cheezein bachati hain, woh kam dramatic par zyada kaam ki hain. Koi bhi police station rape complaint darj karega, crime chahe kahin bhi hua ho, yaani Zero FIR; kisi aurat ki sexual offence wali complaint woman officer hi likhegi; aur use FIR ki free copy milegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo officer mana kare, use BNS Section 199 mein chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. BNSS Section 397 ke hisaab se har hospital, sarkari ho ya private, rape survivor ko turant aur free ilaaj dega [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Jo shehar chahta hai ki attackers dobara hamla na kar paayein, use yeh cheezein har baar kaam karti hui chahiye. Kabhi-kabhaar sunayi gayi phansi yeh kaam nahin kar sakti.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahin.

skin-to-skin-pocso-ruling-reversed-2021.en:
In January 2021, the Bombay High Court held that touching a child over her clothes was not "sexual assault" under Section 7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, because there had been no skin-to-skin contact [[barandbench-satish-2021]]. Ten months later, on 18 November 2021, the Supreme Court set that reading aside: "The important ingredient for constituting the offence of sexual assault under POCSO is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child" [[barandbench-satish-2021]]. That case is closed. The habit of reading child-protection law as narrowly as possible is not.

## January 2021: the 'skin-to-skin' test

POCSO has been in force since 14 November 2012 and protects every child under 18 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. It sorts sexual offences against children into families. Penetrative sexual assault is the gravest. Below it sits sexual assault (Sections 7 to 10), which covers sexual touching without penetration. Sexual harassment needs no touch at all.

The High Court read "touch" in Section 7 to mean bare skin. On that reading, a layer of cloth decided whether a child had suffered sexual assault in the eyes of the law. A school uniform, a frock, a glove on the abuser's hand: any of them could become a defence. The child's experience did not change. Only the law's view of it did. And the rule rewarded the careful abuser, the one who keeps every contact deniable as a game or an accident: exactly the person POCSO was written to stop.

## November 2021: the Supreme Court restores 'sexual intent'

The ruling reached the Supreme Court because the Attorney General for India, the government's top law officer, had challenged it. On 18 November 2021, a bench of Justices U.U. Lalit, S. Ravindra Bhat and Bela M. Trivedi set it aside and moved the question back where the law puts it: why the person touched the child, not what the child was wearing [[barandbench-satish-2021]].

Intent is read from the circumstances: who the person was, where it happened, what was said, what came before and after. The High Court had swapped that question for a measurement.

The stakes are large. In 2024 police registered 69,191 POCSO cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Of these, 20,845, or 30.1%, were registered under Sections 8 and 10, which punish sexual assault and aggravated sexual assault [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That is the category a skin-to-skin rule would have shrunk.

## Not a one-off: the 2026 case of reduced charges

On 10 February 2026, the Supreme Court was again dealing with a High Court. In a case it had taken up on its own, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and N.V. Anjaria ruled on an order that had reduced the charges in a child sexual assault case from attempt to rape to lesser offences.
