The bench said efforts to sensitise judges "have not borne the fruit that was expected", and asked a National Judicial Academy expert committee, headed by former judge Aniruddha Bose, to draft guidelines on sensitivity in sexual-offence cases [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

Both cases turned on a label: what the law would call what was done to a child. Both were corrected only because they climbed to the top court. Most families never get that far. For them, the reading of the judge who hears the case is the law.

Labels matter at the end of a trial too. Only 32.3% of POCSO trials completed in 2024 ended in conviction: 12,672 convictions against 25,476 acquittals and 1,101 discharges [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The data cannot say why any of those trials ended without a conviction, or how many acquittals followed a narrow reading of the law. But where more than two in three trials end without a conviction, a judge who shrinks an offence removes one of the few protections a child has left.

## What counts as sexual assault on a child under POCSO

This is general information, not legal advice.

- **Intent, not skin.** Touching a child with sexual intent is sexual assault, over clothes or not [[barandbench-satish-2021]].
- **Every child under 18, girl or boy.** A child's "consent" is no defence, and boys are protected exactly as girls are [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].
- **No touch needed for harassment.** Sexual remarks or gestures towards a child, or showing a child sexual material, are sexual harassment, punished under Section 12. Police registered 3,502 such cases in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Adults must report.** Anyone who knows or suspects that a child has been sexually abused must tell the police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit. Failing to report can bring up to six months in jail, a fine, or both; a head of an institution who stays silent about a staff member faces up to a year [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Children themselves are exempt.

## If a child tells you: first steps and 1098

Children rarely tell. In the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, done before POCSO existed, 72.1% of children who said they had been sexually assaulted had told no one, and only 3.4% had gone to the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. When a child does speak, the first adult's reaction decides whether they ever speak again.

Consider this situation. An 11-year-old boy tells his tuition teacher that an older cousin keeps touching him "over the clothes" and calls it a game. It is tempting to call it a misunderstanding. Since 2021, the law has said otherwise. What helps:

- Stay calm and believe him. Say: "Thank you for telling me. It is not your fault."
- Don't quiz him for details or ask whether it was over or under his clothes. Write down what he said, in his words, with the date.
- Don't promise to keep it secret. You can't: the law requires you to report it [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]].
- Report it the same day to the police, or call the Child Helpline, 1098, which is linked to the 112 emergency system [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].
- Don't confront the cousin, and don't let the family "settle" it at home.

It took the Supreme Court to fix one bad reading of one word. A child who tells you should not need the Supreme Court to be believed.
skin-to-skin-pocso-ruling-reversed-2021.hg:
January 2021 mein Bombay High Court ne kaha ki kapdon ke upar se ek bachchi ko chhoona Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act ke Section 7 ke under "sexual assault" nahi hai, kyunki skin-to-skin contact nahi hua tha [[barandbench-satish-2021]]. Das mahine baad, 18 November 2021 ko, Supreme Court ne ye reading radd kar di: "The important ingredient for constituting the offence of sexual assault under POCSO is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child" [[barandbench-satish-2021]]. Yaani asli sawaal sexual intent ka hai, skin-to-skin contact ka nahi. Woh case ab band ho chuka hai. Lekin bachchon ki suraksha wale law ko jitna ho sake utna tang padhne ki aadat abhi bhi zinda hai.

## January 2021: 'skin-to-skin' test

POCSO 14 November 2012 se laagu hai aur 18 saal se kam umar ke har bachche ko protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Ye bachchon ke khilaaf sexual offences ko alag-alag categories mein rakhta hai. Sabse gambhir hai penetrative sexual assault. Uske neeche aata hai sexual assault (Sections 7 se 10), jisme bina penetration ke sexual touch shaamil hai. Sexual harassment ke liye toh touch ki bhi zaroorat nahi.

High Court ne Section 7 mein "touch" ka matlab sirf khuli skin se skin ka contact samjha. Is reading ke hisaab se, kapde ki ek parat tay karti ki law ki nazar mein bachche ke saath sexual assault hua ya nahi. School uniform, frock, abuser ke haath ka glove: inme se kuch bhi defence ban sakta tha. Bachche ka anubhav nahi badla. Badli sirf law ki nazar. Aur ye rule us chaalaak abuser ko faayda deta jo har touch ko "game" ya "galti se ho gaya" bata kar bach nikle: yaani theek wahi insaan jise rokne ke liye POCSO banaya gaya tha.

## November 2021: Supreme Court ne 'sexual intent' ko wapas beech mein rakha

Ye faisla Supreme Court tak isliye pahuncha kyunki Attorney General for India, yaani sarkar ke sabse bade law officer, ne khud ise challenge kiya tha. 18 November 2021 ko Justices U.U. Lalit, S. Ravindra Bhat aur Bela M. Trivedi ki bench ne ise radd kar diya aur sawaal ko wapas wahin rakha jahan law use rakhta hai: us insaan ne bachche ko kyun chhua, na ki bachche ne kya pehna tha [[barandbench-satish-2021]].

Intent haalaat se samjha jaata hai: woh insaan kaun tha, ye kahan hua, kya kaha gaya, pehle aur baad mein kya hua. High Court ne is sawaal ki jagah ek naap-tol rakh diya tha.

Ye koi chhoti baat nahi thi. 2024 mein police ne 69,191 POCSO cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inme se 20,845, yaani 30.1%, Sections 8 aur 10 ke under darj hue, jo sexual assault aur aggravated sexual assault ki saza dete hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Skin-to-skin rule isi category ko chhota kar deta.

## Ek baar ki baat nahi: 2026 mein ghataaye gaye charges

10 February 2026 ko Supreme Court phir ek High Court ke faisle se deal kar raha tha. Ek case mein, jo court ne khud uthaaya tha, Chief Justice Surya Kant aur Justices Joymalya Bagchi aur N.V. Anjaria ki bench ne us order par faisla diya jisne ek child sexual assault case mein charges ko attempt to rape se ghata kar halke offences bana diya tha. Bench ne kaha ki judges ko sensitise karne ki koshishon ne "have not borne the fruit that was expected", yaani ummeed ke mutaabik nateeje nahi diye. Usne National Judicial Academy ki ek expert committee se, jiske head former judge Aniruddha Bose hain, sexual-offence cases mein sensitivity par guidelines ka draft banane ko kaha [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

Dono cases ek label par tike the: bachche ke saath jo hua, law use kya naam dega. Dono ki galti tabhi sudhri jab woh sabse oonchi adaalat tak pahunche. Zyada tar parivaar wahan tak kabhi nahi pahunchte. Unke liye, jo judge case sunta hai, uski reading hi law hai.

Trial ke end mein bhi label maayne rakhta hai. 2024 mein poore hue POCSO trials mein se sirf 32.3% conviction par khatam hue: 12,672 convictions, jabki 25,476 acquittals aur 1,101 discharges [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Data ye nahi bata sakta ki ye trials bina conviction ke kyun khatam hue, ya kitne acquittals law ki tang reading ki wajah se hue. Lekin jahan teen mein se do se zyada trials bina conviction ke khatam hote hain, wahan offence ko chhota karne wala judge bachche ke paas bachi gini-chuni protections mein se ek aur chheen leta hai.

## POCSO ke under bachche ke saath sexual assault kya hai

Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

- **Intent, skin nahi.** Sexual intent se bachche ko chhoona sexual assault hai, chahe kapdon ke upar se ho ya nahi [[barandbench-satish-2021]].
- **18 se kam har bachcha, ladki ho ya ladka.** Bachche ki "consent" koi defence nahi hai, aur ladkon ko bilkul ladkiyon jitni hi protection milti hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].
- **Harassment ke liye touch zaroori nahi.** Bachche ki taraf sexual baatein ya ishaare karna, ya bachche ko sexual material dikhana, sexual harassment hai, jiski saza Section 12 mein hai. 2024 mein police ne aise 3,502 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Adults ko report karna hi hoga.** Jise bhi pata ho ya shaq ho ki kisi bachche ka sexual abuse hua hai, use police ya Special Juvenile Police Unit ko batana zaroori hai. Report na karne par chhe mahine tak jail, fine, ya dono ho sakte hain; jo institution head apne staff ke baare mein chup rahe, use ek saal tak ki saza ho sakti hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Bachchon par ye duty laagu nahi hoti.

## Jab koi bachcha aapko bataaye: pehle kadam aur 1098

Bachche bahut kam batate hain. Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein, jo POCSO aane se pehle hui thi, jin bachchon ne kaha ki unka sexual assault hua tha, unme se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahi bataaya tha, aur sirf 3.4% police tak gaye the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Jab koi bachcha bolta hai, toh pehle adult ka reaction tay karta hai ki woh dobara kabhi bolega ya nahi.

Is situation ke baare mein sochiye. 11 saal ka ek ladka apne tuition teacher ko bataata hai ki uska ek bada cousin use baar-baar "kapdon ke upar se" chhoota hai aur ise game kehta hai. Ise galatfehmi keh kar taal dena aasaan lagta hai. Lekin 2021 se law kuch aur kehta hai. Kya madad karta hai:

- Shaant rahiye aur uski baat par yakeen kariye. Kahiye: "Mujhe bataane ke liye thank you. Isme tumhari koi galti nahi hai."
- Usse details ke liye sawaal-jawaab mat kariye, na ye poochiye ki kapdon ke upar se tha ya andar se. Usne jo kaha, uske apne shabdon mein, date ke saath likh lijiye.
- Baat secret rakhne ka vaada mat kariye. Aap rakh hi nahi sakte: law aapse report karwata hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]].
- Usi din police ko report kariye, ya Child Helpline 1098 par call kariye, jo 112 emergency system se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].
- Cousin se khud jhagda mat kariye, aur parivaar ko ghar par hi maamla "settle" mat karne dijiye.

Ek shabd ki ek galat reading sudhaarne ke liye Supreme Court ko aana pada. Jo bachcha aapko kuch bataata hai, uski baat par yakeen karne ke liye Supreme Court ki zaroorat nahi padni chahiye.

sulur-2026-child-case-pocso-speed.en:
In May 2026 a 10-year-old girl near Sulur, in Coimbatore district, Tamil Nadu, was killed. Police say she had been abducted and sexually assaulted. Protests followed, and the case became a public test of how fast the state's police and courts could act. This file follows what the police and courts did. The girl and her family are not named. The two accused are not named either, because nobody has been convicted. The verdict is due on 27 November 2026, four days after this was written.

## Arrest and an early test in the High Court

Police arrested two men on 23 May 2026 and registered the case under the POCSO Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita [[ians-sulur-chargesheet-2026]].

Within days, a petitioner asked the Madras High Court to hand the investigation to a Special Investigation Team. The state told the court that DNA tests were being fast-tracked and a special public prosecutor had been appointed. On 29 May a bench of Justices G.R. Swaminathan and V. Lakshminarayanan closed the plea: "Prima facie we are of the opinion that investigation is going in the right direction. We cannot suspect the police every time" [[livelaw-madras-hc-sulur-sit-plea-2026]].

The court flagged a second problem. It said it would pass separate orders on social media posts that had reportedly disclosed details of the girl's family [[livelaw-madras-hc-sulur-sit-plea-2026]]. Since 2018 the Supreme Court has barred anyone from publishing a rape victim's name or "in a remote manner" disclosing facts that could identify her [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. In high-profile cases the people who break this rule are often not reporters but ordinary users sharing in anger.

## A chargesheet in under three weeks

On 10 June 2026 police filed an 819-page chargesheet before the Coimbatore Special POCSO Court, with 104 prosecution witnesses and 215 documents, including medical and DNA reports [[ians-sulur-chargesheet-2026]]. Reports put the time since the arrests at 18 to 21 days. The law sets the outer limit: under Section 193 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, police must finish investigating rape and child sexual assault within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Trial: charges, witnesses, arguments

The Special Court framed charges against both accused in June and ordered witness examination to start on 24 June and continue day to day [[dtnext-sulur-charges-framed-2026]]. By November, prosecution and defence had finished their oral and written arguments. The verdict was listed for 16 November and then deferred to 27 November, the special public prosecutor noting that the case was voluminous but that no specific reason had been given [[thenewsmill-sulur-verdict-deferred-2026]].

If judgment comes on that date, the trial will have taken about six months. The POCSO Act asks for exactly this: a designated Special Court in every district, the child's evidence recorded within 30 days of the court taking cognisance, and the trial completed, as far as possible, within one year [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## The speed most children never get

| Stage | Sulur case (2026) | India (latest data) |
|---|---|---|
| Investigation | Chargesheet in under three weeks | 21,256 POCSO cases pending investigation at the end of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]] |
| Trial | Verdict due about six months after arrest | 2,86,903 POCSO cases pending trial at the end of 2024, 87.7% of those before the courts [[ncrb-cii-2024]] |
| Fast-track courts | One Special POCSO Court, day-to-day hearings | About 2,45,579 rape and POCSO cases pending in fast-track courts on 31 December 2025 [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]] |

The difference is not the law. It is attention. Sulur had public protests, a government under pressure, a High Court watching and a special prosecutor. In 2024 the accused was a stranger or unidentified in only 3.4% of POCSO penetrative-assault cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Most children are abused by someone they know, at home or nearby, and their cases draw none of that attention. They wait in the same courts for the same judges.

India now has 779 Fast Track Special Courts, 399 of them exclusively for POCSO, and the Union Cabinet extended the scheme to 2031 in November 2026 [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Whether those courts give every child the Sulur timeline, or only the children whose cases make headlines, is the real measure.

> A fast verdict in one case is not proof the system works. It is proof of what the system can do when it decides a child matters.

## What happens next

Whatever the verdict on 27 November, either side can appeal, and any death sentence must be confirmed by the High Court. Rape and POCSO trials must be held in camera, and nothing about the proceedings may be published without the court's permission [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Readers can help in one concrete way: do not share the girl's name, image or family details, and report posts that do.
sulur-2026-child-case-pocso-speed.hg:
May 2026 mein Tamil Nadu ke Coimbatore district mein Sulur ke paas ek 10 saal ki bachchi ki hatya kar di gayi. Police ke mutaabik uska abduction aur sexual assault hua tha. Iske baad protests hue, aur yeh case is baat ki public pariksha ban gaya ki state ki police aur courts kitni tezi se kaam kar sakti hain. Yeh file batati hai ki police aur courts ne kya kiya. Bachchi aur uski family ka naam yahan nahi hai. Do accused ke naam bhi nahi hain, kyunki abhi kisi ko sazaa nahi hui. Verdict 27 November 2026 ko aana hai, yeh likhe jaane ke chaar din baad.

## Arrest, aur High Court mein shuruaati pariksha

Police ne 23 May 2026 ko do aadmiyon ko giraftaar kiya aur case POCSO Act aur Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke tahat darj kiya [[ians-sulur-chargesheet-2026]].

Kuch hi dinon mein ek petitioner ne Madras High Court se maanga ki investigation Special Investigation Team ko di jaaye. State ne court ko bataya ki DNA tests tezi se karaaye ja rahe hain aur ek special public prosecutor appoint kiya gaya hai. 29 May ko Justices G.R. Swaminathan aur V. Lakshminarayanan ki bench ne plea band kar di. Court ne kaha ki pehli nazar mein investigation sahi disha mein ja raha hai, aur "We cannot suspect the police every time", yaani hum har baar police par shak nahi kar sakte [[livelaw-madras-hc-sulur-sit-plea-2026]].

Court ne ek doosri samasya par bhi ungli rakhi. Usne kaha ki woh un social media posts par alag order dega jinmein kathit taur par bachchi ki family ki details khol di gayi thi [[livelaw-madras-hc-sulur-sit-plea-2026]]. 2018 se Supreme Court ne kisi ko bhi rape victim ka naam chhaapne ya "in a remote manner", yaani door se bhi, aisi baatein batane se roka hai jinse uski pehchaan ho sake [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. High-profile cases mein yeh niyam aksar reporters nahi, balki gusse mein share karne wale aam users todte hain.

## Teen hafte se kam mein chargesheet

10 June 2026 ko police ne Coimbatore ki Special POCSO Court mein 819 pages ki chargesheet file ki, jismein 104 prosecution witnesses aur 215 documents the, medical aur DNA reports samet [[ians-sulur-chargesheet-2026]]. Reports ke mutaabik arrests se ab tak 18 se 21 din lage. Law bahari seema tay karta hai: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita ki Section 193 ke tahat police ko rape aur child sexual assault ki investigation do mahine mein poori karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Trial: charges, gawaah, behas

Special Court ne June mein dono accused par charges frame kiye aur order diya ki gawaahon ki gawaahi 24 June se shuru ho aur roz chale [[dtnext-sulur-charges-framed-2026]]. November tak prosecution aur defence ne apni oral aur written behas poori kar li thi. Verdict 16 November ke liye list tha, phir 27 November tak taal diya gaya. Special public prosecutor ne kaha ki case bahut bada (voluminous) hai, lekin court ne koi khaas wajah nahi batayi [[thenewsmill-sulur-verdict-deferred-2026]].

Agar faisla us din aata hai, toh trial lagbhag chhe mahine mein poora hoga. POCSO Act bilkul yahi maangta hai: har district mein ek designated Special Court, court ke cognisance lene ke 30 din mein bachche ki gawaahi, aur jahan tak ho sake ek saal mein trial poora [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Woh raftaar jo zyadatar bachchon ko kabhi nahi milti

| Stage | Sulur case (2026) | India (latest data) |
|---|---|---|
| Investigation | Teen hafte se kam mein chargesheet | 2024 ke ant mein 21,256 POCSO cases ki investigation pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]] |
| Trial | Arrest ke lagbhag chhe mahine baad verdict ki taareekh | 2024 ke ant mein 2,86,903 POCSO cases trial pending, courts ke saamne wale cases ka 87.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024]] |
| Fast-track courts | Ek Special POCSO Court, roz sunwaai | 31 December 2025 ko fast-track courts mein lagbhag 2,45,579 rape aur POCSO cases pending [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]] |

Fark law ka nahi hai. Fark dhyaan ka hai. Sulur mein public protests the, dabaav mein sarkar thi, nazar rakhti High Court thi, aur ek special prosecutor tha. 2024 mein POCSO penetrative-assault cases mein sirf 3.4% mein accused anjaan ya unidentified tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Zyadatar bachchon ka abuse koi jaan-pehchaan wala karta hai, ghar mein ya aas-paas, aur unke cases par aisa koi dhyaan nahi jaata. Woh unhi courts mein, unhi judges ke saamne intezaar karte hain.

India mein ab 779 Fast Track Special Courts hain, jinmein 399 sirf POCSO ke liye hain, aur November 2026 mein Union Cabinet ne yeh scheme 2031 tak badha di [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Asli paimaana yeh hai ki kya yeh courts har bachche ko Sulur wali timeline denge, ya sirf unhe jinke case headlines banate hain.

> Ek case mein tez verdict is baat ka saboot nahi ki system kaam karta hai. Yeh saboot hai ki system kya kar sakta hai jab woh tay kar le ki ek bachcha maayne rakhta hai.

## Aage kya hoga

27 November ko verdict jo bhi ho, dono paksh appeal kar sakte hain, aur kisi bhi maut ki sazaa ko High Court se confirm karana zaroori hai. Rape aur POCSO trials in camera hone chahiye, aur court ki ijaazat ke bina proceedings ke baare mein kuch bhi chhaapa nahi ja sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Readers ek thos tareeke se madad kar sakte hain: bachchi ka naam, tasveer ya family ki details share mat kijiye, aur jo posts aisa karein unhe report kijiye.

supreme-court-gender-stereotypes-handboo.en:
On 12 August 2022 a sessions court in Kozhikode, Kerala, deciding a bail plea, looked at photographs of the complainant and wrote that she was "exposing to dresses which are having some sexual provocative one" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. A year later that sentence reappeared in a footnote of a Supreme Court handbook, as an example of what judges must stop writing. The Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes, released on 16 August 2023 with a foreword by Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud, is the judiciary correcting its own language [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## Why the Supreme Court wrote a glossary for its own judges

The handbook says it aims to help judges and the legal community identify, understand and combat stereotypes about women. It does three things: it flags language that promotes stereotypes and offers alternatives, it identifies common patterns of reasoning built on them, and it highlights binding Supreme Court decisions that reject them [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

A judgment is not an opinion column. Its words are read by police, cited by lawyers and repeated by the next judge. When a court calls a survivor's dress "provocative", it does not just describe her; it hands every later reader a reason to doubt her.

## The banned words and their replacements

The glossary has 42 entries [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Some of the most telling:

| Instead of | The handbook says |
|---|---|
| Eve teasing | Street sexual harassment |
| Forcible rape | Rape |
| Ravished, violated | Sexually harassed / assaulted or raped |
| Provocative clothing or dress | Clothing or dress |
| Chaste woman, fallen woman, seductress, woman of easy virtue | Woman |
| Spinster, unwed mother | Unmarried woman, mother |

Each old phrase does its own damage. "Eve teasing" turns a crime into mischief. Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, sexual harassment carries up to three years in prison, and so does stalking, rising to five on a repeat conviction [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In 2024 police registered 15,609 cases of sexual harassment of women and 9,865 of stalking [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. "Forcible rape" implies that some rape is not forced. "Ravished" borrows a romance novel's vocabulary for a crime. "Chaste" and "fallen" sort women into those who deserve protection and those who do not; the handbook answers every such label with one word, woman.

On "survivor" or "victim", it says both are correct and that the affected person's preference should be respected [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## The myths it names, and the 2022 'provocative dress' order

The handbook lists beliefs that courts have leaned on and calls them false: that a woman's clothing, drinking or smoking invites sexual contact; that rapists are usually strangers; that a genuine survivor cries incessantly or never speaks to the accused again; that a delayed complaint means a false one [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. "There is no 'correct' or 'appropriate' way in which a survivor or victim behaves," it says. On marrying a survivor to her rapist it is blunt: "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape." [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]

It also names stereotypes that dismiss complaints by oppressed-caste and disabled women, and states that "Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Police data backs it on strangers, even though it counts only cases that reach a police station. In 96.8% of rape cases registered in India in 2024, 28,597 of 29,536, the offender was known to the victim [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Against the Kozhikode order, the handbook sets a plain rule: "A man who touches a woman without her consent must not be permitted to take the defence that the woman invited his touch by dressing in a particular way" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## From 'a peaceful affair' to 2026: have courtrooms changed?

In 1978 the Supreme Court acquitted two policemen accused of raping a minor girl in a police station, noting that she had no injuries, calling the intercourse "a peaceful affair" and holding it "not proved to amount to rape" [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. In 2026 the court's own publication, Judgments and Gender, listed that case as an acquittal "due to restrictive reasoning on consent" [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

In March 2021, in Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh, the court struck down a bail condition that required a man accused of sexual assault to ask the complainant to tie a rakhi on him. It told courts to avoid stereotypical or patriarchal notions about women and ordered gender-sensitisation training for every judge [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. The Kozhikode order came the next year. The handbook followed in 2023.

On 10 February 2026, hearing a suo motu case over a High Court order that had reduced the charges in a child sexual assault case from attempt to rape to lesser offences, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and N.V. Anjaria made an admission: efforts to sensitise judges "have not borne the fruit that was expected". It asked a National Judicial Academy expert committee, headed by former judge Aniruddha Bose, to draft guidelines on sensitivity in sexual-offence cases [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

That is the honest scorecard. A glossary can change the words in a judgment. It cannot, on its own, change how a judge weighs a survivor's account.

## Say this instead: a guide for readers, reporters and creators

The handbook was written for judges, but the same words fill headlines, WhatsApp forwards, reels and family arguments. Its rules carry over:

- Describe the act, not the woman: "he sexually harassed her on the street", not "she was eve-teased".
- Leave out her clothes, drinking, the hour and her past relationships. They explain nothing, and in a rape trial her character and past sexual experience are irrelevant to consent under Section 48 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].
- Do not grade her reaction. Tears, silence, a late complaint or a later message to the accused prove nothing either way.
- Use "survivor" or "victim" as she prefers.
- Never publish her name or anything that could identify her; under Section 72 of the BNS that is a crime punishable with up to two years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The handbook is a public Supreme Court document. Quote it when a headline, a post or a relative reaches for "provocative" or "eve teasing". This is general information, not legal advice.
supreme-court-gender-stereotypes-handboo.hg:
12 August 2022 ko Kerala ke Kozhikode ki ek sessions court ne bail plea par faisla dete hue complainant ki photos dekhin aur likha ki woh "exposing to dresses which are having some sexual provocative one" thi, yaani aise kapde pehen rahi thi jo 'sexually provocative' the [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Ek saal baad ye sentence Supreme Court ki ek handbook ke footnote mein dobara chhapa, is misaal ke taur par ki judges ko kya likhna band karna hai. 16 August 2023 ko jaari hui Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes, jiska foreword Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ne likha, judiciary ki apni bhasha sudhaarne ki koshish hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## Supreme Court ne apne hi judges ke liye glossary kyun likhi

Handbook ke mutabik iska maqsad judges aur legal community ko auraton ke baare mein stereotypes pehchaanne, samajhne aur unse ladne mein madad karna hai. Ye teen kaam karti hai: stereotype badhaane wali bhasha ko pehchaanti hai aur uske vikalp deti hai, stereotypes par tike reasoning ke aam patterns ko pakadti hai, aur Supreme Court ke un binding faislon ko saamne laati hai jo inhe khaarij karte hain [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Judgment koi opinion column nahi hota. Uske shabd police padhti hai, lawyers cite karte hain aur agla judge dohraata hai. Jab court kisi survivor ke kapdon ko "provocative" kehta hai, toh woh sirf uska description nahi deta; woh har aane wale reader ke haath mein us par shak karne ki ek wajah thama deta hai.

## Woh shabd jo hatane hain, aur unki jagah kya bolna hai

Glossary mein 42 entries hain [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Inme se kuch sabse zyada bolne wali entries:

| Iski jagah | Handbook kehti hai |
|---|---|
| Eve teasing | Street sexual harassment |
| Forcible rape | Rape |
| Ravished, violated | Sexually harassed / assaulted or raped |
| Provocative clothing or dress | Clothing or dress |
| Chaste woman, fallen woman, seductress, woman of easy virtue | Woman |
| Spinster, unwed mother | Unmarried woman, mother |

Har purana phrase apne tareeke se nuksaan karta hai. "Eve teasing" ek crime ko sharaarat bana deta hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke under sexual harassment ki saza teen saal tak ki jail hai, aur stalking ki bhi, jo dobara conviction par paanch saal tak ho jaati hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 2024 mein police ne auraton ke sexual harassment ke 15,609 aur stalking ke 9,865 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. "Forcible rape" se lagta hai jaise kuch rape zabardasti ke bina bhi hote hain. "Ravished" ek crime ke liye romance novel ki bhasha udhaar leta hai. "Chaste" aur "fallen" jaise label auraton ko do hisson mein baant dete hain, ek jo suraksha ki hakdaar hain aur ek jo nahi; handbook har aise label ka jawab ek shabd se deti hai: woman, yaani aurat.

"Survivor" ya "victim" par handbook kehti hai ki dono shabd sahi hain, aur jis insaan ke saath hua hai, uski pasand ka samman hona chahiye [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## Handbook kin myths ko jhootha kehti hai, aur 2022 ka 'provocative dress' order

Handbook un maanyataon ki list deti hai jin par courts tikte aaye hain, aur unhe galat batati hai: ki aurat ke kapde, sharaab peena ya smoking sexual contact ko nyota dete hain; ki rapists aam taur par anjaan log hote hain; ki 'asli' survivor lagaataar roti hai ya accused se phir kabhi baat nahi karti; ki der se ki gayi complaint jhoothi hoti hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. "There is no 'correct' or 'appropriate' way in which a survivor or victim behaves," handbook kehti hai, yaani survivor ke bartaav ka koi 'sahi' ya 'uchit' tareeka nahi hota. Survivor ki shaadi rapist se karwaane ki soch par woh seedhi baat kehti hai: "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape", yaani shaadi rape ki hinsa ka ilaaj nahi hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Ye un stereotypes ko bhi naam deti hai jo oppressed-caste aur disabled auraton ki complaints ko khaarij karte hain, aur kehti hai: "Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies", yaani dominant caste ke mardon ne itihaas mein caste ka oonch-neech banaye rakhne ke liye sexual violence ko hathiyaar banaya hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Anjaan logon wale myth par police data handbook ke saath khada hai, jabki isme sirf woh cases gine jaate hain jo police station tak pahunchte hain. 2024 mein India mein darj rape cases mein se 96.8% mein, yaani 29,536 mein se 28,597 cases mein, offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Kozhikode wale order ke jawab mein handbook ek seedha rule rakhti hai: "A man who touches a woman without her consent must not be permitted to take the defence that the woman invited his touch by dressing in a particular way", yaani bina consent kisi aurat ko chhoone wale aadmi ko ye bahaana nahi banane diya ja sakta ki aurat ne apne kapdon se use nyota diya [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## 'A peaceful affair' se 2026 tak: kya courtrooms badle?

1978 mein Supreme Court ne do policewalon ko bari kar diya jin par ek police station mein ek minor ladki ke rape ka aarop tha. Court ne note kiya ki ladki ko koi chot nahi thi, intercourse ko "a peaceful affair", yaani shaanti se hua maamla, kaha, aur maana ki ye "not proved to amount to rape", yaani rape saabit nahi hota [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. 2026 mein court ki apni publication Judgments and Gender ne is case ko un faislon mein gina jahan accused "due to restrictive reasoning on consent", yaani consent ko bahut tang nazar se dekhne ki wajah se, bari hue [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

March 2021 mein, Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh mein, court ne ek bail condition radd ki jisme sexual assault ke accused aadmi ko complainant se rakhi bandhwaane ke liye kaha gaya tha. Court ne kaha ki faisle auraton ke baare mein stereotype ya patriarchal soch se door rahein, aur har judge ke liye gender-sensitisation training ka order diya [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Kozhikode wala order iske agle saal aaya. Handbook 2023 mein aayi.

10 February 2026 ko Chief Justice Surya Kant aur Justices Joymalya Bagchi aur N.V. Anjaria ki bench ek suo motu case sun rahi thi. Ye case ek High Court ke us order par tha jisne ek bachche ke saath sexual assault ke case mein attempt to rape ke charge ghata kar halke offences mein badal diye the. Bench ne khud maana ki judges ko sensitise karne ki koshishon ne "have not borne the fruit that was expected", yaani umeed ke mutabik phal nahi diya. Usne former judge Aniruddha Bose ki aguaai wali National Judicial Academy ki ek expert committee se sexual offence cases mein sensitivity par guidelines banane ko kaha [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

Yahi imaandaar scorecard hai. Glossary judgment ke shabd badal sakti hai. Lekin akele woh ye nahi badal sakti ki judge survivor ki baat ko kitna wazan deta hai.

## Ye bolo, woh nahi: readers, reporters aur creators ke liye guide

Handbook judges ke liye likhi gayi thi, lekin yahi shabd headlines, WhatsApp forwards, reels aur ghar ki behson mein bhare pade hain. Iske rules wahan bhi lagte hain:

- Kaam ko describe kariye, aurat ko nahi: "usne sadak par uska sexual harassment kiya", na ki "uske saath eve-teasing hui".
- Uske kapde, sharaab, waqt aur purane rishte beech mein mat laaiye. Inse kuch samajh nahi aata, aur rape trial mein Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam ke Section 48 ke under uska character aur pichhla sexual experience consent ke sawaal par irrelevant hai [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].
- Uske react karne ke tareeke ko number mat dijiye. Aansu, chuppi, der se complaint ya baad mein accused ko bheja gaya message, kisi bhi taraf kuch saabit nahi karte.
- "Survivor" ya "victim", jo woh khud pasand kare, wahi shabd use kariye.
- Uska naam ya aisi koi bhi detail kabhi publish mat kariye jisse uski pehchaan ho sake; BNS ke Section 72 ke under ye crime hai, jiski saza do saal tak ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Handbook Supreme Court ka public document hai. Jab koi headline, post ya rishtedaar "provocative" ya "eve teasing" jaise shabd uthaaye, toh ise quote kariye. Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

two-finger-test-supreme-court-2013-2026.en:
The so-called two-finger test was an internal examination of a rape survivor that claimed to show whether she was sexually active. In 2022 the Supreme Court named the idea behind it: the patriarchal and sexist assumption that a sexually active woman cannot be raped [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]]. The court had already condemned the test once, in 2013. This file follows the courts and the medical system through the 9 years between the two rulings, and the rules that bind doctors now. Our guide to the medical exam after rape explains what happens in the room.

## April 2013: a ruling and a new evidence law

In April 2013, in Lillu @ Rajesh v. State of Haryana, an appeal by a man convicted of rape, a Supreme Court bench of Justices B.S. Chauhan and F.M. Ibrahim Kalifulla held that the two-finger test violates the right of rape survivors to privacy, physical and mental integrity and dignity [[barandbench-lillu-2013]].

The same month, on 2 April 2013, the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 received the President's assent. It inserted Section 53A into the Indian Evidence Act: in trials for rape and other sexual offences, a victim's character or previous sexual experience is not relevant to the question of consent [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. The same Act required every hospital, public or private, to treat rape survivors free of cost [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

Together, these should have ended the test. Medically, as the court would later spell out, it could not show what it claimed. Legally, even if it could, the answer no longer mattered to consent.

## 31 October 2022: 'misconduct', and orders to hospitals and colleges

The court had to return to the subject. In State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai, decided on 31 October 2022, Justices D.Y. Chandrachud and Hima Kohli heard an old case in which a medical board had performed the test on the survivor; the court restored the accused's conviction. They said the test "has no scientific basis and neither proves nor disproves allegations of rape" [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]], and that it "re-victimizes and re-traumatizes" women [[theprint-sc-two-finger-test-2022]].

This time the court attached consequences. Anyone who conducts the test in breach of its directions "shall be guilty of misconduct". It told governments to send the Health Ministry's 2014 guidelines, which rule the test out, to every government and private hospital, and to review the curriculum in medical schools so that the test is not prescribed [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]]. The ruling covers survivors of rape and of penetrative sexual assault, so children examined in POCSO cases are protected too [[barandbench-two-finger-test-2022]].

Read those directions as a diagnosis. Guidelines written in 2014 had to be ordered into hospitals in 2022. Medical teaching had to be checked so that it no longer prescribed the test. The 2013 judgment had settled the law; it had not reached every hospital or every textbook.

## Why one ruling rarely ends a practice

| When | What changed |
|---|---|
| 2 April 2013 | Criminal Law (Amendment) Act gets assent: a survivor's sexual history is irrelevant to consent |
| April 2013 | Lillu: the test violates privacy, integrity and dignity |
| 2014 | Health Ministry guidelines on examining survivors |
| 31 October 2022 | Shailendra Kumar Rai: no scientific basis; conducting it is misconduct |
| 1 July 2024 | BNSS and BSA in force: examination only with consent, report within 7 days, sexual history barred |
| 10 February 2026 | Supreme Court says efforts to sensitise judges have fallen short |

A Supreme Court judgment is binding law, but it does not walk into a district hospital by itself. Doctors learn forensic routines from syllabuses, textbooks and senior colleagues, and a hospital can keep using an old examination format long after the law has moved. A ruling changes practice only when it travels into teaching, formats, training and discipline. That is what the 2022 directions tried to force.

The Supreme Court has said as much about its own judges. On 10 February 2026, in a case over a High Court order that had reduced the charges in a child sexual assault case, a bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant said efforts to sensitise judges "have not borne the fruit that was expected", and asked a National Judicial Academy expert committee to draft guidelines on sensitivity in sexual-offence cases [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]]. If judgments do not automatically change judges, they will not automatically change doctors.

## In the examination room in 2026

Since 1 July 2024, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) have replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Evidence Act [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. Three rules now frame every examination:

- **Consent.** Under Section 184 of the BNSS, police must send a rape survivor for a medical examination, preferably by a government doctor, within 24 hours of receiving the information, and only with her consent. The section makes clear that it does not permit any examination without her consent [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Deadline.** The doctor must send the report to the investigating officer within 7 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **History.** Under Section 48 of the BSA, a survivor's character or previous sexual experience is irrelevant to consent, and under Section 149 she may not be cross-examined about it to prove consent [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

If anyone suggests a "virginity" check or a finger test, the survivor can refuse it: the law does not permit an examination without her consent, and the Supreme Court has said anyone who conducts the test is guilty of misconduct. Note the date, the hospital and the names of the staff, then complain in writing to the hospital's head and the State Medical Council, citing State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai.

This is general information, not legal advice.
two-finger-test-supreme-court-2013-2026.hg:
So-called two-finger test rape survivor ka ek andar ka examination tha, jo daava karta tha ki isse pata chalega ki woh sexually active hai ya nahin. 2022 mein Supreme Court ne iske peeche ki soch ko naam diya: yeh patriarchal aur sexist soch ki ek sexually active aurat ka rape ho hi nahin sakta [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]]. Court 2013 mein bhi is test ko condemn kar chuki thi. Yeh file dono faislon ke beech ke 9 saal mein courts aur medical system ko follow karti hai, aur batati hai ki aaj doctors par kaun se rules laagu hain. Rape ke baad medical exam par hamari guide batati hai ki examination room mein kya hota hai.

## April 2013: ek faisla aur evidence ka naya law

April 2013 mein, Lillu @ Rajesh v. State of Haryana case mein, jo rape ke convict ek aadmi ki appeal thi, Justices B.S. Chauhan aur F.M. Ibrahim Kalifulla ki Supreme Court bench ne kaha ki two-finger test rape survivors ke privacy, physical aur mental integrity aur dignity ke right ko violate karta hai [[barandbench-lillu-2013]].

Usi mahine, 2 April 2013 ko, Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ko President ki manzoori mili. Isne Indian Evidence Act mein Section 53A joda: rape aur dusre sexual offences ke trials mein victim ka character ya pehle ka sexual experience consent ke sawaal par relevant nahin hai [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Isi Act ne har hospital ke liye, chahe sarkari ho ya private, rape survivors ka free ilaaj zaroori kar diya [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

In dono badlaavon ke baad yeh test khatam ho jaana chahiye tha. Medical taur par, jaisa court ne baad mein saaf kaha, yeh woh dikha hi nahin sakta tha jiska daava karta tha. Aur law ke hisaab se, agar dikha bhi deta, to consent ke liye uska jawab ab maayne nahin rakhta tha.

## 31 October 2022: 'misconduct', aur hospitals aur colleges ko order

Court ko is mudde par wapas aana pada. 31 October 2022 ko State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai case mein Justices D.Y. Chandrachud aur Hima Kohli ne ek purana case suna, jismein ek medical board ne survivor par yeh test kiya tha; court ne accused ka conviction bahaal kiya. Unhone kaha ki yeh test "has no scientific basis and neither proves nor disproves allegations of rape", yaani iska koi scientific aadhaar nahin hai aur yeh rape ke aarop ko na saabit karta hai, na jhuthlata hai [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]]. Court ne yeh bhi kaha ki yeh aurton ko "re-victimizes and re-traumatizes", yaani unhe dobara victim banata hai aur dobara trauma deta hai [[theprint-sc-two-finger-test-2022]].

Is baar court ne nateeje bhi tay kiye. Jo bhi uske directions ke khilaaf yeh test karega, woh "shall be guilty of misconduct", yaani misconduct ka doshi hoga. Court ne sarkaron se kaha ki Health Ministry ki 2014 ki guidelines, jo is test ki ijaazat nahin deti, har sarkari aur private hospital tak bhejein, aur medical schools ka curriculum review karein taaki yeh test kahin prescribe na ho [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]]. Yeh faisla rape aur penetrative sexual assault, dono ke survivors par laagu hota hai, isliye POCSO cases mein examine hone wale bachche bhi protected hain [[barandbench-two-finger-test-2022]].

In directions ko ek diagnosis ki tarah padhiye. 2014 mein likhi gayi guidelines ko 2022 mein order dekar hospitals tak pahunchana pada. Medical padhai ko check karna pada taaki woh yeh test prescribe na kare. 2013 ke judgment ne law tay kar diya tha, lekin woh har hospital aur har textbook tak nahin pahuncha tha.

## Ek faisla kisi practice ko aksar khatam kyun nahin karta

| Kab | Kya badla |
|---|---|
| 2 April 2013 | Criminal Law (Amendment) Act ko manzoori: survivor ki sexual history consent ke liye irrelevant |
| April 2013 | Lillu: test privacy, integrity aur dignity ko violate karta hai |
| 2014 | Survivors ke examination par Health Ministry ki guidelines |
| 31 October 2022 | Shailendra Kumar Rai: koi scientific aadhaar nahin; test karna misconduct |
| 1 July 2024 | BNSS aur BSA laagu: examination sirf consent se, report 7 din mein, sexual history par rok |
| 10 February 2026 | Supreme Court: judges ko sensitise karne ki koshishen kaafi nahin rahin |

Supreme Court ka judgment binding law hai, lekin woh khud chalkar kisi district hospital mein nahin pahunchta. Doctors forensic routines syllabus, textbooks aur seniors se seekhte hain, aur koi hospital law badalne ke kaafi baad tak purana examination format chalata reh sakta hai. Koi faisla practice tabhi badalta hai jab woh padhai, formats, training aur discipline tak pahunche. 2022 ke directions yahi karwane ki koshish the.

Supreme Court ne apne judges ke baare mein bhi yahi maana hai. 10 February 2026 ko ek High Court order par chal rahe case mein, jisne ek child sexual assault case mein charges ghata diye the, Chief Justice Surya Kant ki aguwai wali bench ne kaha ki judges ko sensitise karne ki koshishen "have not borne the fruit that was expected", yaani ummeed ke mutabik nateeje nahin aaye. Bench ne National Judicial Academy ki ek expert committee se sexual-offence cases mein sensitivity par guidelines draft karne ko kaha [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]]. Agar judgments judges ko apne aap nahin badalte, to doctors ko bhi apne aap nahin badlenge.

## 2026 mein examination room

1 July 2024 se Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) aur Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) ne Code of Criminal Procedure aur Evidence Act ki jagah le li hai [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. Ab har examination par teen rules laagu hote hain:

- **Consent.** BNSS ke Section 184 ke hisaab se police ko jaankari milne ke 24 ghante ke andar rape survivor ko medical examination ke liye bhejna hoga, behtar ho ki kisi sarkari doctor ke paas, aur sirf uske consent se. Section saaf kehta hai ki yeh uske consent ke bina kisi examination ki ijaazat nahin deta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Deadline.** Doctor ko 7 din ke andar report investigating officer ko bhejni hogi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **History.** BSA ke Section 48 ke hisaab se survivor ka character ya pehle ka sexual experience consent ke liye irrelevant hai, aur Section 149 ke hisaab se consent saabit karne ke liye cross-examination mein usse iske baare mein sawaal nahin poochhe ja sakte [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Agar koi "virginity" check ya finger test suggest kare, to survivor mana kar sakti hai: law uske consent ke bina examination ki ijaazat nahin deta, aur Supreme Court keh chuka hai ki yeh test karne wala misconduct ka doshi hai. Tareekh, hospital aur staff ke naam note kijiye, phir State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai ka hawala dete hue hospital head aur State Medical Council ko likhit complaint kijiye.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahin.

unnao-2017-mla-convicted-sentence-suspen.en:
In 2017, a girl under 18 in Unnao, Uttar Pradesh, accused a BJP MLA of raping her. Every stage of what followed shows how political power presses on a rape case: where it can be tried, what the crime is called in law, and how long the sentence lasts. In December 2019 a Delhi court sent Kuldeep Singh Sengar to prison for the rest of his life. Six years later, two words in the law, "public servant", got that sentence suspended until the Supreme Court stepped in. He is named here because a court convicted him. The survivor is not named, and never will be [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

## 2017: a complaint against a man with power

Consider what that complaint asked of a minor. The police who had to register her FIR and the officials who had to protect her family all worked in the state where the man she named was an elected legislator. Each of them could help her, or slow her down.

The damage reached her family too. Her father died in custody, and on 13 March 2020 a Delhi court sentenced Sengar and six others to 10 years in prison for culpable homicide over his death [[barandbench-unnao-father-2020]].

## Where it was tried: Delhi, not Uttar Pradesh

The Supreme Court moved every Unnao case out of the state, from Lucknow to Delhi [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. It had done the same in the Kathua rape and murder case in 2018, sending that trial to Pathankot in Punjab [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]].

Read that plainly: the top court chose not to leave the trial in the survivor's own state, where the accused was an elected legislator. Most survivors never get that protection, however much power the accused holds where they live.

## December 2019: prison for the rest of his life

On 20 December 2019, a Delhi district and sessions judge sentenced Sengar to imprisonment for the remainder of his life and a fine of Rs 25 lakh, Rs 10 lakh of it for the survivor [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. He was convicted of rape under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and of aggravated penetrative sexual assault under Sections 5(c) and 6 of the POCSO Act [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]].

"Aggravated" means circumstances that the law treats as worse. Here the circumstance was his office: the aggravated charge treated the MLA as a "public servant" [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]]. Hold on to that phrase.

Most child sexual abuse trials do not end like this. In 2024, courts convicted in only 32.3% of POCSO trials that ended: 12,672 convictions against 25,476 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Unnao was one of the exceptions.

## 2025-26: the "public servant" argument and the Supreme Court's answer

In December 2025 the Delhi High Court suspended the life sentence while his appeal was pending. At this interim stage it reasoned that an MLA is not a public servant under Section 21 of the IPC, so he "cannot be brought into the ambit of aggravated penetrative sexual assault". It also noted that he had already served more than seven years [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]].

Put the two points together. Without the aggravated label, the crime falls back to ordinary penetrative sexual assault. In 2017 its minimum sentence was seven years; Parliament raised that to 10 years only in August 2019 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. A question of definition was enough to suspend a life sentence. He stayed in jail anyway, because of the 10-year sentence over her father's death [[barandbench-unnao-father-2020]].

Delay did part of the work. Since 2018 the law has said that rape appeals should be decided within six months [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. This appeal was still pending six years after the conviction, and the years he had served became an argument for suspending the sentence.

On 29 December 2025, a Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant stayed the High Court's order [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]]. On 15 May 2026 the Court set that order aside and sent the matter back, asking the High Court either to decide his main appeal quickly or to pass a fresh order on suspending the sentence [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]]. We could not find a decision on that appeal as of November 2026.

## Power and punishment: what makes a rape "aggravated"

Indian law punishes some rapes more harshly because of who commits them. Under Section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which replaced the IPC on 1 July 2024 [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]], rape carries at least 10 years. The aggravated forms, including rape by police, public servants, relatives, guardians, teachers or "a person in a position of trust or authority towards the woman", carry 10 years up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. For a child, aggravated penetrative sexual assault now carries at least 20 years, up to the rest of natural life, or death [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Our section-by-section POCSO explainer sets out its offences and punishments in plain words. This is general information, not legal advice.

The reasoning is simple. Power makes the crime easier to commit and harder to report. Notice that "a position of trust or authority" does not depend on an official post.

On paper, rape by officials looks rare. In 2024 police registered 27 rape cases under the aggravated category for rape by police personnel and 15 for rape by other public servants [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These clauses cover narrow situations, such as a woman in an official's custody, and a case is counted only if the police invoke the clause. They show what gets written down, not how often power is abused.

Unnao is a case where the law did reach a powerful man. It took a trial moved out of the state and repeated Supreme Court orders. That is not a system working on its own; it had to be pushed at every stage, while the survivor's family paid a heavy price.
unnao-2017-mla-convicted-sentence-suspen.hg:
2017 mein Uttar Pradesh ke Unnao ki ek minor ladki ne BJP ke ek MLA par rape ka aarop lagaya. Uske baad jo kuch hua, uske har mod par dikhta hai ki political power ek rape case ko kaise dabati hai: case kahan chalega, law mein crime ko kya naam milega, aur sazaa kitni lambi hogi. December 2019 mein Delhi ki ek court ne Kuldeep Singh Sengar ko baaki zindagi ke liye jail bhej diya. Chhe saal baad law ke do shabdon, "public servant", ke sahaare yeh sazaa rok di gayi, jab tak Supreme Court ko beech mein nahi aana pada. Sengar ka naam hum isliye le rahe hain kyunki court ne use convict kiya hai. Survivor ka naam hum nahi lenge, kabhi nahi [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

## 2017: ek powerful aadmi ke khilaaf complaint

Sochiye, aisi complaint ek minor ladki se kitna kuch maangti hai. Jis police ko uski FIR likhni thi, aur jin officers ko uski family ki hifaazat karni thi, woh sab usi state mein kaam karte the jahan woh aadmi chuna hua MLA tha. Inmein se har koi uski madad kar sakta tha. Ya uska raasta rok sakta tha.

Nuksaan uski family tak bhi pahuncha. Uske pita ki custody mein maut ho gayi, aur 13 March 2020 ko Delhi ki ek court ne us maut ke liye Sengar aur chhe aur logon ko culpable homicide mein 10 saal jail ki sazaa sunayi [[barandbench-unnao-father-2020]].

## Trial kahan chala: Uttar Pradesh nahi, Delhi

Supreme Court ne Unnao se jude saare case state se bahar bhej diye, Lucknow se Delhi [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. 2018 mein Kathua rape aur murder case mein bhi court ne yahi kiya tha, aur woh trial Jammu-Kashmir se Punjab ke Pathankot bheja gaya tha [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]].

Iska seedha matlab samjhiye. Desh ki sabse badi court ne yeh trial survivor ke apne state mein nahi rehne diya, jahan accused ek chuna hua MLA tha. Zyadatar survivors ko yeh protection kabhi nahi milti, chahe accused unke ilaake mein kitna bhi powerful ho.

## December 2019: baaki zindagi jail mein

20 December 2019 ko Delhi ke ek district aur sessions judge ne Sengar ko baaki zindagi jail ki sazaa sunayi, saath mein Rs 25 lakh ka jurmana. Ismein se Rs 10 lakh survivor ko milne the [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. Use Indian Penal Code (IPC) ki Section 376 ke tahat rape ka doshi paaya gaya, aur POCSO Act ki Sections 5(c) aur 6 ke tahat "aggravated" penetrative sexual assault ka bhi [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]].

"Aggravated" ka matlab hai aise haalaat jinhe law zyada bura maanta hai. Yahan woh haalaat tha uska pad. Aggravated wale charge mein MLA ko "public servant" maana gaya tha [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]]. Yeh shabd yaad rakhiye.

Child sexual abuse ke zyadatar trials aise khatam nahi hote. 2024 mein jin POCSO trials ka faisla aaya, unmein se sirf 32.3% mein conviction hua: 12,672 convictions, jabki 25,476 case mein accused bari ho gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Unnao un gine-chune cases mein se ek tha.

## 2025-26: "public servant" wali daleel, aur Supreme Court ka jawaab

December 2025 mein Delhi High Court ne appeal pending rehte umrqaid ki sazaa rok di. Is shuruaati stage par court ne kaha ki IPC ki Section 21 ke hisaab se MLA public servant nahi hai, isliye us par "aggravated" penetrative sexual assault ka charge nahi banta. Court ne yeh bhi kaha ki woh saat saal se zyada jail kaat chuka hai [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]].

Ab dono baatein jodkar dekhiye. "Aggravated" ka label hatte hi crime normal penetrative sexual assault reh jaata hai. 2017 mein iski kam se kam sazaa saat saal thi; Parliament ne ise 10 saal August 2019 mein jaakar kiya [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yaani definition ka ek sawaal umrqaid ki sazaa rukwane ke liye kaafi tha. Phir bhi Sengar jail mein hi raha, kyunki survivor ke pita ki maut wale case mein use 10 saal ki sazaa ho chuki thi [[barandbench-unnao-father-2020]].

Deri ne bhi apna kaam kiya. 2018 se law kehta hai ki rape ki sazaa ke khilaaf appeal ka faisla chhe mahine mein ho jaana chahiye [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. Yeh appeal conviction ke chhe saal baad bhi pending thi, aur jail mein beete yahi saal sazaa rokne ki daleel ban gaye.

29 December 2025 ko Chief Justice Surya Kant ki aguwai wali Supreme Court bench ne High Court ke order par rok laga di [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]]. 15 May 2026 ko Supreme Court ne woh order radd kar diya aur maamla wapas High Court bhej diya. Court ne High Court se kaha ki ya toh woh Sengar ki main appeal par jaldi faisla kare, ya sazaa rokne ke sawaal par naya order de [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]]. November 2026 tak humein us appeal par koi faisla nahi mila.

## Power aur sazaa: rape "aggravated" kab maana jaata hai

Indian law kuch rapes par zyada sakht sazaa deta hai, yeh dekhkar ki crime kisne kiya. 1 July 2024 se IPC ki jagah Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) laagu hai [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]]. Iski Section 64 ke tahat rape ki sazaa kam se kam 10 saal hai. Aggravated forms mein police, public servants, rishtedaar, guardian, teacher, ya "a person in a position of trust or authority towards the woman" yaani aurat par bharose ya authority wali position ke insaan ka kiya rape aata hai. Inki sazaa 10 saal se lekar baaki poori zindagi ki jail tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Bachche ke saath aggravated penetrative sexual assault ki sazaa ab kam se kam 20 saal hai, jo baaki poori zindagi ki jail ya death penalty tak ja sakti hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. POCSO par hamara section-by-section explainer iske offences aur sazaon ko aasaan shabdon mein samjhata hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Wajah seedhi hai. Power ho toh crime karna aasaan ho jaata hai, aur uski complaint karna mushkil. Dhyaan dijiye, "position of trust or authority" ke liye kisi sarkari post ki zaroorat nahi hai.

Kaagaz par officials ke kiye rape bahut kam dikhte hain. 2024 mein police ne police walon ke kiye rape ki aggravated category mein 27 case darj kiye, aur doosre public servants ke kiye rape mein 15 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh clauses kuch khaas haalaat par hi laagu hote hain, jaise jab aurat kisi officer ki custody mein ho. Aur case is category mein tabhi gina jaata hai jab police khud yeh clause lagaye. Yeh numbers batate hain ki kaagaz par kya likha gaya, yeh nahi ki power ka galat istemaal kitni baar hota hai.

Unnao aisa case hai jismein law ek powerful aadmi tak pahuncha. Iske liye trial ko state se bahar le jaana pada, aur Supreme Court ko baar-baar orders dene pade. Yeh system ka apne aap kaam karna nahi hai. Ise har mod par dhakka dena pada, aur iski bhaari keemat survivor ki family ne chukaayi.

verma-committee-2013-what-parliament-ign.en:
In December 2012, days after the Delhi gang rape, the government asked three people to fix India's rape law: Justice J.S. Verma, Justice Leila Seth and Gopal Subramanium. Their report came on 23 January 2013 [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. An ordinance followed on 3 February 2013, and then a new law. But on the two points where the committee was clearest, Parliament went the other way, and India is still living with that choice.

## About a month to rewrite rape law

It was not the first time Verma had written rules Parliament had not. In 1997, as Chief Justice of India, he led the Supreme Court bench that laid down binding guidelines against sexual harassment at work, to apply until Parliament made a law [[sc-vishaka-rajasthan-1997]].

Two of the committee's positions matter most today. On punishment, it advised against the death penalty for rape, noting that it "may not have a deterrent effect". On marriage, it recommended deleting the marital rape exception in Section 375 of the IPC [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. PRS Legislative Research's summary of the report puts it plainly: "marriage should not be considered as an irrevocable consent to sexual acts" [[prs-verma-committee-summary-2013]].

## What the 2013 law added: new crimes and new duties

The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 got the President's assent on 2 April 2013 and was made to apply from 3 February 2013, the date of the ordinance. It raised the age of consent to 18 [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]] and widened the legal definition of rape to cover other forms of penetration, including with objects [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

It gave harms women had long faced names and sections of their own: acid attack (Sections 326A and 326B), sexual harassment (354A), disrobing (354B), voyeurism (354C) and stalking (354D) [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

It also put duties on the system. Every hospital, public or private, must give a rape or acid-attack survivor first aid or treatment immediately and free, and inform the police; refusing became a crime [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. A police officer who fails to record an FIR for rape faces six months to two years in prison, and a survivor's character or sexual past became irrelevant to the question of consent [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

Imagine a 19-year-old in Indore who reaches a private hospital after being raped. The hospital cannot turn her away or bill her. It must treat her at once and inform the police itself. That duty survived the new codes: it is now Section 397 of the BNSS [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], and the BNS punishes police who fail to record a rape FIR (Section 199) and hospitals that refuse free treatment (Section 200) [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## What Parliament rejected: the advice on death and marriage

On punishment, the same Act made rape that causes death or leaves a woman in a persistent vegetative state open to the death penalty (Section 376A), and made repeat offenders liable to death or to prison for the rest of their natural life (Section 376E) [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

On marriage, it kept Exception 2 to Section 375: sex by a man with his own wife, "the wife not being under fifteen years of age", was not rape [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. From 2013 until 2017, a husband's sex with a 15-to-17-year-old wife was not legally rape [[indiacode-cla-2013]], even though the same law said a girl under 18 could not consent to anyone else. The Supreme Court ended that on 11 October 2017 in Independent Thought v. Union of India, ruling that sex with a wife under 18 is rape [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

Parliament said yes to harsher punishment and no to the one change that would reach inside the home. That is where the survey data points: among ever-married women aged 18-49 who have ever faced sexual violence, 82% named their current husband as the perpetrator and 14% a former husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## 2018: the death penalty spreads

An ordinance of 21 April 2018, made law by an Act that received assent on 11 August, allowed the death penalty for raping a girl under 12 (Section 376AB) and for gang rape of a girl under 12 (Section 376DB) [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. It raised the minimum sentence for rape from seven to ten years [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. A 2019 amendment brought the death penalty into the POCSO Act for aggravated penetrative sexual assault on a child [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Did tougher laws bring more justice? In 2012, courts convicted in about 24% of the rape trials they completed [[ncrb-cii-2012-figures-at-a-glance]]. In 2024 the figure was 24.4%: 5,032 convictions against 13,980 acquittals. At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were still pending trial [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The laws made sentences harsher. They did not change how rarely a rape trial ends in a sentence: most completed trials still end without a conviction.

## December 2026: the Verma question returns

The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which replaced the IPC on 1 July 2024 [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]], kept the exception. Under Exception 2 to Section 63, sex by a man with his wife, if she is 18 or older, is not rape. A husband who forces sex on a wife living separately faces 2 to 7 years under Section 67, far below the 10-year minimum for raping any other woman [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

In October 2024 the Union government told the Supreme Court that marital rape is "more of a social issue rather than a legal issue", and that calling it rape could be "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]]. It argued that other laws, including the Domestic Violence Act, already protect married women. That Act does count sexual abuse as domestic violence, but it is mainly a civil law of protection, residence and maintenance orders [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. The exception the Verma Committee wanted deleted is still being defended in court.

India has been told this before. In July 2014 the UN's CEDAW committee urged India to implement the Verma Committee's recommendations and, repeating a request it had made in 2007, to make marital rape a crime [[cedaw-india-concluding-observations-2014]].

As of 19 November 2026, the Supreme Court had still not ruled. A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said it would fix the final hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026 [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. More than a decade after the report, its question is back in court: does marriage mean consent for life?

This is general information, not legal advice.
verma-committee-2013-what-parliament-ign.hg:
December 2012 mein, Delhi gang rape ke kuch hi din baad, sarkar ne teen logon ko India ka rape law theek karne ka kaam diya: Justice J.S. Verma, Justice Leila Seth aur Gopal Subramanium. Unki report 23 January 2013 ko aayi [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. 3 February 2013 ko ek ordinance aaya, aur phir naya law. Lekin jin do baaton par committee sabse clear thi, un par Parliament ulti disha mein gayi, aur India aaj tak us faisle ka asar jhel raha hai.

## Lagbhag ek mahine mein rape law dobara likhna

Ye pehli baar nahi tha jab Verma aise rules likh rahe the jo Parliament ne nahi banaye the. 1997 mein, Chief Justice of India rehte hue, unhone Supreme Court ki us bench ko lead kiya jisne workplace par sexual harassment ke khilaaf binding guidelines banayi. Ye guidelines tab tak laagu rehni thi, jab tak Parliament khud law na bana de [[sc-vishaka-rajasthan-1997]].

Committee ki do baatein aaj sabse zyada matter karti hain. Saza par, usne rape ke liye death penalty ke khilaaf salaah di, ye note karte hue ki iska "may not have a deterrent effect", yaani phaansi ka darr crime rokne mein shayad kaam na aaye. Shaadi par, usne recommend kiya ki IPC Section 375 se marital rape exception poori tarah hata diya jaaye [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. PRS Legislative Research ki report summary ise seedhe shabdon mein kehti hai: "marriage should not be considered as an irrevocable consent to sexual acts", yaani shaadi ko sexual acts ke liye aisi consent nahi maana jaana chahiye jo kabhi wapas na li ja sake [[prs-verma-committee-summary-2013]].

## 2013 ke law ne kya joda: naye crimes aur nayi zimmedariyan

Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ko 2 April 2013 ko President ki manzoori mili, aur ise 3 February 2013 se laagu maana gaya, jo ordinance ki date thi. Isne age of consent 18 kar di [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]] aur rape ki legal definition badi kar di, taaki doosre tareekon se penetration aur kisi object ka istemaal bhi usme aaye [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

Aurtein saalon se kai tarah ke harm jhel rahi thin. Is law ne unhe apna naam aur apna section diya: acid attack (Sections 326A aur 326B), sexual harassment (354A), kapde utaarne ki neeyat se hamla yaani disrobing (354B), chupke se dekhna ya photo lena yaani voyeurism (354C), aur peecha karna yaani stalking (354D) [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

Law ne system par zimmedari bhi daali. Har hospital, sarkari ho ya private, rape ya acid attack survivor ko turant aur free first aid ya ilaaj dega, aur police ko batayega; mana karna crime ban gaya [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Jo police officer rape ki FIR record nahi karta, use chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai. Aur consent ke sawaal par survivor ka character ya sexual past irrelevant ho gaya [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

Sochiye, Indore ki ek 19 saal ki ladki rape ke baad kisi private hospital pahunchti hai. Hospital use lauta nahi sakta, bill nahi bana sakta. Use turant ilaaj dena hoga aur khud police ko batana hoga. Ye duty naye codes mein bhi bachi rahi: ab ye BNSS ka Section 397 hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Aur BNS dono ko saza deta hai: rape ki FIR na likhne wali police ko (Section 199), aur free ilaaj se mana karne wale hospital ko (Section 200) [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Parliament ne kya thukraya: death penalty aur shaadi par salaah

Saza par, usi Act ne aise rape ke liye death penalty ka rasta khola jisme aurat ki maut ho jaaye, ya woh hamesha ke liye aisi haalat mein chali jaaye jisme body zinda rahe par hosh na laute (persistent vegetative state) (Section 376A). Jo aadmi pehle rape mein convict ho chuka ho aur phir se convict ho, uske liye death ya baaki poori zindagi jail rakhi gayi (Section 376E) [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

Shaadi par, usne Section 375 ka Exception 2 rehne diya: aadmi ka apni wife ke saath sex, "the wife not being under fifteen years of age", yaani agar wife 15 saal se kam ki nahi hai, rape nahi tha [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Matlab 2013 se 2017 tak, 15 se 17 saal ki wife ke saath husband ka sex legally rape nahi tha [[indiacode-cla-2013]], jabki usi law ke hisaab se 18 se kam ki ladki kisi aur ko consent de hi nahi sakti thi. Supreme Court ne 11 October 2017 ko Independent Thought v. Union of India case mein ye khatam kiya, aur kaha ki 18 se kam ki wife ke saath sex rape hai [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

Parliament ne sakht sazaon ko haan kaha, aur us ek badlaav ko na kaha jo ghar ke andar tak pahunchta. Aur survey data ghar ki taraf hi ishara karta hai: 18-49 saal ki jin ever-married women ne kabhi sexual violence jheli, unme se 82% ne apne current husband ko zimmedar bataya, aur 14% ne pehle wale husband ko [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## 2018: death penalty ka daayra aur bada

21 April 2018 ko ek ordinance aaya, jise 11 August ko manzoori paane wale Act ne law banaya. Isne 12 saal se kam umar ki bachchi ke rape (Section 376AB) aur gang rape (Section 376DB) ke liye death penalty jod di [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. Rape ki minimum saza bhi saat saal se badhakar das saal ho gayi [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. 2019 ke ek amendment ne POCSO Act mein bachchon par aggravated penetrative sexual assault ke liye bhi death penalty jod di [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Toh kya sakht laws se zyada insaaf mila? 2012 mein courts ne jitne rape trials poore kiye, unme se lagbhag 24% mein conviction hua [[ncrb-cii-2012-figures-at-a-glance]]. 2024 mein ye figure 24.4% tha: 5,032 convictions aur 13,980 acquittals. 2024 ke end mein 1,85,785 rape cases ka trial abhi pending tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Laws ne sazaayein sakht kar di. Par rape trial kitni kam baar saza tak pahunchta hai, ye nahi badla: aaj bhi zyadatar poore hue rape trials bina conviction ke khatam hote hain.

## December 2026: Verma ka sawaal phir court mein

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne 1 July 2024 ko IPC ki jagah li [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]], aur usne bhi ye exception rakha. Section 63 ke Exception 2 ke hisaab se, agar wife 18 ya usse badi hai, toh husband ka uske saath sex rape nahi hai. Agar wife alag reh rahi ho aur husband zabardasti kare, toh Section 67 mein 2 se 7 saal ki saza hai, jo kisi aur aurat ke rape ki 10 saal ki minimum saza se kaafi kam hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

October 2024 mein Union government ne Supreme Court se kaha ki marital rape "more of a social issue rather than a legal issue" hai, yaani legal se zyada social issue, aur ise rape kehna "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" ho sakta hai, yaani zaroorat se zyada sakht [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]]. Sarkar ka kehna tha ki Domestic Violence Act jaise doosre law married women ko pehle se protect karte hain. Ye Act sexual abuse ko domestic violence zaroor maanta hai, lekin ye mainly ek civil law hai, jisme protection, ghar mein rehne ke haq (residence) aur maintenance ke orders milte hain [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Matlab jis exception ko Verma Committee hatana chahti thi, uska bachaav aaj bhi court mein ho raha hai.

India ko ye baat pehle bhi kahi ja chuki hai. July 2014 mein UN ki CEDAW committee ne India se kaha tha ki woh Verma Committee ki recommendations laagu kare. Saath hi usne marital rape ko crime banane ki maang dohraayi, jo woh 2007 mein bhi kar chuki thi [[cedaw-india-concluding-observations-2014]].

19 November 2026 tak Supreme Court ne faisla nahi diya tha. Chief Justice Surya Kant aur Justices Joymalya Bagchi aur V. Mohana ki bench ne kaha ki final hearing 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko fix hogi [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. Report ke ek dashak se bhi zyada baad uska sawaal phir court mein hai: kya shaadi ka matlab zindagi bhar ki consent hai?

Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

x-v-principal-secretary-2022-case-histor.en:
In the law reports she has no name, only a letter. In July 2022 X, unmarried and about 22 weeks pregnant, asked the Delhi High Court to let her end the pregnancy and was refused. Within a week the Supreme Court found her a way through; on 29 September 2022 it used her appeal to change who India's abortion rules are written for. This is the case history behind our Abortion desk's explainers: how a court read a law to protect autonomy, where it stopped, and why she stayed anonymous. It is general information, not legal advice.

## July 2022: 22 weeks pregnant and turned away

Her problem was a list. Since the 2021 amendment, abortion between 20 and 24 weeks has been allowed only for categories of women named in the rules, and only if two registered doctors agree [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Rule 3B, notified on 12 October 2021, named seven, including survivors of rape, minors, and women whose marital status changes during the pregnancy through widowhood or divorce [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. A woman who had never married was not on it.

The list had a history. The 1971 Act presumed a failed contraceptive gravely injured a woman's mental health only if it was used by "any married woman or her husband" [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]; that became "any woman or her partner" only in 2021 [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. The rules for later pregnancies still sorted women by marriage.

On 15 July 2022 the Delhi High Court refused her interim relief, saying it "cannot go beyond the Statute" [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. That is the literal method: apply the words as written and leave anyone they miss to wait for Parliament. For a woman whose pregnancy advances every day, waiting is itself a refusal.

## 21 July 2022: the interim order and the AIIMS board

She appealed. On 21 July 2022 the Supreme Court modified the High Court's order and allowed her to end the pregnancy if a Medical Board at AIIMS Delhi found it safe [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. AIIMS later reported that the termination was carried out safely [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

That settled her own case. It did not settle the legal question: could a woman be refused care between 20 and 24 weeks only because she had never married? The final judgment answered it for every unmarried woman in India.

## 29 September 2022: autonomy, dignity and the 'artificial' distinction

The bench of Justices D.Y. Chandrachud, A.S. Bopanna and J.B. Pardiwala built on two earlier rulings [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]]. In Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration (2009), the court had explicitly recognised a woman's reproductive autonomy. In K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017), the nine-judge privacy ruling, it had tied the statutory right to abortion to the right to make reproductive choices under Article 21 [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

The reasoning took two steps. Read as covering only married women, Rule 3B would discriminate against unmarried women and violate Article 14, the right to equality [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. So it could not be read that way: unmarried and single women are entitled to abortion between 20 and 24 weeks on the same footing as married women [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]].

> "This artificial distinction between married and single women is not constitutionally sustainable." [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]]

The court did not strike the rule down. It read the category for a "change of marital status" to cover unmarried and single women whose circumstances change during the pregnancy [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]]. Reading a rule by its purpose, with the Constitution in view, is the opposite of "cannot go beyond the Statute". Here it decided the case.

## Marital rape recognised, for one law only

The judgment settled a second question too. Rule 3B's first category is survivors of sexual assault or rape [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. The bench held that "rape" there includes a husband's rape of his wife, "solely for the purposes of the MTP Act", so a wife pregnant from forced sex can seek an abortion up to 24 weeks [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]]. She need not file an FIR or prove the rape in court first [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Why only that law? The challenge to the marital rape exception in the Indian Penal Code was pending before a different bench [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]]. On 11 May 2022 two Delhi High Court judges had split on the exception, and that case went to the Supreme Court [[livelaw-rit-foundation-split-2022]].

Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita still says that sex by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. As of 19 November 2026 the Supreme Court had not ruled, and said it would fix the final hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026 [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. Until then, forced sex by a husband on an adult wife counts as rape for an abortion, but not as the crime of rape.
